Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the English translation.
5. The target language is English.

p.seg: Basic Annals I: Tàizǔ the Elder
Tàizǔ Dàshèng Dàmíng Shénliè Tiānhuángdì,
whose surname was Yēlǜ,
whose taboo name was Yì,
whose courtesy name was Ābǎojī,
and whose childhood name was Chuòlǐzhī,
was a person of the Yēlǜ Mǐlǐ settlement in Xiālàiyìshíliè township, Diélà tribe, Qìdān.
He was the eldest son of Dédé Zǔ Huángdì,
and his mother was Xuānjiǎn Huánghòu Xiāo Shì.
He was born in the thirteenth year of Táng Xiántōng [872 CE].
Initially,
his mother dreamt that the sun fell into her bosom,
and she became pregnant.
When he was born,
the room was filled with divine light and extraordinary fragrance;
his body was like that of a three-year-old child,
and he was immediately able to crawl.
His grandmother, Jiǎnxiàn Huánghòu, found him extraordinary,
and raised him as her own son.
She often hid him in a separate tent,
painted his face,
and did not allow others to see him.
He could walk after three months;
at one year old, he could speak
and foresee future events.
He claimed that divine beings were constantly protecting and assisting him on his left and right.
Although he was still a child,
his words inevitably touched upon matters of state.
At that time, his uncle was leading the state,
and always consulted him when in doubt.
When he grew up,
he was nine feet tall,
with a thick upper body and a slender lower body;
his gaze was piercing,
and he could draw a three-hundred-catties bow.
He served as the Tà Mǎ Juě Shā Lǐ (Horse-Taming-and-Riding Marshal).
At that time, the Minor Huáng Shìwéi did not submit,
but Tàizǔ subdued them through stratagem.
He attacked the Yuèwù and the Wūgǔ, Liùxī, Bǐshā Juě tribes
and conquered them.
The people of the state called him Āzhǔ Shā Lǐ (Commander-in-Chief).
In the first year of Táng Tiānfù [901 CE],
the year Xīnyǒu,
after Héndéjǐn Kèhán was enthroned,
he appointed Tàizǔ as the Yílíjǐn (Commander) of his own tribe,
entrusting him exclusively with military campaigns.
He successively defeated the Shìwéi, Yújué, and the Xī chief Xiálàgē,
capturing many prisoners.
In winter, tenth month,
he was granted the position of Yílíjǐn of the Great Diéliè Prefecture.
The following year, autumn, seventh month,
he led an army of four hundred thousand to attack Hédōng Dàiběi,
capturing nine commanderies,
and taking ninety-five thousand people prisoner,
along with an uncountable number of camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
In the ninth month,
he constructed Longhuà Zhōu south of the Huánghé River
and established the first Kāijiào Sì temple.
The following year, spring,
he attacked the Nǚzhí,
subduing them
and capturing three hundred of their households.
In the ninth month,
he again attacked and captured Huáiyuǎn and other military garrisons in Hédōng.
In winter, tenth month,
he led his army in a raid as far as Jìběi,
returning with captives.
Previously, Dédé Zǔ had captured seven thousand households of the Xī,
and moved them to Qīnghé in Ráolè.
At this point, the Xī Diélà tribe was established for them,
divided into thirteen counties.
Subsequently, Tàizǔ was appointed Yúyuè and overall commander of military and state affairs.
The following year, the year Jiǎzǐ [904 CE],
third month,
the eastern city of Longhuà Zhōu was expanded.
In the ninth month,
he attacked the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi.
Liú Rénngōng, the Jìedùshǐ (Military Governor) of Táng Lúlóng Commandery, mobilized tens of thousands of troops
and dispatched his adopted son Zhào Bà to resist.
When Bà reached Wǔ Zhōu,
Tàizǔ learned of it through spies
and ambushed strong troops beneath Peach Mountain.
He sent Mú Lǐ, a Shìwéi person, to falsely claim he was sent by their chieftain
and arrange a meeting with Bà's army on the plain.
Once they arrived,
the ambush troops sprang out from all four sides,
capturing Bà
and annihilating his forces.
Riding on the victory, they heavily defeated the Shìwéi.
The following year, seventh month,
he again attacked the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi.
Lǐ Kèyòng, the Jìedùshǐ of Táng Hédōng, sent his Communicator Kāng Lìngdé to request an alliance.
In winter, tenth month,
Tàizǔ, with seventy thousand cavalry, met Kèyòng in Yún Zhōu.
During the feast,
Kèyòng requested troops to retaliate against Liú Rénngōng for the battle at Mùguā Jiàn,
and Tàizǔ agreed.
They exchanged robes and horses,
and swore to be brothers.
When they advanced to attack Rénngōng,
they captured several prefectures
and moved all the inhabitants away before returning.
The following year, second month,
he again attacked Liú Rénngōng.
Upon returning,
he raided the Xī north of the mountains
and defeated them.
Zhū Quánzhōng of Biàn Zhōu sent envoys by sea bearing letters, silk, belts, and rare treasures to establish relations.
In the eleventh month,
he dispatched a division to attack the Xī and Xí tribes and the unsubmitted Nǚzhí in the northeast,
and completely defeated and subdued them.
In the twelfth month,
Héndéjǐn Kèhán died.
The officials upheld his dying wish and requested Tàizǔ be enthroned.
Hélǔ and others urged him to accept the throne.
Tàizǔ declined three times,
but then accepted.
First year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín [907 CE],
he ordered the authorities to set up an altar at Rúyūwáng Jíhuìguō,
burned firewood to inform Heaven,
and ascended the imperial throne.
He honored his mother, Xiāo Shì, as the Huáng Tàihòu (Empress Dowager),
and established Empress Xiāo Shì.
The Northern Chancellor Xiāo Xiálà and the Southern Chancellor Yēlǜ Ōulǐsī, leading the officials, presented him with the honored title Tiān Huángdì (Heavenly Emperor),
and the Empress with the title Dì Huánghòu (Earthly Empress).
On the day Gēngzǐ,
an edict decreed that the nine tents of the royal lineage, the Chéngyáoniǎn Shì, should constitute the tenth tent.
Second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
he appointed his younger cousin Diélìdǐ as the Yílíjǐn of the Diéliè Prefecture.
In this month,
he campaigned against the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi
and subdued eight of their tribes.
Summer, fourth month, first day Dīngwèi,
Zhū Quánzhōng, the Prince of Liáng of Táng, deposed his sovereign,
and soon assassinated him.
He enthroned himself as Emperor,
with the state name Liáng,
and sent an envoy to announce this.
Liú Rénngōng's son Shǒuguāng imprisoned his father
and proclaimed himself Jìedùshǐ of Yōu Zhōu Lúlóng Commandery.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
his elder brother Shǒuqí, the Prefect of Píng Zhōu, brought several thousand of his followers to surrender.
He ordered them to be settled in Pínglú city.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐsì,
he campaigned against the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi
and defeated them.
Second year, spring, first month, first day Guǐyǒu [908 CE],
he held court in the main palace to receive homage from all officials and envoys from various states.
On the day Xīnsì,
the office of Tìyǐn (Chief of Imperial Kin) was first established
to oversee the imperial clan.
His younger brother Sālà was appointed to this post.
Lǐ Kèyòng of Hédōng died;
his son Cúnxù succeeded him.
An envoy was sent to express condolences and comfort.
Summer, fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict commanded Sālà to attack the Wūwán and Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi.
Autumn, eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Yōu Zhōu presented Héquān melons.
Winter, tenth month, first day Jǐhài,
the Míngwáng Lóu (Bright King Tower) was constructed.
A long wall was built at the entrance to Zhèndōng Hǎi.
Light troops were dispatched to capture the Tǔhún who had rebelled and joined the Shìwéi.
Third year, spring, first month [909 CE],
he visited Liáodōng.
Second month, first day Dīngyǒu,
Liáng sent Láng Gōngyuǎn to establish relations.
Third month,
Liú Shǒuwén, the Jìedùshǐ of Cāng Zhōu, was attacked by his younger brother Shǒuguāng,
and sent an envoy to request troops to campaign against him.
He ordered his younger brother Shèlìsù and the Yílíjǐn Xiāo Dílǔ to meet Shǒuwén with troops at Běinào Kǒu.
They advanced near the marsh of Hénnghǎi Commandery,
broke the enemy in one strike,
and Shǒuguāng fled in disarray.
Běinào Kǒu was consequently named Huìméng Kǒu (Alliance Meeting Entrance).
Summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
an edict commanded the Left Grandee Secretary Hán Zhīgǔ to erect a stele at Dàguǎng Sì in Longhuà Zhōu to record his meritorious achievements.
Fifth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Yáng Chéng (Sheep City) was established north of Tàn Shān to facilitate trade.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Eagle Army was dispatched to attack the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi
and defeated them.
The Wànniánggǎi tribe in the northwest presented people who pull carts.
Fourth year, autumn, seventh month, first day Wùzǐ [910 CE],
he appointed the Empress's elder brother Xiāo Dílǔ as the Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture.
The tradition of appointing the Empress's clan members as Chancellors began from this point.
Winter, tenth month,
the Xī Ku Zhī, along with Zhālàdǐ and Chúbódé, in Wūmǎ Shān rebelled.
They were attacked and pacified.
There was a solar eclipse.
On the day *bǐngshēn* (丙申),
the Sovereign personally campaigned against the Western Xī.
The Xī occupied dangerous terrain,
and their allegiance was constantly shifting between rebellion and submission.
Repeated attempts to recruit and persuade them were ignored.
In this campaign, every objective was immediately taken.
Consequently, troops were divided to punish the Eastern Xī,
and they were also pacified.
Thus, all the lands of the Xī and the Xí were acquired.
To the east, they reached the sea;
to the south, they extended to Báitán;
to the west, they crossed Sōngmò;
to the north, they reached Huáng Shuǐ.
In total, five divisions
were all brought into the census registers.
The third month,
they encamped at Luán Hé,
where a stone was carved to record the achievement.
They again raided the area of Jìzhōu.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day *rénshēn* (壬申),
an envoy was dispatched to Liáng.
The fifth month,
the imperial younger brothers Làgě, Diélà, Yǐndǐshí, and Ānduān plotted rebellion.
Ānduān’s wife, Niánmùgū, became aware of it,
reported it,
and the truth was verified.
The Sovereign could not bear to execute them;
thus, he ascended a mountain with his younger brothers and sacrificed animals,
making an oath to Heaven and Earth and pardoning their crimes.
Làgě was appointed Yílíjǐn of the Diélà division.
Niánmùgū was enfeoffed as Jìn Guó Fūrén.
Autumn, the seventh month, the day *rénwǔ* (壬午) was the new moon.
Xiélídǐ and envoys from various foreign states came to offer tribute.
The eighth month, on the day *jiǎzǐ* (甲子),
Liú Shǒuguāng usurped the title in Yōuzhōu,
naming his state Yān.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day *wùwǔ* (戊午),
an iron smelting facility was established.
The eleventh month, on the day *rénwǔ* (壬午),
an envoy was dispatched to Liáng.
The sixth year, spring, the first month,
Huàgě was made Tìyǐn.
The second month, on the day *wùwǔ* (戊午),
the Sovereign personally campaigned against Liú Shǒuguāng.
The third month,
he arrived back from Yōuzhōu.
Summer, the fourth month,
Yǐng Wáng Yǒuguī of Liáng murdered his father and enthroned himself.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day *bǐngwǔ* (丙午),
the Sovereign personally campaigned against Zhúbùgū,
forcing their surrender,
capturing tens of thousands of prisoners.
He ordered his younger brother Làgě to divide the troops and attack Píngzhōu.
The eighth month, on the day *rénchén* (壬辰),
the Sovereign encamped at Ēndé Shān.
The Imperial Prince Lǐ Hú was born.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day *wùyín* (戊寅),
Làgě defeated Píngzhōu,
returned,
and then rebelled again with Diélà, Yǐndǐshí, and Ānduān.
On the day *jiǎshēn* (甲申),
an envoy was dispatched to Liáng to offer sacrifices.
On the day *rénchén* (壬辰),
the army returned and encamped at Běi Ālǔ Shān.
Hearing that his younger brothers were blocking the road with troops,
the Sovereign led the army south toward Shíqī Luò.
On this day, brushwood was burned (for sacrifice).
The following day,
they encamped at Qī Dù Hé.
The younger brothers each sent men to apologize for their crimes.
The Sovereign still pitied and cherished them,
allowing them to renew themselves.
That year,
troops were used to punish Liǎng Yě.
Fifty people, including the monk Chóngwén, who were captured, were brought back to Xīlóu,
and Tiānxióng Sì was founded to house them,
thereby demonstrating that Heaven aids the heroic and mighty.
The seventh year, spring, the first month, the day *jiǎchén* (甲辰) was the new moon.
Due to military deployment, court was suspended.
Jìn Wáng Lǐ Cúnxù captured Yōuzhōu,
taking Liú Shǒuguāng prisoner.
On the day *jiǎyín* (甲寅),
the sovereign’s army encamped at Chìshuǐ Chéng.
The younger brother Làgě and others pleaded for surrender.
The Sovereign wore plain attire,
rode a reddish-white horse,
with the generals Yēlǜ Lègū and Xiálàjǐn Ābō as charioteers,
removed his weapons, and dismissed his retinue to receive them,
then offered them additional comfort and instruction.
Làgě and the others withdrew,
and the Sovereign repeatedly sent envoys to pacify and comfort them.
The second month, the day *jiǎxū* (甲戌) was the new moon.
Jūn Wáng Yǒuzhēn of Liáng campaigned against and killed his elder brother Yǒuguī,
and succeeded to the throne.
The third month, on the day *guǐchǒu* (癸丑),
they encamped at Lú Shuǐ.
The younger brother Diélà Gētú was Xī Wáng.
He arrived with Ānduān, leading over a thousand cavalry,
falsely claiming to have come for an audience.
The Sovereign was angry and said:
"You first plotted treasonous rebellion,
and We specially pardoned you,
allowing you to correct your faults and renew yourselves.
Yet you still show such duplicity;
this will bring misfortune upon Us!"
Thereupon, he detained them.
Their followers were divided and assigned to various armies.
Meanwhile, Làgě led his followers to Yǐshìjǐn Diàn,
setting up the imperial banners and drums,
intending to establish himself.
The Empress Dowager secretly sent someone to warn him to flee.
Just then, Mǐgūnǎi and Huáilǐyáng reported that the imperial carriage was approaching,
and his followers dispersed in panic.
They plundered the residents and fled north.
The Sovereign pursued them with troops.
Làgě sent his ally Yǐndǐshí to lead troops straight toward the traveling palace,
burning the baggage train and encampment tents,
and letting his soldiers loose for a massive slaughter.
The Empress urgently dispatched Shǔgǔlǔ to rescue the palace,
managing only to retrieve the imperial banners and drums.
His ally Shénsùgū again raided Xīlóu,
burning the Míngwáng Lóu.
The Sovereign arrived at Tǔ Hé,
fed the horses and rested the troops,
appearing unconcerned.
The generals requested an immediate pursuit.
The Sovereign said:
"Wait until they have fled far away.
Everyone will begin to long for home (their soil).
Once the longing for home is intense,
their resolve will certainly fracture.
Our army, taking advantage of this,
is certain to defeat them!"
He distributed all the captured wealth and livestock obtained previously to the generals and soldiers.
He left the Yílíbì Zhílǐgū in charge of all governmental affairs.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day *wùyín* (戊寅),
he pursued Làgě northwards.
On the day *jǐmǎo* (己卯),
they encamped at Mí Lǐ.
He inquired about the ritual where his younger brothers faced Mùyè Shān and shot "ghost arrows" (to ward off misfortune).
Thereupon, he captured the rebel Jiělǐ, faced him toward that direction,
and used the same method of spiritual exorcism on him.
Upon reaching Dá Lǐ Diàn,
light cavalry were chosen to pursue and catch them at Péizhǐ Hé,
capturing all the rebel faction's baggage train and prisoners.
Five men, including the chiefs of the Shìwéi and Tǔhún, Bálà and Dílǐgū, were first sent to divide their troops and ambush the rebels on the road ahead.
The Běi Zǎixiàng Dílǐgǔ was ordered to lead the attack as the vanguard.
Làgě led his troops to fight back.
Dílǐgǔ pressed them with light troops.
His younger brother Ègǔzhī approached the battle line,
shooting and killing dozens of men,
so the multitude dared not advance.
They held the line against each other until late afternoon,
when the multitude finally collapsed.
They were pursued to Chái Hé,
whereupon the rebels burned their own chariots, wagons, and tents before leaving.
Previously, Bálà and Dílǐgū’s ambush had been sprung;
they combined their attacks,
and consequently inflicted a great defeat.
Làgě fled and dispersed,
abandoning the sacred tent he had stolen on the road.
The Sovereign saw it and bowed in reverence before it.
All the captured prisoners were released to return to their native lands.
His allies Kùgǔzhī and Móduǒ came bound and petitioned for pardon.
The army encamped at Zhádǔ Hé,
where a great rain caused a sudden swell in the river.
The fifth month, on the day *guǐchǒu* (癸丑),
the Běi Zǎixiàng Díniǎn was dispatched to lead the crack cavalry across first.
On the day *jiǎyín* (甲寅),
a report was made that Làgě and Nièlǐgǔn Ābō had been captured at Yú Hé,
and the former Běi Zǎixiàng Xiāo Shílǔ and Yǐndǐshí had attempted suicide by self-stabbing but did not die.
Consequently, black and white sheep were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
On the day *rénxū* (壬戌),
Làgě and Nièlǐgǔn Ābō arrived at the imperial encampment,
binding themselves with ropes,
leading a sheep, and bowing from a distance.
The Sovereign returned to Dà Lǐng.
At this time, the great army had been away for a long time,
and the baggage train was disconnected.
The officers and soldiers cooked colts and gathered wild vegetables for food.
Seventeen or eighteen tenths of the livestock died on the journey.
Prices increased tenfold.
Utensils, clothing, and goods were abandoned at Chǔlǐ Hé,
strewn about for hundreds of *lǐ*.
Consequently, Làgě's name was changed to Bàolǐ.
On the day *bǐngyín* (丙寅),
they arrived at Kù Lǐ,
and sacrificed a dark ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.
Six hundred prisoners and two thousand three hundred horses were divided and bestowed upon the Great and Small Hú Jūn.
On the *xīnsì* day of the sixth month,
he arrived at Yúlǐng.
Because Sǎogǔ, a native of Xiálài County, illegally oppressed the people,
he was dismembered.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor ascended Dū'ān Shān,
and, stroking the ruins of his ancestor Qíshǒu Kèhán,
he walked around, gazed, and sighed.
Hearing that the prison official Nièlǐ arbitrarily fabricated serious charges,
making people suffer intolerably,
some even to death,
he ordered him executed.
On the *rénchén* day,
he encamped at Lánghé,
where he captured the rebel leaders Yǎlǐ and Mílǐ,
and buried them alive beneath the south track of Tónghé.
He released the captives to return,
but many were plundered by Yúgǔlǐ.
The Emperor was enraged,
and led light cavalry to swiftly attack them.
He then dispatched brave generals to pursue and attack them via separate routes,
capturing all their followers and the plunderers.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
he encamped at Ādūn Luò.
Because his adopted son Nièlǐsī rebelled with his younger brothers,
he was shot and killed with a "ghost arrow".
The other six thousand members of his faction
were sentenced according to the severity of their crimes.
Thirty-odd captives taken by Yújué
were also allowed to atone for their crimes
and released back to their own tribes.
Arriving west of Shílǐng,
an imperial edict ordered the collection of weapons abandoned by the returning army due to lack of provisions,
and summoned the northern armies to verify and return them.
Because Yílírjǐn Nièlǐgǔn sided with his younger brothers in rebellion,
the Emperor could not bear to execute him publicly,
and ordered him to throw himself off a cliff to his death.
In the eighth month, autumn, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
he visited Lóngméi Gōng.
Twenty-nine members of the rebel faction were dismembered by carts.
Their wives and daughters were bestowed upon meritorious generals and officers.
The plundered treasures and livestock were returned to their owners;
for those whose original possessions were lost,
he ordered their families to compensate.
Those who could not compensate
were given their former subordinates.
On the *rénxū* day of the ninth month,
the Emperor departed from Xīlóu.
In the tenth month, winter, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
he was stationed at Chìyá.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Huíhú of Hézhōu came to pay tribute.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Dílǐgǔ of the Yǐshì Fǔ and Tèlǐ of the Mígǔlí tribe were executed for their involvement in the rebellion.
An imperial edict commanded the ministers to resolve outstanding lawsuits,
with Hán Zhīgǔ recording the proceedings
and Zhīlǐgū in charge of apprehending fugitives.
In the eleventh month,
sacrifices were offered at Mùyè Shān.
Returning to Zhāowū Shān,
he inspected local customs,
met with elders,
discussed court policies,
and established auspicious and inauspicious rituals.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
a burnt offering was made at Liánhuā Luò.
In the eighth year, spring, on the *jiǎchén* day of the first month,
Hélǔ was appointed Yílírjǐn of the Diélà Department,
and Hūliè was appointed Tìyǐn.
Télímǐn of the Yúgǔlǐ tribe captured and presented the rebel leaders Bùhú, Yǎlǐzhī, and seventeen others.
The Emperor personally interrogated them.
Their confessions implicated many members of the imperial clan and those who were coerced,
so only the chief culprit Bùhú was flogged to death,
the rest were all pardoned and released.
Huàgē, the son of Yúyuè Shuàilǎn, had repeatedly harbored treacherous plots.
The Emperor always treated him with leniency,
but he repeatedly showed no repentance.
The Emperor summoned elders and ministers to confirm his crimes,
and executed him and his sons,
distributing their wealth to the guards.
Over three hundred rebels interrogated by the authorities
had their cases completed.
The Emperor, considering human life to be of utmost importance,
and that death is irreversible,
granted them a feast for one day,
allowing them to engage in their preferred activities,
according to their lifelong tastes.
As the wine flowed,
some sang, some danced, some played target practice, or wrestled,
each indulging their desires to the fullest.
The next day,
they were sentenced according to the severity of their crimes.
The chief culprit Lágé,
and then Diélàgē,
were still treated by the Emperor as his younger brothers;
he could not bear to put them to death,
so he flogged and released them.
As Yīndǐshí and Ānduān were inherently weak,
and were used by Lágé,
their crimes were all pardoned.
However, Xièlǐ, the son of the former Yúyuè Hèdǐlǐ, and Xiálà, Lágé's wife, had genuinely participated in the rebellion,
so an order was given to hang them both.
Nièlǐ, Yīndǐshí's wife, was coerced,
and Zhānmùgū, Ānduān's wife, had once offered loyal advice,
so both were spared.
Then he said to his attendants:
"Though my younger brothers are clever and shrewd,
they harbor treachery and are deeply evil.
They often boast of their extraordinary wisdom,
but are cruelly ruthless;
gullies can be filled, but their greed is insatiable.
When seeking others' faults,
even a small and pardonable one
is considered as heavy as Mount Tài;
when they themselves commit injustice,
even if it's a great evil,
they consider it lighter than a swan's feather.
They consort with petty individuals,
consult women in their plots,
and collude in evil,
thereby endangering the imperial destiny.
Even if they wish not to fail,
how can they succeed?
Yúlúdúgū, the wife of the Northern Prime Minister Shílǔ, was a close relative to the state.
One day she betrayed me
and followed the rebels.
She died of illness before she could be brought to justice.
This was a punishment from Heaven.
Xièlǐ, since childhood, always ate and slept with me.
The affection and favor shown to him surpassed all other relatives,
yet he and his father turned their backs on great kindness and followed the unrighteous.
How can this be forgiven!"
In the seventh month, autumn, on the *bǐngshēn* day, the first day of the month,
the authorities presented the crimes of over three hundred tribal leaders and their co-conspirators in the rebellion,
and they were all executed in the marketplace.
The Emperor sighed, saying:
"To put people to death,
how could this be my desire?
If they had merely wronged me personally,
I could still have pardoned them.
But these people acted wantonly and without principle,
harming loyal and good people,
inflicting suffering on the populace,
and plundering property.
Previously, the common people had tens of thousands of horses,
but now they all walk.
This has never happened since the founding of the state.
It is truly out of necessity that I execute them."
In the tenth month, winter, on the *jiǎzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the Kāihuáng Diàn was built on the foundation of the Míngwáng Lóu.
In the ninth year, spring, in the first month,
the Wūgǔ tribe rebelled
and was suppressed.
In the sixth month, summer,
Qí Xíngběn, a military officer from Yōuzhōu, led his clan and three thousand men and women from his subordinates to surrender.
An imperial edict appointed him Jiǎnxiào Shàngshū, Zuǒ Púyè,
granted him the name Wūyù,
and provided him with provisions.
After several days, he departed,
and Zhōu Déwēi, the governor of Yōuzhōu, accepted him.
When an imperial edict sought his return,
Déwēi's reply was disrespectful,
so a southern campaign was deliberated.
In the tenth month, winter, on the *wùshēn* day,
fishing was conducted at Yālù Jiāng.
Xīnluó sent envoys to offer local products as tribute.
Gāolí sent envoys to present precious swords.
Qián Liú, King of Wúyuè, sent Téng Yànxiū to offer tribute.
That year,
the divine number of Jūnjī Tàiyī was seen several times,
and an imperial edict ordered its image to be depicted.
In the first year of Shéncè, spring, on the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the second month,
the Emperor was in Lónghuà Zhōu.
Yēlǜ Hélǔ, Yílírjǐn of the Diéliè Department, and other officials
led all civil and military officers to request the Emperor to accept a venerable title.
After three petitions, he consented.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
ministers and various vassal states built an altar east of the prefecture.
The Emperor was given the venerable title "Dàshèng Dàmíng Tiānhuáng Dì",
and the Empress was given the title "Yìngtiān Dàmíng Dì Huánghòu".
A general amnesty was declared, and the era name was changed to Shéncè.
Initially,
when digging the ground for the altar,
a golden bell was found,
so the place was named Jīnlíng Gāng.
The forest beside the altar was called Cèsheng Lín.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the third month,
Yílírjǐn Hélǔ of the Diéliè Department was appointed Ālúduǒlǐ Yúyuè.
All officials were promoted in rank, and rewards were distributed with differences.
A three-day feast was granted.
His son Bèi was established as the Crown Prince.
In the fourth month, summer, on the *yǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
Lú Guóyòng, Jìn's Jìedùshǐ of Yōuzhōu, surrendered
and was appointed Liúhòu of the Yōuzhōu army and cavalry.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Liáng sent Láng Gōngyuǎn to congratulate.
On the *gēngyín* day of the sixth month,
Qián Liú, King of Wúyuè, sent Téng Yànxiū to offer tribute.
In the autumn, the seventh month, *rénshēn* day,
he personally led a campaign against the various tribes of the Tūjué, Tǔhún, Dǎngxiàng, Xiǎofān, and Shātuó,
and pacified them all.
He captured their chieftains and 15,600 households,
and over 900,000 items of armor, weapons, utensils, and clothing,
while the amount of treasures, camels, horses, cattle, and sheep was beyond calculation.
In the eighth month,
he captured Shuòzhōu,
and seized the Jìedùshǐ Lǐ Sìběn.
He erected a stone inscription south of Qīngzhǒng to record his achievements.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the first day *guǐwèi*,
he pressed on eastward, capitalizing on his victories.
In the eleventh month,
he attacked the five prefectures of Yù, Xīn, Wǔ, Guī, and Rú,
beheading over 14,700 enemy troops.
From Dàiběi to Héqū, crossing the Yīnshān mountains,
he acquired all of that territory.
Consequently, he changed Wǔzhōu to Guīhuàzhōu,
and Guīzhōu to Kèhánzhōu.
He established the Southwest Pacification Commission (*Xīnánmiàn Zhāotǎosī*),
selecting those with merit to lead it.
During the siege of Yùzhōu,
the enemy watchtower spontaneously collapsed for no reason.
The entire army raised a great roar and pressed the attack,
breaking the city in less than an hour.
At that time, envoys from both Liáng and Wúyuè were present.
An edict ordered them to be led around the city walls to observe the victory.
Consequently, the envoy Ténɡ Yànxiū was bestowed the name Qiúlǚ.
In the twelfth month,
he received the eight garrisons north of the mountains.
In the second year, spring, the second month,
Lú Wénjìn, a deputy general of Jìn's Xīnzhōu, killed the Jìedùshǐ Lǐ Cúnjǔ and came to surrender.
He advanced and attacked that city.
The Magistrate Ān Jīnquán fled,
and Liú Yīn, Wénjìn’s divisional general, was appointed Magistrate.
In the third month, *xīnhài* day,
he attacked Yōuzhōu.
The Jìedùshǐ Zhōu Déwēi used the armies of the five prefectures, Yōu, Bīng, Zhèn, Dìng, and Wèi, to resist west of Jūyōng Guān,
engaging in battle east of Xīnzhōu.
He utterly defeated them,
beheading over 30,000 enemy troops,
and killing Wǔbā, the son of Lǐ Sì'ēn.
He appointed Āgǔzhī, the Empress’s younger brother, as Commander (*Tǒngjūn*),
and Shílǔ as Vanguard,
advancing east out of the pass to raid Yān and Zhào.
They encountered no enemy and returned.
*Jǐwèi* day,
Yúgǔlǐ rebelled.
He ordered Shìlǔ to lead troops to suppress him.
In the summer, the fourth month, *rénwǔ* day,
he besieged Yōuzhōu,
but did not conquer it.
The sixth month, *yǐsì* day,
looking towards the city, a vapor appeared like smoke or fire.
The Emperor said:
“It is not yet time to attack.”
Due to the extreme heat and prolonged flooding rain,
the army was ordered to return.
Hélǔ and Lú Guóyòng were left behind to maintain the guard.
Làgě and his son Sàibǎolǐ rebelled and fled into Yōuzhōu.
In the autumn, the eighth month,
Lǐ Cúnxù sent Lǐ Sìyuán and others to relieve Yōuzhōu.
Hélǔ and his colleagues, due to their small troop numbers, returned.
In the third year, spring, the first month, *bǐngshēn* day,
he appointed his younger brother Ānduān as Grand Palace Tìyǐn,
ordering him to attack Yúnzhōu and the various tribes in the southwest.
In the second month,
the state of Dádàn came to offer a tribute.
*Guǐhài* day,
the Imperial Capital was fortified.
Kāng Mòjì, the Minister of Rites (*Lǐbù Shàngshū*), was made the Commissioner for Rammed Earth Construction (*Bǎnbìng Shǐ*).
Liáng sent an envoy to offer tribute.
Jìn, Wúyuè, Bóhǎi, Gāolì, Huíhú, Zǔbǔ, Dǎngxiàng, and the prefectures of Yōu, Zhèn, Dìng, Wèi, and Lù, each sent envoys to pay tribute.
In the summer, the fourth month, *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor’s younger brother Diéliègē plotted rebellion.
The matter was discovered.
Knowing he was guilty and deserved execution,
he prepared his own burial pit beforehand.
However, all the imperial relatives requested his pardon.
The Emperor had always disliked Nièlǐgǔn, the wife of his younger brother Yíndǐshí.
He then said:
“If Nièlǐgǔn can die in his stead,
then the request will be granted.”
Nièlǐgǔn hanged herself in the pit.
Also, the female slave Gǔ and the rebel Hélǔzhī were buried alive in it.
Diéliègē was then pardoned.
The fifth month, *yǐhài* day,
an edict ordered the construction of a Kǒngzǐ temple, Buddhist monasteries, and Daoist temples.
In the autumn, the seventh month, *yǐyǒu* day,
the Yúyuè Hélǔ passed away.
The Emperor was deeply distressed for a long time,
suspending court for three days,
and bestowed exceptional posthumous honors and gifts.
In the winter, the twelfth month, on the first day *gēngzǐ*,
he proceeded to the former city of Liáoyáng.
*Xīnchǒu* day,
Xiāo Dílǔ, the Chancellor of the Northern Administration (*Běifǔ Zǎixiàng*), passed away.
*Wùwǔ* day,
Wūlǐzhěn, the younger brother of the Yúyuè Hélǔ, was made the Yílíjǐn of the Diéliè Tribe,
and Xiāo Āgǔzhī was made Chancellor of the Northern Administration.
*Jiǎzǐ* day,
the Imperial Grandson Wēiyù was born.
Basic Annals 2: Tàizǔ (Part 2)
In the fourth year, spring, the first month, *bǐngshēn* day,
he shot a tiger at Dōngshān.
The second month, *bǐngyín* day,
the former city of Liáoyáng was renovated.
It was settled with Hàn people and Bóhǎi households.
It was renamed Dōngpíng Jùn,
and a Commissioner of Defense (*Fángyù Shǐ*) was appointed there.
In the summer, the fifth month, *gēngchén* day,
he arrived back from Dōngpíng Jùn.
In the autumn, the eighth month, *dīngyǒu* day,
he paid respects at the Kǒngzǐ temple,
ordering the Empress and the Crown Prince to separately pay respects at the monasteries and temples.
In the ninth month,
he campaigned against the Wūgǔ Tribe.
He heard en route that the Empress Dowager was unwell,
and galloped six hundred *lǐ* in one day to return,
attending to the Empress Dowager.
When her illness abated,
he returned to the army.
In the winter, the tenth month, *bǐngwǔ* day,
he arrived at the Wūgǔ Tribe.
There was a great snowstorm,
and the troops were unable to advance.
The Emperor prayed to Heaven,
and shortly thereafter the weather cleared.
He ordered the Crown Prince to lead the vanguard army to attack.
They defeated them,
capturing 14,200 captives (mouths),
and over 200,000 cattle, horses, chariots, tents, and miscellaneous articles.
From then on, the entire tribe came to submit.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, *yǐchǒu* day,
the Khitan Large Script (*Qìdān Dàzì*) was first created.
In the summer, the fifth month, *bǐngyín* day,
the King of Wúyuè again sent Ténɡ Yànxiū to present rhinoceros horns and coral as tribute.
He was granted an official title and dispatched back.
*Gēngchén* day,
a dragon was seen on the water south of Zhuāilá Shān.
The Emperor shot and captured it,
storing its bones in the Inner Treasury.
In the intercalary sixth month, *dīngmǎo* day,
he appointed his younger brother Sū as Tìyǐn,
and Kāng Mòjì as Yílíbì.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the first day *jǐwèi*,
the various tribes of the Dǎngxiàng rebelled.
*Xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor personally led the campaign.
The ninth month, on the first day *jǐchǒu*,
Liáng sent Láng Gōngyuǎn to offer tribute.
*Rényín* day,
the Large Script was completed.
An edict ordered its promulgation.
The Crown Prince led Wūlǐzhěn, the Yílíjǐn of the Diélá Tribe, and others, to raid the territories of Yúnnèi and Tiāndé.
In the winter, the tenth month, *xīnwèi* day,
they attacked Tiāndé.
*Guǐyǒu* day,
the Jìedùshǐ Sòng Yáo surrendered.
He was bestowed with a bow and arrows, saddled horses, banners, and drums.
His army was renamed Yìngtiān.
*Jiǎxū* day,
the army returned.
Sòng Yáo rebelled again.
*Bǐngzǐ* day,
his city was captured,
Sòng Yáo was seized,
his family members were captured,
and his populace was resettled south of Yīnshān.
The twelfth month, *jǐwèi* day,
the army returned.
In the sixth year, spring, the first month, *bǐngwǔ* day,
he appointed his younger brother Sū as Chancellor of the Southern Administration (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*),
and Diélǐ as Tìyǐn.
The position of Chancellor of the Southern Administration,
since the time his younger brothers instigated rebellion,
many esteemed families in the administration had suffered disaster,
thus the post had been vacant for a long time.
Chúdé Bù Xiádélǐ and Zhǐlǐgǔ had temporarily held the position.
Officials in the administration repeatedly requested that a member of the imperial clan be selected for the post,
but the Emperor believed that the old system should not be lightly changed.
As the requests did not cease,
he informed the Imperial Ancestral Temple before granting the appointment.
The practice of a member of the imperial clan serving as Chancellor of the Southern Administration began at this time.
In the summer, the fifth month, on the first day *bǐngxū*,
an edict codified the laws
and standardized official ranks.
*Bǐngshēn* day,
an edict ordered the portraits of upright officials from previous eras to be painted to serve as an "Illustration of Soliciting Advice" (*Zhāojiàn Tú*),
and commanded senior officials to inquire about the benefits and disadvantages affecting the populace during the first month of each season.
The sixth month, on the first day *yǐmǎo*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the first day *guǐchǒu*,
Wáng Yù, the Commissioner of Defense (*Fángyù Shǐ*) of Jìn’s Xīnzhōu, defected, bringing his mountain-north troops and horses.
*Bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor led the main army into Jūyōng Guān.
On the Guǐmǎo day of the 11th month,
they captured Gǔběikǒu.
On the Dīngwèi day,
forces were divided to seize more than ten cities, including Tán, Shùn, Ānyuǎn, Sānhé, Liángxiāng, Wàngdū, Lù, Mǎnchéng, and Suìchéng,
and their inhabitants were captured and resettled in the interior lands.
On the Guǐchǒu day of the 12th month,
Wáng Yù led his multitude to pay court.
The Emperor called Yù his son,
and rewarded him very generously,
but resettled his followers south of the Huángshuǐ River.
On the Gēngshēn day,
the Crown Prince led Wáng Yù to seize territory in Dìngzhōu,
and Kāng Mòjì attacked Chánglú.
Wáng Dū, the adopted son of Wáng Chǔzhí, the Táng Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) of the Yìwǔ Army, imprisoned his father
and declared himself acting military governor (Liúhòu).
On the Guǐhài day,
Zhuōzhōu was besieged.
A white rabbit was seen climbing the rampart,
and on that very day, they broke the outer wall.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
Prefect Lǐ Sìbì surrendered the city.
On the Yǐhài day,
Cúnxù arrived at Dìngzhōu,
and Wáng Dū welcomed him, paying respects before his horse.
Cúnxù led his troops toward Wàngdū,
where he encountered Tǔnnèi of our army leading 5,000 cavalry.
They surrounded him,
and Cúnxù fought fiercely several times,
but could not break out.
Lǐ Sìzhāo led 300 cavalry to the rescue;
our army retreated slightly,
and Cúnxù was then able to escape.
A major battle followed,
but our army was unsuccessful
and withdrew.
Cúnxù arrived at Yōuzhōu
and sent 200 cavalry to pursue our army.
Our army counterattacked
and captured them all.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
they returned and stopped at Tánzhōu.
People from Yōu came to attack,
but they were routed,
and their deputy general was captured.
An edict commanded the relocation of the people of Tán and Shùn to Dōngpíng and Shěnzhōu.
In the spring of the 2nd month, Gēngshēn day, of the 1st year of Tiānzàn,
they again campaigned in the lands of Yōu and Jì.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
an edict announced the change of era name
and pardoned those sentenced to the extreme penalty or lesser punishments among the troops.
In the summer, on the Jiǎyín day of the 4th month,
they attacked Jìzhōu.
On the Wùwǔ day,
they captured it,
seizing Prefect Hú Qióng,
and placing Lú Guóyòng and Nièlǔgǔ in charge of military and civil affairs.
On the Rénxū day,
a great feast was held for the soldiers.
On the Guǐhài day,
Lǐ Cúnxù besieged Zhènzhōu.
Zhāng Wénlǐ requested aid,
and orders were given to Prince Diéliè and General Kāng Mòdá to go and strike them.
They defeated them
and killed their general Lǐ Sìzhāo.
On the Xīnwèi day,
they attacked Shíchéng County
and captured it.
On the Dīngwèi day of the 5th month,
Zhāng Wénlǐ died,
and his son Chǔjǐn sent an envoy bearing a memorial to express thanks.
In the 6th month,
the Eagle Army was sent to attack the various southwestern tribes,
and the captured goods were bestowed upon the poor people.
In the winter, on the Jiǎzǐ day of the 10th month,
Xiāo Xiádì was appointed Chancellor (Zǎixiāng) of the Northern Administration (Běifǔ).
The Diélà tribe was divided into two administrations: Xié Nièchì was made Yílíjǐn of the Northern Administration,
and Wǎnsī was made Yílíjǐn of the Southern Administration.
An edict also divided the Běidà Nóngwù into two divisions,
and two Military Governors were established to command them.
On the Rén yín day of the 11th month,
Imperial Prince Yáogǔ was appointed Grand Marshal (Dà Yuánshuài) of All Forces,
to seize territory north of Jì.
On the Bǐngshēn day of the 1st month of spring in the 2nd year,
Grand Marshal Yáogǔ conquered Píngzhōu,
capturing Prefect Zhào Sīwēn and Deputy General Zhāng Chóng.
In the 2nd month,
he went to Píngzhōu.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
Píngzhōu was designated the Lúlóng Army,
and a Military Governor was installed.
On the Wùyín day of the 3rd month,
they encamped at Mount Jiàngǎn,
to suppress the rebellious Xī, Húsǔn.
He was captured
and shot with a ghost arrow.
Three hundred of his followers were executed
and drowned in the Gǒuhé River.
The Xī Duòguī division was established,
and Bólǔ'ēn was appointed to provisionally take charge of its affairs.
In the summer, on the Jǐyǒu day of the 4th month,
Liáng sent an envoy to make a formal visit,
and the King of Wúyuè sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
Yáogǔ was ordered to attack Yōuzhōu,
and Díliè, the Yílíjǐn of the Diélà tribe, campaigned in the Shānxī region.
On the Gēngshēn day,
Yáogǔ’s army was stationed east of Yōuzhōu.
Military Governor Fú Cúnshěn sent men out to battle;
they were defeated,
and their general Péi Xìn and his son were captured.
In the intercalary month, on the Gēngchén day,
Yáogǔ reached Zhènzhōu.
On the Rénwǔ day,
he captured Qǔyáng.
On the Bǐngxū day,
he took Běipíng.
In this month,
Lǐ Cúnxù, the Prince of Jìn, ascended the imperial throne,
and named his state Táng.
On the Wùwǔ day of the 5th month,
Yáogǔ’s army returned.
On the Guǐhài day,
a grand feast was held for the soldiers,
and rewards were bestowed according to merit.
On the Xīnchǒu day of the 6th month,
the state of Persia came to offer tribute.
In the 7th month of autumn,
former Chancellor of the Northern Administration Xiāo Āgǔzhī and Wáng Yù campaigned in the territories of Yān and Zhào.
In the winter, on the Xīnwèi day (the first day) of the 10th month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
the Táng armies destroyed Liáng.
In the 1st month of spring in the 3rd year,
troops were sent to seize territory south of Yān.
In the summer, on the Bǐngwǔ day of the 5th month,
Diélǐ, the Tìyǐn, was appointed Yílíjǐn of the Southern Administration.
In this month,
the inhabitants of Jìzhōu were relocated to populate the lands of Liáozhōu.
Bóhǎi killed their Prefect Zhāng Xiùshí and plundered the inhabitants.
On the Yǐyǒu day of the 6th month,
the Empress, the Crown Prince, the Grand Marshal, the two Chancellors, and the leaders of the various tribes were summoned, and an edict was issued, stating:
“The Heavens have descended to oversee us,
and benefit extends to the common people.
A wise ruler and enlightened king
is met but once in ten thousand years.
Since I have received the Mandate of Heaven above
and rule the multitude below,
every time there is a campaign,
it is in accordance with the will of Heaven.
Therefore, my strategies are my own,
my decisions are divine,
and now that the national order is established,
the hearts of the people are fully attached.
Error and divergence return to correctness,
and there is no fault near or far.
It can be said that [my domain] vastly encompasses the sea
and safely shelters Mount Tài!
My state, in its management,
acts as the parent to all regions.
The fundamental laws are established;
why worry about the heirs?
The time for rising and falling is set,
and going and coming rest with Me.
The excellence of these plans and the sagely assembly
are already in harmony with Heaven and man.
How can the kings of the various states
change their ordinary nature?
Three years from now,
in the year Bǐngxū,
at the time of early autumn,
I will certainly have a place of return.
However, two tasks have not yet been completed;
how could I fail those sincerely close to me?
The time is not distant;
prepare quickly for war.”
All who heard the edict were alarmed and afraid,
and none understood its meaning.
On that day,
a major expedition was launched against the Tǔhún, Dǎngxiàng, Zǔbǔ, and other tribes.
An edict commanded the Crown Prince to supervise the state,
and Grand Marshal Yáogǔ accompanied the Emperor.
In the autumn, on the Xīnhài day of the 7th month,
Hélà and others attacked the tribes east of Mount Sùkūnnuó
and defeated them.
On the Yǐyǒu day of the 8th month,
they reached Mount Wūgū
and offered geese as a sacrifice to Heaven.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
they stopped at the Former Chányú State,
ascended Mount Ālǐdiǎn Yādésī,
and offered tufted deer as a sacrifice.
occurred. We encamped at the former Huíhú
city and erected a stone stele to commemorate the achievements.
On *gēngzǐ* day,
we performed the sun worship ritual at Dàilín.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
cavalry was dispatched to attack the Zǔbǔ.
Sū, the Chancellor of the Southern Administration, and Diélǐ, the *Yílíjǐn* of the Southern Chancellery, campaigned in the southwest.
On *yǐmǎo* day,
Sū and the others presented the captives.
On *dīngsì* day,
the waters of the Jīnhé River were channeled,
and stones were taken from Wūshān
and transported by cart to Huánghé and Mùyèshān,
to demonstrate the meaning of mountains and rivers paying homage to the sea and revering the high peaks.
On *guǐhài* day,
the state of Dàshí came to present tribute.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial decree ordered the engraving of the late stele of Pì'è Kèhán,
using Khitan, Turkic, and Han characters to record his achievements.
In this month,
the various vassal tribes of Húmǔsīshān were defeated,
and the army encamped at Yèdésīshān.
Red oxen and dark horses were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
The Huíhú Bālǐ sent an envoy to present tribute.
In winter, the tenth month, *bǐngyín* day, the new moon
occurred. We hunted at Yùlèshān,
capturing thousands of wild beasts
to supply the military rations.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
the army was stationed at Bàlísīshān.
Troops were dispatched to cross the quicksands (*Liúshā*),
capturing Fútúchéng,
and taking all the tribes along the western frontier.
In the eleventh month, *yǐwèi* day, the new moon
occurred. Bìlí'è, the Military Governor (*Dūdū*) of Gānzhōu Huíhú, was captured.
Thereupon, an envoy was sent to admonish his ruler, Wūmǔzhǔ Kèhán.
We hunted tigers at Wūlàxiélǐshān,
reaching Bāshìshān.
For over six hundred *lǐ*, we traveled and hunted simultaneously.
There was fresh food daily,
which supplied all the soldiers.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month, *rén'yín* day,
the victory report was sent to the Empress and the Crown Prince.
In the second month, *bǐngyín* day,
Yáogǔ, the Grand Marshal, raided the Dǎngxiàng.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
the Empress dispatched Kāngmòdá to inquire about the Emperor's daily life,
and presented imperial robes, wine, and meals.
On *yǐhài* day,
Xiāo Āgǔzhǐ returned from raiding Yān and Zhào,
and presented the general's standard (*yáqí*) and military weapons.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
Yáogǔ presented the Dǎngxiàng captives.
In the third month, *bǐngshēn* day,
a feast was held for the army at Shuǐjīngshān.
In summer, the fourth month, *jiǎzǐ* day,
we attacked the lesser vassals to the south
and subjugated them.
The Empress and the Crown Prince came to Zhálǐhé to greet the Emperor.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
Wūmǔzhǔ Kèhán of Huíhú sent an envoy to present tribute and express gratitude.
In the fifth month, *jiǎyín* day,
we spent the summer at the northern passes (*Běixíng*) of the Shìwěi territory.
In autumn, the ninth month, *guǐsì* day,
we arrived back from the Western Campaign.
In winter, the tenth month, *dīngmǎo* day,
Táng reported the destruction of Liáng.
An envoy was immediately sent to respond to the notification.
On *gēngchén* day,
the state of Rìběn came to present tribute.
On *xīnsì* day,
the state of Gāolì came to present tribute.
In the eleventh month, *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Ānguósì,
provided food for the monks,
pardoned prisoners in the capital,
and released the falcons and hawks of the Five Offices (*Wǔfāng*).
On *jǐyǒu* day,
the state of Xīnluó came to present tribute.
In the twelfth month, *yǐhài* day,
an imperial decree stated:
"Of the two goals we set,
one has been completed.
However, the long-standing enmity with Bóhǎi has not yet been avenged.
How can we rest in peace?"
Thereupon, troops were raised for a personal campaign against Dà Yīnxuǎn of Bóhǎi.
The Empress, the Crown Prince, and Yáogǔ, the Grand Marshal, all followed.
In the intercalary month, *rénchén* day,
sacrifices were offered at Mùyèshān.
On *rén'yín* day,
a dark ox and a white horse were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at Wūshān.
On *jǐyǒu* day,
we encamped at Sāgěshān,
and shot the 'Demon Arrow' (*guǐjiàn*).
On *dīngsì* day,
we encamped at Shānglǐng,
and besieged Fúyúfǔ by night.
Tiānxiǎn (1) year, spring, the first month, *jǐwèi* day,
a white vapor pierced the sun.
On *gēngshēn* day,
Fúyúchéng was captured,
and its defending general was executed.
On *bǐngyín* day,
Tìyǐn Ānduān and Xiāo Āgǔzhǐ, the former Chancellor of the Northern Administration, were ordered to lead ten thousand cavalry as the vanguard.
They encountered Dà Yīnxuǎn's veteran troops
and defeated them.
The Crown Prince, Grand Marshal Yáogǔ, Sū, the Chancellor of the Southern Administration, Xié Nièchì, the *Yílíjǐn* of the Northern Chancellery,
and Diélǐ, the *Yílíjǐn* of the Southern Chancellery, besieged Hūhànchéng that night.
On *jǐsì* day,
Dà Yīnxuǎn requested surrender.
On *gēngwǔ* day,
the army was stationed south of Hūhànchéng.
On *xīnwèi* day,
Dà Yīnxuǎn wore plain clothes,
bound himself with a rope and led a sheep,
and led over three hundred of his subordinates out to surrender.
The Emperor treated him with great courtesy and released him.
On *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the commanderies and counties of Bóhǎi.
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
thirteen people, including the attendant Kāngmòdá, were dispatched to enter the city to search for weapons,
but they were killed by the patrol soldiers.
On *dīngchǒu* day,
Dà Yīnxuǎn rebelled again.
The city was attacked
and broken.
The Emperor personally entered the city.
Dà Yīnxuǎn begged for punishment before the Emperor's horse.
An imperial decree ordered soldiers to escort Dà Yīnxuǎn and his clan out.
Sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
The Emperor then returned to the main camp.
In the second month, *gēngyín* day,
the prefectures of Ānbiān, Màojié, Nánhǎi, Dìnglǐ, and the Military Commissioners (*Jiédù*) and Prefects (*Cìshǐ*) from various circuits came to the court.
They were comforted, rewarded, and sent away.
The captured articles, silks, and other goods were bestowed upon the generals and soldiers.
On *rénchén* day,
a dark ox and a white horse were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
A general amnesty was granted,
and the reign title was changed to Tiānxiǎn.
An envoy was sent to Táng to report the subjugation of Bóhǎi.
On *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor again visited Hūhànchéng,
reviewed the contents of the official treasuries,
and granted gifts to the attending officials based on rank.
Bólǔ'ēn, chief of the Xī, and Wáng Yù were granted exceptional rewards
for their meritorious service during the campaign, accompanying forces from Huíhú, Xīnluó, Tǔfān, Dǎngxiàng, Shìwěi, Shātuó, and Wūgǔ.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
the state of Bóhǎi was renamed Dōngdān,
and Hūhànchéng was renamed Tiānfú.
The Crown Prince Bèi was invested as the Human Sovereign King (*Rén Huángwáng*) to rule over it.
The Emperor's younger brother Diélà was appointed Chief Chancellor of the Left (*Zuǒ Dàxiàng*);
the elder chancellor of Bóhǎi was appointed Chief Chancellor of the Right (*Yòu Dàxiàng*);
Dà Sùxián, the Minister of Education (*Sītú*) of Bóhǎi, was appointed Secondary Chancellor of the Left (*Zuǒ Cìxiàng*);
and Yēlǜ Yǔzhī was appointed Secondary Chancellor of the Right (*Yòu Cìxiàng*).
All sentences below death within the territory were pardoned.
On *dīngwèi* day,
Gāolì, Huìmò, Tiělí, and Mòhé came to present tribute.
In the third month, *wùwǔ* day,
Kāng Mòjì, the *Yílíbì*, and Hán Yánluǐ, the Left Minister (*Zuǒ Púshè*), were dispatched to attack Chánglǐngfǔ.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
sacrifice was offered to Heaven.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the palace of the Human Sovereign King.
On *jǐsì* day,
the three prefectures of Ānbiān, Màojié, and Dìnglǐ rebelled.
Ānduān was dispatched to suppress them.
On *dīngchǒu* day,
the three prefectures were pacified.
On *rénwǔ* day,
Ānduān presented the captives,
and two rebel leaders from Ānbiānfǔ were executed.
On *guǐwèi* day,
a banquet was held for the officials of the Dōngdān State,
and gifts were distributed according to rank.
On *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor visited Tiānfúchéng.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
the army returned,
taking Dà Yīnxuǎn and his entire clan with them.
In summer, the fourth month, *dīnghài* day, the new moon
occurred. We encamped at Sǎnziǐshān.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
the Human Sovereign King, leading the officials of the Dōngdān State, bade farewell.
In this month,
Lǐ Sìyuán, the adopted son of Táng, rebelled.
Guō Cūnqiān assassinated his master Cūnxù,
and Sìyuán consequently ascended the throne.
In the fifth month, *xīnyǒu* day,
the two prefectures of Nánhǎi and Dìnglǐ rebelled again.
Yáogǔ, the Grand Marshal, was dispatched to suppress them.
In the sixth month, *dīngyǒu* day,
the two prefectures were pacified.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
we encamped at Shènzhōu.
Táng sent Yáo Kūn to report the national mourning.
In the autumn, seventh month, day Bǐngchén,
Wèi Jūn (Governor of Tiězhōu) rebelled.
Day Yǐchǒu,
Yáogǔ attacked and captured Tiězhōu.
Day Gēngwǔ,
Diélà, the Chief Minister (Zuǒ Dàxiàng) of the Dōngdān State, died.
Day Xīnwèi,
they escorted the Great Yīn Zàn to the west of the Imperial Capital (Huángdū),
and built a city for him to reside in.
Yīn Zàn was granted the name Wūlǔgǔ,
and his wife was named Ālǐzhī.
Zhāng Chóng, the Campaign Administrator (Xíngjūn Sīmǎ) of Lúlóng, rebelled
and fled to Táng.
Day Jiǎxū,
the ruler reached Fúyú Prefecture,
and became unwell.
That night,
a large star fell in front of the tent.
At dawn on day Xīnsì,
a yellow dragon, winding and circling, was seen above the inner city wall (Zǐchéng).
It was about one *lǐ* long,
its brilliance dazzling to the eyes,
and it entered the traveling palace (Xínggōng).
A purple-black vapor obscured the sky,
and only dispersed after a full day.
On this day,
the ruler died,
aged fifty-five.
What the ruler had said in Tiānzàn 3rd year—
"In the early autumn of Bǐngxū,
there must be a resting place (Guīchù)"—
was now confirmed.
Day Rénwǔ,
the Empress assumed regency (Chēngzhì),
provisionally deciding military and state affairs.
Eighth month, day Xīnmǎo,
Kāng Mòjì and others attacked and captured Chánglǐng Prefecture.
Day Jiǎwǔ,
the Empress escorted the imperial coffin (Zǐgōng) back westward.
Day Rén Yín,
Yáogǔ pacified the various prefectures
and hurried to the temporary imperial residence (Xíngzài).
Day Yǐsì,
Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi arrived later.
Ninth month, day Rénxū,
Sū Hōng, the Chancellor (Zǎixiàng) of the Southern Division, died.
Day Dīngmǎo,
the imperial coffin arrived at the Imperial Capital (Huángdū),
and was provisionally interred northwest of the inner city wall (Zǐchéng).
Day Jǐsì,
the ruler was posthumously titled Shēngtiān Huángdì,
with the temple name Tàizǔ.
Winter, tenth month,
Lú Guóyòng, the Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) of Lúlóng Army, rebelled
and fled to Táng.
Eleventh month, day Bǐngyín,
Yēlǜ Diélǐ, the Yílíjǐn of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn), and Yēlǜ Pǐlǔ, the Langjun (gentleman), were killed.
Second year, eighth month, day Dīngyǒu,
Emperor Tàizǔ was buried at Zǔlíng,
and the Military Governor of Zǔzhōu Tiānchéng Army (Zǔzhōu Tiānchéng Jūn Jiédùshǐ) was established to guard the imperial tomb.
Tǒnghé 26th year, seventh month,
his posthumous title was advanced to Dàshèng Dàmíng Tiānhuángdì.
Chóngxī 21st year, ninth month,
the additional posthumous title Dàshèng Dàmíng Shénliè Tiānhuángdì was granted.
The traveling palace where Tàizǔ died was located southwest of Fúyú City, between two rivers.
Later, the Shēngtiān Hall was built there,
and Fúyú was renamed Huánglóng Prefecture.
Eulogy: The ancestors of Liáo
originated from Yándì,
and for generations were the state of Shěnjí.
Their history, insofar as it is known, begins with Qíshǒu.
Qíshǒu was born on Dū'ān Mountain
and moved to the banks of the Huánghé (Yellow River).
The lineage reached Yǎlǐ,
who first established systems and regulations,
appointed officials,
cut wood into tallies (for contracts),
and dug holes in the ground for prisons (láo).
He offered the throne to Zǔwǔ but Zǔwǔ refused to establish himself.
Yǎlǐ begot Pídié.
Pídié begot Kēyǐng.
Kēyǐng begot Nòulǐsī.
He was magnanimous and had few desires;
his orders were not strict, yet the people were transformed.
He is known as Sùzǔ.
Sùzǔ begot Sàlàdé,
who once challenged the Huángshìwéi,
his arrows penetrating several layers of armor (zhá).
He is known as Yìzǔ.
Yìzǔ begot Yúndéshí,
who first taught the people farming and reaping,
and was skilled in animal husbandry.
The state thus became prosperous and wealthy.
He is known as Xuánzǔ.
Xuánzǔ begot Sālāde,
who loved the people and cherished all creatures,
and first established iron smelting,
teaching the people forging and casting.
He is known as Dézǔ,
who was the father of Tàizǔ.
For generations they served as the Yílíjǐn of the Qìdān Yáoniǎn clan,
controlling the reins of government.
Dézǔ's younger brother, Shùlán,
campaigned north against Yújué and Shìwéi,
and raided south against Yì, Dìng, Xī, and Xí.
He first encouraged plank construction (Bǎnzhú),
established cities and towns,
taught the people to plant mulberry and hemp,
and practiced weaving.
He already possessed the ambition of ruling over vast territory and numerous people.
Then Tàizǔ received the abdication of the Khagan (Kèhán)
and consequently founded the state.
Campaigning in the east and attacking in the west,
he was like snapping dry wood or pulling out rotten timber.
From the sea in the east,
west to the Liúshā (Moving Sands),
and north across the Great Desert,
his authority was trusted across ten thousand *lǐ*.
To endure for two hundred years—
how could this be the achievement of a single day?
When Zhōugōng executed Guǎn and Cài,
no one was able to criticize him.
During the rebellions of Làgě and Ānduān,
Tàizǔ spared their lives and employed them again.
Was this not the forbearance of a ruler?
The incident (Biàn) at Fúyú mentioned in the Old History
is also strange indeed!
Basic Annals 3: Tàizōng I
Emperor Xiàowǔ Huìwén Tàizōng,
personal name Déguāng,
courtesy name Dějǐn,
informal name Yáogǔ.
He was the second son of Tàizǔ,
his mother being Empress Chúnqīn, of the Xiāo clan.
Born in the 2nd year of Tiānfù of Táng,
his divine aura was extraordinary.
Hunters captured a white deer and a white eagle,
which people regarded as auspicious omens (Ruì).
When he grew up,
his appearance was imposing and his nature was broad and benevolent.
Many military and state affairs were decided by him.
In Tiānzàn 1st year,
he was appointed Generalissimo of All Armies (Tiānxià Bīngmǎ Dàyuánshuài).
Soon after, he was ordered to command the Six Armies and raid the southern territories.
The following year,
Píngzhōu was captured,
and Zhào Sīwēn and Zhāng Chóng were taken prisoner.
Returning, he defeated the Hú Xùnxī at Jiàngē Mountain,
and all their tribes surrendered.
He subsequently led troops to raid Zhèn and Dìng.
Wherever he went, they fortified their walls and dared not fight.
When the army reached Yōuzhōu,
Fú Cúnshěn resisted them south of the prefecture.
(Yáogǔ) deployed troops to intercept and attack,
greatly defeating them,
and capturing dozens of subordinate generals, including Péi Xìn.
He followed Tàizǔ to defeat the various tribes of Yújuélǐ,
pacified the Dǎngxiàng along the river bend (Héruǎn),
captured the various garrisons west of the mountains (Shānxī),
took the Chányú City of the Huíhú (Uighurs),
pacified Bóhǎi in the east,
and defeated the Dálúgǔ tribe.
Across ten thousand *lǐ* east and west,
he achieved merit in every direction he campaigned.
Tiānxiǎn 1st year, seventh month,
Tàizǔ died,
and the Empress administered military and state affairs.
In the autumn of the following year,
the construction/repair of the Ancestral Mausoleum was completed.
In the winter, on the *rénxū* day of the eleventh month,
Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi led his officials to petition the Hòu, saying:
"The merit and prestige of the Imperial Son, the Grand Marshal,
are recognized by all within and without (the court),
and he ought to succeed to the great lineage."
The Hòu agreed to this.
On that day, he ascended the imperial throne.
On the *guǐhài* day,
he paid respects at the temple of Tàizǔ.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
he performed the *cháicè* rite.
On the *wùchén* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *rénshēn* day,
he held court at the Xuānzhèng Diàn;
the assembled officials offered the honorific title Sìshèng Huángdì.
A general amnesty was granted.
The relevant authorities requested a change of reign title,
but it was not permitted.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
the Huáng Tàihòu was honored as the Tàihuáng Tàihòu;
the Huánghòu was honored as Yìngtiān Huáng Tàihòu;
Consort Xiāo Shì was established as the new Huánghòu.
After the rites were complete,
he reviewed the registers of the palace attendants.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the generals and commanders from the various circuits took leave to return to their garrisons.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the *gēngyín* day,
envoys were dispatched to inform the various kingdoms.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
he reviewed the various herds in the near suburbs.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Nǚzhí dispatched envoys to present tribute.
On the *rényín* day,
he paid respects at the temple of Tàizǔ.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
he reviewed the officials of the various Bureaus of the Banner Drum and the Reception Office.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an imperial edict commanded the selection of eligible youths from the Nine Tents of the Yáoliǎn Shì clan for official posts.
In the spring of the third year, the first month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
he reviewed the military registers of the Northern Division.
On the *gēngxū* day,
he reviewed the military registers of the Southern Division.
On the *dīngsì* day,
he reviewed the three armies: Píshì, Zhuāilà, and Mòlí.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Nǚzhí of Luóniè Hé in Huánglóng Fǔ and the Dá Lúgǔ came to present tribute.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Wáng Yù was appointed as the Xīngguó Jūn Jiédù Shǐ,
acting Zhōngshū Lìng.
The second month,
hunting at Xīnchángluò.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Tìyǐn Nièlǐgǔn presented a white wolf.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Dá Lúgǔ came to present tribute.
The third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Eastern Hunt was performed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
he hunted at Gǔ [unclear character] Shān.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
he hunted at Sōng Shān.
Wáng Dū, the Táng Jiédù Shǐ of the Yìwǔ Army, sent a person to submit with Dìngzhōu.
The Táng ruler mobilized troops to attack him.
[Wáng Dū] sent an envoy to ask for aid,
so [the Emperor] commanded Xī Tūlǐ Tiělà to go and rescue him.
The fourth month, on the *wùyín* day,
he conducted an eastern tour.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
sacrifices were offered to the God of the Roe Deer.
On the *dīnghài* day,
at the hunting ground, he permitted both public and private parties to gather materials such as feathers, fur/leather, and wood.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
arrow materials were gathered at Chì Shān.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
he hunted at Sān Shān.
Tiělà defeated the Táng General Wáng Yànqiú at Dìngzhōu.
The Táng forces gathered in large numbers,
and Tiělà requested reinforcements.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
[the Emperor] commanded the Tìyǐn Nièlǐgǔn and the Dūtǒng Chálà to proceed there.
The fifth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Tiānshàn Táng was established.
He hunted at Suǒlà Shān.
On the *wùshēn* day,
he arrived back from the hunt.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
he commanded the Línyá Tūlǜbù to suppress the Wūgǔ Tribe.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
The sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the *sèsè* rite was performed.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Tūlǜbù presented a victory report on the suppression of the Wūgǔ.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wáng Dū reported that the Táng forces had captured Dìngzhōu,
that Tiělà had died there,
and that Nièlǐgǔn, Chálà, and several dozen others had been captured.
The Emperor regretted deeply
having mobilized the troops at an inappropriate time,
and heavily rewarded the families of the officers and soldiers who died in battle.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
rites were performed at the temple of Tàizǔ.
The eighth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Tūjué came to present tribute.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict commanded the erection of the Monument Commemorating the Birth of the Yìngtiān Huáng Tàihòu at Yíkūn Zhōu.
The ninth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Tūlǜbù sent men to present captives taken from the suppression of the Wūgǔ.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict commanded their distribution among the officials.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
[the Emperor] visited the residence of Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi.
On the *gēngyín* day,
men were sent as envoys to Táng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
[the Emperor] visited the residence of the Rén Huáng Wáng again.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the relevant authorities requested that the Emperor's birthday be designated Tiānshòu Jié,
and the Huáng Tàihòu's birthday be designated Yǒngníng Jié.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐmǎo* new moon,
to celebrate Yǒngníng Jié,
the Emperor led the officials in offering longevity wishes at Yánhé Gōng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
he paid respects at the temple of Tàizǔ.
Táng dispatched an envoy to present a jade flute.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Tiānshòu Jié,
the Emperor presided at Wǔluán Diàn to receive congratulations from the assembled officials and envoys from various nations.
The eleventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Bí Gǔdé came to present tribute.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
[the Emperor] personally led an army to attack Táng.
The twelfth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the *gēngxū* day,
[the Emperor] heard that the Táng ruler had again sent envoys to seek peace.
The Emperor consulted his attendants,
who all said:
"Táng has repeatedly sent envoys,
which is truly out of fear of your majesty's power.
We should not make a rash move yet;
observing the situation and acting when opportunity arises is advisable."
The Emperor agreed with them.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he reached Xìng Guō.
The Táng envoy arrived,
and consequently, the army was ordered to return.
At that time, Rén Huáng Wáng was in the Huáng Dū (Imperial Capital).
An edict commanded Yēlǜ Yǔzhī to relocate the Dōngdān people to populate Dōngpíng.
Some of these people fled into Xīnluó or Nǚzhí territory.
Therefore, an edict stipulated that those who were too poor or weak to relocate
were permitted to be provided for and managed by wealthy commoners of the superior kingdom.
Dōngpíng Jùn was elevated to Nánjīng (Southern Capital).
In the spring of the fourth year, the first month, on the *rénshēn* new moon,
a banquet was held for the assembled officials and envoys from various nations,
and they watched performers and wrestling.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
he went to Guā Guō.
The second month, on the *gēngxū* day,
he reviewed the household registers of the Yáoliǎn Shì clan.
The third month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
sacrifices were offered to the various spirits from afar.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
he arrived back from Guā Guō.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
he paid respects at the temple of Tàizǔ.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
he paid respects at the temporary palace of Tàizǔ.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he visited Tiānchéng Jūn,
and paid respects at the Zǔ Líng (Ancestral Mausoleum).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi came to pay court.
On the *guǐhài* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
The fifth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
he visited the Èryí Diàn,
and hosted a banquet for the assembled officials.
The Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the willow-shooting ceremony was performed at the temporary palace of Tàizǔ.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the *sèsè* rite was performed.
The sixth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Tūlǜbù presented captives from the Wūgǔ.
On the *wùshēn* day,
they were distributed among the generals and soldiers.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
he conducted a western tour.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
several thousand light cavalry were selected to hunt in the nearby mountains.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the imperial procession halted at Liángxíng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngchén* day,
the marketplace was observed,
and a partial amnesty was granted to the prisoners.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
sacrifices were offered to Tàizǔ, and the Emperor proceeded east.
The eighth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor arrived from Liángxíng,
and paid respects at the Tàizǔ Temple.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Rén Huáng Wáng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
paid respects at the Tàizǔ Temple.
The ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
proceeded to Nánjīng.
On the *wùyín* day,
sacrificed at Mùyè Shān.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Rebirth Ritual was performed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
arrived at Nánjīng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *rén yín* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Rén Huáng Wáng,
and hosted a feast for the officials.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor visited the various encampments,
and reviewed the military registers.
On the *gēngxū* day,
as the commanderies and counties of Yúnzhōng had not yet submitted,
a grand review of the Six Armies was held.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict was issued commanding the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú to lead the army quickly toward Yúnzhōng to suppress the commanderies and counties that had not yet submitted.
The eleventh month, the first day (*shuò*) was *bǐngyín*,
the launching of the army was announced to Heaven and Earth.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
a farewell banquet was held for the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú in the western suburbs.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Dà Nèi Tì Yǐn was ordered to announce the launching of the army at Tàizǔ’s Traveling Palace.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
fishing was observed at Sānchā Kǒu.
The twelfth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
arrived from Nánjīng.
Fifth year, spring, the first month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
news of victory arrived regarding the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú having captured Huánzhōu.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
The second month, on the *jǐhài* day,
an edict was issued to repair Nánjīng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Hú returned from Yúnzhōng,
and paid respects at the traveling palace.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Bóhǎi households previously captured were bestowed upon Lǐ Hú.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor, along with the Rén Huáng Wáng, paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
The Empress Dowager, noting that both were skilled in calligraphy,
ordered them to write before her so she might observe it.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
officials were summoned to discuss military and state affairs.
The third month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú requested amnesty for the Imperial Clan member Shèlì Lángjūn, who was imprisoned for a crime,
and an edict was issued granting the request.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Imperial Uncle Ānduān.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Rén Huáng Wáng presented white ramie cloth.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú was formally invested as Shòuchāng Huáng Tàidì,
also holding the title of Grand Marshal of All Military Forces.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Liú Jūyán, the Military Governor (*jiédùshǐ*) of Lónghuà Zhōu, was appointed Executive of the Affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a feast was held for the officials subordinate to the Rén Huáng Wáng in the private hall.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Imperial carriage departed Nánjīng.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict commanded the Rén Huáng Wáng to proceed first to the Ancestral Mausoleum to pay respects at the Tàizǔ Temple.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
a meeting took place at the Ancestral Mausoleum.
The Rén Huáng Wáng returned to his domain.
The fifth month, on the *wùchén* day,
an edict was issued to repair the Niǎotán Traveling Palace.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
paid respects at the Tàizǔ Temple.
The sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the Willow Shooting ceremony was held at the traveling palace.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
proceeded to Yánliǔ Hú.
On the *dīngsì* day,
worshipped the Imperial Portrait of Tàizǔ in the Bright Hall.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Díliè Dé came to offer tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the Wūgǔ came to offer tribute.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
seasonal fruits were offered at the Tàizǔ Temple.
The eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the private chambers of the Dàshèng Huángdì and the Empress were designated the Rìyuè Gōng (Sun-Moon Palace),
and consequently, the Rìyuè Stele was erected.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
proceeded to Jiǔcéng Tái.
The ninth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict commanded Shèlì Pǔníng to go and comfort the Rén Huáng Wáng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict commanded the establishment of the ceremonial guards for the Rén Huáng Wáng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
returned from Jiǔcéng Tái,
and paid respects at the Tàizǔ Temple.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *wùxū* day,
an envoy was dispatched to bestow sacrificial meat upon the Rén Huáng Wáng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Stele of Tàizǔ’s Sacred Accomplishments was erected at Rú Yū Zhèng Jíhuì Guō.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Rén Huáng Wáng presented a jade flute.
The eleventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
Dōngdān reported that the Rén Huáng Wáng had sailed across the sea to Táng.
Sixth year, spring, the first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the generals on the southwestern frontier reported that people from the Xiágā Sī state, desiring assimilation, had arrived.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Díliè Dé came to offer tribute.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
proceeded to Nánjīng.
The third month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
ministers were summoned to discuss military and state affairs.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Bèi Fēi Xiāo Shì, the Consort of the Rén Huáng Wáng, led officials subordinate to her domain to seek an audience.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Táng dispatched an envoy to present greetings.
In this month, the Central Platform Department was established in Nánjīng.
The fifth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
sacrificed at Mùyè Shān.
On the *yǐhài* day,
returned from Nánjīng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
paid respects at the Tàizǔ Mausoleum.
The intercalary month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the Willow Shooting ceremony was held in the nearby suburbs.
The sixth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
proceeded to Liángxíng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Wūgǔ came to offer tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
generals and officers were ordered to lead troops to make a brief foray to the south.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
seasonal fruits were offered at the Tàizǔ Temple.
The Emperor traveled east.
The eighth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Imperial Prince Shùlǜ was born,
and the event was reported at the Tàizǔ Temple.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Bígǔ Dé came to offer tribute.
The ninth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to repair the Capital City.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Tiělí came to offer tribute.
The eleventh month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Táng dispatched an envoy to present greetings.
The twelfth month, the first day (*shuò*) was *jiǎyín*,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàizǔ Temple.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
a messenger was sent carrying an edict to Zhào Déjūn, the Military Governor (*jiédùshǐ*) of the Lúlóng Army of Táng.
Seventh year, spring, the first month, on the *rénchén* day,
the General Who Conquers the West, Kèlǐ, sent Zhuàilā Duókuò to report on military affairs.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Táng dispatched an envoy to present greetings.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
a messenger was dispatched as an envoy to Táng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
sacrificed at Mùyè Shān.
The second month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Zhuàilā Dídé returned from his mission to Wúyuè,
the King of Wúyuè dispatched an envoy to accompany him,
who presented precious vessels.
Another envoy was subsequently dispatched carrying silks to return the courtesy.
The third month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Línyá Dílíbì insulted the Emperor’s person,
and was imprisoned.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
envoys were dispatched to various states.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor led the officials to pay respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Táng dispatched an envoy to present greetings,
and delivered a letter from the Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
The fifth month, the first day (*shuò*) was *rénwǔ*,
the Emperor visited Zǔ Zhōu,
and paid respects at the Tàizǔ Mausoleum.
Sixth month, day Wùchén,
the Monument for Tàizǔ Founding the Nation (Tàizǔ Jiànguó Bēi) was imperially composed.
Day Wùyín,
the Wūgǔ and Dílièdé came to present tribute.
Day Gēngchén,
watched wrestling matches.
Autumn, seventh month, day Xīnsì (new moon),
bestowed gifts upon officials both inside and outside the court, according to rank.
Day Guǐwèi,
granted cloth and silk to the elderly.
Day Bǐngxū,
summoned the assembled ministers and elders to deliberate on governance.
Day Rénchén,
Táng sent an envoy to present a reed pipe instrument with red ivory fittings (hóngyáshēng).
Day Guǐsì,
the envoy returned again,
fearing the report regarding the campaign at Dìngzhōu.
Day Rényín,
Zhào Déjūn, Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of the Táng Lúlóng Army, sent a person to present seasonal fruits.
Day Dīngwèi,
offered new sacrifices at the Tàizǔ Temple.
Eighth month, day Rénxū,
while catching geese at Lake Yánliǔ (Yánliǔ Hú),
a violent storm suddenly arrived.
The boats capsized,
and over sixty people drowned.
It was ordered that their families be provided for and consoled,
and the event was recorded as a warning.
Day Wùchén,
Dílíbì, the Minister (Línyá), escaped from prison.
He was recaptured and interrogated,
and it was learned that the case was originally a false accusation.
He was released.
Ninth month, day Gēngzǐ,
the Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
Winter, tenth month, day Yǐmǎo,
Táng sent an envoy to pay a formal visit.
Day Jǐsì,
sent an envoy to Yúnzhōng.
Eleventh month, day Dīnghài,
sent an envoy to convey greetings to the Huòlǐ State (Huòlǐ Guó).
Day Dīngwèi,
the Zǔbǔ presented thirty pairs of Hǎidōngqīng falcons as tribute.
Twelfth month, day Xīnhài,
the family members of the rebel Nílígǔn were divided and granted to the assembled ministers.
Day Dīngsì,
hunted toward the west,
stopping temporarily at Píngdì Sōnglín (Pine Forest of the Flat Land).
Eighth year, Spring, first month, day Wùzǐ,
the Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
Day Gēngzǐ,
ordered Lǐ Hú, the Imperial Younger Brother (Huáng Tàidì), and Sāgē, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard of Awe (Zuǒ Wēiwèi Shàng Jiāngjūn), to lead troops to attack the Dǎngxiàng.
Day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor personally saw them off.
Second month, day Xīnhài,
the Tǔyùhún and Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
Day Yǐmǎo,
Kèshílǔ returned from his mission to Táng,
and the accompanying tributary items were divided and granted to the assembled ministers.
Third month, day Xīnmǎo,
the Imperial Younger Brother returned victorious from punishing the Dǎngxiàng,
and was banqueted in reward for his efforts.
Day Bǐngshēn,
Táng sent an envoy to request the cessation of troops campaigning against the Dǎngxiàng.
