The Emperor replied that the battle had already been won and that the Dǎngxiàng had submitted to his command.
Summer, fourth month, day Wùwǔ,
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
Fifth month, day Jǐchǒu,
hunted at Mount Dúniú.
The reddish-brown imperial horse ridden by the Tìyǐn Díliǎn died.
Therefore, the mountain was granted the name Mount Liú.
Day Wùxū,
went to Lake Yánliǔ.
Sixth month, day Jiǎyín,
the Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
Day Jiǎzǐ,
Āsàlán of the Huíhú came to present tribute.
Autumn, seventh month, day Wùyín,
performed the ceremony for accepting the Empress.
Day Guǐwèi,
Imperial Prince Tílígǔ was born.
Day Dīnghài,
the Tiělí, Nǚzhí, and Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
Winter, tenth month, day Yǐsì,
the Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
Day Bǐngwǔ,
returned from Lake Yánliǔ.
Day Xīnhài,
Táng sent an envoy to pay a formal visit.
Day Jǐwèi,
sent Bálà as envoy to Táng.
Day Xīnwèi,
the Wūgǔ Tǔlǔmò came to present tribute.
Eleventh month, day Xīnchǒu,
the Grand Empress Dowager died.
Envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning period to Táng and to Imperial King Rén Bèi.
In this month,
Lǐ Sìyuán, the Lord of Táng, died.
His son Cónghòu was enthroned.
Twelfth month, day Dīngmǎo,
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
Ninth year, Spring, first month, day Guǐyǒu,
fished at the Tǔ River (Tǔ Hé).
Day Bǐngshēn,
the Dǎngxiàng presented camels and deer as tribute.
Day Jǐhài,
the Southern Capital (Nánjīng) presented a white roebuck.
Intercalary month, day Wùwǔ,
Táng sent an envoy to announce the death.
On the same day, an envoy was dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices.
Day Rénxū,
traveled east.
The Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
Second month, day Rénshēn,
performed sacrifices at Mount Mùyè.
Day Wùyín,
the Grand Empress Dowager was buried at Dè Mausoleum (Délíng).
Two days prior,
the funeral ceremony was held at Zōutú Palace (Zōutú Diàn),
and the Emperor wore complete mourning attire to see her off.
She was later granted the posthumous title Empress Xuānjiǎn (Xuānjiǎn Huánghòu),
and an imperial edict ordered a monument built at the mausoleum.
Third month, day Guǐmǎo,
the Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
Summer, fourth month,
Lǐ Cóngkē of Táng murdered his lord and enthroned himself.
Imperial King Rén Bèi submitted a memorial from Táng requesting an attack (on the new ruler).
Fifth month, day Jiǎchén,
went to Lake Yánliǔ.
Day Guǐchǒu,
the Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
A great star fell during the daytime.
Sixth month, day Jǐsì (new moon),
the Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
Day Xīnwèi,
the envoy sent by Lǐ Cónghòu of Táng to express gratitude for the condolences and sacrifices first arrived at the imperial palace.
Autumn, eighth month, day Rénwǔ,
personally led the troops on a southern campaign.
Day Yǐyǒu,
Xièlǐ, the Zhuáilá, caught a flying wild goose by hand.
The Emperor considered this unusual,
and consequently used it to make sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
Ninth month, day Gēngzǐ,
stars fell like rain in the southwest.
Day Yǐmǎo,
reached Yúnzhōu.
Day Dīngsì,
captured Héyīn.
Winter, tenth month, day Dīnghài,
swept through Língqiū.
The elders presented cattle and wine to reward the army.
Eleventh month, day Xīnchǒu,
besieged Yángchéng in Wǔzhōu.
Day Rényín,
Yángchéng surrendered.
Day Guǐmǎo,
Wāzhī City surrendered.
The captured able-bodied men were registered for military service.
Twelfth month, day Rénchén,
Imperial Prince Āpō Sàgēlǐ was born.
The Empress was unwell.
In this month, the imperial encampment was located southwest of Bǎihú (Hundred Lakes).
Tenth year, Spring, first month, day Wùshēn,
the Empress died at the temporary imperial residence.
Second month, day Wùyín,
all officials requested adding a further posthumous title,
but it was not permitted.
Day Xīnsì,
the Chancellor Nièlǐgǔn plotted to flee south.
The plot was discovered,
and he was seized.
Third month, day Wùwǔ,
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
Summer, fourth month,
Tuìyùdé, chieftain of the Tǔyùhún, led his followers to submit to the court.
Day Bǐngxū,
the clan of the Empress Dowager’s father and the clan of the mother’s former husband—these two groups—were both appointed as Imperial Maternal Uncles (Guójiù).
Xiāo Miǎnsī was made Grand Mentor (Shàngfǔ) to lead them.
Day Jǐchǒu,
reviewed the prisoners.
Fifth month, day Jiǎwǔ (new moon),
began wearing mourning clothes and observed the Empress’s funeral rites.
Day Bǐngwǔ,
she was buried at Fèng Mausoleum.
The Emperor personally composed the inscription,
and she was granted the posthumous title Empress Zhāngdé.
Day Guǐchǒu,
Wáng Tíngè, the Shèlì, was appointed Military Commissioner of Lónghuà Prefecture.
Sixth month, day Yǐchǒu,
the Tǔhún came to present tribute.
Day Xīnwèi,
traveled to Pǐnbulǐ Lake.
Autumn, seventh month, day Yǐmǎo,
hunted at Mount Nánchì.
In the winter, the eleventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor journeyed to Hóngfú Sì (Hóngfú Temple) to offer food to monks on behalf of the Empress.
He saw a painting of Guānyīn,
which had been donated by Dàshèng Huángdì, Yìngtiān Huánghòu, and Rén Huáng Wáng.
He looked around and said:
“Formerly, I gathered here with my parents and brothers to view this.
Only a short time has passed,
and now I come alone!”
He sighed continuously in sorrow.
He then personally composed a text and inscribed it on the wall,
to fully express his nostalgic feelings.
Readers were saddened by it.
The twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
he went to Jīnpíng Luò.
He dispatched Yèlà Huàgē, Kūlǔlǐ, Ālǔ Sàogū, and others to capture inhabitants in enemy territory.
The eleventh year, spring, the first month,
he fished in the Tǔ Hé (River).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
he went to the Huáng Hé (River).
The third month, on the *gēngyín* day (the first day of the month),
the Nǚzhí came to pay tribute.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
he visited the Ancestral Mausoleum (*Zǔ Líng*).
On the *wùchén* day,
he returned to the Capital,
and visited the Tàizǔ Miào (Temple of Tàizǔ).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Yān commoners who had recovered their professions presented matters concerning Biànzhōu.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
various Nǚzhí tribes came to pay tribute.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
clothing was bestowed upon the Huíhú (Uygur) envoys, with distinctions made.
The fifth month, on the *wùxū* day,
he sought relief from the summer heat along Liǔ Hú (Willow Lake).
The sixth month, on the *wùwǔ* day (the first day of the month),
Bígǔdé came to pay tribute.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Tǔyùhún came to pay tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Wūgǔ came to pay tribute.
On the *rénchén* day,
Princess Púgē led the Sānhé Wūgǔ to court.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Shí Jìngtáng, the Military Governor (*Jiédùshǐ*) of Hédōng under Táng, was attacked by his lord.
He dispatched Zhào Yíng, via the Pacification Commissioner (*Zhāotǎo*) of the Southwest Route, Lú Bùgū, to request aid.
The Emperor reported to the Empress Dowager and said:
“Lǐ Cóngkē murdered his sovereign and established himself;
Gods and men are equally enraged.
It is proper to carry out a Heavenly Punitive Expedition.”
At that time, Zhào Déjūn also sent an envoy,
and Hédōng further dispatched Sāng Wéihàn to report the urgent situation.
Thus, permission was granted to raise the army.
The eighth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Xiāo Xiálǐ was dispatched to inform Hédōng of the date for mobilization.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Tǔyùhún came to pay tribute.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor personally led the troops to assist Jìngtáng.
The ninth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
there was a flying pheasant that fell and died.
Hélǔ'ēn, the Yílíjǐn of the Southern Prefecture, obtained it and presented it.
Divination was performed,
and it was auspicious.
The Emperor said:
“This is an omen that Cóngkē will destroy himself!”
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
they entered Yànmén.
On the *wùxū* day,
they halted at Xīnzhōu,
and sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
On the *jǐhài* day,
they halted at Tàiyuán.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an envoy was sent to inform Jìngtáng, saying:
“We raised an army and came a great distance.
We shall immediately destroy the rebels with you.”
Meanwhile, the Táng generals Gāo Xíngzhōu and Fú Yànqīng came with troops to resist.
Thereupon, the Emperor marshaled his troops and deployed them at Tàiyuán.
When the battle began,
they pretended to retreat.
The Táng generals Zhāng Jìngdá and Yáng Guāngyuǎn formed a line to the west.
Before they could complete their formation,
troops were sent to attack them immediately.
Xíngzhōu and Yànqīng were cut off by the ambush troops,
so the vanguard and rear guard could not assist each other.
Jìngdá and Guāngyuǎn suffered a great defeat,
abandoning their weapons like mountains,
and several tens of thousands of heads were taken.
Jìngdá fled and took refuge in Jìn'ān Zhài (Jìn'ān Stockade).
Dílǔ, the Yílíjǐn, fought him,
and died.
Jìngtáng led his officials and subordinates to meet the Emperor,
who held his hand and comforted him.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Jìn'ān was besieged.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Dílǔ's son, Túlígǔ, was ordered to succeed as Yílíjǐn,
and his father's name was used as his given name,
to commend his loyalty.
Nán Zǎixiàng (Southern Chancellor) Húlǐdǐ, Xī Jiānjūn (Xī Army Supervisor) Yínnǐyǐ, and General Péi'ā retreated fearfully during the battle.
The Emperor summoned them and severely reprimanded them.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Jìngtáng was enfeoffed as the Prince of Jìn (Jìn Wáng).
The Emperor journeyed to his residence.
Jìngtáng and his wife Lǐ led their relatives in presenting cups of wine to wish the Emperor longevity.
When Jìn'ān was first besieged,
crack troops were dispatched to guard crucial points,
to cut off the path of relief forces.
Lǐ Cóngkē sent Zhào Yánshòu with twenty thousand troops to garrison Tuánbǎi Gǔ (Tuánbǎi Valley).
Fàn Yánguǎng garrisoned Liáozhōu with twenty thousand troops.
Zhào Déjūn of Yōuzhōu led more than ten thousand of his troops from Shàngdǎng toward Yánshòu’s army,
intending to combine forces and advance to attack.
Knowing that defenses were prepared,
they all lingered and did not advance.
Cóngkē then led thirty thousand elite cavalry out and halted at Héyáng,
personally supervising the various armies.
However, knowing that they would not provide relief,
he only indulged in drinking heavily and singing sorrowfully every day.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Jìngtáng was summoned to the Emperor's temporary residence (*Xíngzài Suǒ*),
and was granted a seat.
The Emperor spoke to him gently, saying:
“We raised an army and came three thousand *lǐ*;
we won in a single battle.
This is surely the will of Heaven.
Seeing your impressive and magnificent nature,
it is proper that you receive this southern land,
and forever be Our vassal state.”
Thereupon, he commanded the relevant authorities to erect an altar at Jìnyáng,
and perform the full rites of investiture.
The eleventh month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Jìngtáng was formally invested as the Emperor of Great Jìn (Dà Jìn Huángdì).
From the *wùxū* day to the *wùshēn* day,
scouts reported twice that troops were arriving from the south,
and again reported that troops were arriving from the west.
He ordered Tìyǐn Díliǎnwā to resist them.
Táng General Zhāng Jìngdá had been under siege for more than eighty days.
Internal and external communication was cut off,
and military provisions were nearly exhausted.
They reached the point of washing horse dung and grinding wood to feed the horses.
The horses were so starved that they ate each other’s manes and tails,
and when they died, they were eaten.
Guāngyuǎn and others urged Jìngdá to surrender.
Jìngdá said:
“I have only death.
If you wish to surrender,
you had better cut off my head and surrender.”
The intercalary month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yáng Guāngyuǎn and Ān Shěnqí killed Jìngdá and surrendered.
When the Emperor heard that Jìngdá had remained resolute until death,
he said to his attendants:
“Anyone who serves as a minister
should be like this!”
He ordered him to be buried with proper rites.
The surrendered soldiers and five thousand horses were bestowed upon the Jìn Emperor.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth to announce the success.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Púshè Xiāo Kùgǔzhī reported that Zhào Déjūn and the other relief forces were about to flee.
An edict commanded troops to be dispatched at night to pursue and attack.
Déjūn's army and the others all threw down their spears and abandoned their armor,
trampling one another.
Those pushed into the valleys and streams were countless.
The Crown Prince (*Huáng Tàizǐ*) was further ordered to lead light cavalry to occupy strategic points.
They caught up with more than ten thousand infantry,
and all of them surrendered.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the army crossed Tuánbǎi Gǔ (Tuánbǎi Valley).
Wine and dishes were offered in sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
Shortly after, Déjūn and his son were overtaken,
and they led their followers in surrender.
Halted at Lùzhōu,
the Emperor summoned the various generals for consultation.
All requested the troops return to the capital,
and the request was granted.
Nán Zǎixiàng Xiè Líng and Húlǐdǐ, Xī Jiānjūn Yínnǐyǐ, and General Péi'ā were ordered to return first.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Tìyǐn Wā and Línyá Dílíbì came to present captives.
The Jìn Emperor requested permission to return home.
The Emperor held a feast and drank with him.
When the wine flowed freely,
they held hands and pledged to be father and son.
He was gifted one white sable fur coat, twenty horses, and one thousand two hundred warhorses as farewell gifts.
Dílíbì was ordered to lead five thousand cavalry to escort him into Luò.
Upon parting,
the Emperor said to him:
“We shall remain here,
and return only after the disturbances have been settled.”
On the *xīnsì* day,
when the Jìn Emperor reached Héyáng,
Lǐ Cóngkē was destitute and desperate.
He summoned Rén Huáng Wáng Bèi to die with him,
but Bèi refused.
Cóngkē sent someone to kill him,
and then committed self-immolation with his entire family.
An edict commanded that the soldiers who died in battle be collected and buried beside the Fén Shuǐ (River),
and a monument of skulls (*Jīngguān*) be established.
Jìn commanded Sāng Wéihàn to compose a text,
recording the Emperor's achievements and virtues.
Twelfth month, *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) first day of the lunar month.
Sent the close attendant Tǎlǔ (撻魯) to inquire after the state of the Jìn (晉) Emperor.
*Bǐngxū* (丙戌).
Distributed the spoils captured at Jìn'ān (晉安) to the generals and officers.
*Wùzǐ* (戊子).
Sent envoys urgently to report to the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu),
and announced the return of the armies from various circuits.
*Gēngyín* (庚寅).
Departed Tàiyuán (太原).
*Xīnmǎo* (辛卯).
Hearing that the Jìn Emperor had entered Luò (洛),
sent the noble youth (Lángjūn) Xièlǐdé (解里德) to comfort and inquire after him.
*Rénchén* (壬辰).
Reached Xìhé (細河).
Reviewed the troops and horses of the surrendered general Zhào Déjūn (趙德鈞) and his son.
*Wùxū* (戊戌).
Reached Yànmén (雁門).
Divided the troops belonging to Shā Tàibǎo (沙太保) and attached them to various generals.
*Gēngxū* (庚戌).
Went to Yìngzhōu (應州).
*Guǐchǒu* (癸丑).
The three regional military commissioners (*jiédùshǐ*) of Táng (唐) — Dàtóng (大同), Zhāngguó (彰國), and Zhènwǔ (振武) — came to greet and meet [him].
Detained them and did not send them back.
Twelfth year, Spring, first month, *bǐngchén* (丙辰).
Reached Duīzǐkǒu (堆子口).
Wú Luán (吳巒), the supervisor (*pànguān*) of the Táng Dàtóng (大同) Military Commission, closed the city and resisted the command.
Sent Cuī Tíngxūn (崔廷勳) to besiege his city.
*Gēngshēn* (庚申).
The Emperor personally led the campaign,
arrived below the city walls and issued a proclamation to him.
Luán (巒) surrendered.
*Xīnyǒu* (辛酉).
Shot the "Ghost Arrow" (*guǐjiàn*) north of Yúnzhōu (雲州).
*Rénxū* (壬戌).
Sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
*Guǐhài* (癸亥).
Sent the Emperor’s maternal uncle (Guójìu) Ānduān (安端) to dispatch the people of the Western Xī (奚) tribe, so that each might return to their homeland.
*Bǐngyín* (丙寅).
The Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) sent the imperial guard Shílǔ (實魯) to urge the journey forward.
That evening,
[the Emperor] led the light cavalry and advanced first.
*Dīngchǒu* (丁丑).
The Imperial Son Shùlǜ (述律) greeted and paid respects at the Luánhé (灤河).
Announced the completion of the achievement at Tàizǔ’s (太祖) temporary palace (*xínggōng*).
*Wùyín* (戊寅).
Held an audience with the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
Presented precious treasures and curios as a longevity offering.
Second month, *dīnghài* (丁亥).
All captives captured before the army who had defected and entered Yōuzhōu (幽州) were executed.
*Rényín* (壬寅).
Issued an edict to all tribes to rest and recuperate the soldiers.
*Guǐmǎo* (癸卯).
Jìn (晉) sent back the noble youth (Lángjūn) Làgē (剌哥) and the court official Xiāo Shòulǐ (蕭[⿰木受]里), who had been previously seized by Táng (唐), to return to court.
Third month, *gēngshēn* (庚申).
Jìn (晉) sent envoys to come and pay tribute.
*Dīngmǎo* (丁卯).
Fàn Yán'guǎng (范延廣), the regional military commissioner of Tiānxióng (天雄) Army of Jìn (晉), secretly sent people to request allegiance and inclusion.
This was not accepted.
*Jǐsì* (己巳).
Sent the noble youths Dìliègǔ (的烈古) and Méilǐdiéliè (梅里迭烈) as envoys to Jìn (晉).
*Rénwǔ* (壬午).
Envoys from Jìn (晉) and envoys from various states came for an audience.
Summer, fourth month, *jiǎshēn* (甲申).
Earthquake.
Went to the level ground pine forest (Píngdì Sōnglín).
Observed the source of the Huángshǔi River (潢水).
Fifth month, *jiǎyín* (甲寅).
Went to Pínbìdiàn (頻蹕淀).
*Rénshēn* (壬申).
Thunder split the Imperial Hall (Huángdiàn).
Sixth month, *jiǎshēn* (甲申).
Jìn (晉) sent Niè Yánzuò (聶延祚), Minister of Revenue (*hùbù shàngshū*), and others to request [the Emperor] ascend the honorable title (*zūn hào*),
and offered to return the land north of Yànmén (雁門) along with Yōu (幽) and Jì (薊) prefectures,
and further proposed an annual tribute of three hundred thousand bolts of silk.
An imperial edict refused this.
*Gēngxū* (庚戌).
Lièshuài (列率), the Grand Counselor (*shìzhōng*), reported that
Fàn Yán'guǎng (范延廣) had rebelled against Jìn (晉)
and led his troops southward.
Autumn, seventh month, *xīnhài* (辛亥) first day of the lunar month.
Issued an edict instructing all tribes to prepare weapons and armor.
*Guǐchǒu* (癸丑).
Went to Huáizhōu (懷州).
Paid respects at Fènglíng (奉陵) Mausoleum.
*Jiǎzǐ* (甲子).
Jìn (晉) sent an envoy to announce the rebellion of Fàn Yán'guǎng (范延廣).
*Gēngwǔ* (庚午).
Sent Yēlǜ Niǎogǔlǐ (耶律褭古里) as envoy to Jìn (晉) to discuss military affairs.
Eighth month, *guǐwèi* (癸未).
Jìn (晉) sent an envoy again to request [the Emperor] ascend the honorable title.
It was not permitted.
*Gēngyín* (庚寅).
Jìn (晉), Liú Zhīyuǎn (劉知遠) of Tàiyuán (太原), and Lǐ Yuán (李●) of Southern Táng (Nán Táng) each sent envoys to come and pay tribute.
*Gēngzǐ* (庚子).
Jìn (晉) sent an envoy to announce that Dū Biàn (都汴) and Fàn Yán'guǎng (范延廣) had surrendered.
Ninth month, *rénzǐ* (壬子).
Bígǔdé (鼻骨德) came to pay tribute.
*Gēngshēn* (庚申).
Sent Zhílǐgǔ (直里古) as envoy to Jìn (晉) and Southern Táng (Nán Táng).
*Guǐhài* (癸亥).
Zhúbùgū (朮不姑) and the Nǚzhí (女直) came to pay tribute.
*Xīnwèi* (辛未).
Sent envoys to Gāolì (高麗) and Tiělí (鐵驪).
*Guǐyǒu* (癸酉).
The Huíhú (回鶻) came to pay tribute.
Winter, tenth month, *gēngchén* (庚辰) first day of the lunar month.
Celebration of the Empress Dowager’s (Huáng Tàihòu) Yǒngníng Festival.
Jìn (晉), the Huíhú (回鶻), Dùnhuáng (燉煌), and various other states all sent envoys to offer congratulations.
*Rénwǔ* (壬午).
Summoned the Huíhú (回鶻) envoys Húlízhǐ (胡離只) and Ālàbǎo (阿剌保),
and questioned them regarding their customs.
*Dīnghài* (丁亥).
The envoys from various states returned.
Immediately sent Pú Lí Gǔ Píshì Hú Mòlǐ (蒲里骨皮室胡末里) as envoy to their countries.
Eleventh month, *jǐwèi* (己未).
Sent an envoy to seek doctors from Jìn (晉).
*Dīngmǎo* (丁卯).
Tiělí (鐵驪) came to pay tribute.
Twelfth month, *jiǎshēn* (甲申).
Went East.
Sacrificed at Mùyèshān (木葉山).
*Jǐchǒu* (己丑).
The doctors arrived.
Basic Annals 4, Tàizōng (太宗) Part 2
Huìtóng (會同) First Year, Spring, first month, *wùshēn* (戊申) first day of the lunar month.
Jìn (晉) and various states sent envoys to offer congratulations.
The Jìn (晉) envoy further stated that they had already commanded Hé Níng (和凝) to compose the Stele of Sacred Virtue and Divine Merit (*Shèngdé Shéngōng Bēi*).
*Wùchén* (戊辰).
Sent a person as envoy to Jìn (晉).
Second month, *rénwǔ* (壬午).
Shìwěi (室韋) presented white deer.
*Wùzǐ* (戊子).
Tiělí (鐵驪) came to pay tribute.
*Dīngyǒu* (丁酉).
Hunted at Sōngshān (松山).
*Wùxū* (戊戌).
Went east of the Liáohé River (遼河).
*Bǐngshēn* (丙申).
The Emperor pondered on Rén Huángwáng (人皇王).
Sent the General-in-Chief (*tìyǐn*) to lead the imperial clan members and those below them to offer sacrifices at his temporary palace.
*Dīngwèi* (丁未).
Issued an edict to increase the households responsible for provision and lodging (gōngyì hù) along the route taken by the Jìn (晉) envoys.
Third month, *rénxū* (壬戌).
Was about to go East.
Sānkè (三剋) stated that agricultural tasks were just beginning
and requested a reduction in baggage train
and a speedy return to the court.
[The Emperor] consented to this.
*Bǐngyín* (丙寅).
The Nǚzhí (女直) came to pay tribute.
*Guǐyǒu* (癸酉).
Went East.
Summer, fourth month, *wùyín* (戊寅) first day of the lunar month.
Went to the Southern Capital (Nánjīng).
*Jiǎshēn* (甲申).
The Nǚzhí (女直) came to pay tribute.
*Yǐyǒu* (乙酉).
Went to the Hot Springs (Wēnquán).
*Jǐchǒu* (己丑).
Returned to the palace.
Held an audience with the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
*Dīngyǒu* (丁酉).
The Nǚzhí (女直) presented bows and arrows as tribute.
*Jǐhài* (己亥).
Yēlǜ Lǔbùgǔ (耶律魯不古), the Grand Chancellor of the Southwestern Border (*xīnán biān dà xiángwěn*), reported a victory over the Dǎngxiàng (党項).
Fifth month, *jiǎyín* (甲寅).
Jìn (晉) again sent an envoy requesting [the Emperor] ascend the honorable title.
[The Emperor] consented to this.
Sixth month, *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) first day of the lunar month.
Tǔyùhùn (吐谷渾) and the Nǚzhí (女直) came to pay tribute.
*Xīnmǎo* (辛卯).
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) came to pay tribute.
*Guǐsì* (癸巳).
Issued an edict to construct the Hall of Sun, Moon, and Four Seasons (Rìyuè Sìshí Táng),
and to paint the deeds of ancient emperors and kings onto the two corridors.
Autumn, seventh month, *guǐhài* (癸亥).
Sent an envoy to bestow horses upon Jìn (晉).
*Dīngmǎo* (丁卯).
Sent Húlídǐ (鶻離底) as envoy to Jìn (晉),
and Méilǐliǎogǔ (梅里了古) as envoy to Southern Táng (Nán Táng).
*Wùchén* (戊辰).
Sent Yēlǜ Shùlán Diéliègē (耶律述蘭迭烈哥), the Right Chancellor of the Central Terrace Department (*Zhōngtái Shěng Yòuxiàng*), as envoy to Jìn (晉).
Zhào Sīwēn (趙思溫), the regional military commissioner of Línhǎi (臨海) Army, served as his deputy.
[They] invested the Jìn Emperor with the title Emperor Yīngwǔ Míngyì (英武明義皇帝).
Eighth month, *wùzǐ* (戊子).
The Nǚzhí (女直) came to pay tribute.
*Gēngzǐ* (庚zǐ).
Tǔyùhùn (吐谷渾), Wūsūn (烏孫), and Mòhé (靺鞨) all came to pay tribute.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Hēichēzi Shìwēi submitted famous horses as tribute.
Border officials reported that Jìn had dispatched Acting Sīkōng Fēng Dào and Zuǒ Sànqí Chángshì Wěi Xūn to confer the venerable title upon the Empress Dowager,
and Zuǒ Pūshè Liú Xù
and Yòu Jiànyì Dàfū Lú Chóng to confer the venerable title upon the Emperor.
Consequently, Jiānjūn Yínnǐyǐ was sent to serve as the welcoming escort.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to the multitude of officials and the elderly,
decreeing that whenever high ministers were granted noble ranks and official positions,
they should all be bestowed with brocade robes, gold belts, white horses, and gold-adorned saddles and bridles.
This was codified into law.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎxū (the first day of the month),
Lángjūn Dílígū and others were dispatched to convey regards and inquire about the Jìn envoys.
On the day Rén Yín,
Jìn sent envoys to express thanks for the enfeoffment ceremony.
On this day,
there were also envoys who presented a single-humped camel and famous horses.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎchén (the first day of the month),
orders were given to the Southern and Northern Chancellors (Zǎixiàng) and the Yílíjǐn to proceed to the residence and bestow a banquet upon the Jìn envoy Fēng Dào and those below him.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor proceeded to the Kāihuáng Hall
and summoned the Jìn envoys for an audience.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Empress Dowager proceeded to the Kāihuáng Hall.
Fēng Dào and Wěi Xūn conferred the venerable title upon her, saying: Guǎngdé Zhìrén Zhāoliè Chóngjiǎn Yìngtiān Huáng Tàihòu.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Zàishēng Chái Cè Lǐ (Regeneration Firewood Enfeoffment Ceremony) was performed.
On the day Bǐng Yín,
the Emperor proceeded to the Xuānzhèng Hall.
Liú Xù and Lú Chóng conferred the venerable title upon him, saying: Ruìwén Shénwǔ Fǎtiān Qǐyùn Míngdé Zhāngxìn Zhìdào Guǎngjìng Zhāoxiào Sìshèng Huángdì.
A general amnesty was declared,
and the reign title was changed to Huìtóng.
In this month,
Jìn again dispatched Zhào Yíng bearing a memorial to offer congratulations,
and offered in tribute the sixteen prefectures of Yōu, Jì, Yíng, Mò, Zhuō, Tán, Shùn, Guī, Rú, Xīn, Wǔ, Yún, Yìng, Shuò, Huán, and Wèi, along with their maps and registers.
Thereupon, an imperial edict designated the Imperial Capital as Shàngjīng (Supreme Capital),
and its seat (fǔ) was designated Línhuáng.
Yōuzhōu was promoted to Nánjīng (Southern Capital),
and the original Nánjīng was promoted to Dōngjīng (Eastern Capital).
Xīnzhōu was renamed Fèngshèng Zhōu,
and Wǔzhōu was renamed Guīhuà Zhōu.
The Yílíjǐn of the Northern and Southern Administrations (Yuàn) and the Yǐshì were promoted to the rank of King (Wáng).
The Zhǔbù was designated as Lìng (Magistrate),
the Lìng was designated as Cìshǐ (Prefect),
and the Cìshǐ was designated as Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioner).
The Tīlǐyǐ of the Two Departments was designated as Sītú,
the Dálàgān was designated as Fùshǐ (Deputy Envoy),
the Mádōubù was designated as Xiànlìng (County Magistrate),
and the Xiàn Dálàgān was designated as Mǎbù (Cavalry and Infantry).
The positions of Xuānhuī Shǐ and Gémén Shǐ were established,
as well as Kònghè, Kèshěng, Yùshǐ Dàfū, Zhōngchéng, Shìyù, Pànguān, Wénbānyá Shǔ, and the Shìzhú of the various Palaces and Courts;
the Shìzhú of the Horse Herds (Mǎqún) and Yáoniǎn
and the Lángjūn officials of the Southern and Northern Administrations (Fǔ) and the Guójiù Zhàng were designated as Chǎngshǐ;
the Zǎixiàng and Jiédùshǐ Zhàng of the various departments were designated as Sīkōng;
the Tàlín of the two Shìwēi (tribes) was designated as Pūshè;
and the chief officials of the Yīngfāng (Falconry) and Jiānyě (Smelting Supervision) Bureaus were designated as Xiángwěn.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùxū,
Tóngkuò, Ābō, and others were dispatched as envoys to Jìn.
An imperial order conferred upon Jìn's Fēng Dào the title of Acting Tàifù,
upon Liú Xù the title of Acting Tàibǎo,
and the remaining officials were ranked according to their status.
In the second year (938 CE), spring, in the first month, on the day Yǐsì,
due to receiving the enfeoffment from Jìn,
envoys were dispatched to inform Nán Táng and Gāolì.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor proceeded to the Kāihuáng Hall,
hosted a banquet for the Jìn envoy Fēng Dào and those below him,
and presented gifts according to their rank.
On the day Wùshēn,
Jìn dispatched Jīnwǔ Wèi Dàjiāngjūn Mǎ Cóngbīn and Kǎogōng Lángzhōng Liú Zhīxīn to present treasures and currency as tribute.
Orders were given to distribute these among the multitude of officials.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Jìn sent envoys to thank the court for exempting the four border prefectures from taxes.
In the second month, on the day Wùyín,
a banquet was held for the various Kings (Wáng) and Jiédùshǐ who came to congratulate the court on the enfeoffment ceremony.
Furthermore, the Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ) and Tìyǐn Díliǎn were ordered to see them off.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Tàizǔ Temple was visited.
Gifts were bestowed upon the officials and people residing in the capital,
and inner and outer officials received rewards according to their varying ranks.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Wáng Zī, who held the concurrent post of Shìzhōng and Zuǒ Jīnwǔ Wèi Shàng Jiāngjūn, was additionally given the title of Jiǎnxiào Tàiwèi.
In the third month,
hunting took place beside Niǎotán.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
On the day Dīngsì,
the imperial son Shùlǜ was enfeoffed as Shòu'ān Wáng,
and Yǎnsāgě was enfeoffed as Tàipíng Wáng.
On the day Jǐsì,
great gifts were distributed to the common people.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor toured Mùyè Shān.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Dōngjīng Circuit reported that wolves were eating people.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐsì,
the sale of ewes from Nánjīng to outside the border was prohibited.
Sīnǔgǔduōlǐ and others were implicated for stealing government property
and their households were confiscated.
Nán Táng sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the tribute items received were bestowed upon the multitude of officials.
On the day Wùshēn,
an envoy from the Chányú of the Huíhú (Uighurs) requested official appointments.
An edict merely granted the titles of Cìshǐ and Xiànlìng.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
it snowed.
This summer,
the Emperor resided at Pínbì Diàn.
Autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
Jìn sent envoys to present rhinoceros belts.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Tǔyùhún came to offer tribute.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Chǎngshǐ Ābō was found guilty of dereliction of duty while serving as envoy,
and he was ordered to be flogged.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Great King of Yǐshì was found guilty of unfair taxation and conscription.
He was struck on the back with a wooden sword and then released;
furthermore, the required tribute (shànggōng) from the people of the Southern and Northern Administrations (Fǔ) was abolished,
as well as all taxes and levies imposed by the Zǎixiàng and Jiédù that were not based on old regulations.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Díliè was dispatched to bestow fine Wūgǔ horses upon Jìn.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
because two Cìshǐ of the Southern King's Administration (Nán Wáng Fǔ) were corrupt,
each was beaten with one hundred strokes,
and they were subsequently detained in the Yúhòu Zhàng
to be used for the ‘ghost-shooting arrows’ ritual (Bèi Shè Guǐ Jiàn);
officials beloved by the people were selected from the multitude to replace them.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Jìn sent envoys to present annual tribute currency,
memorializing that the gold and currency for the two years Xū and Hài should be transported to Yānjīng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Zǔbǔ Ālídǐ came to offer tribute.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to Jìn.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
because the Emperor deemed the Wūgǔ tribe's land rich in water and grass,
an edict ordered that the households of the Three Shíliè of the Northern and Southern Administrations (Yuàn) be relocated there.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
Tiělí and Dūnhuáng both sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
fishing was conducted at the Tǔ Hé.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
one of the servants of the Huíhú envoy struck another person with a blade.
An edict ordered that the offender be handed over to his own envoy for punishment.
In the third year (939 CE), spring, in the first month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the King of Wúyuè sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day Gēngyín,
the consort of the Rén Huáng Wáng came to pay court.
The Huíhú envoy requested permission to observe the court audience ceremony of the envoys from various states,
and this was granted.
On the day Rénchén,
Péiyè and Ābō were dispatched as envoys to Jìn to present birthday greetings.
Jìn returned the Tǔyùhún tribes from Bīng, Zhèn, Xīn, and Dài Prefectures who had defected.
In the second month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xī Wáng Láogǔníng led six Jiédùshǐ to pay court and offer tribute.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wūgǔ sent envoys to present captives from the Fúlù Kingdom.
The Yílíjǐn of that department was bestowed with banners and drums to honor his achievement.
On the day Rén Yín,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
On the day Xīnhài,
Mòlígǔ Mòlǐ returned from his mission to the Huíhú's Āsàlán,
and he was rewarded with matching robes (duìyī) in commendation.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Nǚzhí along the Yālù Jiāng sent envoys to pay homage.
In the third month, on the day Wùchén,
envoys were dispatched to Jìn
to announce the impending Imperial tour to Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor proceeded to Nánjīng.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Tìyǐn Yēlǜ Nièlígǔdé was commanded to lead ten thousand cavalry as the vanguard.
On the day Rénshēn,
upon reaching Shí Lǐng (Stone Ridge),
Xī Wáng Láogǔníng and Jiānjūn Yínnǐyǐ were severely reprimanded
because their attendance at court audience was untimely.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Lǔbùgū presented the number of captives taken from the Dǎngxiàng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
hunting took place at Shuǐ Mén (Water Gate),
and a white deer was captured.
On the day Gēngyín,
an edict mandated that those in the retinue who disturbed the populace should be dealt with according to military law.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor toured Jìzhōu.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Jìn and Nán Táng each sent envoys to pay homage.
. Arrived
at Yān (Yanjing/Nánjīng). The imperial ceremonial carriage (fǎjià)
was prepared. Entered through
Gǒngchénmén, ascended
the Yuánhédiàn, and performed
the ceremony of entering the inner court (rùgé lǐ). Rén Yín
, sent envoys
to Jìn. Yǐ Sì
, visited the villa
of the Resident General, Zhào Yánshòu. Bǐng Wǔ
, Jìn sent the Xuanhui Commissioners Yáng Duān
, Wáng Tiào, and others to inquire after the Emperor's well-being. Rén Zǐ
, the Emperor held court
at the Biàndiàn, and hosted a banquet
for the envoys from Jìn and various other states. Bǐng Chén
, Jìn sent envoys
to present tea and medicine. Rén Xū
, the Emperor held court
at the Zhāoqìngdiàn, and hosted a banquet
for the assembled officials of Nánjīng. Guǐ Hài
, Jìn sent envoys
to celebrate the Duānwǔ Festival (Dragon Boat Festival). The ceremonial gifts
they presented were bestowed upon the assembled officials. Yǐ Chǒu
, Nántáng
presented a white tortoise. Five Month, day Gēng Wǔ
, a banquet was held
for the assembled officials and the envoys of various states for the Duānwǔ Festival. Ordered the envoys of Huíhú
and Dùnhuáng to perform their native dances
, allowing the other envoys to observe. Gēng Chén
, Jìn sent envoys
to present bows and arrows. Jiǎ Shēn
, sent the Imperial Prince Tiāndé
and the Deputy Minister of Works (Jiǎnxiào Sītú), Dǐ Yònghé, as envoys to Jìn. Wù Zǐ
, reviewed the cavalry
in the Southern Suburbs. Six Month, first day Yǐ Wèi
, the Chancellor of the Eastern Capital, Yēlǜ Yǔzhī
, reported that Dà Sùxián, the Prime Minister of Bóhǎi, was acting unlawfully. An imperial decree ordered
subordinate officials and the local populace to nominate talented and virtuous individuals to replace him. Bǐng Shēn
, reviewed the infantry
in the Southern Suburbs. Gēng Zǐ
, Jìn and Xiálàgǔzhǐ
sent envoys to seek an audience. Rén Yín
, the Imperial carriage departed Yānjīng (Yān Capital)
. Ordered the Director of the Chancellery (Zhōngshū Lìng), Xiāo Sēngyǐn
, to gather the armies from all circuits at Chángzuòyíng. Guǐ Chǒu
, arrived at
Fèngshèngzhōu. Jiǎ Yín
, rewarded and comforted the soldiers
. Autumn, Seventh Month, day Jǐ Sì
, hunted at
Huádǐlièshān. Guǐ Yǒu
, paid respects
to the Empress Dowager. Bǐng Zǐ
, followed the Empress Dowager
to visit Rén Huáng Wáng's consort, who was ill. Wù Yín
, Rén Huáng Wáng's consort, Xiāo shì
, passed away (hōng). Jǐ Mǎo
, because Ān Chóngróng occupied Zhènzhōu
and rebelled against Jìn, an imperial decree ordered the General who Conquers the South, Liǔ Yán
, to prepare the border defenses. Bǐng Xū
, moved Rén Huáng Wáng's temporary palace
to the place where his consort had died. Xīn Mǎo
, Jìn sent envoys requesting
permission to perform the sacrifice in the Southern Suburbs (Nánjiāo lǐ)
. This was permitted. Eight Month, day Jǐ Hài
, decreed that the officials and people of Dōngdān
should wear mourning clothes for their King's consort, Bèi Fēi Xiāo shì. Gēng Zǐ
, Zǔbǔ
came to offer tribute. Rén Yín
, sent envoys
to Nántáng. Yǐ Sì
, Zǔbǔ, Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi
, Rèn Liè, and other states came to offer tribute. Nántáng
sent envoys requesting a blue tent,
and it was granted to them. Wù Shēn
, Ān Duān's private walled settlement
was established as Báichuānzhōu. Xīn Hài
, the envoy of Bígǔdé
requested the bestowal of a noble rank,
and he was granted the rank of Prime Minister of his state. Jiǎ Yín
, Zǔbǔ
came to offer tribute. Yǐ Mǎo
, established the official staff
for Báichuānzhōu. Bǐng Chén
, decreed that the areas near the Yúxiēlǐ Hé
and Lúqú Hé
should be granted as farmland to the three *shíliè* tribesmen: Ōujǐn Tūlǚ and Yǐsībó from the Southern Administration, and Wēnnà Hélà from the Northern Administration. Nine Month, day Gēng Wǔ
, the Palace Attendant (Shìzhōng), Cuī Qiónggǔ
, reported:
"The ruler of Jìn has heard that Your Majesty often goes hunting,
and requests that you moderate this activity."
The Emperor replied:
"My hunting expeditions
are not simply for pleasure;
they are for practicing military skills."
An imperial decree was then issued to instruct him. Rén Wǔ
, a border general reported defeating the Tǔyùhún
and capturing their chief
. An imperial decree ordered that only the chief perpetrator
and his able-bodied followers should be executed;
the remainder were all released. Bǐng Xū
, Jìn sent envoys
to present famous horses as tribute. Wù Zǐ
, Nǚzhí
and the King of Wúyuè sent envoys to offer tribute.
Winter, Tenth Month, day Xīn Chǒu
, sent Kèláng as envoy to Wúyuè,
and Lüègū as envoy to Nántáng. Gēng Shēn
, Jìn sent envoys
to offer cloth as tribute,
and requested permission to personally sacrifice at Nányuè (Southern Peak)
. This was granted. Eleventh Month, day Jǐ Sì
, Nántáng sent envoys carrying a wax-sealed letter
discussing secret matters concerning Jìn. Dīng Chǒu
, decreed that the relevant authorities
should instruct the populace in sowing seeds and spinning thread. Abolished
the custom whereby if a wife (elder sister) died, the husband would take her younger sister as a replacement. Twelfth Month, first day Rén Chén
, led all the officials
to pay respects at Tàizǔ's temporary palace. Jiǎ Wǔ
, performed the bonfire sacrifice (fánchái)
. When the ritual was complete,
sacrificed at the Spirit Tent
. Bǐng Shēn
, sent envoys
to Jìn. Bǐng Chén
, decreed that Qìdān people who had been granted Hàn official titles
should follow Hàn rites,
and were permitted to intermarry with Hàn people. Dīng Sì
, decreed that a cool palace (liángdiàn)
should be built on the southwestern rampart of the Imperial City in Yānjīng. That winter
, the imperial residence
was established at Sǎndiàn. The fourth year, Spring, First Month, day Rén Xū
, for those people of the Yǐshì, Pǐnbēi, and Tūguǐ three tribes
who, being widowed or poor, could not sustain themselves,
the government arranged marriages for them. Bǐng Zǐ
, Nántáng sent envoys
to offer tribute. Gēng Chén
, the Nièlā and Wūkuí tribes
presented figures on the captives taken from the Dǎngxiàng. Jǐ Chǒu
, decreed the calculation of merits
achieved in the campaign against the Dǎngxiàng. Second Month, day Bǐng Shēn
, the Crown Prince
captured a white deer. Jiǎ Chén
, Jìn sent envoys
to present fragrant herbs and medicines. Bǐng Zǐ
, Tiělí
came to offer tribute. Dīng Sì
, decreed that the relevant authorities
should compile the deeds of the founding ancestor, Qíshǒu Kèhán. Jǐ Wèi
, Jìn sent Yáng Yànxún
to offer tribute and also
to report on the arrogance and defiance of Ān Chóngróng at Zhènzhōu
. He was subsequently detained and not sent back. That month
, Ān Chóngróng of Jìn's Zhènzhōu
seized Zhuáilá, the Liao envoy. Third Month
, specially appointed Kuòlǐ
, the Huíhú envoy, as Yūyuè,
and bestowed upon him banners, flags, bows, swords, clothes, and horses.
Other gifts were bestowed according to rank. Guǐ Yǒu
, because permission had been granted for the Nánjiāo sacrifice
, Jìn sent envoys
to express thanks,
presenting ten *yì* (200 taels) of gold. Summer, Fourth Month, day Jǐ Mǎo
, Jìn sent envoys
to present cherries.
Five Month, day Gēng Chén
, Sū, the Yílíjǐn of the Tǔyùhún, and others rebelled and defected to Jìn. Sent Diélà
to address Jìn and the defense commissioner of Tàiyuán regarding this matter. Six Month, day Xīn Mǎo
, Zhào Chóng, the Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhènwǔ Jūn
, expelled his Military Commissioner, Yēlǜ Huàlǐ,
and rebelled at Shuòzhōu,
defecting to Jìn. Bǐng Wǔ
, ordered the Xuanhui Commissioner Niǎogǔzhǐ
to proceed to Shuòzhōu,
and surround the city with troops.
If an envoy from Jìn arrived
and requested the lifting of the siege,
he was immediately not to listen,
but instead to send the envoy by relay post to the capital. Autumn, Seventh Month, day Guǐ Hài
, Nántáng sent envoys
bearing a wax-sealed letter. Bǐng Yín
, Niǎogǔzhǐ reported, requesting permission to send an envoy to Shuòzhōu to command surrender
. The defenders still held their fortifications firmly and refused entry
. He further reported that Jìn had sent tribute items
. Ordered that the tribute items received
should immediately be given as rewards to the generals and officers attacking the city. Jǐ Sì
, the relevant authorities reported that there was a honeycomb containing honey
on the chariot of the Divine Banner (Shéndú Chē).
The astrologers interpreted this
as auspicious. Rén Shēn
, Jìn sent envoys
to present a crystal inkstone. Eight Month, day Guǐ Sì
, Nántáng presented
a wax-sealed letter. Gēng Zǐ
, Jìn sent envoys
to present rhinoceros horn bows and bamboo arrows. The King of Wúyuè sent envoys
bearing a wax-sealed letter.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénshēn
, there was a comet (bèi xīng) in the area corresponding to the Jìn constellation/territory.
On the day Dīngchǒu
, the Emperor proceeded to Guīhuà Zhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnchǒu
, the relevant authorities reported a great harvest in Yān and Jì.
On the day Guǐmǎo
, the King of Wúyuè sent an envoy to present tribute.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín
, Jìn informed them that they were campaigning against Ān Chóngróng.
On the day Gēngwǔ
, the Tǔyùhún requested surrender,
and an envoy was dispatched to pacify and instruct them.
The Zǔbǔ came to present tribute,
and their goods were bestowed upon those around the Emperor.
On the day Bǐngzǐ
, the Nǚzhí from the Yālù Jiāng presented tribute.
On the day Rénwǔ

, it was decreed that congratulations were to be received for the two festivals, Yǒngníng and Tiānshòu, as well as for the New Year (Zhèngdàn), Chóngwǔ (Double Fifth), Winter Solstice (Dōngzhì), and the Lá Festival
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùzǐ
, Jìn sent an envoy to report that the Military Commissioner (Jiédù Shǐ) of Shānnán, Ān Cóngjìn, had rebelled.
An edict was issued to suppress him according to expediency.
On the day Gēngyín
, Southern Táng sent an envoy bearing a wax-sealed letter.
On the day Wùxū
, Jìn sent Wáng Shēngluán to present tribute.
On the day Wùshēn
, Jìn informed them of the defeat of Ān Chóngróng,
and subsequently sent Yáng Yànxún back.
On the day Xīnhài
, Jìn sent an envoy requesting the withdrawal of the garrison troops.
An edict ordered Tìyǐn Shuògǔ to return with his troops.
On the day Jiǎyín
, Shuò Zhōu was attacked and captured.
The Commander of the Kònghè troops, Xiélǐ, was sent to comfort the army.
At this time, Niǎogǔzhī died in battle beneath the city walls.
The Emperor was enraged,
ordering the execution of all able-bodied men (dīngzhuàng) within the city,
and further assigned thirty households (shàng hù) of the rebellious populace as Niǎogǔzhī’s personal retainers (bù qǔ).
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the first day Bǐngchén
, the Emperor was in Guīhuà Zhōu
and held court (shòu cháo) for the assembled officials in the traveling palace.
The tribute items from various circuits (zhū dào) were presented to the Empress Dowager and bestowed upon the Imperial Clan and various officials.
On the day Wùwǔ
, an edict sought frank advice.
Yēlǜ Hǎisī, a gentleman (lángjūn) of the Northern Princely Household, responded to the edict.
He was summoned for an audience, where his words pleased the Emperor,
and he was specially appointed as Commissioner of Palace Affairs (Xuānhuī Shǐ).
An edict ordered the Chancellor (Zhèngshì Lìng) Sēngyǐn and others to relocate Qìdān households and establish garrisons along the southern border.
On the day Wùchén
, Jìn sent the severed head of Ān Chóngróng in a box as an offering.
The Emperor had frequently desired to personally campaign against Chóngróng,
but upon this development, he stopped.
On the day Guǐyǒu
, an envoy was dispatched to Jìn.
In this month
, Jìn sent an envoy to congratulate them because Shuò Zhōu had been pacified
. Consequently, the Commissioner of the Guest Bureau (Kèsǐng Shǐ), Yēlǜ Huàgē
, was dispatched as an envoy to Jìn, bringing a birthday gift.
In the second month, on the day Rénchén
, the Emperor planned a southern tour.
Since there were still areas in the various circuits (zhū lù) that had not been pacified,
he summoned the Crown Prince and the assembled officials for a discussion
. They all said
: "Although the three prefectures of Xiāng, Zhèn, and Shuò are now pacified,
the Tǔyùhún, having been misled by Ān Chóngróng,
have still not sworn allegiance.
It is appropriate to raise troops to suppress them
in order to warn the various tribes."
The Emperor said
: "This coincides exactly with Our own thoughts."
Consequently, an edict appointed Prince Míng Wēi'ēn to replace Yúyuè Xìn'ēn as Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route (Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎo Shǐ) to campaign against them,
and furthermore, Prince Míng was instructed
that he should first practice military matters on the frontier before taking office.
On the day Jiǎwǔ
, he proceeded to Nánjīng.
An envoy was dispatched to Jìn to demand the rebel Tǔyùhún.
On the day Yǐwèi
, the Bígǔdé presented tribute.
The third month, on the first day Yǐmǎo
, Jìn sent Sòng Huīyè, the Defense Commissioner (Fángyù Shǐ) of Qí Zhōu,
and Zhāng Yán, the Palace Tea and Wine Master (Hànlín Chájiǔ Shǐ), to inquire about the Emperor's health.
In the intercalary month
, the Emperor halted his progress at Yángmén.
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jiǎyín
, the Tiělí presented tribute,
and their goods were distributed and bestowed upon the assembled officials.
On the day Bǐngzǐ
, Jìn sent an envoy to present saddled horses for the Willow-Shooting ritual.
In the fifth month, on the fifth day, which was Wùzǐ
, slaughtering was forbidden.
In the sixth month, on the first day Guǐchǒu
, Prince Qí of Jìn, Chóngguì, sent an envoy to present tribute.
On the day Dīngsì
, Túdǔgǔ and Sùsā came to present tribute.
On the day Yǐchǒu
, the ruler of Jìn, Jìngtáng, died.
His son, Chóngguì, ascended the throne.
On the day Wùchén
, Jìn sent an envoy to announce the mourning.
Court was suspended for seven days.
On the day Gēngwǔ
, an envoy was dispatched to Jìn to offer condolences and sacrifices.
On the day Dīngchǒu
, upon hearing that the Empress Dowager was unwell (bù yù),
the Emperor immediately hurried inside to attend to her,
personally tasting all the medicinal decoctions.
He also reported the situation to the temple of Tàizǔ,
visited the Púsà Táng,
and provided food for fifty thousand monks.
She recovered in the seventh month.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngyín
, Jìn sent Liáng Yán, General of the Metropolitan Guard (Jīnwú Wèi Dà Jiāngjūn), and Zhū Chóngjié, Director of the Four Quarters Hostel (Pàn Sìfāng Guǎn Shì), to express thanks.
Their letter referred to him as "grandson"
, not using the designation "subject"
The Commissioner of the Guest Bureau, Qiáo Róng, was sent to reproach them.
Jǐng Yánguǎng replied
: "The former emperor was established by your Sagely Dynasty;
the present ruler was enthroned by our own state.
It is permissible to be neighbors and grandsons,
but it is not permissible to present memorials referring to him as a subject."
When Róng returned,
he reported the details,
and the Emperor first conceived the intention of invading the south.
On the day Xīnmǎo
, the Zǔbǔ, Bígǔdé, and Wūgǔ presented tribute.
Generals Tàdélǐ and Púgǔ led the surrendering general Xiádé to the court,
and together presented their captives.
On the day Dīngwèi
, Jìn sent an envoy to report the mourning for the passing of his grandmother.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnyǒu
, the Nǚzhí, Zǔbǔ, and Wūgǔ each presented regional products as tribute.
On the day Jiǎzǐ
, Jìn recovered Xiāng Zhōu.
On the day Wùchén
, an edict instructed Liú Zhìyuǎn, Military Commissioner of Hédōng, to send the rebel Wūgǔ Commander, who was traveling from Yānjīng, to the Imperial Court.
On the day Guǐyǒu
, Xiāo Bàishí, Military Commissioner of the Tiānchéng Army, was dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices in Jìn.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénchén
, an envoy was dispatched to congratulate the Jìn Emperor on his succession.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐsì
, troops from various circuits were mobilized.
General Mìgǔdé was dispatched to attack the Dǎngxiàng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi
, the Wǔdìng Army reported that a date tree had grown from a pine.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐhài
, Jìn sent an envoy to express thanks.
This winter
, the Emperor halted his progress at Chìchéng.
In the sixth year, spring, the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo
, Jìn sent an envoy to present relics of the former emperor.
On the day Xīnyǒu
, Jìn sent an envoy requesting permission to reside in Biàn.
Permission was granted.
The third month, on the first day Jǐmǎo
, the King of Wúyuè sent an envoy to present tribute.
On the day Jiǎshēn
, Méilǐchuǎnyǐn returned and submitted.
On the day Wùzǐ
, Southern Táng sent an envoy bearing a wax-sealed letter.
On the day Dīngwèi
, Jìn arrived at Biàn
and sent an envoy to express thanks.
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day Wùshēn
, there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài
, an envoy was dispatched to Jìn to present a birthday gift.
In the sixth month, on the first day Dīngwèi
, the Tiělí presented tribute.
On the day Jǐwèi
, the Xī Chúgǔlǐ tribe presented a white musk deer.
On the day Xīnyǒu
, Mò Zhōu presented a white magpie.
Jìn sent an envoy to present gold as tribute.
Autumn, the eighth month, on the first day Dīngwèi
, Jìn again presented gold as tribute.
On the day Jǐwèi
, he proceeded to Fèngshèng Zhōu.
Jìn sent his son, Yánxù, to pay court.
Winter, the eleventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo
, the Grand Commandant of Shàngjīng, Yēlǜ Díniǎn, captured a Jìn spy,
thus discovering their duplicity.
On the day Jiǎchén
, the Tiělí presented tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngwèi
, he proceeded to Nánjīng
to discuss attacking Jìn.
Zhào Yánshòu, Zhào Yánzhāo, Ān Duān, Xièlǐ, and others were ordered to advance by separate routes through Cāng, , Yì, and Dìng.
The main army followed.
In this year
, Yáng Yànzhāo requested moving his military post (zhèn) to Nàluò and Xīnzhèn.
Permission was granted.
The seventh year, Spring, the first month, *jiǎxū* day, the first day of the lunar month.
Zhào Yánshòu and Yánzhāo led the vanguard of 50,000 cavalry and reached Rènqiū.
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
Ān Duān entered Yànmén,
and besieged Xīn and Dài.
On *jǐmǎo* day,
Zhào Yánshòu besieged Bèizhōu.
His military officer Shào Kē opened the south gate and admitted the Liáo troops.
The Grand Administrator Wú Luán threw himself into a well and died.
On *jǐchǒu* day,
they reached Yuánchéng.
Yánshòu was appointed Jìedùshǐ of Wèi and Bó prefectures, etc.,
enfeoffed as the Prince of Wèi (Wèi Wáng),
and led his division to garrison Nánlè.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
troops were dispatched to attack Líyáng.
Zhāng Yànzé of Jìn came to resist.
On *xīnchǒu* day,
Jìn dispatched an envoy to renew the old good relations.
An imperial edict ordered the cession of the prefectures north of the Héběi (Yellow River),
and the dispatch of Sāng Wéihàn and Jǐng Yánguǎng to discuss (the matter).
The second month, *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the lunar month.
Bózhōu was attacked,
and the Prefectural Governor Zhōu Rú surrendered the city.
Yáng Guāngyuǎn, Jìedùshǐ of Pínglú Jūn of Jìn, secretly guided the Liáo army to cross the river from Mǎjiākǒu.
Jǐng Yánguǎng, a Jìn general, ordered Shí Bīn to defend Májiākǒu,
and Bái Zàiróng to defend Mǎjiākǒu.
Not long after,
Zhōu Rú led the Liáo army Mádá to encamp east of the river,
and attacked Běijīn in Yùnzhōu,
in support of Guāngyuǎn.
Jìn dispatched Lǐ Shǒuzhēn, Huángpǔ Yù, Liáng Hànzhāng, and Xuē Huáiràng leading 10,000 troops,
advancing simultaneously by water and land along the river.
The Liáo army surrounded a separate Jìn general at Qīchéng.
The Jìn ruler personally led troops to rescue him,
and the Liáo army withdrew.
When Shǒuzhēn and the others arrived at Mǎjiākǒu,
Mádá dispatched 10,000 infantry to construct fortifications,
10,000 cavalry to guard the perimeter,
while the rest of the troops garrisoned west of the river.
Before the crossing was complete,
the Jìn troops attacked them,
and the Liáo army suffered a setback.
The third month, *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the lunar month.
Zhào Yánshòu stated:
"All the Jìn armies have established palisades along the river,
but are timid and dare not fight.
If we lead a large army directly to Chányuān,
and occupy their bridges,
Jìn can surely be taken."
On that day,
the Jìn troops were stationed at Chányuān,
with their vanguard Gāo Xíngzhōu located at Qīchéng.
Yánshòu and Yánzhāo were then ordered to lead tens of thousands of cavalry to deploy to the right of Xíngzhōu,
while the emperor personally led elite troops to deploy to his left.
The battle lasted until dusk.
The emperor again used strong cavalry to charge into their central army,
and the Jìn army was unable to fight.
Coincidentally, there was a spy who reported that the Jìn army's eastern flank was small in number,
and the city palisades along the river were not secure.
Therefore, (the Liáo forces) immediately attacked their eastern flank,
and the masses all fled and collapsed.
Troops were unleashed in pursuit,
resulting in a great defeat of (the Jìn army).
On *rénwǔ* day,
Zhào Yánzhāo was left to guard Bèizhōu,
and the captured households were moved to the interior.
Summer, the fourth month, *guǐchǒu* day,
they returned and reached Nánjīng.
On *xīnwèi* day,
(the emperor) went to Liángxíng.
The fifth month, *guǐyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Bálǐdé reported defeating Dézhōu,
and capturing the Prefectural Governor Yǐn Jūfán and twenty-seven officers and officials.
The sixth month, *jiǎchén* day,
the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi came to present tribute.
On *yǐsì* day,
the states of Mòlǐ and Yàolǐ, among others, came to present tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, *jǐmǎo* day,
Yáng Guāngyuǎn of Jìn dispatched someone bearing a wax-sealed letter.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
Jìn dispatched Zhāng Huī bearing a memorial requesting peace.
Huī was detained and not sent back.
The eighth month, *xīnyǒu* day,
the Huíhú dispatched an envoy to request a marriage alliance,
but it was refused.
In this month,
Jìn troops from Zhènzhōu came to attack Fēihú.
Yēlǜ Kǒng'ā, Jìedùshǐ of Dàtóng Jūn, fought and defeated them.
The ninth month, *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the lunar month,
(the emperor) traveled north.
Winter, the tenth month, *dīngwèi* day,
Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
On *rénxū* day,
the Tiānshòu Festival was held.
All neighboring states presented congratulations,
except Jìn, which did not arrive.
The eleventh month, *rénshēn* day,
an imperial edict summoned troops from all circuits,
ordering them to assemble north of the Wēnyú River on the first day of the intercalary month.
The twelfth month, *guǐmǎo* day,
(the army) launched a southern campaign.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
they reached Gǔběikǒu.
Intercalary month, *jǐsì* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the troops from all circuits were reviewed at the Wēnyú River.
On *jǐmǎo* day,
Zhōu was besieged,
and its nine counties were subjugated.
The eighth year, Spring, the first month, *gēngzǐ* day,
troops were divided to attack Xíng, Míng, and Cí prefectures,
killing and pillaging almost everything.
They entered the territory of Yèdū.
The troops of Zhāng Cóng'ēn, Mǎ Quánjié, and Ān Shěnqí were all arrayed south of the Ānyáng River in Xiāngzhōu.
Huángpǔ Yù and Mùróng Yànchāo, the Prefectural Governor of Púzhōu, led a thousand cavalry to observe the Liáo army.
Upon reaching Yèdū,
they encountered tens of thousands of Liáo troops.
They fought while retreating,
reaching Yúlín Diàn.
The Liáo army subsequently arrived.
Yù and Yànchāo fought fiercely for over a hundred rounds.
Yù's horse died,
and he fought on foot.
Shěnqí led cavalry to cross the water to rescue him,
and the Liáo army subsequently withdrew.
The second month,
Wèi was besieged.
Dù Chóngwēi, a Jìn general, led troops to rescue it.
On *wùzǐ* day,
Zhé Cóngruǎn, a Jìn general, captured Shèngzhōu.
The third month, *wùxū* day,
the army captured Qízhōu,
and killed its Prefectural Governor Shěn Bīn.
On *gēngxū* day,
Dù Chóngwēi and Lǐ Shǒuzhēn attacked Tàizhōu.
On *wùzǐ* day,
Zhào Yánshòu led the vanguard close to Tàichéng.
On *jǐwèi* day,
Chóngwēi and Shǒuzhēn led their troops to flee south.
(The Liáo forces) pursued them to Yángchéng,
and severely defeated them.
(The Jìn forces) again used infantry to form a square formation to resist,
and fought for over twenty rounds.
On *rénxū* day,
they engaged in close combat again for over ten *lǐ*.
On *guǐhài* day,
the Jìn troops were besieged at Báituánwèi Cūn.
The Jìn troops set up sharpened logs (deer antlers) to form a camp.
That evening there was a great wind.
At dawn,
the Tiěyào Army was ordered to dismount,
tear out the sharpened logs,
and vigorously enter and attack with short weapons.
Taking advantage of the wind, fire was set and dust was raised,
to increase the momentum.
The Jìn army shouted loudly, saying:
"Why is the Grand Commander (Dūzhāotǎo) not employing troops,
letting our soldiers die in vain!"
All the generals vigorously rushed out to fight.
Zhāng Yànzé, Yào Yuánfú, and Huángpǔ Yù led troops out in a great battle.
The other generals followed closely,
causing the Liáo army to retreat several hundred paces.
The wind intensified further,
and daylight became dark as night.
Fú Yànqīng used 10,000 cavalry to strike the flank of the Liáo army,
and led infantry to advance simultaneously.
The Liáo army was at a disadvantage.
The emperor rode a Xī carriage and retreated more than ten *lǐ*.
As the Jìn pursuers were pressing hard,
he seized a camel, rode it, and then returned.
The Jìn troops retreated to defend Dìngzhōu.
Summer, the fourth month, *jiǎshēn* day,
(the emperor) returned and reached Nánjīng,
and flogged those who did not fight hard several hundred times each.
On *gēngyín* day,
a banquet was held for the generals and soldiers at Yuánhé Diàn.
On *guǐsì* day,
(the emperor) went to Liángxíng.
The sixth month, *wùchén* day,
the Huíhú came to present tribute.
On *xīnwèi* day,
Tǔyùhùn and Bígǔdé both came to present tribute.
On *xīnsì* day,
the Hēichēzǐ Shìwéi came to present tribute.
On *dīnghài* day,
Zhào Yánshòu reported in a memorial that Jìn troops had attacked Gāoyáng,
and the garrison general fought and repelled them.
Autumn, the seventh month, *yǐmǎo* day,
(the emperor) hunted in Píngdì Sōnglín.
Jìn dispatched Mèng Shǒuzhōng bearing a memorial requesting peace,
and (the emperor) replied using the previous terms.
The eighth month, *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered Shìwèi Xiāo Sùsā to inspect the herds at Běixíng.
In the ninth month, on the day Rén'yín,
the Emperor arrived at Chìshān.
He hosted a banquet for his attendant ministers
and inquired about the essential affairs of the military and the state.
They replied:
“Regarding the affairs of the military and the state,
loving the people is the foundation.
If the people are wealthy, the troops are sufficient;
if the troops are sufficient, the state is strong.”
The Emperor concurred.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
he returned to Shàngjīng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
sacrifices were offered at Mùyè Shān.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùxū,
the Nǚzhí and Tiělí came to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, Guǐhài,
the Emperor paid a formal visit to Tàizǔ’s temporary palace.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yēlǜ Kǒng'ā, the Jìedùshǐ of Yúnzhōu, captured a Jìn spy.
On the day Wùchén,
the winter sacrifice (Là) was held,
and emissaries from various states were granted robes and horses.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Huíhú came to offer tribute.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
Bí'gǔdé presented the military register.
In the third month, on the day Jǐhài,
Tǔyùhún dispatched Military Inspector Xùliè to present one thousand households of captured persons.
Xùliè was granted the title of Jiǎnjiào Sīkōng.
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month, Xīnyǒu,
Bái Kějiǔ of Tǔyùhún came to defect.
In this month,
the Emperor traveled to Liángxíng.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Sūn Fāngjiǎn, the Jìn garrison commander of Yìzhōu, requested to join the interior (defect).
In the sixth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Ancestral Mausoleum (Zǔlíng),
and renamed the Shrine of the Secluded Spirits (Mìshéndiàn) to Chángsī (Long Remembrance).
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnhài,
an imperial edict ordered the mobilization of troops from all circuits,
stating that anyone who dared to damage the grain crops
would be judged according to military law.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Hélà, the chieftain of the Zǔbǔ, was made Yílíjǐn of his own tribe.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the Wūgǔ came to offer tribute.
In this month,
the Emperor personally led the southern expedition.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénchén,
the troops from all circuits were reviewed at Zǎolín Diàn west of Yúyáng.
In this month,
Zhào Yánshòu fought against Zhāng Yànzé of Jìn near Dìngzhōu,
and defeated him.
Winter, the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Wùzǐ,
the army advanced to besiege Zhènzhōu.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
scouting cavalry first reported the arrival of the Jìn troops.
Crack troops were sent to cut off the river bridge,
and the Jìn troops retreated to secure Wǔqiáng.
Díliǎn, the Great King of the Southern Department,
and General Gāo Móhàn divided their forces and advanced through the remote paths of Yíngzhōu.
Dù Chóngwēi dispatched Liáng Hànzhāng, the Jìedùshǐ of Bèizhōu, to lead troops to resist them.
They engaged in battle
and inflicted a great defeat,
killing Liáng Hànzhāng.
Dù Chóngwēi and Zhāng Yànzé led their forces to occupy Zhōngdù Bridge.
Zhào Yánshòu used infantry to strike first,
and Gāo Yànwēn followed up with cavalry.
They pursued the fleeing enemy,
leaving tens of thousands of corpses,
beheaded the general Wáng Qīng,
and Sòng Yànyún fell into the water and drowned.
Chóngwēi and the others retreated to secure Zhōngdù Zhài.
Lǐ Yīn, the Jìedùshǐ of Yìwǔ Jūn, surrendered the city,
and the army then advanced,
setting up camp flanking the Hūtuó River.
Three *lǐ* away from Zhōngdù Zhài,
they divided their forces to surround it.
At night, cavalry were arrayed in a circle to guard it;
during the day, troops were sent out to raid and plunder.
The Emperor again commanded Yēlǜ Shuògǔlǐ, the Chief of the Palace Guards (Dà Nèi Tìyǐn), and Zhào Yánshòu to divide their forces to maintain the siege.
The Emperor personally led cavalry to cross the river at night and emerge behind the enemy,
attacking and capturing Luánchéng,
where several thousand cavalry surrendered.
Generals and officers were dispatched to occupy the strategic points.
An order was issued within the army to prepare military provisions,
and that for three days no cooking smoke was permitted to be raised.
Any Jìn person captured
was to be tattooed and released.
All those transporting supplies, upon seeing this, abandoned their goods and fled.
Consequently, the Jìn forces were cut off internally and externally;
their food was exhausted and their power depleted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Dù Chóngwēi, Lǐ Shǒuzhēn, Zhāng Yànzé, and others led their twenty myriad troops to surrender.
The Emperor, followed by tens of thousands of cavalry,
approached a large hill,
and received their surrender while seated upon his horse.
He appointed Dù Chóngwēi as acting Grand Mentor (Shǒu Tàifù) and Resident Governor of Yèdū,
Lǐ Shǒuzhēn as Jìedùshǐ of Tīnpíng Jūn,
while the rest retained their former posts.
Half of the surrendered soldiers were handed over to Chóngwēi,
and the other half assigned to Zhào Yánshòu.
He commanded Xièlǐ, the Grandee Secretary (Yùshǐ Dàfū), Fù Guì'ér, the Army Inspector (Jiānjūn)
and Zhāng Yànzé to take an imperial edict into Biàn
to instruct the mother of the Jìn Emperor, Lǐ Shì,
to put her mind at ease,
and also to summon Sāng Wéihàn and Jǐng Yánguǎng to come first.
A thousand cavalry troops were left to guard Wèi,
while the Emperor himself led the main army south.
On the day Rénshēn,
Xièlǐ and the others arrived at Biàn.
Jìn Emperor Chóngguì, dressed in mourning clothes, bowed to receive the order,
and carried his mother, Lǐ Shì, to present a memorial requesting punishment.
Initially,
Chóngguì had severed peaceful relations.
Wéihàn repeatedly advised him to stop,
but he did not listen.
When the delegation arrived, Yànzé killed Wéihàn,
and fabricated a story that he had hanged himself.
An imperial edict ordered that Wéihàn be collected and buried,
his fields, gardens, and residence restored,
and his family was generously comforted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Yànzé moved Chóngguì, his mother, and his wife to the Kāifēng Fǔ Office,
and ordered Lǐ Róng, the Commander of the Crane-Controlling Guard (Kònghè Zhǐhuīshǐ), to supervise troops to guard them.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor arrived at Chìgāng.
Chóngguì led his whole family out of Fēngqiūmén,
bound with ropes and leading sheep, waiting (to surrender).
The Emperor could not bear to look upon them,
and ordered them moved to the Fēngchán Sì monastery.
The Jìn officials wore white robes and black gauze caps,
bowing low to await punishment.
The Emperor said:
“Their lord betrayed the trust;
what crime have the ministers committed?”
He ordered them to keep their posts as before,
and immediately appointed Ān Shūqiān as General-in-Chief of the Metropolitan Guard (Jīnwǔ Wèi Shàngjiāngjūn).
Shūqiān stepped out of the ranks and stood alone.
The Emperor said:
“Your request concerning Xíngzhōu
is something We have not forgotten.”
He then promoted him to Jìedùshǐ of Zhènguó Jūn.
This was because he had secretly requested to defect while he was in Xíngzhōu.
General Kāng Xiáng seized Jǐng Yánguǎng and presented him.
An edict listed his crimes using ivory tallies—
there were eight in all.
He was bound and sent to the capital,
but committed suicide on the road.
Dàtóng first year, spring, the first month, on the first day of the month, Dīnghài,
the Emperor entered Biàn with the full imperial carriage procession (fǎjià),
and ascended the Chóngyuán Diàn to receive congratulations from all the officials.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Liú Mǐn, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was granted provisional authority over the Kāifēng Fǔ.
Qín Jìmín, Lǐ Yànshēn, and Yáng Chéngxūn, the Defense Commissioner of Zhèngzhōu, were executed,
while Yáng Chéngxūn’s younger brother, Chéngxìn, was made Jìedùshǐ of Pínglú Jūn
and inherited his father’s title.
Originally,
when Yáng Guāngyuǎn was in Qīngzhōu, he sought to defect;
however, his son Chéngxūn did not comply,
killing his aide Qiū Tāo and his younger brother Chéngzuò, and instead submitted to the Jìn.
This is why he was executed.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
because Zhāng Yànzé had arbitrarily moved Chóngguì to Kāifēng,
killed Sāng Wéihàn,
and let his troops loose to engage in major looting,
acting wickedly,
he was executed in the marketplace.
The Jìn people chopped up his flesh and ate it.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Chóngguì was demoted to Chónglù Dàfū,
Jiǎnjiào Tàiwèi,
and sealed as the Marquis of Faithlessness (Fùyì Hóu).
On the day Guǐsì,
Zhāng Lì was made Píngzhāng Shì,
Lǐ Sōng of Jìn was made Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Shǐ),
Féng Dào was made Grand Mentor (Tàifù),
Hé Níng was made Academician of the Hanlin Academy,
Zhào Yíng was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo),
Liú Xù was made Defender Grand Mentor (Shǒu Tàibǎo),
and Féng Yù was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo).
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhào Yíng, Féng Yù, and Lǐ Yàntāo were dispatched with three hundred cavalry to escort the Marquis of Faithlessness, his mother Lǐ Shì, his concubine Ān Shì,
his wife Féng Shì, his younger brother Chóngruì, and his sons Yánxù and Yánbǎo, to be settled at Huánglóng Fǔ.

They were accompanied by fifty palace maids, three eunuchs, fifty men from the Eastern and Western Ranks, one medical officer, four Crane-Controlling Guards, seven cooks, three members of the Tea and Wine Directorate, three ceremonial officers, and ten strong soldiers.
established the state title Dà Liáo,
granted a great amnesty,
and changed the era name to Dàtóng.
Zhènzhōu was raised to the status of Zhōngjīng (Central Capital).

Zhào Yánshòu was appointed Grand Chancellor (*Dà Chéngxiàng*) concurrently holding the posts of Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Zhèngshì Lìng*), Commissioner of Military Affairs (*Shūmì Shǐ*), and Zhōngjīng Resident Administrator (*Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu*).
Civilian and military officials and soldiers, both domestic and foreign, received graded ranks and rewards.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Liú Zhīyuǎn, the Military Governor (*Jiédùshǐ*) of Hédōng and Prince of Běipíng, proclaimed himself emperor,
with the state title Hàn.
An imperial decree appointed Gěng Chóngměi as Military Governor of Zhāoyì Command,
Gāo Tángyīng as Military Governor of Zhāodé Command,
Cuī Tíngxūn as Military Governor of Héyáng Command,
to severally hold key strategic points.
The third month, *bǐngxū* day, the new moon,
Xiāo Hàn was appointed Military Governor of Xuānwǔ Command,
and generals and officials were given graded ranks and rewards.
On the *rényín* day,

the officials and clerks of the various governmental offices of Jìn, the imperial consorts, the eunuchs, practitioners of arts and techniques, various craftsmen, maps and documents, astronomical instruments, stone classics (*shíjīng*), bronze statues (*tóngrén*), the clepsydra (water clock) of the Míngtáng, the music scores of the Grand Master of Ceremonies (*Tàicháng*), the various court musical instruments, the imperial honor guard paraphernalia, ritual objects, and armor and weaponry,
were all sent to Shàngjīng (Supreme Capital).
Liáng Huī, the commander of Cízhōu, surrendered Xiāngzhōu to Hàn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Gāo Tángyīng was ordered to suppress him.
Summer, the fourth month, *bǐngchén* day, the new moon,
[The Emperor] departed from Biànzhōu,
with Féng Dào, Lǐ Sōng, Hé Níng, Lǐ Hàn, Xú Táifú, Zhāng Lì, and others accompanying him.
Upon reaching Chìgāng,
that night there was a sound like thunder,
originating near the imperial tent,
and a great star again fell in front of the banners and drums.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
crossing the ferry at Líyáng,
the Emperor looked back and said to his attendant ministers:
"I have committed three errors on this expedition: allowing the troops to plunder fodder and grain,
is the first;
seizing the private property of the people,
is the second;
and not promptly dispatching the various military governors back to their commands,
is the third."
The Imperial Younger Brother (*Huáng Tàidì*) sent an envoy to inquire about matters at the front.
The Emperor replied:
"Initially, with two hundred thousand troops, we compelled Dù Chóngwēi and Zhāng Yànzé to surrender,
and pacified Zhènzhōu.
When we entered Biàn,
looking at the officials who filled the established posts, we eliminated those [unfit],
and appointed those who were suited by their talent.
Although the infrastructure of the departments remains,
the officials have become negligent and decadent,
like after the fledglings have flown away,
leaving only an empty nest.
Having long endured separation and upheaval,
things have reached this state.
Bandits are gathered everywhere,
corvée labor does not cease,
and provisions are not delivered on time,
the people cannot bear their lot.
Hédōng has not yet submitted its allegiance,
and the chieftains along the western route are also banding together.
Reflecting day and night,
the methods to control this [situation],
are only three: sharing sincerity with the various officials, harmonizing the military sentiment, and pacifying the common people.
Currently, seventy-six areas have submitted,
gaining 1,090,118 households.
Were it not for the scorching heat in Biànzhōu,
and the climate being difficult to inhabit,
staying for just one year,
Great Peace could be achieved easily (as if pointing to the palm of one's hand).
Furthermore, Zhènzhōu was renamed Zhōngjīng,
in preparation for imperial tours.
The desire to attack Hédōng
awaits a separate plan.
This is the general outline."
On the *wùchén* day,
upon reaching Gāoyì,
he became unwell.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
he passed away at Luánchéng,
aged forty-six.
In the ninth month of that year, *rénzǐ* day, the new moon,
he was buried at Fèngshān,
his mausoleum was called Huáilíng,
and his temple name was Tàizōng.
In the seventh month of Tǒnghé 26 (1008 CE),
the honorific posthumous title Xiàowǔ Huángdì (Filial and Martial Emperor) was conferred.
In the ninth month of Chóngxī 21 (1052 CE),
this was augmented to Xiàowǔ Huìwén Huángdì (Filial, Martial, Benevolent, and Cultured Emperor).
Eulogy: Tàizōng had just stabilized the many regions,
and those near and far submitted to his influence.
He established the state title,
instituted protocols and regulations,
and rectified common governmental affairs,
examined titles against reality,
recorded prisoners,
taught farming and weaving,
and matched the widowed and the solitary.
He sought officials who would speak frankly,
and upon obtaining Lángjūn Hǎisī, he immediately promoted him to Commissioner of Court Affairs (*Xuānhuī*).
He commended Zhāng Jìngdá of Táng for his loyalty to his lord,
and finally buried him with full rites.
He abandoned his relaxed tours and accepted the plea concerning the "three restraints."
He pitied the officers and soldiers and issued an order for rest and recuperation.
Personally campaigning against the state of Jìn,
Chóngguì surrendered bound.
This can be called having both wide-reaching majesty and virtue,
and brilliant strategies appearing intermittently.
After entering Biàn,
he showed no hint of arrogance,
and provided the instruction regarding the
"three errors."
Tradition praises the Earl of Zhèng for handling victory well,
and the *Shū* (Classic of History) praises the *Qín Shì* (Oath of Qín) for admitting mistakes;
Tàizōng truly possessed both traits,
how outstanding he was!
Annals, Chapter 5: Shìzōng
Shìzōng, the Xiàohé Zhuāngxiàn Huángdì (Filial, Harmonious, Solemn, and Sagacious Emperor),
personal name Ruǎn,
courtesy name Wùyù.
He was the eldest son of the Ràngguó Huángdì (Emperor who Yielded the State),
and his mother was Empress Ròuzhēn, née Xiāo.
The Emperor was grand and imposing in appearance,
lenient internally and strict externally,
skilled in riding and archery,
fond of giving,
and the people looked up to him.
Tàizōng loved him as a son.
In the ninth year of Huìtóng (946 CE),
he followed [the Emperor] on the campaign against Jìn.
In the spring, second month, of Dàtóng 1 (947 CE),
he was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yǒngkāng.
Summer, the fourth month, *dīngchǒu* day,
Tàizōng passed away at Luánchéng.
On the *wùyín* day,
when the imperial coffin reached Zhènyáng,
he ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
upon reaching Dìngzhōu,
he ordered Tiāndé, Shuògǔ, Xièlǐ, and others to escort the imperial coffin ahead to Shàngjīng.
The Empress Dowager (*Tàihòu*) heard that the Emperor had ascended the throne,
and sent the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú to lead troops to oppose him.
The sixth month, *jiǎyín* day, the new moon,
upon reaching Nánjīng (Southern Capital),
the *Yílíjǐn* of the Five Courts Ānduān and the *Xiángwěn* Liúgē dispatched a rider to report,
requesting to serve as the vanguard;
upon arriving at Tàidé Quán,
they encountered Lǐ Hú’s army,
and defeated them in battle.
The Emperor sent Lángjūn Qíndé and others to both armies to convey a message of reconciliation.
Autumn, intercalary seventh month,
upon reaching the Huáng Hé,
the Empress Dowager and Lǐ Hú marshaled their troops to resist at Hèngdù,
resulting in a standoff for several days.
Following Wūzhì’s plan,
they both disbanded their forces and hastened to Shàngjīng.
Soon after, having heard that the Empress Dowager and Lǐ Hú again harbored rebellious intentions,
they were moved to Zǔzhōu;
the Minister of Education (*Sītú*) Huàshè and Chǔbǔlǐ were executed.
The eighth month, *rénwǔ* day, the new moon,
his mother, Lady Xiāo, was honored as Empress Dowager (*Huáng Tàihòu*).
The Empress Dowager’s clan, the Cìjǐ Sàgǔlǔ, was made the Imperial Maternal Uncles Tribe (*Guójìu Zhàng*),
and a *Xiángwěn* was appointed to oversee it.
Households of the Chóngdé Palace were distributed among the meritorious officials who supported the Emperor,
including fifty [households] each to Wā, the Grand King of the Northern Court (*Běiyuàn Dàwáng*), and Hǒu, the Grand King of the Southern Court (*Nányuàn Dàwáng*),
and one hundred each to Ān Tuán and Chǔ Bǔ.
The descendants of Dírǔ and Tiělà who had previously been enslaved and had their property confiscated for no fault of their own were restored.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the post of Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Court (*Běiyuàn Shūmì Shǐ*) was established for the first time,
and Ān Tuán was appointed to it.
The ninth month, *rénzǐ* day, the new moon,
the Emperor Sìshèng (Successor to the Sage) was buried at Huáilíng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Cháicè rite was performed,
and the assembled officials conferred the honorific title Tiānshòu Huángdì (Heaven-Granted Emperor).
A great amnesty was granted,
and Dàtóng 1 was changed to Tiānlù 1.
His deceased father was posthumously titled Ràngguó Huángdì (Emperor who Yielded the State).
Ānduān was put in charge of the state of Dōngdān,
and enfeoffed as the Prince of Míng.
Chágē was made Prince of Tàiníng,
Liúgē was made *Tìyǐn*,
and Gāo Xūn was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Court (*Nányuàn Shūmì Shǐ*).
In the second year (948 CE), spring, the first month,
Tiāndé, Xiāo Hàn, Liúgē, Péndū, and others plotted rebellion.
Tiāndé was executed,
Xiāo Hàn was flogged,
Liúgē was exiled to the border,
and Péndū was punished by being sent on a mission to the Xiágāsī state.
Liú Zhīyuǎn, the ruler of Hàn, died,
and his son Chéngyòu was enthroned.
Summer, the fourth month, *gēngchén* day, the new moon,
Nán Táng sent Lǐ Lǎng and Wáng Zuò to offer condolences and congratulations,
and also delivered a sealed wax pellet message,
proposing a discussion to attack Hàn.
Autumn, the seventh month, *rénshēn* day,
the Imperial Prince Xián was born.
Winter, the tenth month, *rénwǔ* day,
Zhào Yánshòu, the Prince of Wèi and Resident Administrator of Nánjīng, passed away.
Dié Lù, the Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat (*Zhōngtái Shěng Yòuxiàng*), was appointed Resident Administrator of Nánjīng,
and enfeoffed as the Prince of Yān.
In the eleventh month,
the imperial retinue halted south of Zhāngwǔ.
In the third year, spring, the first month,
Xiāo Hàn and Princess Ābùlǐ plotted rebellion.
Hàn was executed,
and Ābùlǐ died of disease in prison.
