On the day Gēngshēn,
a general amnesty was issued.
Officials both inside and outside the court were each promoted one rank.
Summer, the sixth month, on the day Wùyín,
Chàngshǐ Yēlǜ Húlízhěn was appointed King of the Northern Chancellery (Běi Yuàn Dàwáng).
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Tìyǐn Tuíyù was enfeoffed as Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery (Qīshuǐ Jùnwáng).
Autumn, the ninth month, on the first day Xīnchǒu,
the assembled officials were summoned to discuss the campaign against the south.
Winter, the tenth month,
generals were dispatched leading troops to attack and take Gāolǎozhèn in Bèizhōu,
securing the territories of Yèdū, Nángōng, and Tángyáng,
killing Shǐ Wànshān, the Prefect of Shēnzhōu,
and capturing a great number of people.
In the fourth year, spring, the second month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Cháge, the Prince of Tàiníng, came to court,
and was retained for service.
In this month,
the Department of State Affairs (Zhèngshì Shěng) was established.
The third month, on the first day Wùxū,
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) dispatched Zhào Yánsì and Zhāng Fú, among others, to congratulate on the victory of the Southern Campaign.
Autumn, the ninth month, on the first day Yǐchǒu,
went to Shānxī.
Winter, the tenth month,
the Emperor personally led the campaign against the south,
attacking and taking the cities of Ānpíng, Nèiqiū, and Shùlù, among others,
and returning with great spoils.
In this year,
Empress Xiāo was formally invested.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the first day Guǐhài,
went to Bǎiquán Hú.
Guō Wēi of Hàn assassinated his ruler and established himself,
naming the state Zhōu,
and dispatched Zhū Xiàn to announce this.
An envoy was immediately dispatched carrying excellent horses.
Liú Chóng of Hàn established himself at Tàiyuán.
The second month,
Zhōu dispatched Yáo Hànyīng and Huá Zhāoyìn to come.
Their letter used defiant language regarding protocol,
so Hànyīng and the others were detained.
Summer, the fifth month, on the first day Rénxū,
Zhào Yíng, the Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, died.
Court was suspended for one day,
and an order was given for him to be buried in Biàn.
An imperial edict ordered that the Lùshì Cānjūn and Zhǔbù of prefectures and counties
be assigned positions by the Department of State Affairs (Zhèngshì Shěng).
The sixth month, on the first day Xīnmǎo,
Liú Chóng, being attacked by Zhōu,
dispatched an envoy calling himself 'nephew,'
begging for aid,
and further requesting formal enfeoffment.
Yàn Wáng Dié*** and Privy Council Commissioner (Shūmìshǐ) Gāo Xūn were immediately dispatched to formally invest him as the Shénwǔ Emperor of Great Hàn (Dà Hàn Shénwǔ Huángdì).
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) dispatched Jiǎng Hóng,
begging for the raising of troops for assistance.
In this summer,
the Emperor avoided the heat at Bǎiquán Lǐng.
The ninth month, on the first day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor personally led the campaign against the south.
On the day Rénxū,
the army halted at Xiánggǔ Shān in Guīhuà Zhōu.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Yànguó Huángdì (Emperor Who Relinquished the Throne) was sacrificed to at the temporary palace.
The assembled officials were all intoxicated,
and Cháge rebelled.
The Emperor was assassinated,
at the age of thirty-four.
In the first year of Yìnglì,
he was buried on the Western Mountain of Xiǎnzhōu,
the mausoleum being named Xiǎnlíng.
In the second year,
his posthumous title was Emperor Xiàohé,
and his temple name was Shìzōng.
In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year of Tǒnghé,
the posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Xiàohé Zhuāngxiàn.
The Eulogy says: Shìzōng
was a ruler of average talent.
He entered to succeed the great lineage,
but had not yet reigned for three years.
Upon receiving the wax-sealed letter from Táng,
he immediately discussed campaigning against the south.
As he lacked prudence,
it was inevitable that he neglected comprehensive defense.
This indeed led to disaster.
Nevertheless, he was filial, friendly, lenient, and compassionate,
and possessed the bearing of a sovereign.
Before the army could return,
the tragedy arose from his excessive drinking.
How could this not be lamented!
Annals, Volume Six: Mùzōng I
Mùzōng, Emperor Xiào'ān Jìngzhèng,
personal name Jǐng,
courtesy name Shùlǜ.
He was the eldest son of Emperor Tàizōng,
his mother being Empress Jìng'ān Xiāo.
In the second year of Huìtóng,
he was enfeoffed as the Prince of Shòu'ān.
In the fifth year of Tiānlù, autumn, the ninth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Shìzōng was murdered.
The rebellious subject Cháge and others were executed.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
he immediately ascended the imperial throne.
The assembled officials presented the honorific title Emperor Tiānshùn,
and the era name was changed to Yìnglì.
On the day Wùchén,
went to Nánjīng (Southern Capital).
In this month,
Liú Chéngxùn was dispatched to announce the mourning to Hàn.
Winter, the eleventh month,
Hàn, Zhōu, and Southern Táng (Nán Táng) each dispatched envoys to offer condolences.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered that court assemblies follow the precedents of the Sìshèng Huángdì,
using Hàn rites.
The twelfth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Hàn dispatched an envoy to present bows, arrows, saddles, and horses.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Tiělí and Bígǔdé both came to offer tribute.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) dispatched an envoy presenting a wax-sealed letter,
and submitting rhinoceros and water-buffalo leather armor, ten thousand suits in total.
On the day Rénxū,
Hūgǔzhì, the Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), plotted rebellion,
and was executed.
The second month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Nǚzhí came to offer tribute.
The third month, on the day Guǐhài,
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) dispatched an envoy presenting a wax-sealed letter.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
another envoy was dispatched to offer tribute.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Yēlǜ Tàliè was appointed King of the Southern Chancellery (Nán Yuàn Dàwáng).
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day Bǐngxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐhài,
Tiělí presented eagles and falcons.
The fifth month, on the first day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor held court.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Southern Táng (Nán Táng) dispatched an envoy to offer tribute.
The sixth month, on the day Rénchén,
Guójiù and State Affairs Commissioner (Zhèngshì Lìng) Xiāo Méigǔdé,
and Lǐ Hǎn, Scholar of Xuānzhèng Hall, among others, plotted to flee south.
When the affair was discovered,
an imperial edict exposed their crimes.
On the day Yǐwèi,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Rén yín,
Hàn, being invaded by Zhōu,
dispatched an envoy seeking aid.
An order was given for Gāo Móhàn, Right Chancellor of the Central Department, to proceed there.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Hélǔ, the elder brother of the Wet Nurse, was appointed hereditary Yílíjǐn of the Āsù Shíliè tribe.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
State Affairs Commissioner Lóu Guó, Línyá Díliè, Shìzhōng Shéndū, Lángjūn Hǎilǐ, and others plotted disorder and were apprehended.
The eighth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Méigǔdé, Lóu Guó, and others were executed,
and Lǐ Hǎn was flogged and then released.
The ninth month, on the first day Jiǎyín,
Yúnzhōu presented four stalks of auspicious grain,
with two heads (per stalk).
On the day Wùwǔ,
an edict ordered that on the day Cháge was first pacified,
Heaven should be sacrificed to using black and white sheep and black wine,
and this should become an annual custom.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor hunted at Tànshān.
Sacrifice was made to Heaven.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Díliè tribe came to offer tribute.
Winter, the tenth month, on the first day Jiǎshēn,
Hàn dispatched an envoy to present grape wine.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Sītú Lǎogǔ and others presented white pheasants.
On the day Wùshēn,
Huíghǔ and Xiágǎsī both dispatched envoys to offer tribute.
The eleventh month, on the first day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor held court.
On the day Jǐsì,
there was an earthquake.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the winter solstice occurred,
and for the first time, the old ritual of bowing to the sun was performed.
The people of Shuòzhōu presented a black rabbit.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi, the first day of the month,
Gāo Móhàn and his soldiers besieged Jìnzhōu.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
on account of the Emperor's birthday,
he fed monks
and released imprisoned criminals.
On the day Jiǎchén,
he hunted in the near suburbs.
He performed sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Xīnhài,
Míng Wáng Ānduān died.
In the third year, spring, intercalary first month, on the day Rénwǔ, the first day of the month,
Hàn, because Gāo Móhàn had repelled the Zhōu army,
sent an envoy to express thanks.
Second month, on the day Xīnhài, the first day of the month,
an edict ordered the use of the former seal of Sìshèng Huángdì.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Tàibǎo Dìliè repaired Yìzhōu city,
and Zhènzhōu sent troops to challenge him to battle,
but he repelled them.
Third month, on the day Gēngchén, the first day of the month,
Nán Táng sent an envoy to present tribute,
and incidentally attached a letter addressed to Hàn.
An edict ordered it to be delivered.
On the day Gēngyín,
he went to Yìngzhōu to play polo.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Hàn sent an envoy to present a polo shirt and horses.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
he watched fishing at Shéndé Hú.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Tiělí came to present tribute.
Fifth month, on the day Rén'yín,
Hàn sent an envoy who reported that the monument erected by Shíjìn to the Sacred Virtue and Divine Merit of the former Emperor had been destroyed by the Zhōu people,
and requested that it be re-engraved.
This was permitted.
Sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Yìngtiān Huáng Tàihòu died.
Autumn, seventh month,
the Emperor did not hold court.
Eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
on account of his birthday,
prisoners were released.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Hàn sent an envoy to request aid.
The Sānhé Wūgǔ, Tǔfān, Tǔyùhún, and Bígǔdé all sent envoys to present tribute.
Ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Hàn sent an envoy to present medicine.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Tàishī Tánggǔdé was ordered to manage the imperial mausoleum of the late Huáng Tàihòu.
Lǐ Húzi Wǎn, Lángjūn Jī Gàn, and Dìliè plotted rebellion.
When the matter was discovered,
their testimony implicated Tàipíng Wáng Yǎnsāgě, Línyá Huágē, and Lángjūn Xīnluó, among others.
They were all arrested.
Eleventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Huáng Tàihòu was given the posthumous title Zhēnliè,
and was buried in Zǔlíng.
Hàn sent an envoy to attend the ceremony.
That winter,
the Emperor stayed temporarily in Fèngshèng Zhōu.
Because of flooding in Nánjīng,
an edict remitted this year's rent/tax.
Fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Wùyín,
Huíhú came to present tribute.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Huágē, Jī Gàn, and others were executed.
Wǎn and Yǎnsāgě were both released.
That month,
the sovereign of Zhōu, Wēi, passed away,
and his adopted son Jìn Wáng Chái Róng succeeded him.
Second month, on the day Bǐngwǔ, the first day of the month,
Zhōu attacked Hàn.
Zhèngshì Lìng Yēlǜ Dílù was ordered to aid them.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Hàn sent an envoy to present tea and medicine.
The Emperor visited Nánjīng.
Summer, fifth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Xīn and Dài commanderies rebelled against Hàn.
Nányuàn Dàwáng Tàliè was sent to assist Dílù in suppressing them.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Tàliè defeated the Zhōu general Fú Yànqīng at Xīnkǒu.
Sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Tàliè presented the spoils captured.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Hàn citizens who had been mistakenly captured by the Liáo army
sent an envoy to request their return.
An edict ordered that they all be released.
Ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Hàn, being invaded by the Zhōu people,
sent an envoy to report this.
Winter, eleventh month,
Zhāngguó Jūn Jiédùshǐ Xiāo Díliè and Dàbǎo Xǔ Cóngyūn reported the victory at Xīn and Dài commanderies.
Twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu, the first day of the month,
the Emperor visited Zǔlíng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Hàn sent an envoy to present tribute.
That winter,
the Emperor stayed temporarily at Xìngguō.
Fifth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnwèi, the first day of the month,
Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
Second month, on the day Gēngzǐ, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Hàn sent an envoy to request the bestowal of an honorific title
upon the Emperor, but this was not permitted.
On the day Rénxū,
he went to Niǎotán.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Zhōu invaded Hàn,
and Hàn sent an envoy to request aid.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Lángjūn Xiāo Hǎilì was ordered to serve as the Northern Chancellor (Běi Fǔ Zǎixiàng) hereditarily.
Autumn, ninth month, on the day Gēngchén,
the sovereign of Hàn was ill,
and sent an envoy to report this.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Nǚzhí came to present tribute.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor visited the temple of Tàizōng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Nán Táng sent an envoy to present tribute.
Eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi, the first day of the month,
the sovereign of Hàn, Chóng, passed away.
His son Chéngjūn sent an envoy to report this,
and also requested succession.
An envoy was dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices,
and subsequently, he was invested and granted credentials.
Twelfth month, on the day Yǐchǒu, the first day of the month,
the Emperor visited the temple of Tàizǔ.
On the day Xīnsì,
Hàn sent an envoy to discuss military affairs.
Sixth year, summer, fifth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor visited Huáilíng.
Sixth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Hàn sent an envoy to discuss military affairs.
Autumn, seventh month,
the Emperor did not hold court.
Ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor visited Zǔlíng.
Winter, eleventh month, on the day Rén'yín,
Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
Twelfth month, on the day Jǐwèi, the first day of the month,
the Emperor visited the temple of Tàizǔ.
Seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
Second month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Nán Táng sent an envoy bearing a letter written on a wax pellet.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor stayed temporarily at Huáng Hé.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Wùwǔ, the first day of the month,
the Emperor returned to Shàngjīng.
Previously,
the sorceress Xiāo Gǔ presented a prescription for an elixir of longevity,
which required using the gall bladders of men as an ingredient.
In just a few years,
many people were killed.
By this time,
the Emperor realized her deceit.
On the day Xīnsì,
she was shot and killed.
Fifth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Hàn sent an envoy to present tribute.
Sixth month, on the day Bǐngchén, the first day of the month,
Zhōu sent an envoy to offer greetings.
Nán Táng sent an envoy to present tribute.
Eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Zhōu sent an envoy to offer greetings.
That autumn,
the Emperor did not attend to governmental affairs.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor hunted at Qī Yīng Shān.
Twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor issued an edict to his ministers, saying:
“When one is guilty,
the law dictates punishment.
If I happen to unleash my anger
and unjustly harm the innocent,
you, my ministers, must remonstrate urgently,
and must not merely obey outwardly.”
On the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor returned to Shàngjīng.
Eighth year, spring, second month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor stayed temporarily at Huáng Hé.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Nánjīng Liúshǒu Xiāo Sīwēn attacked and captured the border prefectures and districts.
An envoy was sent to commend him.
Fifth month,
Zhōu captured Shùchéng Xiàn.
Sixth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Xiāo Sīwēn requested additional troops
and implored the Emperor to visit Yān (Yān capital region).
Autumn, seventh month,
the Emperor hunted at Zhuàilá Shān.
Until the ninth month,
he hunted deer in various mountains
and did not hold court.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Hǎn (Later Hàn) sent an envoy to report that Zhōu (Later Zhōu) had invaded again.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the envoy arrived a second time.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
he arrived again.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month, on the *wùchén* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at the Huánghé (River).
Summer, the fourth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhōu invaded.
On the *wùxū* day,
Xiāo Sīwēn (蕭思溫), the Resident General of Nánjīng, was made General Commandant of Troops and Horses (*Bīngmǎ Dū Zǒngguǎn*) to attack them.
In this month,
Zhōu captured the three passes of Yìjīn, Wǎqiáo, and Yūkǒu.
The fifth month, on the first day (*shuò*) *yǐsì*,
Yíng and Mò two prefectures were lost.
On the *guǐhài* day,
went to Nánjīng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Zhōu troops retreated.
The sixth month, on the first day *yǐhài*,
held court.
On the *wùyín* day,
Róngchéng County was restored.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
traveled west,
going to Huáizhōu.
In this month,
Zhōu Lord Róng (*Zhōu Zhǔ Róng*) passed away,
and his son Zōngxùn was enthroned.
Autumn, the seventh month,
troops from Nánjīng were dispatched to guard Fànyáng.
Winter, the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day,
returned to Shàngjīng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Prince Dǐliè (敵烈), former Commissioner of the Privy Council (*Xuānhuī Shǐ*) Hǎisī (海思), and Xiāo Dágan (蕭達干), among others, conspired in rebellion,
the matter was discovered,
and they were interrogated.
On the *xīnsì* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth and to the ancestors,
announcing the failure of the rebellious faction.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the assembled officials were summoned to discuss current affairs.
The tenth year, spring, the first month,
Zhào Kuāngyìn (趙匡胤), General Commandant of the Palace Guard (*Diànqián Dū Diǎnjiǎn*) of Zhōu, abolished Zhōu and established himself,
establishing the state name Sòng.
Summer, the fifth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
visited Huáilíng (Mausoleum).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Hàn reported that Lùzhōu had submitted and pledged allegiance.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
arrived back from Huáilíng.
The sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Hàn reported that Sòng troops were besieging Shízhōu,
and [we] dispatched Ālà (阿剌), the Military Governor (*Jiédù Shǐ*) of Dàtóng Army, leading four tribes to go and assist;
an edict ordered Xiāo Sīwēn (蕭思溫) to assist them with three tribes of soldiers.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day *jǐhài*,
Sòng troops captured Shízhōu,
and Lùzhōu rebelled again;
a Hàn envoy came to report this.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Shòuyuǎn (耶律壽遠), the Chancellor (*Zhèngshì Lìng*), and Chǔ'ē Bù (楚阿不), the Grand Guardian (*Tàibǎo*), among others, conspired in rebellion,
and were executed.
Used wine and dried meat to offer sacrifices to Heaven and Earth at Hēishān (Mountain).
The eighth month,
went to Qiūshān (Mountain),
and proceeded to Huáizhōu.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
used the stone *suānní* (lion-like creature) used for holding down cushions to beat and kill the close attendant Gǔgē.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hú’s (李胡) son Xǐyǐn (喜隱) conspired in rebellion,
and his testimony implicated Lǐ Hú,
who was imprisoned and died.
The eleventh month,
Hǎisī (海思) submitted a memorial from prison,
detailing beneficial policies.
The eleventh year, spring, the second month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Xǐyǐn was released.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Diélàgē (迭剌哥), the son of the Minister of the Masses (*Sītú*) Wūlǐzhī (烏里只), falsely accused his father of plotting rebellion,
and furthermore, fraudulently used the relay service and killed a traveler;
based on his father's request [for clemency],
he was beaten with a rod and released.
The third month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Xiāo Sīwēn (蕭思溫) memorialized that the Star of Longevity (*Lǎorén Xīng*) had appeared,
petitioning for a general pardon.
Intercalary month, on the first day *jiǎzǐ*,
went to the Huánghé (River).
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day *guǐsì*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In this month,
shot deer,
and did not hold court.
The fifth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Wáng Bái (王白) and Lǐ Zhèng (李正), the Astronomers Royal (*Sī Tiān*), presented the calendar.
The sixth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
issued a pardon.
Winter, the eleventh month,
the Jupiter star (*Suì Xīng*) encroached upon the moon.
The twelfth year, spring, the first month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
viewed lanterns at night.
The second month, on the first day *jǐchǒu*,
appointed Xiāo Hùsī (蕭護思), the Censor-in-Chief (*Yùshǐ Dàfū*), as Commissioner of the Northern Chancellery (*Běiyuàn Shūmì Shǐ*),
and bestowed upon him official court robes, saddle, and horse.
Summer, the fifth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
due to the drought,
ordered the attendants to splash water on each other;
soon after,
it indeed rained.
The sixth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
offered sacrifices at Mùyèshān (Mountain) and the Huánghé (River).
Autumn,
went to Hēishān and Chìshān to shoot deer.
The thirteenth year, spring, the first month,
starting from the *dīngsì* day,
drank heavily day and night for nine days.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Sòng intended to build fortifications at Yìjīn Pass,
ordered Gāo Xūn (高勳), the Resident General of Nánjīng, and Cuī Tíngxūn (崔廷勳), the Commandant of Troops (*Tǒngjūn Shǐ*), to harass them with soldiers.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
killed the gamekeeper Hǎilǐ.
The second month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Hàn sent an envoy to report,
that they wished to patrol the border territory,
and requested military support to create a show of force.
On the *rénchén* day,
went to the Huánghé (River).
On the *guǐsì* day,
observed the assembled officials shooting,
and bestowed gifts according to rank.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Star of Longevity appeared.
The third month, on the first day *guǐchǒu*,
killed the deer-keeper Mílǐjí,
and displayed his head to those in charge of the deer.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *rényín* day,
hunted at the Huánghé (River).
The fifth month, on the *rénxū* day,
viewed the spotted deer presented by the Kingdom of Wòlǎnggǎi (斡朗改) which had given birth to a fawn.
The sixth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
a close attendant injured a roe deer,
and was beaten to death with a rod.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
killed Xiámǎ (霞馬), the roe deer-keeper.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered all circuits to review prisoners.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day *xīnhài*,
Hàn reported that Sòng was invading.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
seasonal foods were offered at the temple.
The eighth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
it being his birthday,
released the hawks and falcons of the Five Stables.
On the *wùxū* day,
visited a nearby mountain,
called deer and shot them,
returning only after seventeen days.
The ninth month, on the first day *gēngxū*,
used a black ox and a white horse to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
Drank heavily at the temporary camp,
not stopping until the end of the night.
On the *xīnhài* day,
used wine and dried meat to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth,
and again drank heavily through the entire night.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Hàn reported that Sòng was invading.
The eleventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
hunted,
and drank at the hunter’s house,
for a total of four days.
The twelfth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
shot wild deer,
and bestowed gifts upon the hunters according to rank.
On the *gēngyín* day,
killed Hézhǔ (曷主), the swineherd.
Basic Annals 7: Mùzōng (Part 2)
The fourteenth year, spring, the first month, on the first day *wùyín*,
ritually installed the Spirit Banner (*Shéndú*).
On the *wùxū* day,
Hàn quickly reported that a Sòng general was coming to attack.
(Reported immediately.)
The second month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict ordered Tàliè (撻烈), the Commissioner of Pacification for the Southwest (*Xīnán Miàn Zhāotǎo Shǐ*), to advance troops to assist Hàn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
went to the Huánghé (River).
On the *wùchén* day,
dismembered seven deer-keepers, including Mòdá (沒答) and Hǎilǐ (海里), in the field,
piled up earth to mark the spot.
On the *jǐsì* day,
went to Lǎolíndōngluò.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Hàn sent an envoy to report that Sòng troops had been defeated at Shízhōu.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Hàn, having repelled the Sòng army,
sent an envoy to offer thanks.
In this month,
sweet dew (*gānlù*) fell in Huánglóng Fǔ.
In the fifth month,
hunting deer at Bái Yīng Shān,
lasting until the end of the ten-day period.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐng wǔ* day, the first day of the month,
hunting at Yù Shān,
remaining there the entire month and forgetting to return.
In Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rén chén* day,
sacrifices were offered to Hēi Shān with wine and dried meat.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐ sì* day,
went to Wèizi Lǐng,
called deer and shot them,
obtaining four deer.
The forest official (Yúrén) Nǚ Guī and others were given various gifts according to rank.
On the *dīng wèi* day,
returned to the palace.
On the *wù shēn* day,
because the emperor's birthday coincided with the Great Amnesty (Tiān Shè),
he did not receive congratulations,
but granted a partial amnesty to the prisoners in the capital (Jīng Shī).
On the *yǐ mǎo* day,
inspected the prisoners.
In the ninth month,
the Huáng Shìwěi rebelled.
In Winter, the tenth month, on the *bǐng wǔ* day,
the attendant Wū Gǔ Zhě presented a whetstone,
and was rewarded with 250 *liǎng* of silver.
On the *bǐng chén* day,
Zhǎng Lù Shěn Sī replaced Wò Lǐ as Zhásà Huán.
He was given a gold belt, a gold cup,
and 200 *liǎng* of silver.
Those under his jurisdiction, up to and including those sentenced to death, fell under his exclusive authority.
The eleventh month, on the *rén wǔ* day,
the winter solstice occurred.
Feasting and drinking lasted until dawn.
From this time on, he slept during the day and drank at night.
The attendant Xiǎo Liù was killed within the Forbidden Precincts.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐng wǔ* day,
a black rabbit was used to sacrifice to the gods.
Wū Gǔ rebelled,
plundering the people's wealth and livestock.
The Xiāngwěn, Sēng Yǐn, fought with them,
suffered a great defeat.
Sēng Yǐn, Yǐ Shí, and others died in the battle.
In the fifteenth year, Spring, the first month, on the *jǐ mǎo* day,
the Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Shǐ), Yǎ Lǐ Sī, was appointed Acting Commander-in-Chief (Xíngjūn Dūtǒng),
and the Hǔ Jūn Xiāngwěn, Chǔ Sī, was appointed Acting Military Supervisor (Xíngjūn Dūjiān).
Three hundred additional troops from the Tū Lǚ Bù tribe were added,
combining forces from various tribes to suppress the rebellion.
Bólè Dǐ, the son of Wū Gǔ Yílí Jǐn, alone did not rebel.
An imperial edict was issued to praise him.
In this month,
the star of the Elder was visible.
The second month, on the *rén yín* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Emperor proceeded east.
On the *jiǎ yín* day,
because ducks were caught,
the punishments of tattooing the face and cutting in half at the waist for those in the Eagle Bureau (Yīng Fáng) were abolished,
and their labor service was restored.
In this month,
Wū Gǔ killed their chief Sū Lí Dǐ.
The remaining multitude surrendered,
but rebelled again.
The third month, on the *guǐ yǒu* day,
the attendant Dōng'ér presented the spoon and chopsticks late.
The Emperor stabbed him personally with a blade.
On the *dīng chǒu* day,
Yín Ní Jí, the chieftain of the Dà Huáng Shìwěi, rebelled.
On the *guǐ wèi* day,
forty households of the Wǔ Fáng personnel rebelled and joined Wū Gǔ.
On the *guǐ sì* day,
the forest official Shā Là Dié failed to report on time after scouting geese,
and was subjected to the punishments of burning and iron combing, and died.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐ sì* day,
the Xiǎo Huáng Shìwěi rebelled.
Yǎ Lǐ Sī, Chǔ Sī, and others attacked them,
but were defeated by the Shìwěi.
Envoys were dispatched to interrogate them.
On the *yǐ mǎo* day,
Tū Lǐ replaced Yǎ Lǐ Sī as Commander-in-Chief,
and Nǚ Gǔ was appointed Supervising General.
They led light cavalry to advance and suppress the rebels.
Tà Mǎ Xún Jí Lǐ was also ordered to carry an imperial edict to persuade and placate them.
The fifth month, on the *rén shēn* day,
Xún Jí Lǐ reported in a memorial,
that the rebels refused to follow the injunctions.
Yǎ Lǐ Sī used the pastoral troops of the Tà Lǐn and Sū districts to pursue the rebels to the Chái Hé,
but was unsuccessful in battle.
On the *jiǎ shēn* day,
Kù Gǔ Zhǐ reported in a memorial that Yín Ní Jí, the Shìwěi chief, had fled and entered Dí Liè territory.
The sixth month, on the *xīn hài* day,
Yú Lǔ Gǔ presented fine horses,
and was rewarded with 2,000 *liǎng* of silver.
The attendant Hū Là Bǐ Mǎ Zhì was the first to report this,
and was rewarded with 1,000 *liǎng* of silver.
In this month,
Dí Liè came and surrendered.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎ xū* day,
Yǎ Lǐ Sī reported that Wū Gǔ had reached Héidé Luò.
The Yílí Jǐn Huà Lǐ and the Yílí Bì Cháng Sī were dispatched to attack them.
On the *dīng chǒu* day,
Wū Gǔ plundered the residents of Yúlín Yù, north of Shàngjīng.
The Chancellor (Línyá) Xiāo Gān was dispatched to suppress them.
On the *gēng chén* day,
Yǎ Lǐ Sī and others fought Wū Gǔ,
but were unsuccessful.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *dīng wèi* day,
Cháng Sī fought Wū Gǔ,
and defeated them.
The twelfth month, on the *jiǎ chén* day,
because the attendant Xǐ Gē returned home privately,
his wife was killed.
On the *dīng wèi* day,
the attendant Suí Lǔ was killed.
The imperial traveling court stopped at Hēi Shān Píng Diàn.
In the sixteenth year, Spring, the first month, on the *dīng mǎo* day, the first day of the month,
being drunk,
the Emperor refused to receive congratulations.
On the *jiǎ shēn* day,
the Emperor traveled incognito through the marketplace,
and bestowed silver and silk upon wine sellers.
On the *yǐ yǒu* day,
the attendant Bái Hǎi was killed, along with the household servants Shān Fú and Yā Là Gě, the doorkeeper of the Commissioner of Military Affairs Lǎo Gǔ, and Tà Mǎ Shī Lǔ.
The third month, on the *jǐ sì* day,
the Emperor proceeded east.
On *gēng wǔ* day, ducks were caught.
On *jiǎ shēn* day, geese were caught.
In all cases, drinking lasted until dawn.
The fifth month, on the *jiǎ shēn* day,
due to the annual drought,
the Emperor went boating on the pond to pray for rain.
As it did not rain,
he abandoned the boat and stood in the water to pray.
After a short while, it rained.
The sixth month, on the *bǐng shēn* day,
believing that Bái Hǎi had died unjustly,
silver and silk were bestowed upon his family.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rén wǔ* day,
the Emperor issued an injunction to the relevant authorities: Wherever the imperial traveling court goes,
tall markers must be erected
to ensure the people do not trespass.
Violators shall be judged with death.
The eighth month, on the *dīng yǒu* day,
Hàn dispatched envoys to present golden vessels and armor as tribute.
The intercalary month, on the *yǐ chǒu* day,
the Emperor watched wild deer enter the tame deer herd,
and stood on his horse drinking until dusk.
The ninth month, on the *gēng zǐ* day,
feasting and drinking for the Double Ninth Festival began,
continuing day and night,
only stopping on the *rén zǐ* day.
On the *jǐ wèi* day,
the Langrén Niǎo Lǐ was killed.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *gēng chén* day,
because the ruler of Hàn was in mourning for his mother,
envoys were dispatched to offer condolences and burial gifts.
The twelfth month, on the *jiǎ zǐ* day,
the Emperor visited the house of the vintner Bálà Gē.
He then visited the residence of the Commander-General of the Palace Guard, Yēlǜ Yílà Gě.
Feasting and drinking continued for several days.
He bestowed a golden basin, fine brocade, and one hundred pregnant horses.
Many attendants were granted official positions.
On the *wù chén* day,
Hàn dispatched envoys to present tribute.
In this winter,
the imperial traveling court stopped at Hēi Shān Píng Diàn.
In the seventeenth year, Spring, the first month, on the *gēng yín* day, the first day of the month,
the Chancellor Xiāo Gān
and the Princely Son Yēlǜ Xián Shì returned after suppressing Wū Gǔ.
The Emperor grasped their hands,
bestowed cups of wine,
and appointed Xián Shì as Right Píshì Xiāngwěn.
Yǎ Lǐ Sī, Chǔ Sī, and Xiá Lǐ, those three men, were given thin, weak wine to insult them.
On the *yǐ mǎo* day,
the Yílí Bì Gǔ Yù presented Wū Gǔ captives.
The second month, on the *jiǎ zǐ* day,
Gāo Xūn memorialized that Sòng was about to fortify Yì Jīn Guān.
He requested to use a detached force to harass them.
The Emperor granted the request.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *wù chén* day,
the falconer Dí Lǔ was killed.
On the *bǐng zǐ* day,
the Emperor performed the willow-shooting ritual to pray for rain,
and furthermore splashed water on all the officials.
The fifth month, on the *xīn mǎo* day,
the deer keeper Zhá Gě was killed.
On the *rén chén* day,
Xiāo Hǎi Lí, the Chancellor of the Northern Administration, died.
The court was suspended,
and the Double Fifth feast was canceled.
The sixth month, on the *jǐ wèi* day,
the pheasant keepers Shòu Gē and Niàn Gǔ were dismembered,
and forty-four deer keepers were killed.
In this summer,
the imperial traveling court stopped at Niǎo Tán.
In the eighth month of autumn, on the day Xīnyǒu,
was the Emperor’s birthday.
Because the Minister of Political Affairs, Ābùdǐ, was critically ill,
he did not receive congratulations.
In the ninth month, beginning from the day Bǐngxū,
he hunted at Hēishān and Chìshān,
until the end of the month.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Yǐchǒu,
he killed the wine attendant Cuìnǐ.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
he killed the close attendant Tíngshòu.
On the day Rénchén,
he killed the pig attendants Ābùzhá, Gělǔ, Zhú Lǐzhě, and Nièlǐkuò.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Astronomical Bureau reported that the moon was due to be eclipsed but was not obscured.
The Emperor considered this an auspicious sign
and happily drank until dawn.
On the day Rén Yín,
he killed the deer attendants Tángguǒ, Zhígē, and Sǎlà.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
he personally killed the cook Hǎilǐ
and then minced his flesh.
That winter,
the Emperor stayed at Hēihé Píngdiàn.
In the eighteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Yǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
an imperial banquet was held.
The Emperor did not receive congratulations.
On the day Jǐhài,
he viewed the lanterns in the marketplace.
He bought wine with one hundred ounces of silver
and ordered his officials also to buy wine,
drinking freely for three nights.
In the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
he visited the house of Xiáshílǐ, the Commissioner of the Five Bureaus,
and banqueted until dawn.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎshēn, the first day of the month,
he went to the Huánghé River.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
he caught a wild goose
and sacrificed it to Heaven and Earth.
He commissioned the crafting of a large wine vessel,
carved with deer patterns,
and named it
“Lùwǔ” (Deer Jar).
He stored wine in it to offer sacrifice to Heaven.
On the day Gēngxū,
he killed the falconer Hútèlǔ, the close attendant Huàgě, and the prison warden Hǎilǐ,
and moreover, chopped up Hǎilǐ’s corpse.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Guǐchǒu, the first day of the month,
he killed the swine attendant Chāolǐzhǐ.
On the day Jǐsì,
he issued an edict that among the officials attending court, those with talent, capacity, and aptitude
should be promoted without regard to hierarchy;
while those who were old and infirm
should have their salaries increased and be permitted to retire at home.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīnghài,
it was the Double Fifth Festival.
Because he was drunk, he did not receive congratulations.
On the day Rénchén,
he caught geese at Shùgǔ Shuǐ
and drank outdoors all night.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
he drank heavily with the Minister of Political Affairs Xiāo Páiyā, the Southern Capital Defense Commissioner Gāo Xūn, the Grand Tutor Zhāogǔ,
Liú Chéngxùn, and others,
continuing for days and nights.
On the day Jǐhài,
he killed the deer attendants Pǒdé, Làgē, Tāoguī, Zhábùgē, Sūgǔniè, Chūbǎo, Mígǔtè, Dídá, and others.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
he killed the swine attendant Túnnú.
On the day Jǐwèi,
he established a spirit tent for Yīlàgě, the Grand Inspector of the Palace Guards,
and partially pardoned the prisoners in the capital region.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Tàliè, who had been punished, obtained a female dog in a falcon’s nest and presented it.
That summer,
the Emperor sought refuge from the heat at Niǎotán.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the ruler of Hàn, Chéngjūn, died.
His son Jìyuán succeeded him
and came to report.
The Emperor dispatched an envoy to express condolences and offer sacrifices.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
he killed the Xiāngwěn Bālà, Yèlà Héndǔ, and four others.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
he ascended a small mountain to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Wùxū,
knowing that Sòng intended to attack Hédōng,
he instructed Tàliè, the Commander-in-Chief of the Southwest Region and King of the Southern Department, to prepare defenses.
On the day Jǐhài,
he hunted a bear.
He summoned the deer attendant Pūgū and granted the chambers in the Yè Tíng (Imperial Women’s Quarters) to Yīlàgě.
On the day Jiǎchén,
he made Yīlàgě concurrently the Minister of Political Affairs
and also granted him several tens of Lǐ of the land of the Mòzhēn east of Hēishān.
He appointed the woman Guī as a close attendant,
and the Jurchen Xiāngwěn Jiāmò as the Yīlíjǐn of his own department.
That autumn,
he hunted in the mountains around Xījīng.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Xīnhài, the first day of the month,
Sòng besieged Tàiyuán.
The Emperor ordered Tàliè to be the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces
and dispatched troops from various circuits to rescue it.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
it was the winter solstice.
Being drunk,
he did not receive congratulations.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
he killed the wine attendant Dāliègě.
That winter,
the Emperor stayed at the river east of Hēishān.
In the nineteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Jǐmǎo, the first day of the month,
he held an imperial banquet
and did not receive congratulations.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
it was the Beginning of Spring.
Being drunk,
he ordered Yīlàgě, the Grand Inspector of the Palace Guards, to perform the ceremony of striking the earthen ox in his place.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
he played the Yègé game with his officials.
On the day Wùxū,
while drunk, he abruptly promoted his attending officials.
On the day Yǐsì,
he issued an edict to the Grand Commandant Huàgē, saying:
“Should my judgment while drunk lead to inappropriate actions,
you must not simply comply.
When I sober up,
you may report the matter back to me.”
From the Beginning of Spring until the end of the month, he drank
and neglected governance.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Liú Jìyuán, the successor of Hàn,
sent an envoy requesting official enfeoffment and recognition.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
he dispatched Hán Zhīfàn to invest him as Emperor.
On the day Guǐhài,
he killed the former vanguard Mò Jí Yìlà,
chopped up his corpse,
and discarded it.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Hàn sent an envoy to present a white stag.
On the day Jǐsì,
he went to Huáizhōu.
He hunted and caught a bear.
In the midst of happy drinking, while fully drunk,
he rode back to the temporary palace.
That night,
the close attendant Xiǎogē, the bath attendant Huāgē, the cook Xīngǔ, and six others rebelled.
The Emperor was assassinated
at the age of thirty-nine.
His temple name was Mùzōng.
Later, he was interred next to Huáilíng.
In the twenty-first year of Chóngxī,
he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiào'ān Jìngzhèng.
Eulogy: Emperor Mùzōng reigned for eighteen years.
He knew that sorceresses and demonic behavior should be punished
and instructed his subjects to sharply remonstrate against excessive punishment—
this shows he was not unenlightened.
However, he was recklessly addicted to wine
and was insatiably devoted to hunting.
When an attendant tracking geese missed the deadline,
he inflicted the punishment of branding iron and iron comb;
when he caught a duck, he was greatly pleased,
and abolished the order to tattoo the faces of the attendants in the Falconry Bureau.
His rewards and punishments were arbitrary,
and he ignored court affairs,
while his passion for killing never ceased.
It was fitting
that a change arose from his immediate vicinity!
Basic Annals 8: Jǐngzōng I
Emperor Jǐngzōng Xiàochéng Kāngjìng,
whose taboo name was Xián,
courtesy name Xiánníng,
and childhood name Míngyǐ.
He was the second son of Emperor Shìzōng,
and his mother was Empress Huáijié, of the Xiāo clan.
During Chāgē’s rebellion,
the Emperor was just four years old.
When Emperor Mùzōng ascended the throne,
he was raised in the Yǒngxīng Palace.
After he grew up,
Emperor Mùzōng became addicted to alcohol and neglected governance.
One day, the Emperor spoke about current affairs with Hán Kuāngsì,
but Yēlǜ Xiánshì stopped him.
The Emperor understood
and spoke no more.
In the nineteenth year of *Yīnglì* (969), Spring, second month, on the *wùchén* day,
he entered for an audience.
Mùzōng said:
"My son has already reached maturity,
and the administration can be entrusted to him."
On the *jǐsì* day,
Mùzōng was assassinated.

The Emperor led the Flying Dragon Commissioner *Nǚlǐ*, the Chamberlain *Xiāo Sīwēn*, and the Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs *Gāo Xūn*, leading a thousand armored cavalrymen, and sped there.
At dawn,
they arrived at the Imperial temporary residence,
and wept grievously.
The assembled officials urged him to ascend,
and thus he immediately took the throne as Emperor before the coffin.
All officials conferred the honorific title Tiānzàn Huángdì (Heaven-Assisted Emperor),
issued a general amnesty,
and changed the era name to Bǎoníng.
The Grand Inspector of the Palace Guards, *Yélǜ Yílà*,
and the Right *Píshì Xiángwěn*, *Xiāo Wūlǐzhǐ*, were executed
for laxity in guarding the residence.
Third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
he entered Shàngjīng (Supreme Capital),
and appointed *Xiāo Sīwēn* as the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
The Prince of Tàipíng, *Yǎnsāgě*, fled into *Shātuó*.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the *Yílíbì*, *Niánmùgǔn*, was executed for secretly supporting *Yǎnsāgě*.
On the *guǐsì* day,
*Yǎnsāgě* came to court.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, *Xiāo Sīwēn*, was concurrently appointed Chief Minister of the Northern Administration.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, *Gāo Xūn*, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Qín.
Summer, fourth month, on the *wùshēn* first day of the month,
the Prince of Tàipíng, *Yǎnsāgě*, was advanced in rank and enfeoffed as the Prince of Qí.
The Prince of Zhào, *Xǐyǐn*, was re-enfeoffed as the Prince of Sòng;
*Lóngxiān* was enfeoffed as the Prince of Píng;
*Shāo* as the Prince of Wú;
*Dàoyǐn* as the Prince of Shǔ;
*Bìshè* as the Prince of Yuè;
*Díliè* as the Prince of Jì;
and *Wǎn* as the Prince of Wèi.
Fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Noble Consort *Xiāo* (Shì) was established as Empress.
On the *bǐngshēn* first day of the month,
they performed the ritual of shooting the willow branch to pray for rain.
The relevant authorities requested that the Emperor’s birthday be designated the Tiānqīng Jié (Heavenly Clarity Festival),
and this was granted.
On the *rényín* day,
Hàn (the Northern Hàn state) sent *Lǐ Kuāngbì*, *Liú Jìwén*, *Lǐ Yuánsù*, and others to offer congratulations.
Winter, tenth month,
he proceeded east to *Niǎotán*.
Eleventh month, on the *jiǎchén* first day of the month,
he performed the *cháicè* sacrifice,
worshiped at Mùyè Shān (Muye Mountain),
and made his temporary stop at Hègǔ (Crane Valley).
On the *yǐsì* day,
*Xiāo Sīwēn* was enfeoffed as the Prince of Wèi,
and the Northern Court Great King, *Wūzhì*, was granted the title of *Yúyuè*.
Second year of Bǎoníng (970), Spring, first month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
he went to the Huáng Hé (Yellow River).
Summer, fourth month,
he proceeded to Dōngjīng (Eastern Capital),
and offered sacrifices to the Ràngguó Huángdì (Emperor Who Yielded the State) and the temple of Shìzōng.
Fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
he proceeded west.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
while stopping at Pándào Lǐng,
robbers assassinated the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, *Xiāo Sīwēn*.
Sixth month,
he returned to Shàngjīng.
Autumn, seventh month,
he appointed the Right *Píshì Xiángwěn*, *Xiánshì*, as the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Ninth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
evidence was found that the Emperor’s maternal uncles, *Xiāo Hǎizhǐ* and *Hǎilǐ*, had murdered *Xiāo Sīwēn*.
They were all executed,
and their younger brother, *Shéndǔ*, was exiled to Huánglóng Fǔ.
Winter, twelfth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Hàn sent envoys to present tribute.
Third year of Bǎoníng (971), Spring, first month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
the Right *Yílíbì*, *Xīdì*, sent a person to present captives from *Díliè*.
An imperial decree awarded the meritorious officers and soldiers.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Court of the Petition Drum (*Dēngwéngǔ Yuàn*) was established.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Commissioner for Military Affairs of Nánjīng (Southern Capital) and Duke of Wèi, *Hán Kuāngměi*, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yè.
Second month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
he proceeded east.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
he dispatched the *Duó'è* Commissioner to *Āsàlán* Uighur.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with a black ox and a white horse.
Third month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the Flying Dragon Commissioner, *Nǚlǐ*, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Khitan Traveling Palace.
Summer, fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Consort *Chuòlǐ* and *Púgē*, consorts of Shìzōng, practiced black magic,
and were granted death.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
he worshiped at Mùyè Shān,
and performed the ceremony of rebirth.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
he returned from his procession east.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
*Xiāo Shéndǔ* was executed.
Sixth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Hàn sent an envoy to inquire after the Emperor's well-being.
Thereafter, they arrived monthly.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Uighurs sent envoys to present tribute.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, *Xiánshì*, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.
Eighth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
he went to Qiū Shān (Autumn Mountain).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
he sacrificed at the tomb of his Imperial elder brother *Hǒu*,
and posthumously designated him Crown Prince,
with the posthumous title Zhuāngshèng.
Ninth month, on the *yǐsì* day,

gifts of households, cattle, and sheep were bestowed in differing amounts upon the tutors and nurses, including the Guardian *Fù*, Chamberlain *Dálǐdié*, Grand Protector *Chǔbǔ*, Grand Protector *Pó'ér*, Nurse *Huíshì*, and *Yāyǎ*.
Furthermore, the servants from the former imperial residence were formed into the *Tàmǎ* Department,
and officials were established to manage them.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
he proceeded to Guīhuà Zhōu.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he went to Nánjīng.
Winter, tenth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Gods were sacrificed to with black and white sheep.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Hàn sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Bígǔdé and Tǔyùhún came to present tribute.
Eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the *Yúyuè* of Lúqú Hé, *Yánnílǐ*, and others led four hundred fifty households to submit,
requesting to be registered under the Imperial Palace.
An imperial decree retained their households,
divided them among the three palaces, Dūnmù, Jìqìng, and Yǒngxīng,
and, having generously awarded them, sent them away.
Twelfth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with a black ox and a white horse.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Imperial Prince *Lóngxù* was born.
That winter,
the Emperor made his temporary stop at Jīnchuān.
Fourth year of Bǎoníng (972), Spring, second month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Hàn sent envoys to congratulate
on the birth of the Imperial Prince.
Intercalary month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Prince of Qí, *Yǎnsāgě*, passed away.
Third month, on the *gēngshēn* first day of the month,
he was posthumously designated Imperial Grand Uncle (*Huáng Tàishū*).
Summer, fourth month, on the *gēngyín* first day of the month,
*Xiāo Sīwēn* was posthumously enfeoffed as the Prince of Chǔ.
That summer,
the Emperor made his temporary stop at Bīngjǐng.
Autumn, seventh month,
he went to Yúnzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
Winter, tenth month, on the *dīnghài* first day of the month,
he went to Nánjīng.
Twelfth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict commanded officials, both within and outside the court, to submit sealed reports.
Fifth year of Bǎoníng (973), Spring, first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the *Tìyǐn*, *Xiūgē*, attacked the Dǎngxiàng,
defeated them,
and reported the number of captives taken.
Hàn sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor went to the Wǔfèng Lóu (Five Phoenix Tower) to watch the lanterns.
Second month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the close attendant *Shílǔlǐ* mistakenly touched the divine standard (*shéndú*).
According to the law, this warranted death,
but he was released after being beaten with rods.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Prince of Yuè, *Bìshè*, presented the number of Dǎngxiàng captives taken.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with a black ox and a white horse.
On the *xīnhài* day,
he proceeded to Xīnchéng (New City).
Third month, on the *yǐmǎo* first day of the month,
he proceeded again to Xīnchéng.
The Empress's ancestor, *Húmǔlǐ*, was posthumously enfeoffed as the Prince of Hán;
her uncle, *Húlǔgǔ*, was posthumously granted the title of Grand Administrator (*Zhèngshì Lìng*);
and *Nígǔzhǐ* was concurrently appointed Chamberlain (*Shìzhōng*).
Summer, fourth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
a white vapor was seen in daylight.
Fifth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the *Yúyuè*, *Wūzhì*, passed away,
and court was suspended for three days.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Nǚzhí invaded the border,
killed the Metropolitan Inspector *Dálǐdié* and the *Zhuàilá* *Wòlǐlǔ*,
and drove away and plundered the cattle and horses of the border people.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
*Āsàlán* Uighur came to present tribute.
In the sixth month, on *gēngyín* (25th day),
the Jurchen (Nǚzhēn) Chancellor (zǎixiàng) and *Yílíjǐn* came to offer tribute.
On *bǐngshēn* (39th day),
Hàn (Northern Hàn) dispatched a messenger to report concerning matters with Sòng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *gēngchén* (17th day),
Yēlǜ Xiélǐdǐ, Regional Commander (jiéduōshǐ) of the Bǎodà Army, was appointed Left Grand Councilor (zuǒxiāng) of the Central Directorate (Zhōngtáishěng).
In this month,
the imperial entourage stopped at Yànzichéng.
In the ninth month, on *rénzǐ* (49th day),
Hélǔ Tǎlǎn, the tribal chief of Bǐgǔdé, came to present tribute.
In winter, the tenth month, on *dīngyǒu* (4th day),
the emperor went to Nánjīng.
In the eleventh month, on *xīnhài* (18th day), the first day of the month,
the emperor finally captured Xiǎogē, Huāgē, Xīngǔ, and others, close attendants who were part of the Yìnglì rebel faction,
and had them executed.
In the twelfth month, on *wùxū* (35th day),
Hàn was about to change its reign title
and sent an envoy to request permission (bǐngmìng).
In this month,
the emperor went to Guīhuà Zhōu.
Sixth year (976 CE). In spring, the first month, on *guǐwèi* (40th day),
the emperor went to Nánjīng.
In the third month,
Sòng sent an envoy to request peace.
Yēlǜ Chāngshù, Prefect (cìshǐ) of Zhuō Zhōu, was given the additional title of Attendant Counselor (shìzhōng) and entrusted with negotiating peace with Sòng.
In summer, the fourth month,
Wáng Xǐyǐn of Sòng was deposed for involvement in a conspiracy to rebel.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *dīngwèi* (14th day), the first day of the month,
Zhuó Gǔ, Director of the Palace Gate (géménshǐ), was given the additional title of Grand Commandant Supervising the Ministries (jiǎnjiào tàiwèi) concurrently serving as Grand Censor (yùshǐ dàfū).
His son, Hǎilǐ, for reporting the matter concerning Xǐyǐn,
was appointed Military Commissioner (fángyùshǐ) of Lǒng Zhōu by remote commission.
On *gēngshēn* (17th day),
the emperor hunted in the Píngdì Sōnglín forest.
In winter, the tenth month, on *yǐhài* (2nd day), the first day of the month,
the emperor returned to Shàngjīng.
In the twelfth month, on *wùzǐ* (25th day),
the monk Zhāomǐn was appointed Chief Supervisor (dū zǒngguǎn) of Monks and Nuns across the Three Capitals and various circuits (sān jīng zhū dào sēngní),
and was given the additional title of Attendant Counselor (shìzhōng).
Seventh year (977 CE). In spring, the first month, on *jiǎxū* (11th day), the first day of the month,
Sòng sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
On *rén'yín* (19th day),
a distant sacrifice was offered at Mùyè Shān.
In the second month, on *guǐhài* (30th day),
Liú Jìwén, Regional Commander of Yànmén of Hàn, came to offer tribute
and presented local products.
On *bǐngyín* (3rd day of the 3rd month),
a sacrifice of a black ox and a white horse was made to Heaven and Earth.
In the third month, on *rénwǔ* (9th day),
Yēlǜ Sùsà and others presented captured captives from the Dǎngxiàng,
who were distributed among the officials.
In summer, the fourth month,
the Heir Apparent (lángjūn) Shěnsī was sent as an envoy to Sòng.
On *jǐyǒu* (26th day),
a sacrifice was offered at Mùyè Shān.
On *xīnhài* (28th day),
the willow shooting ceremony was held to pray for rain.
The emperor went to Pínbì Diàn to escape the summer heat.
In the fifth month, on *bǐngxū* (3rd day),
a sacrifice was offered to Shéngū.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Yàn Pō, a guard general (wèijiàng) of Huánglóng Fǔ, killed the Surveillance Commissioner (dūjiān) Zhāng Jū and rebelled.
The Secretariat Chief (chǎngshǐ) Yēlǜ Hélǐbì was dispatched to suppress him.
In the ninth month,
Yàn Pō was defeated at Zhì Hé,
and his younger brother Ān Tuán was sent to pursue him.
Yàn Pō fled and secured himself in Wūyě Chéng.
Ān Tuán then returned,
and the remaining rebels, over a thousand households, were established in the city of Tōngzhōu.
This autumn,
the emperor returned from Pínbì Diàn.
In winter, the tenth month,
fishing was done at Tǔ Hé.
Eighth year (978 CE). In spring, the first month, on *guǐyǒu* (20th day),
Sòng sent an envoy for a diplomatic mission.
In the second month, on *rén'yín* (29th day),
the emperor issued an edict to the Academicians of the History Office (Shǐguǎn Xuéshì),
stating that when recording the Empress's words, they should also use the terms
“Zhèn”
and
“Yǔ” (imperial pronouns),
establishing this as a fixed rule.
In the third month, on *xīnwèi* (18th day),
five envoys were dispatched to tour the four directions to investigate those who were widowed, solitary, orphaned, childless, poor, lacking, or had lost their positions,
and to relieve them.
In summer, the sixth month,
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, Pacification Commissioner (zhāotǎoshǐ) for the Southwest Front, was appointed Northern Court Grand King (Běiyuàn Dàwáng).
In autumn, the seventh month, on *bǐngyín* (3rd day), the first day of the month,
Ānzhǐ, the wife of King Níng Zhǐmò, was executed.
Zhǐmò, Gāo Xūn, and others were dismissed from office.
On *xīnwèi* (8th day),
Sòng sent an envoy to congratulate the emperor on the Tiānqīng Festival.
In the eighth month, on *guǐmǎo* (20th day),
Hàn sent an envoy to report that an unrestricted gathering (wúzhēhuì) was held on the Tiānqīng Festival,
with meals offered to monks to pray for blessings.
On *dīngwèi* (24th day),
the emperor went to Qiū Shān.
On *jǐyǒu* (26th day),
Hàn reported concerning matters with Sòng.
In this month,
the Jurchen (Nǚzhēn) invaded the eastern border of Guìdé Zhōu.
In the ninth month, on *jǐsì* (6th day),
the emperor visited Huáilíng.
On *xīnwèi* (8th day),
Chálín, Commander-in-Chief (tǒngjūnshǐ) of Dōngjīng, and Xiángwěn Hè reported that the Jurchen had raided the five stockades of Guī Zhōu,
plundered them, and departed.
On *yǐhài* (12th day),
Bǐgǔdé presented tribute.
On *rénwǔ* (19th day),
Hàn was invaded by Sòng forces
and sent an envoy to request aid.
The emperor ordered Yēlǜ Shā, Chancellor of the Southern Directorate (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng), and Jì Wáng Díliè to go to their assistance.
On *wùzǐ* (25th day),
Hàn, with Sòng armies pressing the border,
sent the Commandant-Consort (fùmǎ dūwèi) Lú Jùn to report.
In winter, the tenth month, on *xīnchǒu* (28th day),
Hàn sent thanks for the Liáo army having repelled the Sòng forces.
In the eleventh month, on *bǐngzǐ* (3rd day),
Kuāngyìn, the ruler of Sòng, died.
His brother, Jiǒng, enthroned himself
and sent an envoy to report.
On *xīnmǎo* (8th day),
the Heir Apparents Wáng Liù and Tàmǎ Nièmùgǔ were sent as envoys to Sòng to express condolences.
In the twelfth month, on *rén'yín* (19th day),
Xiāo Zhǐgǔ and Mǎ Zhé were sent to congratulate Sòng on the enthronement.
On *dīngwèi* (24th day),
Hàn reported that the Sòng army had returned and plundered their military stores,
and requested grain as assistance.
On *wùwǔ* (25th day),
an imperial edict restored the Ministry of Rites Examination Bureau (Lǐbù Gòngyuàn) in Nánjīng.
In this month,
the state of Hélàsī (Khakas) sent an envoy to present tribute.
Annals of Emperor Jǐngzōng, Part 2 (Běnjì Jiǔ Jǐngzōng Xià)
Ninth year (979 CE). In spring, the first month, on *bǐngyín* (3rd day),
the Jurchen (Nǚzhēn) sent an envoy to present tribute.
In the second month, on *gēngzǐ* (17th day),
Sòng sent an envoy to deliver relics of their former emperor.
On *jiǎyín* (21st day),
a sacrifice of a black ox and a white horse was made to Heaven and Earth.
In the third month, on *guǐhài* (30th day),
Yēlǜ Shā and Díliè presented Sòng captives captured during the campaign to aid Hàn.
On *wùchén* (5th day of the 4th month),
an imperial edict granted 200,000 *hú* of grain to aid Hàn.
In summer, the fifth month, on *gēngwǔ* (17th day),
Hàn sent an envoy to express thanks
and to report concerning matters with Sòng.
On *jǐchǒu* (26th day),
twenty-one Jurchen came to request the positions of Chancellor and *Yílíjǐn*.
They were successively appointed.
In the sixth month, on *bǐngchén* (13th day),
Wáng Xǐyǐn of Sòng was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Southwest Front.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *gēngshēn* (27th day), the first day of the month,
the Uighur (Huíhú) sent an envoy to present tribute.
On *jiǎzǐ* (1st day of the 8th month),
Sòng sent an envoy for a diplomatic mission.
On *rénshēn* (9th day),
Hàn reported concerning the Sòng invasion.
On *bǐngzǐ* (13th day),
an envoy was dispatched to provide warhorses as aid to Hàn.
In the eighth month,
Hàn sent an envoy to present grape wine.
In winter, the tenth month, on *jiǎzǐ* (1st day),
Yēlǜ Shā brought Kěchǒu and Mǎiyǒu, Dǎngxiàng surrendered chiefs, for an audience.
The emperor issued an edict to placate and instruct them.
On *dīngmǎo* (4th day),
Kěchǒu was appointed Minister of Education (Sītú),
and Mǎiyǒu was appointed Grand Guardian (Tàibǎo).
They were each granted gifts and sent off.
On *rénshēn* (9th day),
the Jurchen sent an envoy to present tribute.
On *yǐyǒu* (12th day),
Hàn again sent an envoy to report concerning matters with Sòng.
In the eleventh month, on *dīnghài* (24th day), the first day of the month,
the Directorate of Astronomy (Sītiān) reported that a solar eclipse was due but did not occur.
On *wùxū* (5th day of the 12th month),
more than four hundred households of Tuyuhun (Tǔyùhún) rebels who had entered Tàiyuán
were tracked down and returned.
On *guǐmǎo* (10th day),
a sacrifice was offered at Mùyè Shān.
On *yǐsì* (12th day),
Grand Guardian Diéliègē and others were sent as envoys to Sòng.
On *yǐmǎo* (22nd day),
Hàn again sent an envoy to report concerning matters with Sòng.
In the twelfth month, on *wùchén* (25th day),
the emperor hunted in the near suburbs,
and the spoils were used in a sacrifice to Heaven.
Tenth year (980 CE). In spring, the first month, on *guǐchǒu* (10th day),
the emperor went to Chángluò.
In the second month, on *gēngwǔ* (27th day),
the Āsàlán Uighurs came to present tribute.
In the third month, on *gēngyín* (7th day),
a sacrifice was offered at Xiǎnlíng.
In summer, the fourth month, on *dīngmǎo* (24th day),
the emperor proceeded west.
On *jǐsì* (26th day),
the Jurchen sent an envoy to present tribute.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Nǚlǐ was granted death (executed).
People were dispatched to execute Gāo Xūn and others.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Imperial halting place was by Yánliǔhú.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàizǔ Temple.
Ninth month, on the first day, Guǐwèi,
Píng Wáng Lóngxiān's son, Chéngē, plotted to murder his father,
and was torn apart by chariots (dismembered) publicly.
That winter,
the Imperial halting place was at Jīnchuān.
Qiánhēng First Year, spring, first month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Tàmǎ Chángshòu was dispatched as an envoy to Sòng,
to inquire about the reasons for raising an army to attack Liú Jìyuán.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Chángshòu returned,
stating:
"Hédōng defied the mandate,
so punishment is warranted.
If the Northern Court (Liáo) does not provide aid,
the peace treaty will remain as before;
otherwise, there will be war."
Second month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Hàn (Northern Hán), because Sòng troops were pressing its border,
sent an envoy to request aid.
An edict ordered the Southern Palace Chancellor Yēlǜ Shā to be the Commander-in-Chief (Dūtǒng), and Jì Wáng Díliè to be the Supervising General (Jiānjūn) to go assist them;
it also commanded the Southern Court Great King Xiézhěn to follow with his department,
and the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Mǒzhī to supervise them.
Third month, on the day Xīnsì,
Sùsā sent people with Huàgē and others of separate tribes to surrender,
and they were accepted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Hàn sent an envoy to thank them for placating and admonishing the military and civilians.
An edict ordered the Northern Court Great King Xīdǐ and Yǐshì Wáng Sāhé, among others, to garrison Yān with troops.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Hàn again reported Sòng troops had entered the territory.

An edict ordered the Great General of the Left Ox Cavalry Guard Hán Gē and the Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Dàtóng Army, Yēlǜ Shànbǔ, to provide southern aid with the troops from their circuits.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Nǚzhí sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Yēlǜ Shā and others fought Sòng at Báimǎlǐng,
and were defeated.
Jì Wáng Díliè, along with the Military Commissioner of the Tūlǚbù Department, Dūmǐn, and the Xiángwěn of the Huángpíshì, Tángkuò, all died there.
The officers and soldiers suffered heavy casualties.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Hàn reported on military campaign matters.
Lú Jùn rushed a report from Dàizhōu announcing an emergency.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Díliè came to offer tribute.
Fifth month, on the first day, Jǐmǎo,
Sòng troops arrived at Hédōng,
Hàn fought them,
but was defeated.
Liú Jìwén and Lú Jùn defected (came to seek refuge).
Sixth month,
Liú Jìyuán surrendered to Sòng,
and Hàn perished.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Liú Jìwén was enfeoffed as Pénchéng Jùn Wáng.
Lú Jùn was made Administrator of Affairs with the Dignity of a Chancellor (Tóng Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāngshì).
The Sòng ruler came and invaded.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Northern Court Great King Xīdǐ,
the Commander Xiāo Tǎogǔ, and Yǐshì Wáng Sāhé attacked him.
They fought at Shāhé,
and were defeated.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Sòng ruler besieged Nánjīng.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict instructed Yēlǜ Shā, Xīdǐ, Tǎogǔ, and others regarding military matters.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Shā and others fought the Sòng army at Gāoliánghé,
and initially retreated slightly;
Xiūgē and Xiézhěn struck them flank-wise,
utterly defeating them.
The Sòng ruler barely escaped with his life,
reached Zhuōzhōu,
and secretly fled in a donkey cart.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the remaining Sòng forces were attacked,
the casualties were immense,
and the captured weapons, armor, seals, grain supplies, and currency were beyond counting.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yēlǜ Shā sent men to present the prisoners and spoils.

Because Hán Déràng (Acting Governor of Nánjīng Prefecture), Yēlǜ Xuégǔ (Acting Commander-in-Chief of the Horse and Foot Army of Nánjīng), and Liú Hóng (Administrator of the Three Offices) were all able to pacify the populace
and defend the city walls,
they were all granted imperial edicts praising and rewarding them.
Eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Tìyǐn of the Zǔbǔ, Hélǔ, and the Yílíjǐn, Ālǐdǔ, along with others, came to court.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yēlǜ Shā and others presented the captives.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Shā and Mǒzhī were censured for the battle at Báimǎ (Báimǎlǐng),
but were subsequently pardoned due to their merit in driving away the Sòng ruler;
Xīdǐ retreated upon encountering the enemy,
and was struck with the flat of a sword;
Sāhé, although he retreated,
kept his ranks in order,
and was pardoned;
those under Jì Wáng Díliè who first fled were executed,
and those from Dūjiān downward were flogged.
On the day Rénshēn,
a banquet was held for Shā, Mǒzhī, and other generals and officers,
and rewards were bestowed according to rank.
Ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Yān Wáng Hán Kuāngsì was made Commander-in-Chief (Dūtǒng),
Southern Palace Chancellor Yēlǜ Shā was made Supervising General (Jiānjūn),
Tìyǐn Xiūgē, Southern Court Great King Xiézhěn, Acting Xī King Mǒzhī, and others each led their departmental troops in a southern campaign;
furthermore, Yēlǜ Shànbǔ, the Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Army, was ordered to lead the Shānxī troops to advance along different routes.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Hán Kuāngsì fought the Sòng army at Mǎnchéng,
and was utterly defeated.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Grand Tutor (Tàibǎo) Shěnsī fought the Sòng army at Huǒshān,
and defeated them.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict enumerated the five crimes of Hán Kuāngsì,
but pardoned him.
Eleventh month, on the day Wùyín,
a banquet was held and rewards were given to Xiūgē and the meritorious generals and officers.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Guō Xí, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Court concurrently Administrator of Governmental Affairs (Zhèngshì Lìng), submitted a memorial advising against hunting,
which was graciously accepted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the winter solstice occurred,
a general amnesty was declared,
and the reign title was changed to Qiánhēng.
Twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Yān Wáng Hán Kuāngsì was nominally appointed Military Commissioner of Jìnchāng Army,
and demoted in rank to Qín Wáng.
On the day Rénxū,
Shǔ Wáng Dàoyǐn (Governor of Nánjīng Prefecture),
was transferred and enfeoffed as Jīng Wáng.
That winter,
the Imperial halting place was at Nánjīng.
Second Year, spring, first month, on the first day, Bǐngzǐ,
the Imperial Prince Lóngxù was enfeoffed as Liáng Wáng,
and Lóngqìng as Wáng.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Tìyǐn Xiūgē was made Northern Court Great King,
and the former Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiánshì was enfeoffed as Xīpíng Jùn Wáng.
Second month, on the day Wùchén,
went to Qīnghé.
Third month, on the day Dīnghài,
the Vice Commander of the Southwest Circuit Pacification Commission Yēlǜ Wángliù and the Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Huàgē sent people to present captured Dǎngxiàng (Tanguts).
Intercalary month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
a bustard flew and landed near the Imperial tent,
and was captured and used to sacrifice to Heaven.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngchén,
prayed for rain.
On the day Wùzǐ,
summer heat was avoided at Yānzǐchéng.
Fifth month,
lightning struck the pines at Qiánlíng.
Sixth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xǐyǐn again plotted rebellion,
and was imprisoned in Zǔzhōu.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Wángliù and others presented captured Dǎngxiàng.
Eighth month, on the day Wùxū,
proceeded East.
Winter, tenth month, on the first day, Xīnwèi,
sorcerers were commanded to offer sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the God of War.
On the day Xīnsì,
preparations were made for the southern campaign,
and sacrifices were offered to the flags and drums.
On the day Guǐwèi,
arrived at Nánjīng.
On the day Dīnghài,
enemies were captured,
and spirit arrows were shot.
On the day Gēngyín,
arrived at Gù'ān,
and sacrificed a black ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Jǐhài,
Wǎqiáoguān was besieged.
Eleventh month, on the first day, Gēngzǐ,
Sòng troops launched a night attack on the camp.
The Military Commissioner of the Tūlǚbù Department, Xiāo Gàn, and the Xiángwěn of the Four Victory Army, Yēlǜ Héndé, fought and repelled them.
On the day Rén'yín,
Xiūgē defeated the Sòng army east of Wǎqiáo.
The defending general Zhāng Shī led troops out to fight,
but Xiūgē fiercely attacked,
and defeated them.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Sòng army arrayed south of the water.
Xiūgē crossed the water, attacked and routed them,
pursuing them as far as Mòzhōu,
inflicting heavy casualties.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Sòng troops returned again,
and were nearly annihilated in the ensuing attack.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the army returned to the capital.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
they returned and halted at Nánjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the day *gēngwǔ* (the first day of the month),
Xiūgē (休哥) was appointed *Yúyuè* (于越).
A great feast was held for the soldiers.
In the spring of the third year, the second month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
the Emperor traveled east.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
he returned to *Nánjīng* (南京).
In the third month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
the Imperial Prince Hánbā (韓八) died.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
he was buried between the Huáng (潢) and Tǔ (土) rivers,
and Yǒngzhōu (永州) was established.
Hán Kuāngsì (韓匡嗣), the King of Qín (秦), was appointed Commissioner of Pacification for the Southwest Region (*Xīnánmiàn Zhāotǎoshǐ*).
In the summer, the fifth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the Han army in Shàngjīng (上京) revolted.
They attempted unsuccessfully to abduct and install Xǐyǐn (喜隱).
They falsely installed his son, Liú Lǐshòu (留禮壽).
Chúshì (除室), the Grand Defender of Shàngjīng, captured him.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
Liú Lǐshòu was executed.
In the winter, the tenth month,
the Emperor visited Púguīpō (蒲瑰坡).
In the eleventh month, on the day *xīnhài*,
Chúshì was promoted to Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (*Tóng Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāngshì*).
In this month,
Guō Xí (郭襲), the Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ*), was appointed Military Commissioner (*Jiédùshǐ*) of the Wǔdìng Army (武定軍).
In the twelfth month,
Hán Déràng (韓德讓), the Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Army (遼興軍), was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Chancellery.
In the spring of the fourth year, the first month, on the day *jǐhài*,
the Emperor visited Huálín (華林) and Tiānzhù (天柱).
In the third month, on the day *yǐwèi*,
was Qīngmíng (清明).
Archery competitions were held with the princes and high ministers,
followed by feasting and drinking.
In the summer, the fourth month,
the Emperor personally led the southern campaign.
Upon reaching Mǎnchéng (滿城),
the battle turned unfavorably.
Xī Wǎlǐ (奚瓦里), the Acting Grand Commandant (*Shǒu Tàiwèi*), was killed by a stray arrow.
Shànbǔ (善補), the Commander of Forces, was surrounded by an ambush.
Xiézhěn (斜軫), the Commissioner of Military Affairs, rescued him.
An imperial edict ordered Shànbǔ to be punished with a caning for lack of preparedness.
In the fifth month,
the army returned.
They spent the summer in Yànzǐchéng (燕子城).
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day *rénchén*,
an envoy was sent to grant Xǐyǐn death.
In the eighth month,
the Emperor visited Xījīng (西京).
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
the Emperor visited Yúnzhōu (雲州).
On the day *jiǎchén*,
he hunted at Xiánggǔ Shān (祥古山).
The Emperor became unwell.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
upon reaching Jiāoshān (焦山),
he died at his traveling residence.
He was thirty-five years old,
having reigned for thirteen years.
The dying edict designated Lóngxù (隆緒), Prince of Liáng (梁), as successor,
and decreed that major military and state affairs should follow the commands of the Empress.
In the first month, on the day *rénxū*, of the Tǒnghé (統和) era (Year One),
he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiàochéng (孝成皇帝),
and the temple name Jǐngzōng (景宗).
In the twenty-first year of Chóngxī (重熙),
the posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Xiàochéng Kāngjìng (孝成康靖皇帝).
Eulogy says: Since the rise of Liáo (遼) sixty years ago,
during the period of Shéncè (神冊) and Huìtóng (會同),
there was no rest;
the rulers of Tiānlù (天祿) and Yìnglì (應曆)
did not achieve a natural end;
since Bǎoníng (保寧),
everyone hoped for stability.
Given Jǐngzōng’s (景宗) talents—
trusting those he appointed,
faithfully rewarding and surely punishing—
it seemed he could achieve great things.
However, he exhausted the nation's strength helping Hédōng (河東),
suffering army defeats and the loss of generals,
which did not save Hédōng from ruin.
Although he once claimed compensation from Sòng (宋),
the gain did not compensate for the loss.
He recognized Kuāngsì’s (匡嗣) crimes,
yet only counted them without punishing him;
he approved of Guō Xí’s (郭襲) counsel,
but accepted it without implementing it;
the Buddhist monk Zhāomǐn (昭敏) disturbed public morals with heterodox teachings,
yet Jǐngzōng favored him with the title of Palace Attendant (*Shìzhōng*).
Was this not confusing!
Basic Annals 10: Shèngzōng I
Emperor Shèngzōng Wénwǔ Dàxiào Xuān (聖宗文武大孝宣皇帝),
personal name Lóngxù (隆緒),
courtesy name Wénshūnú (文殊奴).
He was the eldest son of Emperor Jǐngzōng (景宗),
and his mother was Empress Ruìzhì Xiāo Shì (睿智皇后蕭氏).
The Emperor, while young, loved reading and writing,
and could compose poetry by the age of ten.
When he grew up,
he excelled in archery,
understood music,
and enjoyed painting.
In the second year of Qiánhēng (乾亨),
he was enfeoffed as the Prince of Liáng (梁王).
In the autumn of the fourth year, the ninth month, on the day *rénzǐ*,
Jǐngzōng died.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
he ascended the imperial throne before the coffin,
being twelve years old at the time.
The Empress, following the dying edict, acted as regent,
and issued edicts to all circuits (*dào*).
In the winter, the tenth month, on the day *jǐwèi* (the first day of the month),
the Emperor began to attend court.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the assembled officials presented the honorific title Emperor Zhāoshèng (昭聖皇帝),
honored the Empress as Empress Dowager (*Huáng Tàihòu*),
and declared a general amnesty.
Bógǔzhé (勃古哲), Prince of the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Dàwáng*), was placed in overall charge of the affairs of the various prefectures in Shānxī (山西).
Xiūgē (休哥), Prince of the Northern Chancellery (*Běiyuàn Dàwáng*) and *Yúyuè*, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Expeditionary Army (*Nánmiàn Xíngjūn Dūtǒng*).
Héshuòrú (和朔奴), Prince of Xī (奚), served as his deputy.
Xiāo Dàoníng (蕭道寧), Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery, led his regional army to garrison Nánjīng.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
the Emperor visited Xiǎnzhōu (顯州).
In the eleventh month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Qiánzhōu (乾州) was established.
In the twelfth month, on the day *wùwǔ* (the first day of the month),
Yēlǜ Sùsā (耶律速撒) campaigned against the Zǔbǔ (阻卜).
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Dàoyǐn (道隱), Prince of Jīng (荊) and Grand Defender of Nánjīng, reported that Sòng (宋) had sent an envoy offering a rhinoceros horn belt and requesting peace.
An edict, citing the lack of a formal letter, rejected the offering.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
Tàlāgān Nǎiwànshí (撻剌干乃万十), while drunk, spoke improperly about matters of the inner court.
Although legally punishable by death,
he was caned and released.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
Hán Kuāngsì, Prince of Qín and Commissioner of Pacification for the Southwest Region, died.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
the coffin of the late Emperor (*Dàxíng Huángdì*) was placed in the Zōutú Hall (菆塗殿).
On the day *gēngchén*,
officials of the Central Chancellery (*Zhōngtái Shěng*) were reviewed and rearranged.
In the spring of the first year of Tǒnghé, the first month, on the day *wùwǔ* (the first day of the month),
because the late Emperor lay in state,
no court audience was held.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
following the dying edict,
Zhìmù (質睦), the elder half-brother of the previous emperor, was summoned before the Zōutú Hall,
and reinstated as the Prince of Níng (寧王).
Favors were bestowed upon Shì Fǎng (室昉), the Chancellor, and Pǔlǐng (普領), the Commissioner of the Court of the Imperial Insignia (*Xuānhuīshǐ*).
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Dàoyǐn, Prince of Jīng, fell ill.
An edict ordered an envoy to inquire about his health.
On that same day,
the Empress Dowager personally visited his residence to check on his sickness.
On the day *wùchén*,
Yēlǜ Zhāngwǎ (耶律章瓦), Military Commissioner of the Wūwēi Wūgǔlǐ (烏隈烏骨里) Department, was appointed Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
Dàoyǐn, Prince of Jīng, died.
Court was suspended for three days.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as the Prince of Jìn (晉王),
and an envoy was sent to comfort his family.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Xiūgē, the *Yúyuè*, was appointed Grand Defender of Nánjīng,
and was additionally granted the seal and ribbon of the Director-General of the Southern Expeditionary Camp (*Nánmiàn Xíngyíng Zǒngguǎn*),
overseeing all border affairs.
Tàmǎ Jiělǐ (撻馬解里) of Bóhǎi (渤海), having received great favor from the previous emperor,
requested to be buried alive with him.
An edict rejected the request,
but granted him goods to honor him.
On the day *wùyín*,
envoys were dispatched to bestow medicine upon Xiūgē, the *Yúyuè*, Chóuníng (籌寧), Prince of Xī, and Pǒdé (頗德), the Commander of Forces, among others.
Kěndǔ (懇篤) was ordered to deliver Xiūgē’s notice upon arriving at his post (*xiàchēbǎng*),
to inform the people of Yān (燕).
On the day *xīnsì*,
Sùsā presented captives from the Zǔbǔ.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
Ānjí (安吉), the Prefect of Zhuōzhōu (涿州), reported that Sòng was building a city north of the river.
An edict commanded Xiūgē, the *Yúyuè* and Grand Defender, to interfere with this construction,
and prevent its completion.

Consort Zhào (趙妃), Princess Húgǔdiǎn (胡骨典), Chóuníng, Prince of Xī, Ānníng (安寧), the Chancellor, Pǔnūníng (普奴寧), Prince of the North (*Běi Dàwáng*), Qūliè (屈烈), the *Tìyǐn*, Shāo (稍), Prince of Wú (吳), Zhǐmò (只沒), Prince of Níng, along with the *Huángzhàng* (潢帳), Imperial Maternal Uncles (*Guójìu*), Khitan, and Han officials, all contributed funds for the imperial mausoleum expenses.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
the Princess of Qí State (*Qíguó Gōngzhǔ*) led the inner and outer court ladies to present gifts likewise.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
Hán Déwēi (韓德威), Commissioner of Pacification for the Southwest Region, reported that fifteen departments of the Dǎngxiàng (党項) had invaded the border,
and that he had defeated them with troops.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
because Sùsā had defeated the Zǔbǔ,
an edict was issued praising him.
He was further instructed to join the Grand Han in campaigning against the various Dǎngxiàng departments.
On the day *dīnghài*,
Shì Fǎng, Commissioner of Military Affairs and concurrently Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Zhèngshì Lìng*), requested to be relieved of his concurrent post due to old age.
The edict did not grant permission.
the prohibition decreed that officials, clerks, soldiers, and commoners in the area must not gather crowds or speak privately without reason, nor violate the prohibition against traveling at night.
Those who violated it would be punished.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Nánjīng reported in a memorial,
that it was heard that Sòng was heavily stockpiling grain on the border, and that the Sòng commander-in-chief was proceeding to Táishān.
An edict commanded Xiūgē to prepare rigorously against them.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Jǐngzōng Huángdì was buried at Qiánlíng.
Lǎng, a favored courtier, and Tàlǔ, an entertainer who managed drinks, were buried alive with him.
