The Emperor and the Empress Dowager then composed a letter and had it placed with the departed Emperor.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Empress Dowager visited the mausoleum to offer sacrifices.
She commanded that portraits of close officials be painted in the Yùróng Diàn (Hall of the Imperial Countenance).
Rewards were bestowed upon the workers at the imperial tomb and the staff according to their rank.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the late Emperor's relics were granted to the imperial clan and close ministers.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yēlǜ Shànbǔ, the Military Commissioner of Nánjīng, reported in a memorial that more than seventy villages on the Sòng border had defected and submitted.
An edict commanded that they be placated and settled.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Yùróng Diàn was renamed the Yùdiàn (Jade Hall),
and Jiǔgǔ (Wine Valley) was renamed Shènggǔ (Sacred Valley).
Sùsā reported success in attacking the Dǎngxiàng.
An envoy was dispatched to commend and comfort them.
On the day Wùshēn,
Huàgē, the Tìyǐn, was made Northern Court Grand Prince (Běiyuàn Dàwáng).
Jiělǐng was made Southern Prefecture Chancellor (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng).
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor visited Shèngshān,
and subsequently paid respects at the Three Mausoleums.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Imperial Daughter Chángshòu Gōngzhǔ (Princess Chángshòu) was married to Wúliú, the son of Guójìu Zǎixiàng (Imperial Uncle Chancellor) Xiāo Póxiàng.
The third month, on the day Wùwǔ, Tuílā, the Jìedùshǐ (Regional Military Governor) of Tiāndé Jūn, and his son died in battle.
His younger brother, Nièlǐ, inherited the title.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the court stopped at Dúshān.
An envoy was sent to reward the meritorious officers and soldiers of the Southwest Front.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yēlǜ Hélǔníng, the Tàiwèi (Grand Commandant) of the Grandfather's Tent, was made Tìyǐn.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the imperial carriage halted at Píngdiàn on the Liáohé River.
On the day Xīnsì,
Xiāo Dàoníng, the Guójìu (Imperial Uncle) and Tóng Píngzhāngshì (Concurrently Administrator of Governmental Affairs), was made Jìedùshǐ of Liáoxīng Jūn.
He was also granted the honorific title Zhōngliàng Zuǒlǐ Gōngchén (Meritorious Subject of Loyalty and Assistance in Governance).
On the day Rénwǔ,
a dark ox and a white horse were sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngxū (the first day of the lunar month),
the Emperor visited Dōngjīng.
Yēlǜ Mòzhǐ, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Fùshǐ), was concurrently appointed Shìzhōng (Palace Attendant),
and made the Resident Administrator of Dōngjīng (Dōngjīng Liúshǒu).
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor paid respects at Tàizǔ Miào (Temple of Grand Ancestor).
On the day Guǐsì,
an edict commanded that gifts be bestowed upon official women who were widowed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor proceeded south.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor paid respects at the Three Mausoleums.
Goods presented by Dōngjīng were distributed as gifts to the officials responsible for the imperial tombs.
Furthermore, an edict granted Dàhàn, the Commissioner for Pacification of the Southwest Route (Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ), a sword,
authorizing him to execute independently anyone who disobeyed orders.
On the day Rén'yín,
sacrifices were offered at Níngshén Diàn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor paid respects at Qiánlíng.
On the day Yǐsì,
a messenger was sent with wine and dried meat to sacrifice at the tomb of Píngzhāng Yēlǜ Héyáng.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor visited the residence of Lady Wūgǔlǐ,
and paid respects to the imperial portrait of Tàizǔ.
After the ceremony was complete,
he visited the residence of Princess Húgǔdiǎn for a drink.
The gifts bestowed were very generous.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the great ministers, noting that the Empress Dowager was participating in governance,
suggested she should be granted a honorific title.
They requested that the relevant authorities thoroughly establish the crowning ritual.
An edict commanded the Bureau of Military Affairs (Shūmì Yuàn) to inform the regional generals along the border
that when the ceremony day arrived,
they should only send their sons and younger brothers to present memorials of congratulation,
lest the border defenses be neglected.
The Bureau of Military Affairs requested an edict commanding Pǒdé, the Sītú (Minister of the Interior) of the Northern Prefecture, to translate the legal texts presented by Nánjīng.
This was granted.
The Emperor then proceeded to Huīzhōu.
Yēlǜ Qìnglǎng was appointed Jìedùshǐ of Xìnzhōu.
The fifth month, on the day Bǐngchén (the first day of the lunar month),
Xiāo Dàoníng, the Guójìu and Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāngshì (Administrator of Governmental Affairs and Palace Gate), requested permission to return to his parents' home to perform rites
in celebration of the Empress Dowager's birthday.
Qíguó Gōngzhǔ (Princess of Qí) along with official women and various ministers presented gifts.
A banquet was held,
and gifts were bestowed upon the elders of the Guójìu's Tent according to rank.
On the day Rénxū,
the Commissioner for Pacification of the Southwest Route requested additional troops to attack the various tribes of the Western Tūjué.
An edict commanded Yēlǜ Púnúníng of the Northern Princely Establishment (Běi Wángfǔ) to lead troops from the Díbì and Díliè two tribes to assist him.
On the day Guǐhài,
because Yūyuè Xiūgē, while serving in the Southern Court (Nányuàn), had overused the administrative staff,
an edict commanded the Southern Grand Prince (Nán Dàwáng) not to follow this precedent.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Yēlǜ Shànbǔ recalled those who had defected to Sòng,
resulting in over a thousand households returning to the state.
An edict commanded that they be placated and comforted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the court stopped at Yǒngzhōu,
and sacrificed at the tomb of Prince Yàoshīnǔ.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict commanded close ministers to discuss the ritual for presenting the Empress Dowager with a honorific title.
Hán Dédù, the Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Shǐ), drafted the proposal based on the precedent of the Empress Dowagers of the Later Hàn dynasty administering court affairs and presented it.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
a dark ox and a white horse were sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor visited Mùyè Shān.
Dàhàn, the Commissioner for Pacification of the Southwest Route, reported in a memorial
that he recently dispatched Zhuàilā Bálàgē to deliver an ultimatum to the various Dǎngxiàng tribes.
A great many of them had come to submit.
An edict was issued praising him.
The sixth month, on the day Yǐyǒu (the first day of the lunar month),
an edict commanded the relevant authorities
that on the day the Empress Dowager was crowned,
officials of the third rank and above should be supplied with ceremonial robes,
and those below the third rank should wear the robes used for the Great Arrow-Shooting Rite (Dàshèliǔ zhī Fú).
The Commissioner for Pacification of the Southwest Route reported that the Dǎngxiàng chieftain, having seized Wēiyǐn, son of the Yílíjǐn, and others, petitioned for submission.
An edict commanded that they be welcomed and settled,
but also to investigate their sincerity,
and to strictly maintain border defenses.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor returned to Shàngjīng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the relevant authorities reported

that Lú Jùn, the Tóng Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāngshì (Concurrently Administrator of Governmental Affairs and Palace Gate) and Fùmǎ Dūwèi (Commander of the Imperial Cavalry), was not compatible with the Princess.
An edict commanded that they separate.
Jùn was consequently sent out as Jìedùshǐ of Xīngguó Jūn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
rites were performed at the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple).
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor led the ministers in conferring the honorific title Chéngtiān Huángtàihòu (Empress Dowager Who Supports Heaven) upon the Empress Dowager.
The ministers conferred the honorific title Tiānfǔ Huángdì (Emperor Who Assists Heaven) upon the Emperor.
A general amnesty was granted,
and the era name was changed to Tǒnghé.
On the day Dīngwèi,
imperial favor was extended throughout the realm (both internal and external officialdom),
and civil and military officials were all advanced one rank in peerage.
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed acting Sītú.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎyín (the first day of the lunar month),
the Empress Dowager began to oversee governmental affairs.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor personally reviewed the prisoners.
Prince Lóuguó, the Sītú, was found guilty of claiming illness to avoid attending the rites at the imperial mausoleum.
He was given twenty strokes with the bamboo rod.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Rebirth Ceremony (Zàishēng Lǐ) was performed.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Niǎoyǎn, the Prefect of Línhuáng, presented food and drinks.
The Emperor and the various princes divided into teams to play polo (jījū).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Hán Déwēi sent Xiángwěn Xiámǎ who broke the Dǎngxiàng forces, capturing many prisoners and gains,
and also sent the son of the Yílíjǐn to be presented to the court.
On the day Xīnsì,
meritorious officers and soldiers of the Southwest Front were rewarded.
The eighth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor made a western tour.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor paid respects at the Zǔlíng (Ancestral Mausoleum).
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Empress Dowager offered sacrifices at the tomb of Xiāo Sīwēn, the King of Chǔ State.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Emperor and the Empress Dowager paid respects at Huáilíng,
and then proceeded to Huáizhōu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor and Xiézhěn exchanged bows and arrows, saddles, and horses before the Empress Dowager,
pledging to be friends.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor hunted at Chìshān.
An envoy was sent to offer bear fat and dried venison at the Níngshén Diàn of Qiánlíng.
Because Sūn Zhēn, the Director of Governmental Affairs (Zhèngshì Lìng), had no son,
an edict commanded Táowēi, the Lángjūn (Gentleman) of the Guójìu Xiǎowēng Tent, to become his heir.
On the day Yǐsì,
an edict commanded Yūyuè Xiūgē to supervise Yuánchéng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Hán Déwēi submitted a memorial requesting permission to attack the Dǎngxiàng who had rebelled again.
An edict granted permission;
furthermore, several thousand troops from other divisions were dispatched to assist him.
In the ninth month, on *Guǐchǒu* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
because of drought and locusts in Dōngjīng and Píngzhōu,
an edict was issued to provide relief.
On *Yǐmǎo*,
[the Emperor] paid respects at the three palaces: Yǒngxīng, Chángníng, and Dūnmù.
On *Bǐngchén*,
the Grand Defender (*Liúshǒu*) of Nánjīng reported
that autumn rains had harmed the crops,
requesting the temporary suspension of border tariffs and taxes,
to facilitate grain trading with Shānxī.
This was granted.
On *Gēngshēn*,
[the Emperor] paid respects at Xuānjiǎn Huángdì's temple.
On *Xīnyǒu*,
[the Emperor] proceeded to Zǔzhōu,
and paid respects at the Ancestral Mausoleum (*Zǔlíng*).
On *Rénxū*,
[the Emperor] returned to Shàngjīng.
On *Xīnwèi*,
the officials concerned requested that the Emperor's birthday be designated the Qiānlíng Jié (Festival of the Thousand Years).
This was granted.
The Empress Dowager (*Huáng Tàihòu*) stated that the late Yúyuè Wū Zhǐ had achieved merit through mentorship and guidance,
and that his descendants should be rewarded.
Consequently, his son Pànyāng was appointed Línyá.
On *Bǐngzǐ*,
[the Emperor] went to Lǎowēng Chuān.
In winter, the tenth month, on *Guǐwèi* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
the Astronomical Bureau (*Sītiān*) reported the sighting of the star Lǎorénxīng (Canopus).
On *Wùzǐ*,
Princess Shūgē was married to the Imperial Uncle (*Guójiù*) Xiángwěn Zhàogū.
On *Guǐsì*,
Sùsā reported that the Díliè tribe and rebel vassals had come to surrender,
and all their former territory was restored.
On *Yǐwèi*,
based on the words of Yúyuè Xiūgē, the Grand Defender of Yānjīng,
concerning the annual tribute offered by the various Military Commissioners (*Jiédùshǐ*),
following the precedent for Qìdān officials,
only saddles and horses were to be presented.
This was granted.
On *Dīngyǒu*,
Wú Wáng Shāo was appointed Grand Defender of Shàngjīng,
concurrently managing the affairs of the Prefect (*Yǐn*) of Línhuáng.
The Emperor was preparing to campaign against Gāolì (Koryŏ),
and personally reviewed the troops commanded by Yēlǜ Mòzhǐ, the Grand Defender of Dōngjīng.
On *Bǐngwǔ*,
Xuānhuīshǐ concurrently Shìzhōng Pú Líng, Línyá Kěndé, and others were ordered to lead troops for an eastern campaign.
They were granted banners, drums, and silver tallies.
In the eleventh month, on *Rénzǐ* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
[the Emperor] observed fishing at Tà Mǎ Luò.
On *Guǐchǒu*,
Yìngzhōu reported,
having captured a Sòng spy,
who stated that Sòng was clearing roads at Wǔtái Shān,
intending to enter the border of Língqiū.
An edict ordered that both the spy and the person who sheltered him be dismembered in the marketplace.
On *Gēngchén*,
the Emperor and the Empress Dowager offered sacrifices at Qiánlíng,

and issued an edict instructing the Right and Left Chancellors (*Xiāng*), Right and Left Administrators (*Píngzhāngshì*), Deputy Grand Defender Adjutants (*Fù Liúshǒu Pànguān*), Military Commissioner Adjutants (*Zhūdào Jiédùshǐ Pànguān*), Military Affairs Adjutants (*Zhūjūnshì Pànguān*), and Secretariat Administrators (*Lùshì Cānjūn*) of the three capitals,
to uphold impartiality and fairness,
and not to practice favoritism.
If county magistrates (*Xiàn Lìng Zǔo*) encountered unwarranted levies or demands from prefectural officials or imperial envoys,
they were not to comply out of fear.
[The court] would continuously gather intelligence and listen [to reports],
to determine awards and demotions.
Among the populace, those who had living parents
but registered separately and lived apart,
neighbors were allowed to report them,
and they would be punished.
Those who were filial to their parents,
and whose three generations lived together,
their households would be honored.
In the twelfth month, on *Rénwǔ* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
[the Emperor] paid respects at Níngshén Diàn,
and dispatched envoys to offer separate sacrifices at the various mausoleums.
Wine was bestowed upon the officials and subordinates guarding the palace halls.
On this day,
[the Emperor] proceeded to Xiǎnzhōu.
On *Dīnghài*,
the silk and brocade annual tribute from Xiǎnzhōu was distributed among those on the left and right (i.e., courtiers).
On *Jiǎwǔ*,
[the Emperor] proceeded eastward.
On *Jǐhài*,
the Empress Dowager observed fishing at Yùpén Wān.
On *Xīnchǒu*,
[the Emperor] observed fishing at Jùnyuān.
On *Jiǎchén*,
a decree was issued stating that for settled legal cases involving capital punishment that have been formalized and dispatched, if there was an injustice,
permission was granted to appeal to the Censorate.
That evening,
ten thousand fish lanterns (*wànyú dēng*) were lit at Shuāngxī.
On *Wùshēn*,
the Qiānlíng Jié was celebrated.
Sacrifices were made to the Sun and Moon.
When the rites were complete,
the hundred officials offered congratulations.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on *Jiǎzǐ*,
[the Emperor] went to Chángluò.
In the second month, on *Guǐsì*,
Imperial Uncle (*Guójiù*) Xiāo Tàlǎn, Military Commissioner of Zhāngdé Jūn, came to court.
On *Jiǎwǔ*,
General Yēlǜ Díbùchūn was presented with a spring robe and a belt.
On *Bǐngshēn*,
Yēlǜ Púníng, Commissioner of Military Movements on the Eastern Route and Xuānhuīshǐ, reported a victory in the campaign against the Nǚzhí.
An envoy was dispatched to hold his hand and offer praise and encouragement.
On *Gēngzǐ*,
[the Emperor] paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
The Empress Dowager consequently followed him to observe hunting at Ráolè Chuān.
On *Yǐsì*,
Yēlǜ Kuíwā, Military Commissioner of the Wǔguó Wūkuí Yújué, stated that the various tribes under his jurisdiction were difficult to govern,
and requested an edict granting him a sword,
allowing him to act at his discretion.
This was granted.
On *Bǐngwǔ*,
the Emperor held an archery contest with the Imperial Princes (*Zhū Wáng*) and high officials (*Dàchén*).
On *Dīngwèi*,
Hán Déwēi returned from campaigning against the Dǎngxiàng,
and subsequently raided Hédōng.
He presented his captives,
and was granted an edict praising his actions.
In the third month, on *Yǐmǎo*,
the Huálí department requested that henceforth the Xiángwěn only be selected and appointed from within their own department.
The Emperor said:
"The officials of all departments are appointed based only on securing the right person.
How can we establish a restriction limiting selection only to that department?"
The request was denied.
The late Zhào Yánxù, who was Administrator of the Affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery (*Tóng Píngzhāngshì*), was posthumously granted the concurrent title of Shìzhōng.
In summer, the fourth month, on *Dīnghài*,
Xuānhuīshǐ concurrently Tóng Píngzhāngshì Yēlǜ Pǔníng and Chief Inspector (*Dūjiān*) Xiāo Qíndé presented news of a victory against the Nǚzhí.
Pǔníng was appointed concurrently Minister of Political Affairs (*Zhèngshì Lìng*),
Qíndé was appointed Grand General of the Divine Martial Guard (*Shénwǔ Wèi Dà Jiāngjūn*),
and each was bestowed with gold utensils and other items.
On *Gēngyín*,
the Empress Dowager presided over the resolution of delayed legal cases.
On *Xīnmǎo*,
sacrifices were made to the Earl of Wind (*Fēng Bó*).
On *Rénchén*,
Liú Chéngguī, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs (*Xuānhuī Nányuàn Shǐ*), was appointed Military Commissioner of Chéngdé Jūn.
Zhāng Déyún, Commander-in-Chief of Chóngdé Gōng (*Dū Bùshǔ*) and Military Commissioner of Bǎoyì Jūn, was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs (*Xuānhuī Běiyuàn Shǐ*).
In the fifth month, on *Yǐmǎo*,
sacrifices were offered at Mùyè Shān.
On *Dīngchǒu*,
[the Emperor] stopped the imperial carriage by Yánliǔ Hú.
In the sixth month, on *Jǐmǎo* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
the Empress Dowager resolved legal cases,
continuing until the end of the month.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *Guǐchǒu*,
the Empress Dowager performed the ceremony of rebirth (*zàishēng lǐ*).
In the eighth month, on *Xīnmǎo*,
Yēlǜ Mòzhǐ, Grand Defender of Dōngjīng concurrently Shìzhōng, reported that
eight Nǚzhí clans, including Zhúbùzhí and Sàilǐ, requested to join the internal governance with all their people.
An edict ordered that they be accepted.
In the ninth month, on *Wùshēn* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
[the Emperor] stopped the imperial carriage at Tǔhé.
On *Xīnwèi*,
marking the death anniversary (*jìrì*) of Jǐngzōng,
an edict instructed the various circuits (*Zhūdào*), capitals (*Jīng*), and garrisons (*Zhèn*) to dispatch officials to perform incense offerings and provide food for monks.
In winter, the tenth month, on *Dīngchǒu* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
Yēlǜ Pǔníng, Governor (*Cìshǐ*) of Guīhuà Zhōu, was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhāngdé Jūn.

Hán Zhuó, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard (*Yòu Wǔwèi Dà Jiāngjūn*), was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhāngguó Jūn concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Bodyguard Forces (*Shìwèi Qīnjūn Bīngmǎ Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ*).
In the eleventh month, on *Rénzǐ*,
Zhèng Gǔ, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì*) and Gěishìzhōng, was appointed Governor of Rúzhōu.
In this month,
Sùsā and others campaigned against the Zǔbǔ,
and killed their chieftain Tàlāgān.
In the twelfth month, on *Xīnchǒu*,
Mǎ Déchén, Academician of the Hanlin Academy concurrently Chief Drafter (*Chéngzhǐ*), was appointed Academician of Xuānzhèng Diàn.
Yēlǜ Pǒdé was appointed Commander of Nánjīng (*Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ*).
Yēlǜ Yáoshēng was appointed Grand Palace Chamberlain (*Dà Nèi Tìyǐn*).
Dà Rénjìng was appointed Right Administrator of the Central Platform Secretariat of Dōngjīng (*Dōngjīng Zhōngtái Shěng Yòu Píngzhāngshì*).
In the third year, spring, the first month, on *Bǐngwǔ* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
[the Emperor] went to Chángluò.
On *Dīngsì*,
Xíng Bàopǔ, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed Shàngshū, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites (*Lǐbù Shìláng*), and Chief Drafter (*Zhī Zhìgào*).

Liú Jǐng, Left Reminder (*Zuǒ Shíyí*) and Chief Drafter, and Niú Zàngyòng, Langzhong of the Ministry of Personnel (*Lìbù Lángzhōng*) and Chief Drafter, were both appointed Administrative Attendants (*Zhèngshì Shèrén*).
In the second month, on *Bǐngzǐ* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
Niú Zàngyòng was appointed Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Zhī Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì*).
In the third month, on *Yǐsì* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
the Bureau of Military Affairs reported that many Qìdān households subject to corvée labor (*yìhù*) were impoverished,
and requested that wealthy households replace them.
The Emperor consequently reviewed the registers of the various departments.
The Nièlà and Wūkuí departments had few households but heavy labor duties,
and they were consequently granted a partial exemption.
In summer, the fourth month, on *Yǐhài* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
sacrifices were offered at Mùyè Shān.
On *Rénwǔ*,
Zhào Kuāngfú, Governor of Fèngzhōu, was appointed Military Commissioner of Bǎojìng Jūn.
On *Guǐwèi*,
Wáng Tíngxù, Grand General of the Left Palace Guard (*Zuǒ Jiānmén Wèi Dà Jiāngjūn*), was appointed Military Commissioner of Fèngxiān Jūn.
Hán Déníng, Military Commissioner of Zhāngwǔ Jūn, was appointed Military Commissioner of Chóngyì Jūn.
In the fifth month, on *Rénzǐ*,
[the Emperor] returned to Shàngjīng.
On *Guǐyǒu*,

Imperial Uncle (*Guójiù*) Xiāo Dàoníng was appointed Administrator of the Affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery (*Tóng Píngzhāngshì*) and Manager of the Military and Civil Affairs of Shěnzhōu (*Zhī Shěnzhōu Jūnzhōu Shì*).
In the sixth month, on *Jiǎxū* (day 1) of the lunar calendar,
[the Emperor] went to Bǎipō.
The Empress Dowager personally resolved delayed legal cases.
On *Yǐhài*,
Wáng Xīyán, Military Commissioner of Guīyì Jūn, was appointed Military Commissioner of Xīngguó Jūn.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiǎchén (the first day of the month),
an imperial edict ordered all circuits (dào) to repair weapons and armor,
in preparation for the eastern campaign against Gāolì.
On jiǎyín,
the Emperor proceeded eastward.
On jiǎzǐ,
Lángjūn Bānnǎo was dispatched to bestow funeral articles upon Qínwáng Hán Kuāngsì.
On bǐngyín,
the imperial procession halted at Tǔhé.
Because the river had swelled rapidly,
an order was given to construct a boat bridge.
The next day, the Emperor traveled by palanquin (bù niǎn) to hold court and attend to governance.
The star of the elderly (Lǎorén Xīng) was sighted.
On dīngmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to inspect the weapons of the various armies in Dōngjīng and the roads for the eastern campaign.
Xiāo Dàoníng, Minister of State (Píngzhāngshì), was appointed Military Commissioner (Jié dùshǐ) of Zhaodé Army.

Guō Xí, Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Army, Grand Minister of Works (Shǒu Sīkōng), and concurrently Director of Political Affairs (Zhèngshì Lìng), was appointed Military Commissioner of Tiānpíng Army.

Liú Yángòu, Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Army, Acting Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent (Shǒu Tàizǐ Tàishī), and concurrently Director of Political Affairs, was appointed Military Commissioner of Yìchéng Army.
Shàngfù Qínwáng Hán Kuāngsì was posthumously granted the title Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Lìng).
Eighth month, on the day guǐyǒu (the first day of the month),
due to the saturated marshes (jùrù) of Liáozé,
the campaign against Gāolì was called off.
The Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Shǐ) Yēlǜ Xiézhěn was ordered to serve as Commander-in-Chief (Dū Tǒng),
and the Commandant (Dūwèi) Xiāo Kěndé was appointed Army Supervisor (Jiānjūn),
to lead troops to attack the Nǚzhí.
On dīngchǒu,
the procession reached ● Chéng.
On gēngchén,
the Emperor arrived at Xiǎnzhōu
and paid respects at Níngshén Diàn.
On xīnsì,
the Emperor visited Qiánzhōu
and viewed the new palace.
On guǐwèi,
paid respects at Qián Líng (the mausoleum).
On jiǎshēn,
officials of the Southern and Northern Administrations were ordered to inspect the woods and forests around the imperial mausoleums in groups,
and Qiánzhōu and Xiǎnzhōu were ordered to report the number of village temples (lǐshè) under their jurisdiction.
On bǐngxū,
the Xiángwěn of the Northern Píshì presented seven brave warriors.
On wùzǐ,
Lady Xiāo, the wife of the deceased Southern Administration King (Nányuàn Dàwáng) Xiélǐng Yǐlǐwǎn, petitioned, stating that she was unable to bury her husband.
An edict ordered the relevant authorities to provide assistance.
On gēngyín,
the Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Campaign reported that the roads were still sodden and muddy,
making immediate advance impossible.
An edict commanded them to wait until the swamps dried up before penetrating deep into the territory.
On guǐsì,
the Empress Dowager paid respects at Xiǎn Líng.
On gēngzǐ,
paid respects at Qián Líng.
On xīnchǒu,
the Emperor proceeded westward.
Intercalary ninth month, on guǐyǒu,
Xíng Bàopǔ was ordered to inspect and audit Xiǎn Líng.
On bǐngzǐ,
the procession reached the seashore.
On gēngchén,
the Double Ninth Festival (Chóngjiǔ) was held.
The court ascended Luòtuó Shān,
and chrysanthemum wine was bestowed upon the officials.
On xīnsì,
an imperial edict was issued instructing the generals and commanders of the Eastern Campaign
to advance and attack once the waters receded.
On bǐngshēn,
Zhúbùlǐ, the chancellor (zǎixiàng) of the Nǚzhí, came to offer tribute.
On wùxū,
the imperial procession halted at Dōnggǔ Shān.
On jǐhài,
Sùsā reported that the various tribes led by Zhúbùgū had reached the nearby swamp (diàn),
and Yílǐjǐn Yìlǔgū requested permission to engage in capturing and looting.
The Emperor said:
“These tribes have done no harm to the state.
Why should we capture and loot them?
This would merely stir up trouble.”
The request was denied.
Winter, eleventh month, on jiǎxū,
an edict ordered Wúwáng Shāolǐng to manage the funeral and sacrificial rites of Qínwáng Hán Kuāngsì.
On dīngchǒu,
an edict appointed Pó Dǐlǐ, the wife of the Army Supervisor of the Northeast Circuit, to care for and pacify the border populace.
On wùyín,
Princess Húgǔ Diǎn was bestowed with gold, silk, and artisans for her husband’s funeral.
On xīnmǎo,
Hán Déràng was appointed concurrently as Director of Political Affairs.
On guǐsì,
it was prohibited for cloths and silks exchanged in the market at the traveling palace (xíngzài) to be inconsistent with the standard measures.
On bǐngshēn,
Xiāo Tàlǎn and Púsà Nú, Commanders-in-Chief (Dū Tǒng) of the Eastern Campaign against the Nǚzhí,
submitted a report detailing the geography and products encountered along their route.
Basic Annals, Chapter 11: Shèngzōng II
Fourth year, spring, first month, on jiǎxū,
the Emperor watched fishing at Tǔhé.
Línyá Yēlǜ Móulǔgū and Xiāo Tàlǎn, Military Commissioner of Zhāngdé Army, reported their captives and spoils from the Eastern Campaign.
An edict was bestowed upon them offering praise and commendation.
On bǐngzǐ,
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Línyá Qíndé, among others, reported seizing over 100,000 captives, over 200,000 horses, and various goods from the campaign against the Nǚzhí.
On jǐmǎo,
the Emperor paid court to the Empress Dowager.
Pending lawsuits were decided.
On rénwǔ,

Xiézhěn, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Qíndé and Móulǔgū, both Línyá, Tàlǎn, Military Commissioner, Shìluó, Commander of the Forces (Tǒngjūn Shǐ), Mǒzhǐ, Attendant Counselor (Shìzhōng), Díliè, Army Supervisor of the Xī King’s establishment, and Ānjí, along with others, returned their armies after defeating the Nǚzhí.
Nílǐjí, an attendant, was dispatched with an edict to commend their achievements,
and they were personally received, comforted, and instructed.
Wine and fruit were bestowed upon them as reward.
On jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor visited Chángluò.
Second month, on rén yín,
Lǐ Jìzhōng, Commander-in-Chief of the Four Tribes (Sì Fān Dū Tǒngjūn), was appointed Acting Minister of Education (Jiǎnxiào Sītú) and Pillar of the State (Shàng Zhùguó).
On guǐmǎo,
Lǐ Jìqiān of Xīxià defected from Sòng and surrendered to the Liao.

He was appointed Military Commissioner of Dìngnán Army, Commissioner for Observation and Administration of Yín, Xià, Suī, and Yòu Prefectures, Grand Master of the Palace with Special Advancement (Tè Jìn Jiǎnxiào Tàishī), and Military Governor (Dūdū) of the various forces of Xiàzhōu.
Wǎnǐqǐyí, the chieftain of the Western Fān, was appointed Military Commissioner of Bǎodà Army and Commissioner for Observation and Administration of Fū, Fāng, and other prefectures.
On jiǎyín,
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, Xiāo Tàlǎn, Móulǔgū, and other tribal leaders came to court.
The ceremony of Yǐnzhì was performed,
and rewards were bestowed according to rank.
On bǐngyín,
the procession reached Niǎolǐ Jǐng.
Third month, on jiǎxū,
Yúyuè Xiūgē reported that Sòng had dispatched Cáo Bīn, Cuī Yànjìn, and Mǐ Xìn via the Xióngzhōu route,
Tián Zhòngjìn via the Fēihú route,
and Pān Měi and Yáng Jìyè via the Yànmén route to invade.
Qígōu, Zhuōzhōu, Gù'ān, and Xīnchéng had all fallen.
An edict commanded Pú Lǐng, Commissioner of Palace Affairs (Xuānhuī Shǐ), to hasten to Yānnán
to discuss military strategy with Xiūgē;
envoys were separately dispatched to conscript troops from various tribes to reinforce Xiūgē and attack the enemy;
Yēlǜ Mǒzhǐ, Resident General of Dōngjīng, was further dispatched to follow up with a large army,
and he was bestowed with a sword, granting him discretionary power to execute.
On yǐhài,
the Emperor announced his personal command of the campaign to the ancestral temples, mausoleums, mountains, and rivers.
On bǐngzǐ,
Yēlǜ Pǒdé, Commander of the Forces, defeated the Sòng army at Gù'ān.
Xiūgē cut off their provisions,
captured generals and officials,
and seized a great number of horses, oxen, and military equipment.
On gēngchén,
Zhào Yànzhāng, Prefect (Cìshǐ) of Huánzhōu, defected with the city
and joined Sòng.
On xīnsì,
Sòng troops entered Zhuōzhōu.
Zhào Xīzàn, Deputy Military Commissioner of Shùnyì Army, defected with Shuòzhōu
and joined Sòng.
At this time, the Emperor and the Empress Dowager were stationed at Tuóluō Kǒu.
An edict hurried the troops from the Eastern Campaign to come as reinforcement.
On rénwǔ,
an edict ordered Línyá Qíndé to garrison the coast of Píngzhōu with troops in preparation against Sòng.
The Military Commissioner of Píngzhōu, Dílǐgū, was simultaneously informed:
if Qíndé had not yet arrived,
send someone to urge him to depart;
if horses were scarce, requisition civilian horses;
if armor was lacking,
take it from the armor workshops in Xiǎnzhōu.
On guǐwèi,
the Liáo army battled Tián Zhòngjìn of Sòng at Fēihú,
suffering a defeat.
Dà Péngyì, Defender-in-Chief (Fángyù Shǐ) of Jìzhōu, Mǎ Yūn, Prefect of Kāngzhōu,
and Hé Wàntōng, Commander of the Cavalry (Mǎjūn Zhǐhuīshǐ), were captured.
On dīnghài,
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Administration, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the forces in Shānxī.
Pú Lǐng, Commissioner of Palace Affairs of the Northern Administration, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Campaign,
to serve as deputy to Yúyuè Xiūgē.
Ài Zhèng, Military Commissioner of Zhāngguó Army, and Sòng Xióng, Judge of the Surveillance Commissioner (Guānchá Pànguān), defected with Yìngzhōu
and joined Sòng.
On gēngyín,
Ālà, Envoy of the Flying Dragon (Fēilóng Shǐ), and Yàdágē, a civil official (Wénbān Lì), were dispatched to inspect horses to supply the various armies that had advanced first.
An edict commanded the Commandant (Fùmǎ Dūwèi) Xiāo Jìyuǎn to take charge of them.
On xīnmǎo,

Lǚ Xíngdé, Commander-in-Chief of the Cavalry and Infantry of Wǔdìng Army and Defender-in-Chief of Yǐngzhōu, Zhāng Jìcóng, Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and Liú Zhījìn, Commander-in-Chief of the Cavalry, along with others, defected at Fēihú
and joined Sòng.
On guǐsì,
Línyá Móulǔgū was bestowed with four flags and drums and one sword,
and ordered to lead the elite troops of the Imperial Guards south to assist Xiūgē.
On bǐngshēn,
Mù Chāo, Commander-in-Chief of the Infantry, defected with Língqiū
and joined Sòng.

An edict dispatched an envoy to present a secret instruction to Xiézhěn, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and the seal of Zhāngguó Army Military Commissioner to Sháowā, urging them to proceed with the campaign.
In summer, the fourth month, *jǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
The Imperial train reached the northern suburbs of Nánjīng.
*Gēngzǐ* day,
Tìyǐn Yáoshēng and the Southwestern Director of Pacification Hán Déwēi submitted victory reports.
*Xīnchǒu* day,
Sòng general Pān Měi captured Yúnzhōu.
*Rényín* day,
Mòzhī, Móulǔgū, Qíndé, and others were dispatched to lead auxiliary forces to assist Xiūgē,
and were also bestowed banners, drums, and the *Sháowā* seal to commend and encourage the generals and officers.
*Guǐmǎo* day,
Xiūgē again submitted a victory report.
The Emperor offered wine and dried meat to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth,
and led his officials to offer congratulations to the Huáng Tàihòu.
An imperial edict ordered Qíndé to return to his camp.
*Bǐngwǔ* day,
Pǒdé presented the tally of the captured armor and weapons.
*Wùshēn* day,
The Army Supervisor and Grand Commissioner of the Department of Palace Affairs, Pú Líng, reported that the enemy forces had retreated,
and Xī King Chóuníng, Northern Great King Púnúníng, Director of Armies Pǒdé, and others pursued them with troops,
and all won victories.
Chǎngshǐ Qíndé was sent carrying an imperial edict to commend them,
and an edict also ordered Shìzhōng Mòzhī to command all armies and proceed to the temporary residence.
Jìngbù Bù Military Governor Hélúdǔ and Huáng Píshì Xiángwěn Jiělǐ, among others, each presented the captured arms and armor.
Another edict ordered the crack cavalry from the two departments to proceed to Yùzhōu,
to assist Tàlǎn.
Hénɡzhànɡ Lánɡjūn Lǎojūnnú led the various *lángjūn* (gentlemen) to patrol north of Jūyōng.
General Huàgē commanded the forces of Píngzhōu,
Hénɡzhànɡ Lánɡjūn Núgē was appointed Director of the Huáng Píshì,
Lánɡjūn Yèlǐ was appointed Director of the Northern Prefecture,
each leading infantry to Yùzhōu to assist Xiézhěn.
*Gēngxū* day,
Xiézhěn was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Armies of All Circuits,
Vice Commander of Tàlǎn’s Armies,
and Director of Dízǐ,
replacing Shànbǔ and Hán Déwēi.
*Guǐchǒu* day,
Because Ài Zhèng, Zhào Xīzàn, the Vice Military Governors of Yīngzhōu and Shuòzhōu, Xī Army Junior Officer Àilǐxiá, and Bóhǎi Junior Officer Guànhǎi rebelled and defected to Sòng,
their family property and dependents were confiscated,
and distributed among the meritorious generals and officers.
Sòng generals Cáo Bīn and Mǐ Xìn crossed the Jùmǎ Hé northward,
and confronted Yúyuè Xiūgē,
challenging him to battle.
Their camps stretched six or seven *lǐ* long, arrayed North to South.
At that time, the Emperor was 50 *lǐ* east of Zhuōzhōu.
*Jiǎyín* day,
An edict commanded Yúyuè Xiūgē, Xī King Chóuníng, Grand Commissioner Pú Líng, and the two Southern and Northern Kings to strictly guard the waterways,
lest enemy troops manage to secretly reach Zhuōzhōu.
*Yǐmǎo* day,
Xiūgē and others defeated the Sòng army,
presenting the captured equipment, armor, and wealth.
An edict was issued bestowing commendation.
Yùzhōu Left and Right Commanders Lǐ Cúnzhāng and Xǔ Yànqīn, among others, killed Military Governor Xiāo Chuòlǐ,
captured the City Supervising Commissioner and Tóngzhōu Military Governor Gěng Shàozhōng,
and rebelled with the city,
defecting to Sòng.
*Bǐngchén* day,
Zhuōzhōu was recovered.
A report was made to Heaven and Earth.
*Wùwǔ* day,
The Emperor reached the northern marsh of the Shāgū Hé,
summoning Línyá Qíndé to discuss military affairs.
All generals and officers came to present their captives and gains.
Xī King Chóuníng and the two Southern and Northern Kings led the generals and officers of their departments to attend court.
The Emperor used a spontaneously fallen bustard presented by the chamber attendant Niánmǐlǐ to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
*Jǐwèi* day,
Xiūgē and Pú Líng came to attend court.
An edict ordered the Three Departments to supply summer clothing cloth to the front lines.
*Gēngshēn* day,
The Emperor paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
*Xīnyǒu* day,
The grand army reached Gù'ān.
*Rénxū* day,
Gù'ān city was besieged.
Director of Armies Pǒdé was the first to scale the wall,
and the city was subsequently breached.
Vast numbers of captives and spoils were taken.
Residents who had previously been captured,
were ordered to be redeemed using state property.
*Jiǎzǐ* day,
The officers and soldiers who attacked the city were rewarded according to their ranks.
In the fifth month, *gēngwǔ* day,
the Liáo forces battled Cáo Bīn and Mǐ Xìn at Qīgōu Guān,
severely defeating them.
They were pursued to the Jùmǎ Hé,
where the number of those drowned was uncountable;
the remaining troops fled to Gāoyáng,
where they were again attacked by the Liáo forces.
Tens of thousands died,
abandoning spears and armor like hills.
Several tens of thousands of transport laborers were hidden in the empty city of Qīgōu.
They were surrounded.
*Rénshēn* day,
Due to the birthday of the Huáng Tàihòu,
they were released and allowed to return.
*Guǐyǒu* day,
The troops returned in triumph,
reaching Xīnchéng.
Xiūgē and Pú Líng reported that all Sòng soldiers who fled were executed.
*Jiǎxū* day,
Because of the military victory,
envoys were dispatched to inform all circuits, capitals, and garrisons.
*Dīngchǒu* day,
An edict was issued to all generals and officers,
stipulating that merits be assessed and rewards granted,
without any falsehood.
*Jǐmǎo* day,
The Imperial train reached south of Gù'ān,
sacrificing a black ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.
*Gēngchén* day,
The captured Sòng men were used to shoot the 'ghost arrow'.
An edict ordered Xiángwěn Páiyà to lead the forces of the Hónɡyì Gōnɡ and the four armies—Southern Píshì, Northern Píshì, Lánɡjūn, and Zhuàilá—to the border of Yīngzhōu and Shuòzhōu,
to jointly defend against the Sòng troops in Shānxī who had not yet retreated, along with Tìyǐn Yáoshēng and Director of Pacification Hán Déwēi.
*Xīnsì* day,
Yáoshēng's army was sent to Shānxī.
*Rénwǔ* day,
The Emperor returned to Nánjīng.
*Guǐwèi* day,
Xiūgē, Chóuníng, and Púnúníng presented their captives and gains.
Xiézhěn sent Aide Púgū to report the recapture of Yùzhōu,
where over 20,000 heads were severed.
Following up on the victory, they captured Língqiū and Fēihú.
Púgū was rewarded with wine and silver vessels.
*Bǐngxū* day,
The Emperor held court at Yuánhé Diàn,
giving a grand banquet for the generals and officers who had followed the army.
Xiūgē was enfeoffed as Sòng Guówáng.
Pú Líng, Chóuníng, Púnúníng, and all other meritorious generals and officers were promoted in rank and rewarded accordingly.
*Dīnghài* day,
The Emperor departed Nánjīng.
An edict commanded Xiūgē to prepare equipment and armor,
and store grain,
awaiting a major Southern campaign in the autumn.
*Wùzǐ* day,
Xiézhěn reported that the Sòng army had again besieged Yùzhōu,
and that he had defeated them.
An edict ordered troops to be granted to Yáoshēng, Hán Déwēi, and others.
*Rénchén* day,
Due to Sòng forces reaching Píngzhōu,
and Yáoshēng and Hán Déwēi failing to pursue and kill all of them,
an imperial edict was issued criticizing and rebuking them.
It further instructed,
that those who occupied cities and had not yet surrendered,
must be completely surrounded and slaughtered,
allowing none to escape.
*Guǐsì* day,
The surrendered soldiers from the front lines were distributed among the imperial retinue.
*Yǐwèi* day,
Pǒdé and the various generals, officers, and soldiers were rewarded.
In the sixth month, *wùxū* day, the first day of the month,
an edict summoned Hán Déwēi to the capital,
and Director of Armies Pǒdé was promoted to Auxiliary Grand Preceptor.
*Jiǎchén* day,
An edict commanded the Nánjīng Resident General Xiūgē to dispatch artillery men westward to assist Xiézhěn.
*Yǐsì* day,
As Yílìbì Zhílǐgǔ’s department transported supplies to the traveling palace,
marching 50 *lǐ* per day in the heat,
the men and horses became exhausted.
An envoy was dispatched to reprimand him.
*Dīngwèi* day,
The Emperor crossed Jūyōng Guān.
*Rénzǐ* day,
The Nánjīng Resident General reported that the people’s annual payment of salt and iron money to the Three Departments,
when converted to silk, was less than its actual value.
An edict ordered the amount to be increased.
*Jiǎyín* day,
Xiézhěn reported the recapture of Huánzhōu.
*Yǐmǎo* day,
The Huáng Tàifēi, the various kings, and princesses welcomed the Emperor on the ridge,
and an edict ordered the imperial tent pitched beside the road.
A portrait of Jǐngzōng was displayed.
The Emperor led his accompanying officials in offering wine,
and the captives and spoils were displayed before the portrait.
Subsequently, a grand banquet was held.
*Wùwǔ* day,
The Emperor visited Liángxíng.
The captives were distributed among the Imperial relatives and wet nurses.
*Jǐwèi* day,
News arrived regarding the envoy sent to convey imperial instructions to the Huíɡǔ.
Hélièɡě Guódùlǐ, Yàlǐ, and others were detained by Zhúbùgū.
An edict commanded Sùsā to immediately bestow money and silks upon Zhúbùgū,
explaining the Imperial Court’s intention to welcome those from afar,
and thus the envoys were able to proceed.
*Guǐhài* day,
Military Governor Hán Pígē, Academician of the Hanlin Academy Xínɡ Bàopǔ, and others were appointed Commissioners for Imperial Edict and Pacification in Yúnzhōu.
*Bǐngyín* day,
The captives taken by Grand Commandant Wáng Bā were distributed among Consort Zhào Fēi and Yúyuè Díniǎn Yǐlǐwǎn.
Shūmìshǐ Xiézhěn sent Shìyù Nièlǐdǐ and Gànqíngē to report the recovery of Shuòzhōu,
and the capture of the Sòng general Yáng Jìyè,
and to present the captured seals, ribbons, imperial patents, and edicts belonging to the officers;
Nièlǐdǐ and the others were bestowed wine and silver vessels.
On the day Xīnsì,
the victory was announced to Heaven and Earth.
Two hundred forty people who surrendered from Sòng were distributed as gifts to the attending ministers.
Furthermore, because many enemies had been slain,
an edict ordered that Buddhist rites be held for one month at Kāilóng Sì in Shàngjīng,
and food be provided to ten thousand
monks.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Xiézhěn reported: The main army reached Wèizhōu,
and encamped west of the city.
Having received intelligence reports,
that the enemy troops were about to arrive,
they set up an ambush to await them.
When the enemy arrived,
they released the troops to counter-attack,
pursuing the fleeing and chasing the routed,
reaching Fēihú Kǒu.
They then pressed their advantage, advancing westward with beating drums,
entering Huánzhōu,
killing over a thousand defending officials and soldiers.
The Sòng general Yáng Jìyè was initially proud of his bravery and prowess;
he was called Yáng Wúdí (Yang the Invincible).
He held several northern prefectures, including Yún and Shuò.
At this point,
he led his troops thirty *lǐ* south of Shuòzhōu,
reaching Lángyá Cūn.
Disliking the name,
he did not advance;
but his attendants strongly requested it,
so he proceeded.
He encountered Xiézhěn,
and the ambushes arose from all four sides.
He was struck by a stray arrow,
fell from his horse, and was captured.
His wounds became infected, and he refused to eat;
he died after three days.
His head was subsequently boxed and presented.
An edict ordered Xiángwěn Xiámàishì to transmit his head to Yuè Xiūgē,
to be displayed to all the armies,
and further, the victory at Shuòzhōu was to be proclaimed to the generals and officials of Nánjīng and Píngzhōu.
Thereafter, the Sòng defenders of Yún, Yìng, and other prefectures,
hearing of Jìyè's death,
all abandoned their cities and fled.
In the eighth month, on the first day Dīngyǒu,
six officials of the Xiānlítàlǎn Guān were established,
to govern those belonging to the palace registry among the Gǔlǐ, Nǚzhí, Dílièyú, and other tribes.
Běidàwáng Púnúníng was appointed Supervisor of the Five Prefectures of Shānhòu.
On the day Yǐsì,
Hán Déràng reported that concerning the prefectures and districts plundered by Sòng forces,
the crops belonging to the displaced populace,
should be harvested by recruited people,
and half of the yield be given to those who harvested them.
This was approved.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiézhěn returned from the campaign,
and presented the captives.
On the day Jǐwèi,
based on the advice of Shì Fǎng and Hán Déràng,
the taxes and levies for the current year in Shānxī were remitted.
An edict commanded that the merits and faults of all generals and officers in Shānxī be evaluated, and they be rewarded or punished accordingly.
Yǐshì Zhàng Zǎixiàng Ānníng, whose merits and faults balanced out,
had one copy of his official patent revoked;
Dìjū Bù Jiédùshǐ Fónú was punished with fifty strokes of the rod.
Tìyǐn Yáoshēng, Zhuáilá Chuāliè, Shuòzhōu Jiédùshǐ Shènsī, Yìngzhōu Jiédùshǐ Gǔzhǐ, Yúnzhōu Jiédùshǐ Huàgē, Jūnxiào Lǐ Yuándí, Wèizhōu Jiédùshǐ Fóliú, Dūjiān Cuī Qí, and Liú Jìchēn,
all had their offices stripped for fleeing upon hearing of the enemy;
Chuāliè was further assigned to perform penal servitude in his native region;
Wáng Liù, Commander of the Guójìu Army, was punished with fifty strokes of the rod.
On the day Rénxū,
the officers under Xiézhěn, having previously defeated the Nǚzhí,
and later achieving victory against Sòng,
were ranked according to their merit and granted increased rewards.
On the day Guǐhài,
Xiézhěn was given the additional title of Shǒu Tàibǎo.
In the ninth month, on the first day Bǐngyín,
the Imperial Consorts and those above them presented gifts to the Empress-Designate,
offering clothing, materials, camels, and horses,
to assist with the distribution of gifts during the family gathering.
On the day Jiǎxū,
they halted at Hēihé.
For the Double Ninth Festival (Chóng Jiǔ), they ascended a high point on the southern mound of Gāoshuǐ,
and offered sacrifices to Heaven.
Chrysanthemum wine was bestowed upon the wives of the attending ministers.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
they halted north of Héyáng.
On the day Wùyín,
the official wives (both inner and outer court) presented gifts for the family gathering ceremony.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Empress Xiāo Shì was formally installed.
On the day Bǐngxū,
they halted at Rúzhōu.
Since the main army was about to campaign south,
an edict was issued dispatching Píshì Xiángwěn Qǐdí and Lángjūn Zhuáilá to proceed immediately to their respective armies to repair armor and weapons.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Běidàwáng Púnúníng was summoned to the Emperor's temporary residence (Xíngzàisuǒ).
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
The Empress Dowager performed the Regeneration Ceremony (Zàishēng Lǐ).
In Winter, the tenth month, on the first day Bǐngshēn,
the Dǎngxiàng and Zǔbǔ sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
The Empress Dowager again performed the Regeneration Ceremony (Zàishēng Lǐ),
offering sacrifices to the spirits and praying for blessings on the Emperor.
On the day Jǐhài,
Wúliú, Lángjūn of the Yǐshì Royal Tent, was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
Zhèngshì Lìng Shì Fǎng reported that since the Sòng troops had been in the four prefectures of Shānxī,
the people had dispersed,
and bandits were widespread.
He requested that the responsible authorities be ordered to suppress them.
Xīnzhōu Jiédùshǐ Púdǎlǐ was ordered to select men to patrol and inspect the various routes.
Hégézhǐlǐ, Lángjūn of the Běidàwáng Tent, reported seventeen crimes committed by the King of that prefecture, Púnúníng.
An edict ordered Héngzhàng Tàibǎo Hégúodǐ to investigate the case.
Púnúníng confessed to eleven of the crimes,
and was released after receiving twenty strokes of the rod.
Hégézhǐlǐ also confessed to six counts of false accusation.
An order was given to thoroughly evaluate his guilt and punish him.
Zhīshì Qíndé was implicated and punished,
with one hundred blows of the heavy stick,
and dismissed from office.
On the day Jiǎchén,
they exited Jūyōng Guān.
On the day Yǐsì,
an edict ordered that as the various capitals and garrisons mobilized their troops in succession,
all minor affairs were temporarily suspended from judicial review.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhuáilá were dispatched along the border to scout and observe.
On the day Xīnhài,
The tents of the Imperial Clan were ordered to be stationed at Yánfāng Diàn in Dōngjīng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict on a placard was delivered to Yuè Xiūgē,
proclaiming the southern campaign to the six prefectures south of the Jùmǎ Hé.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
The Emperor visited Nánjīng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
based on the request of Nányuàn Dàwáng Liúníng,
the taxes and levies for the current year owed by the people of the Southern Chancellery region were remitted.
On the day Rénxū,
Silver furs, blue furs, and various other goods were bestowed upon the metropolitan officials, monks, Daoists, and elders.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
The Emperor and his ministers divided into teams to play *jījú* (polo).
In the eleventh month, on the day bǐngyín, the first day of the month,
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
On the day gēngwǔ,
Hán Déràng, Minister of Political Affairs (Zhèngshì Lìng), was appointed acting Minister of Works (Sītú).
On the day rénshēn,
because the tax collection at Gǔběi, Sōngtíng, and Yúguān was illegal,
causing obstruction to merchants and travelers,
envoys were dispatched to interrogate the matter.
The Nǚzhí requested to join the campaign with their troops;
permission was granted.
On the day guǐyǒu,
the Emperor attended the main palace (Zhèngdiàn)
and greatly rewarded the generals and officers of the southern expedition.
On the day bǐngzǐ,
during the southern campaign,
they camped at Xiádǐguō.
The Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) personally inspected the supplies and armor.
On the day dīngchǒu,
Xiūgē was made Supreme Commander of the Vanguard (Xiānfēng Dūtǒng).
On the day wùyín,
the winter solstice occurred.
The Emperor led his attending ministers to offer sacrifices to the imperial portrait (Yùróng) of Jǐngzōng.
On the day xīnsì,
an edict ordered Běi Dàwáng Púnú Níng to reside in Fèngshèng Zhōu.
Public affairs concerning the five prefectures west of the mountains (Shānxī Wǔ Zhōu Gōngshì)
were henceforth to be decided jointly by him and the Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) Púdǎlǐ.
On the day guǐwèi,
sacrifices were made to the sun and moon,
praying for good fortune for the Commandant-Escort (Fùmǎ Dūwèi) Qíndé.
On the day yǐyǒu,
Superintendents (Jiān) were established for all the tribes (Zhū Bù).
Orders were given that the troops under their command must maintain their respective camps and formations,
and not intermingle.
On the day bǐngxū,
Móulǔgū and Xiāo Jìyuǎn were dispatched to patrol the border.
The captured Sòng soldiers were used for shooting the "ghost arrow" ritual (shè guǐjiàn).
On the day dīnghài,
Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with a black ox and a white horse.
On the day xīnmǎo,
they camped at Báifótǎ Chuān.
A domesticated fox that had shed its fur naturally was captured,
which was taken as an auspicious omen,
and sacrifices were made to Heaven and Earth.
An edict commanded Commandant-Escort Xiāo Jìyuǎn, Línyá Móulǔgū, Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Línbā, and others to firmly guard the borderlands,
and prevent the infiltration of spies.
Within the army, horses were not allowed to be ridden without reason,
nor were the troops permitted to damage the mulberries and fruits in the southern territory.
On the day rénchén,
they arrived at Tángxīng Xiàn.
At that time, the Sòng army was encamped north of the Hūtuó Qiáo.
Selected generals were sent to shoot arrows indiscriminately at them.
The bridge could not be defended,
so they advanced and burned the bridge.
On the day guǐsì,
they crossed the Shā Hé.
Xiūgē arrived to discuss military affairs.
Běi Píshì Xiángwěn Pái'yà presented two Sòng spies he had captured.
The Emperor bestowed clothing and goods upon them,
and ordered them to return and persuade Tàizhōu to submit.
Lú Bǔgǔ, Military Governor of the Chǔtè Bù, and Metropolitan Superintendent (Dūjiān) Yēlǜ Pàn fought the Sòng army at Tàizhōu,
and were unsuccessful.
On the day jiǎwǔ,
they sacrificed to the Páolù Shén (Spotted Deer God).
Because Lú Bǔgǔ fled during the battle,
one degree of his official appointment (Gàoshēn) was revoked.
His Judicial Administrator (Pànguān) and Metropolitan Superintendent were each beaten with the staff.
Langjūn Zhuáilā Shuānggǔlǐ encountered the Sòng vanguard at Wàngdū.
He captured nine of their soldiers,
and seized eleven armored horses (Jiǎmǎ).
He was rewarded with wine and silver vessels.
On the day yǐwèi,
an edict informing all the armies of the crimes committed by Lú Bǔgǔ and others was issued.
Yùzhǎn Lángjūn Huàgē was temporarily appointed Military Governor of the Chǔtè Bù.
Héngzhàng Lángjūn Fúliú was made Metropolitan Superintendent,
replacing Lú Bǔgǔ.
Táowèi, acting commander of the Imperial Maternal Uncle Army (Guójìu Jūn), requested the establishment of two commanders to lead the scattered troops.
An edict appointed Lángjūn Shìyīn, Pǒdé, and others to these roles.
The Military Governor of Zhāngdé Jūn,
Xiāo Tàlǎn, and General Dízi were ordered to capture territory along the eastern route.
An edict commanded Xiūgē, Pái'yà, and others to discuss military affairs.
In the twelfth month, on the day jǐhài,
Xiūgē defeated the Sòng army at Wàngdū,
and dispatched a messenger to present the captives.
On the day rényín,
they set up camp north of the Hūtuó.
An edict commanded Xiūgē to use cavalry to cut off the Sòng troops,
preventing them from entering Xíngzhōu.
Grand Preceptor (Tàishī) Wáng Liù was ordered to carefully scout and observe.
On the day guǐmǎo,
Junior Officer (Xiǎoxiào) Hézhǔ encountered Sòng supplies.
He led his troops, killed and captured many,
and also burned their fodder and grain.
On the day jiǎchén,
an edict commanded the Nán Dàwáng (Southern Great King) and Xiūgē to combine forces and advance in attack.
Chancellor (Zǎixiàng) Ānníng led the Dílí Bù and the Sānkè Jūn to form the rearguard.
The Emperor led the main army and battled the Sòng generals Liú Tíngràng and Lǐ Jìngyuán at Mòzhōu,
defeating them.
On the day yǐsì,
the Sòng generals Hè Lìngtú, Yáng Chóngjìn, and others were captured.
Imperial Maternal Uncle Xiángwěn Tàliègē and Palace Commissioner (Gōngshǐ) Xiāo Dǎlǐ died.
On the day bǐngwǔ,
an edict summoned Xiūgē and others into the inner hall (Nèidiàn),
and rewarded them with wine.
On the day dīngwèi,
a victory mound (Jīngguān) was constructed.
The Southern Capital (Nánjīng) Imperial Guards were again deployed to attack Yángtuán Chéng.
The defending general surrendered the city.
An edict prohibited pillaging.
On the day jǐyǒu,
they camped at Shényú Cūn.
An edict commanded the reporting of the numbers of millet, wheat, weapons, and armor found in Yángtuán Chéng.
On the day xīnhài,
Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with two animals, one black and one white.
On the day guǐchǒu,
Fèngmǔ Zhèn was captured,
and widespread looting and taking of captives was allowed.
On the day bǐngchén,
Xíngzhōu surrendered.
On the day dīngsì,
Shēnzhōu was captured.
Because it had not surrendered immediately,
the defending general and those below him were executed,
and the troops were allowed to pillage extensively.
Lǐ Jìqiān led five hundred cavalry out of the fort (Fāsài),
requesting a marriage alliance with the Great State,
and wishing to eternally serve as a protective vassal.

An edict conferred the title Princess Yìchéng (Yìchéng Gōngzhǔ) upon Tīng, the daughter of the Military Governor of the Princely Tent (Wángzǐ Zhàng Jiédùshǐ) Yēlǜ Xiāng, and married her off (to Lǐ Jìqiān).
Three thousand bolts (pǐ) of horses were bestowed.
Annals, Chapter 12: Shèngzōng III
The fifth year, Spring, first month, on the day yǐchǒu,
Dōngchéng Xiàn was defeated,
and the troops were allowed to pillage extensively.
On the day dīngmǎo,
they camped at Wén'ān.
A messenger was sent to persuade them to surrender,
but they refused.
They were subsequently attacked and defeated.
All their able-bodied men were killed,
and their elderly and children were captured.
On the day wùyín,
the Emperor returned to the Southern Capital (Nánjīng).
On the day jǐmǎo,
the Emperor held court at Yuánhé Diàn,
and greatly rewarded the officers and soldiers.
On the day rénchén,
he proceeded to Huálín and Tiānzhù.
Second month, on the day jiǎwǔ, the first day of the month,
he arrived back from Tiānzhù.
Third month, on the day guǐhài, the first day of the month,
he visited Chángchūn Gōng.
He enjoyed viewing flowers and fishing.
Peonies (mǔdān) were generously bestowed upon his close ministers,
and joyous banquets lasted for several days.
On the day dīngchǒu,
because Zhuáilā Jiělǐ, who served under the Dìjū Bù, had performed meritorious service in scouting,
he was ordered to join the Yùzhǎn Lángjūn rank of attendants (Qíhòu).
Summer, fourth month, on the day guǐsì, the first day of the month,
he proceeded to the Southern Capital (Nánjīng).
On the day dīngyǒu,
the Emperor led the hundred officials in conferring the exalted title upon the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu), calling her Ruìdé Shénlüè Yìngyùn Qǐhuà Chéngtiān Huáng Tàihòu.
After the ceremony was complete,
the assembly of ministers conferred the exalted title upon the Emperor, calling him Zhìdé Guǎngxiào Zhāoshèng Tiānfǔ Huángdì.
On the day wùxū,
an edict commanded the relevant authorities (Yǒusī) to list the veteran officials with merit,
and grant them special favors according to their ranks.
On the day guǐchǒu,
the ice wells (bīngjǐng) were opened to cool the summer heat.
Sixth month, on the day rénchén, the first day of the month,
the great ministers were summoned to resolve general administrative affairs (shùzhèng).
On the day bǐngshēn,
Yēlǜ Sū was appointed Magistrate (Cìshǐ) of a distant prefecture (Yáojùn).
Autumn, seventh month, on the day wùchén,
Sāgélǐ, Military Governor of the Nièlā Bù, having governed beneficently,
the people requested that he remain.
This was permitted.
In this month,
the Emperor hunted in Píngdì Sōnglín (Pine Forest of the Flat Land).
Ninth month, on the day bǐngxū,
he proceeded to the Southern Capital (Nánjīng).
He resided there through the winter.
Sixth year, Spring, first month, on the day gēngshēn,
he went to Huálín and Tiānzhù.
Second month, on the day dīngwèi,
Chóuníng, King of the Xī, killed the innocent man Lǐ Hào.
The authorities concerned (Suǒsī) discussed the severity (of the noble's crime),
and requested that his punishment be waived,
ordering him instead to pay money to support Hào's family.
This was accepted.
On the day jiǎyín,
Liú Jīng, Military Governor of the Dàtóng Jūn and Concurrent Administrator of Governmental Affairs (Tóng Píngzhāng Zhèngshì), retired from office.
Third month, on the day jǐwèi,
Xiūgē submitted a memorial regarding the affairs of Sòng.
The Emperor personally reviewed it.
On the day bǐngyín,
Zhào Zōngdé, Qí Tài, Wáng Shǒupíng, Shào Qí, and Yán Méi of the Directorate of Astronomy (Sītiān) were rewarded because, having followed the campaigns for four years,
their forecasts regarding celestial phenomena had often been verified.
Gifts were bestowed according to their differences in rank.
On the day guǐwèi,
Lǐ Jìqiān dispatched an envoy to present tribute.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi (28),
The Emperor proceeded to Nánjīng.
On the day Dīngyǒu (34),
Húlishì violently assaulted Hán Déràng, causing him to fall from his horse.
The Empress Dowager was enraged,
and had him killed.
On the day Wùxū (35),
The Emperor proceeded to the residence of the King of Sòng, Xiūgē.
The fifth month, on the day Guǐhài (60),
Yēlǜ Shā, the Chancellor of the Southern Administration, died.
The intercalary month, on the day Bǐngxū (23), the first day of the month,
Fèngshèng Zhōu reported that the Jīnlíng Gé (Golden Bell Pavilion) constructed by Tàizǔ had collapsed,
and requested further repairs.
An imperial decree stated that due to the southern campaign,
fearing the people would be overly burdened,
it should be attended to after the army returned.
On the day Rén'yín (39),
The Āsàlán Huíhú (Arslan Uyghurs) came to offer tribute.
On the day Jiǎyín (51),
The Wūwēi Yújué Department stated that the sable and squirrel furs offered as annual tribute were not native products,
but were all traded from elsewhere to be presented,
and requested a change in tribute items.
An imperial decree ordered that henceforth, they only present cattle and horses.
The sixth month, on the day Guǐhài (60),
Ālàhuǎng, the Grand Guardian (Tàibǎo) of the Dǎngxiàng, came to court,
offering local products as tribute.
On the day Yǐchǒu (2),
An edict was issued to the troops and horses of all circuits (Dào) to prepare siege equipment for the southern campaign.
On the day Yǐyǒu (22),
Yílíjǐn Ālǔbó escorted Cáo Gōngshùn, the Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Shāzhōu, back.
He was granted the title Yúyuè.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Bǐngxū (23),
The Emperor observed the market.
On the day Jǐhài (36),
Hán Déwēi, the Commissioner of Pacification of the Southern Front (Nánmiàn Zhāotǎoshǐ), was dispatched to suppress the various barbarians (Fān) of Hé and Huáng who had violated imperial orders.
Warhorses were bestowed upon the armies under Xiūgē and Páiyà.
On the day Jǐyǒu (46),
The imperial traveling lodge was established at the Luò Hé.
On the day Rénzǐ (49),
Hán Déwēi was promoted to Grand Master of Court (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī), concurrently Administrator of Government (Zhèngshì Lìng), and Chancellor (Ménxià Píngzhāngshì).

Yēlǜ Mǒzhī, the Governor of Dōngjīng (Dōngjīng Liúshǒu) concurrently serving as Grand Mentor (Shìzhōng) and Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery (Qīshuǐ Jùnwáng), was made Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Army (Dàtóng Jūn Jiédùshǐ).
On the day Guǐchǒu (50),
Páiyà requested the establishment of more postal stations in Zhuōzhōu.
The eighth month, on the day Bǐngchén (53),
The Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with a black bull and a white horse.
On the day Wùwǔ (55),
Xiūgē, along with Páiyà and Niǎolǐhé, captured prisoners.
Upon reaching Yìzhōu,
they encountered Sòng troops,
killed their commander, and returned.
On the day Gēngshēn (57),
The Emperor proceeded to the hot springs at Lí Yuán.
On the day Guǐhài (60),
As they were about to attack Sòng,
envoys were sent to sacrifice at Mùyè Shān.
On the day Dīngchǒu (14),
The seaside Nǚzhí sent the envoy Sùlǔlǐ to court.
Sùsāgē, the Xiángwěn overseeing the Northwest Circuit, having campaigned against the Zhélì and Zhùlǐ Departments,
presented the captured prisoners and spoils.
Xiāo Qíndé, the Línyá of the Eastern Circuit, and Shí Lǎo, the Commander (Tǒngjūn), having defeated the Nǚzhí forces,
presented captured prisoners.
Yēlǜ Mǒzhī, the Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Army, reported that due to frost and drought this year, there was a shortage of food,
and requested raising the price when converting cash to grain (sù),
to benefit the poor citizens.
An imperial decree assented to this.
The coastal Nǚzhí sent Sīlǔlǐ to submit local tribute.
The ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn (33),
Huàgē and Zhúbùgū Chōnggǔlǐ came to offer tribute.
Xiūgē sent Xiángwěn Yìdélǐ to present the captured Sòng spies.
On the day Dīngyǒu (34),
The Empress Dowager proceeded to Hán Déràng’s tent,
bestowing generous rewards,
and ordered the attending officials to divide into groups for a game of *Shuānglù* (backgammon) to enjoy themselves fully.
On the day Wùxū (35),
The Emperor proceeded to Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐhài (36),
Rites were performed at the temple of Emperor Tàizōng.
Táng Yuándé was appointed Military Commissioner of Fènglín Army (Fènglín Jūn Jiédùshǐ).
On the day Guǐmǎo (40),
Sacrifices were offered to the flags and drums before campaigning south.
On the day Gēngxū (47),
The army halted at Zhuōzhōu,
shooting silk letters into the city advising surrender.
The city did not listen.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐmǎo (52),
troops were deployed to attack the city from four sides.
Only when the city was breached did it surrender.
The Emperor then pacified and instructed the populace.
Xiāo Qíndé, the Imperial Son-in-Law (Fùmǎ), and Tàilǎn, the Grand Preceptor (Tàishī), were both struck by stray arrows.
Qíndé was carried in the imperial carriage back to camp.
Hearing that the Sòng forces had retreated,
Xiézhěn and Páiyà were sent to pursue and attack them,
and inflicted a great defeat.
On the day Wùwǔ (55),
Shāduī Post Station was attacked,
and captured.
On the day Jǐsì (6),
The Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with black and white sheep.
On the day Gēngwǔ (7),
The surrendered Sòng troops were divided into seven commands,
named the Guīshèng Jūn (Army Returning to the Sage).
On the day Rénshēn (9),
Mǎ Déchén, Military Advisor and Scholar of Xuānzhèng Hall, stated that while the Sòng army had been persuaded to surrender,
he feared they would ultimately not be useful,
and requested they all be released back.
The imperial decree did not grant this.
On the day Bǐngzǐ (13),
Chóuníng reported a victory, having defeated Lángshān.
On the day Xīnsì (18),
A further report was made regarding the defeat of Sòng troops at Yìjīn Guān.
On the day Guǐwèi (20),
The army advanced to Chángchéngkǒu.
Lǐ Xīng, the Sòng garrison commander of Dìngzhōu, came with troops to resist.
Xiūgē defeated them,
and pursued the routed enemy for five or six *lǐ*.
The eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn (21), the first day of the month,
The Emperor, intending to attack Chángchéngkǒu,
decreed that all armies prepare siege instruments.
On the day Gēngyín (27),
The army stationed at Chángchéngkǒu,
and oversaw the main army attacking from four sides.
The defenders broke out of the encirclement,
abandoned the city, and fled.
Xiézhěn tried to recruit them,
but they would not surrender.
The Emperor and Hán Déràng intercepted and attacked them,
killing and capturing nearly all of them.
Those captured were assigned to the Yān army.
On the day Xīnmǎo (28),
Mǎnchéng was attacked,
and besieged.
On the day Jiǎwǔ (31),
The city was captured.
The defending troops opened the north gate and fled.
The Emperor sent a messenger to instruct their commanders,
who then led their troops to surrender.
On the day Wùxū (35),
Qízhōu was captured,
and troops were allowed to loot extensively.
On the day Jǐhài (36),
Xīnlè was captured.
On the day Gēngzǐ (37),
Xiǎolángshān Stockade was defeated.
On the day Dīngwèi (44),
One thousand Sòng troops exited Yìjīn Guān.
Táo Wěi, the Imperial Maternal Uncle (Guójìu) and Gentleman (Lángjūn), and Shígē, the Xiángwěn, attacked and repelled them,
killing one deputy general.
On the day Jǐyǒu (46),
Xiūgē presented twenty horses captured by Huáng Píshì Xiángwěn while campaigning near Mòzhōu,
along with twenty soldiers.
An order was given to bestow clothes and belts upon the surrendered men,
and have them assigned to Yānjīng.
On the day Xīnhài (48),
The Western Circuit again sent over two hundred surrendered soldiers.
Furred garments were provided for those who were cold.
Mǎ Déchén was temporarily put in charge of the Xuānhuī Yuàn affairs.
The twelfth month, on the day Jiǎyín (51), the first day of the month,
Warrhorses were bestowed upon Qǐdé and Tūgǔlǐ, the Píshì Xiángwěn.
Dádǎlǐ, the Gentleman of the Emperor’s Tent (Héngzhàng Lángjūn), engaged in looting,
and was ordered to be beaten with a staff.
On the day Bǐngchén (53),
The Emperor hunted at Shā Hé.
Xiūgē presented Sòng spies captured by Yēlǔ, the Xī Xiángwěn.
On the day Dīngsì (54),
Xiāo Jìyuǎn, the Northern Chancellor (Běi Zǎixiàng), and others were sent to scout Ānpíng.
The Imperial Guard Cavalry Headquarters reported that in the attacks on Qízhōu and Xīnlè,
Liú Zàn, the Commander (Dōutóu), and thirty other men had rendered meritorious service,
and requested increased rewards.
In this month,
the main army was stationed in Sòng territory.
In this year,
an imperial decree ordered the opening of the tribute examinations (Gòngjǔ),
and one person who excelled was allowed to pass the examination.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month, on the day Guǐwèi (1st day of the month),
the armies were withdrawn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Guō Róng (郭榮), the defending general of the Sòng’s Jībì Fort (雞壁砦), led his troops to surrender.
An imperial decree ordered them to be stationed in Nánjīng.
On the day Gēngyín,
they reached Chángchéngkǒu (長城口).
Three soldiers went out of the camp to raid and loot.
They were publicly flogged before the troops.
The captured goods were distributed and bestowed upon the attendants.
On the day Rénchén,
Lǐ Jìqiān (李繼遷), who had grievances with his elder brother Jìběng (繼捧),
requested to establish friendly relations.
The Sovereign knew that he was not sincere,
and did not grant permission.
On the day Guǐsì,
an order was issued to the various armies to hasten to Yìzhōu (易州).
On the day Jǐhài,
the attendants were forbidden from cutting down the people’s mulberry and catalpa trees.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Yìzhōu was attacked.
Sòng troops came out from Suìchéng (遂城) to reinforce them.
The Tiělín Army (鐵林軍) was dispatched to attack them,
capturing five of their Commanders (zhǐhuīshǐ).
On the day Jiǎchén,
the main army advanced simultaneously,
and broke Yìzhōu,
accepting the surrender of the Prefect (cìshǐ), Liú Chí (劉墀).
The soldiers defending the parapets fled south.
The Sovereign led the army to intercept them,
and none dared to venture out.
Immediately, Mǎ Zhì (馬質) was made Prefect,
and Zhào Zhì (趙質) was made Commissioner of Military Affairs (Bīngmǎ Dūjiān).
The soldiers and common people of Yìzhōu were moved to Yānjīng (燕京).
As Xià Xiānshòu (夏仙壽), son of the Tōngjīng (東京) cavalry general Xià Zhēnxiǎn (夏貞顯), was the first to ascend (the wall),
he was granted the title of Prefect of Gāozhōu (高州).
On the day Yǐsì,
the Sovereign visited Yìzhōu,
and held court in the Wǔhuā Pavilion (五花樓),
pacifying and reassuring the officials and common people.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
a sacrifice of a black ox and a white horse was made to Heaven and Earth.
An imperial edict was issued to the three capitals and various circuits.
On the day Wùshēn,
they reached Láishuǐ (淶水),
and paid respects at the temple of Emperor Jǐngzōng (景宗皇帝).
An imperial decree ordered Yēlǜ Shǒuxióng (耶律守雄), the Prefect of Zhuōzhōu (涿州), to escort the eight hundred surrendered people from Yìzhōu
back to their native territories.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
they reached Qīgōu (岐溝),
and performed the ritual of shooting the ghost arrow (shè guǐjiàn).
On the day Xīnhài,
they returned to Nánjīng,
and the martial law (jiěyán) on the six armies was lifted.
The second month, on the day Rénzǐ (1st day of the month),
the Sovereign presided over the Yuánhé Hall (元和殿) to receive congratulations from the officials.
An imperial decree ordered the two hundred households from Jībì Fort to relocate and reside in Tánzhōu (檀州), Shùnzhōu (順州), and Jìzhōu (薊州).
On the day Jiǎyín,
the states of Huíhú (回鶻), Yútián (于闐), Shīzǐ (師子), and others came to offer tribute.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
a great feast was given to the soldiers,
and ranks and rewards were distributed according to status.
Hán Dé ràng (韓德讓), the Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmìshǐ), was enfeoffed as the Prince of Chǔ (Chǔguówáng).

Xiāo Níngyuǎn (蕭寧遠), the Son-in-Law Commandant (Fùmǎ Dūwèi), was granted the title of Participating in Political Affairs and Executive Secretary of the Department of the Gate of the Palace (Tóng Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāngshì).
On this day,
the Sovereign visited the Chángchūn Palace (長春宮).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial decree stipulated that for those captured during the Southern Campaign who had relatives distributed among various tribes,
official money should be provided to redeem them,
so that they could follow their families.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Nǚzhí (女直) troops who participated in the Southern Campaign were rewarded,
and permitted to return east.
On the day Bǐngyín,
candidates for official positions (jǔrén) were forbidden from secretly sending anonymous letters
to slander the imperial court.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Tǔbō (吐蕃) and Dǎngxiàng (党項) came to offer tribute.
On the day Jiǎxū,
a request from Yúnzhōu (雲州) to retain and remit their own taxes and levies to the local circuit was
granted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Huógǔdé (活骨德) of the Nǚzhí was made Chancellor (xiàng) of his own tribe.
Shamans (wūxí) were dispatched separately to offer sacrifices to the famous mountains and great rivers.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Prince FóBǎonú (佛寶奴), the Emperor's son, was born.
On the day Wùyín,
Āsàlán (阿薩蘭), Yútián, and Xiáliè (轄烈) all sent envoys to offer tribute.
The third month, on the day Rénwǔ (1st day of the month),
envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices at Mùyè Mountain (木葉山).
Grazing and collecting forage that damaged crops were forbidden.
Seventeen Sòng imperial examination graduates (jìnshì) brought their families and came to pledge allegiance.
The relevant officials were ordered to examine those who had successfully passed the exams,
to fill positions as officers in the National Academy (Guóxué),
while the rest were granted positions as County Chief Clerks (Xiàn Zhǔbù) or Lieutenants (Wèi).
Lǐ Jìqiān sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day Dīnghài,
an imperial decree ordered Zhào Zhì, Administrator of Yìzhōu, to collect the bones of the soldiers who died in battle,
and build a "capital mound" (jīngguān).
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Yúyuè (于越), Prince Sòng (Sòngguówáng), was presented with a crown embroidered with red beads and golden threads (hóngzhūjīnxiàn).
He was ordered to enter the divine tent (shénzhàng) to perform the rite of rebirth (zàishēnglǐ).
The Empress Dowager bestowed very generous gifts.
The eight households of Jībì Fort people, including Chéng Tínglǎng (成廷朗), were assigned to Fēihú (飛狐).
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an imperial decree pardoned the overdue taxes in Yúnzhōu.
Yǐshì Wáng (乙室王) Guànníng (貫寧) was playing polo
when Gāo Sì (高四), a gentleman (lángjūn) of his subordinate tribe, recklessly charged his horse and caused his death.
An imperial decree ordered an investigation into the crime of Gāo Sì.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial decree ordered the opening of the Qífēng Road (奇峰路) to connect with the Yìzhōu market.
On the day Wùxū,
the daughter of Yēlǜ Xiāng (耶律襄) of the Prince's Tribe (Wángzǐ zhàng) was enfeoffed as Princess Yìchéng (Yìchéng Gōngzhǔ),
and married to Lǐ Jìqiān.
This spring,
the Imperial traveling lodge was established at Yánfāng Pond (Yánfāng Diàn).
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Sovereign returned to the Capital.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiāo Tàlǎn (蕭闥覽), the Empress's Maternal Uncle and Grand Preceptor (Guójiù Tàishī), requested on behalf of his son Pái Yà (排亞) to marry Princess Yánshòu (Yánshòu Gōngzhǔ), the imperial daughter.
This was granted.
On the day Bǐngchén,
respects were paid at the temple of Emperor Tàizōng (太宗皇帝).
Wūgǔ (烏骨), the Grandee Secretary (Yùshǐ Dàfū), was appointed Great King of the Yǐshì (Yǐshì Dàwáng).
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Sovereign visited the Yánshòu Temple (延壽寺) to feed the monks.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Mǎ Déchén (馬得臣), the Grand Master Remonstrant (Jiànyì Dàfū), submitted a memorial criticizing the Sovereign's preference for playing polo:
"Your servant humbly submits a memorial offering sharp remonstrance:
‘Your servant observes that His Majesty, in his leisure time from holding court,
takes pleasure in playing polo.
Your servant believes that this activity is improper in three ways: When superiors and subordinates form opposing sides,
and the sovereign and his ministers compete for victory,
if the sovereign gains and the minister snatches,
or if the sovereign loses and the minister rejoices—
this is the first impropriety;
When moving back and forth and crossing paths,
blocking and intercepting front and back,
a competitive spirit fiercely arises,
and ceremonial propriety is completely abandoned.
If, out of greed for the crescent-shaped stick,
the celestial robe (the emperor's garment) is accidentally struck,
the minister has committed an impropriety,
yet it is difficult for the sovereign to assign blame—
this is the second impropriety;
Treating lightly the dignity of the Son of Heaven (wànshèng zhī guì),
and pursuing amusement on the open field.
Although the ground may be flat,
it is extremely hard and firm.
Although the horses may be excellent,
they can still stumble and fall.
If, due to charging and striking,
control is lost,
how can the Sacred Body (Shèng tǐ) be guaranteed against injury?
And how can the Empress Dowager not be alarmed and fearful?
This is the third impropriety.
Your servant hopes that Your Majesty will be mindful of the importance of the imperial succession
and cease this dangerous game.’"
When the memorial was presented,
the Sovereign greatly accepted and approved it.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Huántōng Jīn (還金) of Tǔhún (吐渾), Ānjìn (安進) of Huíhú, and Dúxuān (獨𩽆) of Tǔbō, who had come from Sòng, surrendered.
They were all bestowed with clothes and belts.
The Empress Dowager paid respects at the temple of Qíshǒu Kèhán (奇首可汗).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Yēlǜ Yǎo (耶律杳) of the Shèlì Army (舍利軍) was made Chánggǔn (常袞, an official title).
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Imperial traveling lodge was established at Lóngquán (龍泉) in Rúzhōu (儒州).
The fifth month, on the day Gēngchén (1st day of the month),
Pú Lǐng (蒲領) and others, Commissioners of the Office of the Controller (Xuānhuīshǐ), were dispatched to lead troops to guard against Sòng along various routes.
Kònggǔlí (控骨離), Vice-Envoy of the Yáolián (Yáoliǎn Fùshǐ), was made Commander of the Shèlì Yèlà (Shèlì Yèlà Xiángwěn).
On the day Xīnsì,
sacrifices were offered to the Earl of Wind (Fēng Bó) at Báimǎ Village (白馬村) in Rúzhōu.
Xiū Gē (休哥) led his army to Mǎnchéng (滿城),
recruiting over seven hundred surrendered soldiers.
He sent an envoy to present them.
An imperial decree ordered them to be assigned to Dōngjīng.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Sovereign hunted along the Sānggān River (桑乾河).
On the day Rénchén,
a memorial from Yānjīng reported that Sòng troops had reached the border.
It stated that since the weather was hot, they did not dare engage in battle yet,
and would temporarily station at Yìzhōu,
advancing to attack when the enemy moved,
and withdrawing the army when they retreated.
This was approved.
On the *gēngxū* day of the sixth month,
Taishī Zhè Mǔ, for being obsequious,
was beaten twenty times.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict permitted commoners to cultivate wastelands in Yànlè and Mìyún counties,
〔一八〕and exempted them from taxes and corvée for ten years.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Xuānzhèng Diàn Xuéshì Mǎ Déchén died.
An edict posthumously granted him the title of Tàizǐ Shàobǎo,
and awarded him 100,000 *qián* [money]
and 100 *shí* [dan] of grain.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict ordered the release of various animals to poor people in the border regions.
In this month,
Xiūgē and Páiyà defeated Sòng troops in Tàizhōu.
〔一九〕
In autumn, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the seventh month,
the emperor held court in the Hánliáng Diàn.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhongchéng Yēlǜ Hémài Gē was appointed acting Yílíbì,
and Héngzhàng Lángjūn Yēlǜ Yánshòu was made Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the *guǐsì* day,
troops were dispatched for a southern campaign.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
four individuals each from the Dīlíbì, Nièlā, and Wūhuì tribes were added to the household of Nánběi Lù Fūrén Pólǐdé,
〔二０〕and seals and ribbons were granted.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the officers and soldiers of the southern campaign were rewarded.
On this day,
the emperor and the empress dowager paid respects at Jǐngzōng Huángdì’s temple.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the eighth month,
Gāo Zhèng and one other *jìnshì* were passed.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the use of nets and traps to catch rabbits was prohibited.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the eleventh month,
Yútián's Zhāng Wénbǎo presented books on inner alchemy.
