On the *jiǎyín* day of the twelfth month,
fishing took place at Shěnzǐ Luò.
On the *guǐhài* day,
hunting took place at Hǎocǎo Lǐng.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals 13, Shèngzōng 4
In the eighth year, spring, on the *xīnsì* day of the first month,
the emperor visited Táihú.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict ordered the resolution of pending lawsuits.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the emperor visited Shěnzǐ Luò.
On the *dīngwèi* day, the first day of the second month,
Yútián and Huíhú each sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the third month,
Lǐ Jìqiān sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Tàibái and Yínghuò contended,
for a total of fifteen times.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Xìngguō was fortified,
and Sòng captives were settled there.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yízhōu was established.
In summer, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the fourth month,
Yánzhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Shòuyīng governed beneficently.
The people requested he stay,
which was granted.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
due to drought,
the various tribes faced food shortages,
and were relieved.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the fifth month,
the surrendered Sòng soldiers were distributed among the various armies.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Nǚzhí Zǎixiàng Āhǎi came to pay tribute,
and was enfeoffed as Shùnhuà Wáng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the emperor sought relief from the summer heat at Hútǔ Báishān.
An edict ordered a survey of private land.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the sixth month,
Běimiàn Línyá Mólǔgǔ was appointed Běiyuàn Dàwáng.
Āsàlán Huíhú Yúyuè and Dálàgān each sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the moon occulted the first star of Tiānsì.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
In autumn, on the *gēngchén* day of the seventh month,
Nánjīng Xióngjūn was renamed Shénjūn.
An edict ordered the various palace-division commands in the Dōngjīng circuit
to establish Dìngbà, Bǎohé, and Xuānhuà three counties;
Báichuān Zhōu to establish Hónglǐ;
Yíkūn Zhōu to establish Guǎngyì;
Liáoxī Zhōu to establish Chángqìng;
and Qiánzhōu to establish Āndé county each.
The ten prefectures of Suì, Guī, Sōng, Ráo, Níng, Hǎi, Ruì, Yù, Tiělǐ, Fèngdé,
and the eight counties of Yùtián, Liáofēng, Sōngshān, Hóngyuǎn, Huáiqīng, Yúnlóng, Píngzé, Píngshān
were abolished, and their populations were distributed among other prefectures.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the eighth month,
black and white sheep were sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
On the *yǐhài* day of the ninth month,
the four tribes of Běi Nǚzhí requested to become inner tributaries.
On the *rénchén* day,
Lǐ Jìqiān offered Sòng captives.
In winter, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of the tenth month,
an envoy was again sent to report a great defeat of Sòng forces.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zǔbù and others sent envoys to pay tribute.
In this month,
the emperor sojourned in Dàwáng Chuān.
On the *gēngyín* day of the eleventh month,
due to famine among the Tǔyùhún people,
they were relieved.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Tàibái was visible in daylight.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month,
Lǐ Jìqiān captured Sòng's Línzhōu and Fūzhōu and other prefectures,
and sent an envoy to report it.
Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an envoy was sent to enfeoff Lǐ Jìqiān as Xiàguó Wáng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Huíhú came to pay tribute.
In this year,
Zhèng Yúncóng and one other were passed as *jìnshì*.
In the ninth year, spring, on the *jiǎxū* day of the first month,
Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict prohibited private ordination of monks and nuns.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the emperor visited Táihú.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Shūmìshǐ and Jiānxiū Guóshǐ Shì Fǎng and others presented the Veritable Records,
and were given gifts of varying value.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
five hundred surrendered Sòng soldiers were selected and organized into the Xuānlì Jūn.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an edict exempted the three capitals and various circuits from rent and taxes,
and also abolished the land survey.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the second month,
Xiàguó sent an envoy to report a victory against Sòng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zhuōzhōu Cìshǐ Yēlǜ Wángliù was appointed Tìyǐn.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Jiànwēi Kòu, Zhènhuà, and LáiYuǎn three cities were built,
and garrisons were stationed there.
On the *xīnwèi* day, the first day of the intercalary month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Hànlín Chéngzhǐ Xíng Bàopú, Sānsī Shǐ Lǐ Sì, Jìshìzhōng Liú Jīng, Zhèngshì Shèrén Zhāng Gàn, and Nánjīng Fù Liúshǒu Wú Hào were sent to various circuits to resolve pending lawsuits.
On the *gēngzǐ* day, the first day of the third month,
the Shìwéi and Wūgǔ tribes were relieved.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Kùbù Yuánwàiláng Mǎ Shǒuqí, Cāngbù Yuánwàiláng Qí Zhèng, Yúbù Yuánwàiláng Cuī Yòu,
and Jìběi Xiànlìng Cuī Jiǎn and others were again sent to various circuits to resolve pending lawsuits.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the emperor visited Nánjīng.
In summer, on the *jiǎxū* day of the fourth month,
Huíhú came to pay tribute.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Xiàguó Wáng Lǐ Jìqiān sent Dù Bái to express gratitude for the enfeoffment.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the emperor sought relief from the summer heat at Tànshān.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the fifth month,
Qínwáng Hán Kuāngsì's private city was made into Quánzhōu.
On the *dīnghài* day of the sixth month,
Tūjué came to pay tribute.
In this month,
continuous rain in Nánjīng damaged crops.
In autumn, on the *guǐmǎo* day of the seventh month,
a general census of households was conducted.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an edict ordered various circuits to recommend talented and virtuous individuals, investigate corrupt and cruel officials, care for the elderly, and prohibit extravagance and transgression.
For those who died in service to the state, their sons and grandsons were to be given official positions.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Xiàguó, having recovered Suízhōu and Yínzhōu,
sent an envoy to report it.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the eighth month,
auspicious grain grew in Tóngzhōu,
and sweet dew descended in Dōngjīng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Nǚzhí presented a deer-caller.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Dōngjīng presented a three-legged crow.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the ninth month,
Bígǔdé came to pay tribute.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the emperor sojourned in Miàochéng.
An earthquake occurred in Nánjīng.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Jǐhài*,
the sacrifices of a black ox and a white horse were offered to Heaven and Earth.
In the twelfth month,
Lǐ Jìqiān, King of Xiàguó, secretly defected to Sòng.
[We] dispatched the Pacification Commissioner, Hán Déwēi, bearing an edict to warn him.
In this year,
the *Jìnshì* Shí Yòngzhōng alone passed the highest examination.
In the tenth year, spring, the first month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*,
the custom of slaughtering horses during funeral and burial rites was forbidden,
as was the hoarding of armor, helmets, gold, silver, curios, and valuables.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
[the Emperor] went to Táihú.
In the second month, on *Yǐchǒu* (the first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
Hán Déwēi reported that Lǐ Jìqiān claimed illness and refused to appear,
so [Hán] proceeded to Língzhōu, captured and plundered, and returned.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
Wùrě came to offer tribute.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
the rents and taxes of Yúnzhōu were remitted.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
Xiàguó, regarding the captures and plundering by Hán Déwēi,
sent an envoy to submit a report,
and [the Emperor] bestowed an edict of comfort and reassurance.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
relief and tax exemption were granted to the displaced people of Yúnzhōu.
In the third month, on the day *Jiǎchén*,
Tiělí came to offer tribute.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
[the Emperor] went to Tànshān.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Táihú was designated Wàngxìnglǐ.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
ministers were ordered to compete in archery.
In the fifth month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
the displaced people of Shuòzhōu were granted relief and tax exemption for three years.
In the seventh month, on the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Tiělí came to offer tribute.
In the eighth month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
[the Emperor] observed the crops,
and furthermore dispatched envoys to separately inspect the sprouts and crops.
In the ninth month, on the day *Guǐmǎo*,
[the Emperor] visited Jīnhésì on Wǔtáishān and hosted a meal for the monks.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day *Rénshēn*,
the King of Xiàguó sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day *Wùyín*,
Tiělí came to offer tribute.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Rénchén*,
Huíhú came to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Gēngchén*,
[the Emperor] hunted at Rúzhōu Dōngchuān.
Paid homage to Heaven.
In this month,
Xiāo Dé, Residential Administrator of Dōngjīng, and others, were ordered to attack Gāolì.
In the eleventh year, spring, the first month, on the day *Rényín*,
Huíhú came to offer tribute.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
money from the Imperial Treasury was distributed to the troops of the Nánjīng Commandery.
Zhì, King of Gāolì, dispatched Piáo Liángróu to present a memorial requesting forgiveness for his offenses.
An edict was issued granting him several hundred *lǐ* of Nǚzhí territory east of the Yālù Jiāng.
In the second month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
Wáng Shì, the wife of a Bàzhōu commoner, was executed
for using sorcery to mislead the populace.
Summer, the fourth month,
[the Emperor] visited Tànshān to escape the heat.
In the sixth month,
there was heavy rain.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the Sānggān and Yánghé Rivers overflowed west of Jūyōng Guān,
destroying nearly all the grain and crops.
Many residents of Fèngshèng and Nánjīng had their houses and homes submerged and drowned.
In the eighth month,
[the Emperor] went to the Autumn Mountains.
Winter, the tenth month, on *Jiǎshēn* (the first day of the lunar month),
the imperial carriage halted at Púguībǎn.
In this year,
the *Jìnshì* Wáng Xīzài and one other person passed the highest examination.
In the twelfth year, spring, the first month, on *Guǐchǒu* (the first day of the lunar month),
Huǒyīnzhèn was flooded,
drowning more than thirty villages.
An edict was issued to dredge the old channel.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
Yēlǜ Shuòlǎo, who held the office of Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery, was appointed as *Tìyǐn*.
An edict was issued to remit the rent within fifty *lǐ* of the imperial camp.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
[the Emperor] visited Yánfāngdiàn.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
the taxes and levies of Yízhōu were abolished.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
the *Lángjūn* Yēlǜ Bǐshě and others plotted rebellion,
and were executed.
On the day *Rénxū*,
Yēlǜ Jǐng, the Great King of the Southern Chancellery, was appointed Residential Administrator of Shàngjīng,
and enfeoffed as the Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery.
Lǐ Zàiyòu, a commoner of Bàzhōu, was one hundred thirty-three years old.
He was granted rolls of silk, a brocade robe, and a silver belt,
supplied with mutton and wine monthly,
and his household was granted relief.
In the second month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the rents and taxes of Nánjīng households affected by the flood were remitted.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
Gāolì came to offer tribute.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
the annual tribute of sheep from various tribes, as well as customs duties, were remitted.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Huíhú came to offer tribute.
In the third month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
Gāolì sent an envoy to request the return of captured people and livestock,
and an edict was issued to redeem and return them.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
[the Emperor] visited Nánjīng.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
an envoy was sent to soothe and admonish Gāolì.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
trees with joined branches appeared in Zhuōzhōu.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
[the Emperor] went to Chángchūngōng to observe the peonies.
In this month,
the Nánjīng Commandery Military Commissioner’s Office was re-established.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
[the Emperor] visited Nánjīng.
On the day *Rénchén*,
Liú Shù, Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Chancellery.
On the day *Wùxū*,
because the stone statue of Jǐngzōng was completed,
[the Emperor] visited Yánshòusì and hosted a meal for the monks.
In the fifth month, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
an edict exempted old soldiers of the Běi Píshì Army who were unfit for duty from service.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
[the Emperor] went to Tànshān to escape the heat.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
the term of Hán Déchōng, Military Commissioner of Wǔdìngjūn, expired,
but his people requested he remain,
and this was granted.
In the sixth month, on *Xīnsì* (the first day of the lunar month),
an edict decreed that magistrates of prefectures and counties who possessed talent and had committed no faults
should be appointed upon reducing their qualification rank by one step.
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
Jiǎ Jùn, Prefect of Kèhànzhōu, presented a new calendar.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
an edict ordered that soldiers in the Lóng and Fèng armies who were old or infirm should be replaced.
In this month,
Venus and Jupiter were in conjunction.
Autumn, the seventh month, on *Xīnhài* (the first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
envoys were dispatched to inspect the crops in all circuits.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Shì Fǎng, Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Chancellery, was made Residential Administrator of Zhōngjīng,
and given the honorific title of *Shàngfù*.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
Nǚzhí sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day *Wùchén*,
[the Emperor] observed the harvest.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
an edict decreed that Qìdān people who committed the Ten Abominations should be dealt with according to the Hān Statutes.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Xíng Bàopǔ, Academician Recipient of Edicts, was appointed as Vice Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
In the eighth month, on *Gēngchén* (the first day of the lunar month),
an edict ordered the Empress Dowager to lead the troops of the Wūgǔ and other tribes of the Northwestern Circuit, as well as the garrison troops of Yǒngxīng Palace,
to pacify and settle the western border.
Xiāo Tàlǐn was appointed to oversee the military affairs.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
Sòng sent an envoy requesting peace,
but it was not granted.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
Xiāo Túgǔ, State Uncle of the Tent, was made *Yílìbì*.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
an edict was issued to warn and instruct officials both inside and outside the court.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
prisoners were reviewed;
those convicted of miscellaneous offenses leading to death penalty or lesser crimes were released.
In the ninth month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
Shìwéi, Dǎngxiàng, Tǔyùhún, and others came to offer tribute.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Sòng again sent an envoy requesting peace,
but it was not granted.
On the day *Rénxū*,
the Rite of Baying the Inner Chamber was performed.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Zǔbǔ and others came to offer tribute.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
[the Emperor] hunted at the Western Mountains of Kèhànzhōu.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
an edict was issued establishing the Law of Equal Taxation.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
the offices of Vice Minister and Chief of the Court of Judicial Review were established.
The eleventh month, on the *wù shēn* (戊申) day, the first day of the month,
the ceremony of rebirth was performed.
The Tiělí (鐵驪) came to offer tribute.
An edict was issued that those Sòng (宋) people captured by various tribes who were officials, scholars, or possessed skills,
and those in the armies of various circuits who were brave and strong,
should all have their names reported.
On the *gēng xū* (庚戌) day,
an edict ordered prefectures and counties to recommend candidates distinguished in *míng jīng* (明經) (classical studies) and *mào cái yì děng* (茂材異等) (outstanding talents).
On the *jiǎ yín* (甲寅) day,
an edict ordered Nánjīng (南京) to decide pending lawsuits.
On the *jǐ wèi* (己未) day,
Wèi Déshēng (衞德升) and five other captured Sòng (宋) people were appointed to office.
The twelfth month, on the *wù yín* (戊寅) day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict ordered that the three tribes of the Xīwáng Fǔ (奚王府), Àolǐ (奧理),
Duòkuí (墮隗), and Méizhǐ (梅只), be combined into one,
and the two *è kè* (二剋) groups each be divided into separate departments,
thus completing the number of six departments.
On the *jiǎ shēn* (甲申) day,
plowing oxen were bestowed upon the poor households managed by the Nánjīng Tǒngjūnsī (南京統軍司).
On the *wù zǐ* (戊子) day,
Gāolì (高麗) offered female entertainers and music,
which was refused.
On the *gēng yín* (庚寅) day,
vagrants who preyed on the populace were banned.
On the *guǐ sì* (癸巳) day,
the Nǚzhí (女直) reported that Sòng (宋) people had crossed the sea and offered bribes to their country, and also reported the rebellion of the Wùrě (兀惹).
On the *dīng wèi* (丁未) day,
the Emperor proceeded to Nánjīng (南京).
In this year,
two successful candidates in the imperial examinations, Lǚ Démào (呂德懋) and the other, were granted the *jí dì* (及第) degree.
The thirteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *rén zǐ* (壬子) day,
the Emperor proceeded to Yánfāng Diàn (延芳淀).
On the *jiǎ yín* (甲寅) day,
Guǎnglíng Xiàn (廣靈縣) was established.
On the *dīng sì* (丁巳) day,
the taxes of Tàizhōu (泰州), Suìchéng (遂城), and other counties were increased.
On the *gēng shēn* (庚申) day,
an edict ordered various circuits to encourage agriculture.
On the *guǐ hài* (癸亥) day,
the term of office of Xiāo Jiělǐ (蕭解里), Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Chángníng Jūn (長寧軍), ended.
The people requested that he remain,
and this was granted.
On the *gēng wǔ* (庚午) day,
the Emperor went to Chángchūn Gōng (長春宮).
The second month, on the *dīng chǒu* (丁丑) day, the first day of the month,
the Nǚzhí (女直) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎ chén* (甲辰) day,
Gāolì (高麗) sent Lǐ Zhōuzhēn (李周楨) to offer tribute.
The third month, on the *guǐ chǒu* (癸丑) day,
Xià Guó (夏國) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *wù chén* (戊辰) day,
more than a hundred people from Wǔqīng Xiàn (武清縣) entered Sòng (宋) territory and plundered.
An order was given to execute them,
and return the people, livestock, and property they had seized.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐ mǎo* (己卯) day,
Xíng Bàopǔ (邢抱朴), Director of the Chancellery (Cānzhī Zhèngshì), resigned his office due to mourning for his mother,
but was recalled to service (*qǐ fù*).
On the *bǐng xū* (丙戌) day,
an edict stated that civilian households throughout the circuits who had been coerced into serving as retainers (*bù qǔ*) since the Yìnglì (應曆) era
should still be registered with the prefectures and counties.
On the *jiǎ wǔ* (甲午) day,
the Emperor went to Tànshān (炭山) to escape the heat.
The fifth month, on the *rén zǐ* (壬子) day,
Gāolì (高麗) presented falcons.
On the *yǐ hài* (乙亥) day,
the three administrations (Fǔ) of Běi (北), Nán (南), and Yǐshì (乙室) requested to confiscate horses from rich households to prepare for military needs.
This was not permitted;
instead, they were supplied with government horses.
The sixth month, on the *bǐng zǐ* (丙子) day, the first day of the month,
the term of office of Liú Jìchēn (劉繼琛), Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Qǐshèng Jūn (啟聖軍), ended.
The people requested that he remain,
and this was granted.
On the *dīng chǒu* (丁丑) day,
an edict reduced the land tax and levies instituted the previous year.
On the *jiǎ shēn* (甲申) day,
the private fortress built by Āmòlǐ (阿沒里), Commissioner of the Privy Council (Xuānhuīshǐ), was designated Fēngzhōu (豐州).
On the *bǐng xū* (丙戌) day,
an edict permitted the people of Chāngpíng (昌平), Huáiróu (懷柔), and other counties to request the cultivation of wastelands.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐ sì* (乙巳) day, the first day of the month,
the Nǚzhí (女直) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *dīng sì* (丁巳) day,
Wū Zhāodù (烏昭度) of Wùrě (兀惹)
and Yàn Pǒ (燕頗) of Bóhǎi (渤海) invaded the Tiělí (鐵驪).
Xīwáng Héshuònú (奚王和朔奴) and others were dispatched to suppress them.
On the *rén xū* (壬戌) day,
an edict ordered the Lóngwèi (龍衞) and Wēishèng Jūn (威勝軍) troops in Wèi (蔚), Shuò (朔), and other prefectures to rotate garrison duty.
The eighth month, on the *bǐng zǐ* (丙子) day,
Xià Guó (夏國) sent envoys to present horses.
On the *rén chén* (壬辰) day,
an edict ordered the repair of temples for mountain and marsh deities, and the shrines of former sages,
and that sacrifices be offered to them at the appropriate seasons.
The ninth month, on the *wù wǔ* (戊午) day,
because the number of students at the Nánjīng Tàixué (南京太學) had greatly increased,
one estate with a water mill was specially granted to them.
On the *dīng mǎo* (丁卯) day,
the stone statues of Jǐngzōng (景宗) and the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) were respectfully installed at Yánfāng Diàn (延芳淀).
Winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐ hài* (乙亥) day,
charitable granaries (*yì cāng*) were established.
On the *xīn sì* (辛巳) day,
the Huíhú (回鶻) came to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎ shēn* (甲申) day,
Gāolì (高麗) sent Lǐ Zhībái (李知白) to offer tribute.
On the *wù zǐ* (戊子) day,
Wùrě (兀惹) submitted.
An edict was issued to soothe and instruct them.
On the *gēng zǐ* (庚子) day,
Bígǔdé (鼻骨德) came to offer tribute.
The eleventh month, on the *yǐ sì* (乙巳) day,
the Āsàlán Huíhú (阿薩蘭回鶻) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *xīn yǒu* (辛酉) day,
envoys were sent to invest Wáng Zhì (王治) as the King of Gāolì Guó (高麗國).
On the *wù chén* (戊辰) day,
Gāolì (高麗) sent ten boys to learn the national language.
The twelfth month, on the *jǐ mǎo* (己卯) day,
the Tiělí (鐵驪) sent envoys to offer tribute of falcons and horses.
On the *xīn sì* (辛巳) day,
Xià Guó (夏國) sent envoys to report their defeat of the Sòng (宋) people.
In this year,
two successful candidates, Wáng Yòngjí (王用極) and the other, were granted the *jí dì* degree.
The fourteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *jǐ yǒu* (己酉) day,
fishing was conducted on the Lù Hé (潞河).
On the *dīng sì* (丁巳) day,
taxes and levies were waived for the Three Capitals (*sān jīng*) and various prefectures.
On the *bǐng yín* (丙寅) day,
Xià Guó (夏國) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *gēng wǔ* (庚午) day,
Yán Guì (閻貴), a domestic servant of Āmòlǐ (阿沒里), Commissioner of the Privy Council (Xuānhuīshǐ), was appointed Governor (Cìshǐ) of Fēngzhōu (豐州).
The second month, on the *gēng yín* (庚寅) day,
the Huíhú (回鶻) sent envoys to offer tribute.
The third month, on the *rén yín* (壬寅) day,
Wáng Zhì (王治), the King of Gāolì (高麗), submitted a memorial requesting a marriage alliance.
Permission was granted for the daughter of Xiāo Dé (蕭德), Defense Commissioner of Dōngjīng (東京 Liúshǒu) and Imperial Son-in-Law (Fùmǎ), to marry him.
On the *gēng xū* (庚戌) day,
Gāolì (高麗) again sent ten boys to learn the national language.
On the *jiǎ yín* (甲寅) day,
Hán Déwēi (韓德威) reported victory in suppressing the Dǎngxiàng (党項).
On the *jiǎ zǐ* (甲子) day,
an edict ordered the settlement and assembly of displaced people from Shuòzhōu (朔州).
Summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎ xū* (甲戌) day,
supervisors (Dūjiān) were established for each of the various *jiū* (糺) (tribal groups) on the eastern border.
On the *gēng yín* (庚寅) day,
the Emperor went to Tànshān (炭山) to escape the heat.
On the *jǐ hài* (己亥) day,
Dà'ānshān (大安山) was excavated
to retrieve the money hidden there by Liú Shǒuguāng (劉守光).
In this month,
Xīwáng Héshuònú (奚王和朔奴), Xiāo Dé (蕭德), Defense Commissioner of Dōngjīng (東京 Liúshǒu), and three others were stripped of their offices
for failing to suppress the Wùrě (兀惹).
The title of *lìng wěn* (令穩) of various tribes was changed to Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ).
The fifth month, on the *guǐ mǎo* (癸卯) day,
an edict ordered Xíng Bàopǔ (邢抱朴), Director of the Chancellery (Cānzhī Zhèngshì), to decide pending lawsuits in Nánjīng (南京).
On the *gēng xū* (庚戌) day,
one hundred and seven men of the Wēishèng Jūn (威勝軍) in Shuòzhōu (朔州) rebelled and defected to Sòng (宋).
The sixth month, on the *xīn wèi* (辛未) day,
the Emperor went to Tànshān (炭山) to escape the heat.
The Tiělí (鐵驪) came to offer tribute.
On the *yǐ yǒu* (乙酉) day,
the Huíhú (回鶻) came to offer tribute.
On the *jǐ chǒu* (己丑) day,
Gāolì (高麗) sent an envoy to inquire after the Emperor's well-being.
Thereafter, they arrived irregularly.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *wù wǔ* (戊午) day,
the Huíhú (回鶻) and others came to offer tribute.
Intercalary month, on the *dīng chǒu* (丁丑) day,
the Wǔyuàn Bù (五院部) presented a golden horse obtained by digging into the ground.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *bǐng chén* (丙辰) day,
Liú Suì (劉遂) was ordered to teach sword fighting techniques to the soldiers of the Shénwǔ Jūn (神武軍) in Nánjīng (南京).
He was rewarded with robes, belts, and silk currency.
On the *wù wǔ* (戊午) day,
Wū Zhāodù (烏昭度) requested to submit and become part of the interior domain.
The eleventh month, on the *jiǎ xū* (甲戌) day,
an edict prohibited military officers from hunting outside the proper season, thereby obstructing agriculture.
On the *yǐ yǒu* (乙酉) day,
the stone statues of Jǐngzōng (景宗) and the Empress Dowager (Tàihòu) were respectfully installed at Qiánzhōu (乾州).
In this month,
Āsàlán (阿薩蘭) of the Huíhú (回鶻) sent an envoy to request a marriage alliance for his son,
which was not permitted.
The twelfth month, on the *jiǎ yín* (甲寅) day,
because the newly established tax law in Nánjīng Dào (南京道) was too heavy,
it was reduced.
On the *jiǎ zǐ* (甲子) day,
Tàlǐn (撻凜) lured the rebellious chieftain Ālǔdūn (阿魯敦) and sixty others to their death and executed them.
Tàlǐn (撻凜) was enfeoffed as the Prince of Lánlíng Jùnwáng (蘭陵郡王).
The Emperor proceeded to Nánjīng (南京).
In this year,
three successful candidates, Zhāng Jiǎn (張儉) and the others, were granted the *jí dì* degree.
In the fifteenth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
visited Yánfāng Diàn.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
because the Héxī Dǎngxiàng rebelled,
an imperial edict commanded Hán Déwēi to suppress them.
On the day Gēngchén,
an imperial edict instructed all circuits to urge the people to plant trees.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Wǔ Zhōu, the leader of the Wū Rě, came and surrendered.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Nǚzhí sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an imperial edict ordered the resolution of pending prisoners in Nánjīng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
taxes for refugees were abolished.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngshēn (the first day of the lunar month),
went to Chángchūn Gōng.
On the day Wùxū,
wealthy citizens of the various departments were urged to contribute money to assist the poor.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the populace of Liángmén, Suìchéng, Tàizhōu, and Běipíng was moved to the interior.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the state of Xià Guó sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Jiǎyín,
inquired about the well-being of the Empress Dowager.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Hán Déwēi reported a victory in defeating the Dǎngxiàng.
On the day Dīngsì,
an imperial edict ordered the people to cultivate unused land in the various departments.
In the third month, on the day Yǐchǒu (the first day of the lunar month),
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
On the day Wùchén,
people were recruited to cultivate the wasteland of Luánzhōu,
and their rent and taxes were exempted for ten years.
On the day Jǐsì,
Xià Guó defeated the Sòng troops,
and sent envoys to announce it.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Lǐ Jìqiān, the King of Xià Guó, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Xīpíng Wáng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
a general census of palace households was conducted,
and tax arrears and grain from the Yìcāng in Nánjīng were waived.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Héxī Dǎngxiàng requested to be annexed to the inner court.
On the day Gēngyín,
Wū Zhāodù of the Wū Rě, due to the great distance of his territory,
requested exemption from presenting eagles, horses, and sable furs annually;
an imperial edict ordered that tribute on the Imperial Birthday and the New Year be as before,
but the rest was waived.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Sòng ruler Jǐong passed away,
and his son succeeded to the throne.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Imperial Consort Dowager presented news of victory on the western border.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi (the first day of the lunar month),
the annual tribute of deer from the five departments of the Xī was abolished.
On the day Wùxū,
reviewed the prisoners.
On the day Rényín,
grain from the Yìcāng was distributed to relieve the citizens of the various counties in Nánjīng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Hán Déníng, the Jìedùshǐ of Guǎngdé Jūn, having governed well,
when his term of office was completed,
his people requested he remain;
this was granted.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
visited Nánjīng.
On the day Dīngsì,
offered sacrifices at the temple of Emperor Tàizōng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
went to Tànshān to escape the summer heat.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ (the first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐsì,
an imperial edict ordered the resolution of pending cases in Píngzhōu.
In this month,
the eight departments of the Díliè killed their Xiángwěn and rebelled;
Xiāo Tàlǐn pursued and attacked them,
capturing half of the tribal population.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the Tiělí came to present tribute.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Xià Guó sent envoys to thank for the enfeoffment and investiture.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
the Dǎngxiàng came to present tribute.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the separate departments of the Tǔyùhún were prohibited from selling horses to the Sòng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Gāolì sent Hán Yànjìng with ceremonial gifts to mourn the passing of the Princess of Yuègúo.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered the speedy resolution of judicial cases in Nánjīng.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
hunted in the Pine Forest on the Plain,
The Empress Dowager warned, saying:
“Former sages have said: Desire should not be indulged.
My son is the lord of the world,
galloping about hunting in the fields.
If, by any chance, there were an accident involving the bit and rein,
it would surely bring grief to me.
You must heed this deeply!”
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the garrison soldiers on the eastern border were dismissed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
visited Ráozhōu,
and offered sacrifices at the temple of Tàizǔ.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Xiāo Tàlǐn reported a victory in suppressing the Zǔbǔ.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénchén (the first day of the lunar month),
the Imperial carriage halted at Tuóshān,
and the tribute items from the various departments of the Xī kings were abolished.
On the day Yǐwèi,
presented seasonal clothing to the palace guards.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
temples on various mountains were prohibited from arbitrarily ordaining monks and nuns.
On the day Wùxū,
the restrictions on the Yúluò fishing grounds in the Dōngjīng Dào were relaxed.
On the day Wùshēn,
because judicial cases in Shàngjīng were excessive and redundant,
the officials in charge were interrogated.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
reviewed the prisoners.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénxū (the first day of the lunar month),
reviewed the prisoners.
On the day Bǐngxū,
visited Xiǎnzhōu.
On the day Wùzǐ,
paid respects at Xiǎnlíng.
On the day Gēngyín,
paid respects at Qiánlíng.
In this month,
Wáng Zhì, the King of Gāolì, passed away;
his nephew Sòng sent Wáng Tóngyǐng to report the news.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐsì,
fished in the Tǔ Hé.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Imperial carriage halted at Tuóshān.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Xià Guó sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Jiǎyín,
sent an envoy to offer sacrifices to Wáng Zhì, the King of Gāolì,
and decreed that his nephew provisionally oversee the affairs of state.
On the day Bǐngchén,
reviewed the prisoners.
In this year,
granted degrees to the two successful candidates in the metropolitan examination, Chén Dǐng and others.
Basic Annals 14: Shèngzōng 5
In the sixteenth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
went to Chángluò.
In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Xià Guó sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
appointed Yēlǜ Xǐluó, the Supreme General of the Palace Guard, as the Left Chancellor of the Zhōngtái Shěng.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Nǚzhí sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Yǐhài,
the chieftain of the Bígǔdé came to present tribute.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
relief was provided to the citizens in the prefectures and counties under the administration of Chóngdé Gōng who were affected by floods.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the practice of the people supplying official salaries was abolished,
and salaries were provided from the Imperial Treasury.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
prayed for rain.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
went to Mùyè Shān.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
sacrificed to the White Horse God.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
offered sacrifices at Mùyè Shān,
announcing the plan for a southern campaign the following year.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Tiělí came to present tribute.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
returned to Shàngjīng.
Bestowed gifts upon women over ninety years of age.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùzǐ (the first day of the lunar month),
offered sacrifices at Zǔ Líng and Huái Líng.
In this month,
escaped the heat at Tànshān.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngsì (the first day of the lunar month),
reviewed the prisoners,
and attended to governmental affairs.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīnghài (the first day of the lunar month),
traveled east.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngsì (the first day of the lunar month),
the Imperial carriage halted at Déshèng Kǒu.
In winter, the eleventh month,
sent an envoy to invest Sòng as the King of Gāolì.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngxū (the first day of the lunar month),
Xiūgē, the Prince of Sòng Guó, passed away;
court was suspended for five days.
The Emperor’s younger brother Wáng Lóngqìng was promoted in enfeoffment to Prince of Liáng Guó and Governor of Nánjīng,
and the Prince of Zhèng, Lóngyòu, was promoted to Prince of Wú Guó.
In this year,
granted degrees to the two successful candidates in the metropolitan examination, Yáng Yòuxuán and others.
In the seventeenth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐmǎo (the first day of the lunar month),
went to Chángchūn Gōng.
the fourth month,
went to Tànshān to avoid the summer heat.
The sixth month,
Wùrě Wū Zhāoqìng came.
Autumn, the seventh month,
issued an imperial edict concerning the campaign against Sòng to all circuits (dào).
The ninth month, on the day Gēngchén (the first day of the lunar month),
journeyed to Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐhài,
attacked the south.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
shot the “Ghost Arrow.”
Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, the Grand Councilor of the Northern Chancellery (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ) and Prince of Wèi, died.
Hán Déràng was appointed concurrently to manage the affairs of the Northern Chancellery (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ).
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
attacked Suìchéng,
but did not take it.
Xiāo Jìyuǎn was dispatched to attack the stone fort at Lángshānzhèn,
and defeated it.
Subsequently reached Yíngzhōu,
and battled the Sòng army,
capturing their generals Kāng Zhāoyì and Sòng Shùn,
and seizing countless weapons, implements, and armor.
Advanced to attack Lèshòuxiàn,
and captured it.
Subsequently reached Suìchéng,
where the enemy masses held the water’s edge to resist.
Cavalry was unleashed to charge them,
slaughtering nearly all of them.
That year,
the jinshi (presented scholars), Chū Xī and four others, passed the examination.
The eighteenth year, spring, the first month,
returned to Nánjīng,
rewarded the deserving officers and soldiers,
and punished those who disobeyed orders.
An imperial edict commanded all armies to return to their original circuits (dào).
The second month,
journeyed to Yánfāngdiàn.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
made an imperial stop at Qīngquándiàn.
The fifth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
avoided the summer heat at Tànshān.
The sixth month,
Tiělàbù, the younger brother of Gǔniǎn, the rebellious chieftain of the Zǔbǔ, led his tribesmen to surrender.
Gǔniǎn had nowhere to go,
and subsequently surrendered.
An imperial edict commanded his execution.
Autumn, the seventh month,
made an imperial stop at Tāngquán.
The ninth month, on the day Yǐhài (the first day of the lunar month),
made an imperial stop at Hēihé.
Winter, the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū (the first day of the lunar month),
Lǐ Jìqiān’s son, Dézhāo, the Prince of Xīpíng, was appointed Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Shuòfāng Command.
The twelfth month,
the Huíhú (Uighurs) came to pay tribute.
That year,
the jinshi (presented scholars), Nán Chéngbǎo and three others, passed the examination.
The nineteenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnsì,
Guānyīn, the General (Xiángwěn) of the Attendant Corps (Zhīhòu Lángjūn Bān), was appointed Great King of the Six Departments of the Xī.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Huíhú presented a famous physician who was a Buddhist monk (Fànsēng).
The third month, on the day Yǐhài,
the state of Xià sent Lǐ Wénguì to pay tribute.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Pacification and Review Office of the Southwest Region reported a victory against the Dǎngxiàng.
On the day Rénchén,
Empress Xiāo Shì was demoted to Esteemed Consort (Guìfēi) due to a crime.
Grand Chancellor Hán Déràng was granted the name Déchāng.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐsì,
journeyed to the residence of Lóngyòu, the Prince of Wú, to inspect his illness.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
inquired after the health of the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
The fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
avoided the summer heat at Tànshān.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Xiāo Shì was installed as Empress Qítiān.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yēlǜ Wángnú, the General (Xiángwěn) of the Qiānyuèlà, was appointed Great King of the Yǐshì.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
sacrificed a black ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.
The sixth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Kāng Zhāoyì, the captured Sòng general, was appointed Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Zhaoshùn Command.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the state of Xià reported the capture of three prefectures: Sòng, Huán, and Qìng.
An imperial edict was issued to praise them.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Yēlǜ Núguā, the Commander-in-Chief of Dōngjīng, was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Chancellery (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng).
The eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Dálúgǔ tribe came to pay tribute.
The ninth month, on the day Jǐsì (the first day of the lunar month),
inquired after the health of the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
On the day Wùzǐ,
made an imperial stop at Chāngpíng.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Pacification and Review Office of the Southwest Region reported a victory in the campaign against the Tǔyùhún.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
journeyed to Nánjīng.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐhài,
attacked the south.
On the day Rényín,
subsequently reached Yángōu.
Lóngyòu, the Prince of Wú, was transferred and enfeoffed as the Prince of Chǔ.
He remained behind to guard the capital (Jīngshī).
On the day Dīngwèi,
Lóngqìng, the Prince of Liáng, led the vanguard army forward.
On the day Xīnhài,
shot the “Ghost Arrow.”
On the day Rénzǐ,
sacrificed a black ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Liáo army battled the Sòng forces at Suìchéng
and defeated them.
On the day Gēngshēn,
sacrificed black and white sheep to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Bǐngyín,
subsequently reached Mǎnchéng.
Due to the muddy conditions, the army returned to the capital.
The eleventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
shot the “Ghost Arrow.”
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Sòng forces emerged from Yūkǒu and Yìjīnguān to invade.
The scouts Móu Wā and Zhāo Gǔ of the Imperial Hunters (Yúrén) attacked and defeated them.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
watched the fishing at Rúménluò.
Intercalary month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Bígǔdé came to pay tribute.
On the day Jǐwèi,
reduced the taxes on passes and markets.
The twelfth month, on the day Gēngchén,
exempted Nánjīng and Píngzhōu from rents and taxes.
The twentieth year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
went to Yánfāngdiàn.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
a five-colored rainbow appeared in the east.
An edict was issued to pacify and comfort the tribes of the Southwest Region who had submitted.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the state of Xià sent an envoy to present horses and camels as tribute.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yí Lídǐ, the Chancellor (Zǎixiàng) of the Nǚzhí, came to pay tribute.
The second month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Nǚzhí sent their son to attend court.
Gāolì (Koryŏ) sent an envoy to congratulate on the victory against Sòng.
The third month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Xiāo Jìyuǎn, the Chancellor of the Northern Chancellery (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng), and others were dispatched to campaign in the south.
On the day Rénxū,
made an imperial stop at Yuānyāngluò.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngyín (the first day of the lunar month),
Dálǐdǐ, the Grand Guardian (Tàibǎo) of the Civil Service (Wénbān), defeated the Sòng forces at Liángmén.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Xiāo Tàlǐn, the Commander-in-Chief of Nánjīng, defeated the Sòng army at Tàizhōu.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the generals and officers of the southern campaign presented the captives;
titles and rewards were granted according to merit.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Tiělí sent an envoy to pay tribute.
The fifth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
journeyed to Tànshān to avoid the summer heat.
The sixth month,
the state of Xià sent Liú Rénxù to announce the capture of Língzhōu.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ (the first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Xíng Bàopǔ was appointed Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Gāolì sent an envoy to present a map of their country’s geography as tribute.
The ninth month, on the day Guǐsì (the first day of the lunar month),
paid respects at Xiǎnlíng,
and announced the victory of the southern campaign.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐhài (the first day of the lunar month),
arrived back from Xiǎnlíng.
The twelfth month,
the Five Tents and Six Military Commissionerates of the Xī Princely Residence presented the lands of Qījīnshān and Tǔhéchuān.
They were rewarded with gold and silk.
That year,
wheat in Nánjīng and Píngzhōu grew stalks with two ears.
The jinshi (presented scholars), Xíng Xiáng and six others, passed the examination.
The twenty-first year, spring, the first month,
went to Yuānyāngluò.
The third month, on the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict commanded the officials compiling the daily records not to record trivial matters.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
paid court to the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
On the day Wùwǔ,
Tiělí came to pay tribute.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Nǚzhí sent an envoy to pay tribute.
On the day Wùchén,
Five tribes—Wùrě, Bóhǎi, Àolǐmǐ, Yuèlǐdǔ, and Yuèlǐjí—sent envoys to pay tribute.
That month,
Yēlǜ Núguā and Xiāo Tàlǐn captured the Sòng general Wáng Jìzhōng at Wàngdū.
The fifth month, on the day Gēngyín (the first day of the lunar month),
avoided the summer heat at Tànshān.
On the day Dīngsì,
Lǐ Jìqiān, the Prince of Xīpíng, died.
His son, Dézhāo, sent an envoy to report the news.
On the day Jǐmǎo of the sixth month,
the title of Shàngshū Lìng was posthumously granted to Jìqiān,
and Dīng Zhèn, Commissioner of the Western Upper Palace Gate, was sent to express condolences and comfort.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Dǎngxiàng came to pay tribute.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Tiělàlǐ of the Zǔbǔ led various tribes to surrender.
In this month,
Kědūn Chéng was repaired.
In the autumn, the seventh month, day Gēngxū,
the Zǔbǔ and the Wūgǔ came to pay tribute.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yēlǜ Shìlǔ, Administrator of the Xī Princely Residence, was appointed Nányuàn Dàwáng.
In the eighth month, day Yǐyǒu,
Tiělàlǐ of the Zǔbǔ came to court.
On the day Bǐngxū,
paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
In the ninth month, day Jǐhài,
Lǐ Dézhāo of Xià Guó sent an envoy to express thanks for the condolences and gifts.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
visited the hot springs at Nǚ Hé Tāng Quán,
and changed its name to Sōnglín.
In winter, the tenth month, day Dīngsì (the first day of the month),
the Imperial carriage stopped at Qī Dù Hé.
On the day Wùchén,
Lóngyòu, Prince of Chǔ Guó, was appointed Xīnán Miàn Zhāotǎo Shǐ.
In the eleventh month, day Rénchén,
Dàoshìnú, Gāo Jiǔ, and others, sons of the late Yúyuè Yēlǜ Xiūgē, plotted rebellion,
and were executed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the population of the Nányuàn tribes was comprehensively registered.
In the twelfth month, day Guǐwèi,
the tribute payments from the Sānjīng and various circuits were abolished.
In the twenty-second year, spring, the first month, day Dīnghài,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
The second month, day Yǐmǎo (the first day of the month),
the Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Xíng Bàopǔ, Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Nányuàn, passed away;
Court was suspended for three days.
In the third month, day Jǐchǒu,
the tribute payments from the Fan tribes celebrating the Qiānlíng Festival, as well as the tributes for the Winter Solstice and the Double Fifth, were abolished.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Lǐ Dézhāo of Xī Xià sent an envoy to present Jìqiān’s belongings.
In summer, the fourth month, day Dīngmǎo,
paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
In the fifth month,
went to Tàn Shān to escape the heat.
In the sixth month, day Wùwǔ,
Kědūn Chéng was designated Zhènzhōu,
and the army garrison was named Jiàn'ān.
In autumn, the seventh month, day Jiǎshēn,
sent an envoy to enfeoff Lǐ Dézhāo of Xià Guó as Xīpíng Wáng.
On the day Dīnghài,
the tribes of Wùrě, Púnúlǐ, Pōu'ālǐ, Yuèlǐdǔ, Àolǐmǐ, and others came to pay tribute.
In the eighth month, day Bǐngchén,
the Dǎngxiàng came to pay tribute.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Tiělàlǐ, chief of the Zǔbǔ, came to court.
On the day Wùchén,
Tiělàlǐ requested a marriage alliance,
which was not permitted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Imperial carriage stopped at Quǎnyá Shān.
In the ninth month, day Jǐchǒu,
Gāolì was notified concerning the southern punitive expedition.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
visited Nánjīng.
The Nǚzhí sent envoys to present the wife and children of Wū Zhāoqìng whom they had captured.
On the day Dīngwèi,
sacrifices were offered at the temple of Emperor Tàizōng.
Mólǔgǔ, Great King of the Northern Chancellery, and Lǎojūnnú, Grand Commandant, were put in charge of the troops of the Northern and Southern Princely Residences.
On the day Gēngxū,
Lóngyòu, Prince of Chǔ Guó, was ordered to remain and guard the capital.
In the intercalary month, day Jǐwèi,
started the punitive expedition to the south.
On the day Guǐhài,
arrived at Gù'ān.
The captured spies were used in the ghost-arrow ceremony.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
sacrifices of a black ox and a white horse were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Liáo forces fought the Sòng troops at Tángxīng,
and thoroughly routed them.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Xiāo Tàlǐn fought the Sòng army at Suìchéng
and defeated them.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the army encamped at Wàngdū.
In winter, the tenth month, day Yǐyǒu,
sacrifices of black and white sheep were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Bǐngxū,
attacked Yíngzhōu,
but failed to overcome it.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Qízhōu was taken,
and rewards were given to the surrendered troops.
Sacrifices of wine and dried meat were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Lǐ Dézhāo, Prince of Xīpíng, sent an envoy to thank [the court] for the imperial enfeoffment documents.
In the eleventh month, day Guǐhài,
Yēlǜ Kèlǐ, Grand Commander of the Cavalry, encountered Sòng troops at Míngzhōu
and repelled them.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Xiāo Páiyā, Resident Administrator of Dōngjīng, captured and presented Sòng officials from Wèifǔ, including Tián Féngjí, Guō Shǒuróng, Cháng Xiǎn, and Liú Chuò.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Shànbǔ, Great King of the Nányuàn, reported that Sòng had sent a messenger to present Wáng Jìzhōng with bows and arrows
and secretly requested peace.
An edict ordered Jìzhōng to meet the envoy,
and peace was permitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Déqīng Military Prefecture was breached and captured.
On the day Rénshēn,
arrived at Chányuān.
Xiāo Tàlǐn was killed by a hidden crossbow bolt.
On the day Yǐhài,
Tōnglì Military Prefecture was breached and captured.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Sòng sent Cáo Lìyòng, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Reverent Deportment, to request peace.
Immediately, Hán Shī, Commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard, was sent back holding a document in reply.
The twelfth month, day Gēngchén (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse;
it was total.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Sòng again sent Cáo Lìyòng.
Because there was no intention to return territory,
Yáo Jiǎnzhī, Grand General of the Gate Guard, was sent holding a document in response.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Sòng sent Lǐ Jìchāng to request peace,
agreeing to treat the Huáng Tàihòu as their paternal aunt,
and willing to annually provide 100,000 ounces of silver
and 200,000 bolts of silk.
This was permitted,
and Dīng Zhèn, Commissioner of the Palace Gate, was immediately sent holding a document in reply.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an edict ordered all armies to stand down from alert.
In this month,
the armies returned.
The Huáng Tàihòu granted the surname Yēlǜ to Hán Déchāng, Grand Chancellor and Prince of Qí,
and transferred his princedom to Jìn.
In this year,
Lǐ Kěfēng and two other successful candidates passed the civil service examination.
In the twenty-third year, spring, the first month, day Wùwǔ,
returned and stopped at Nánjīng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
a grand banquet was held for the generals and soldiers;
titles and rewards were granted according to merit.
In the second month, day Bǐngxū,
the government monopoly market was re-established at Zhènwǔ Military Prefecture.
On the day Dīngsì,
Xià Guó sent an envoy to announce the capture of Sòng's Qīngchéng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
Huàgē, the Tìyǐn, was appointed Nányuàn Dàwáng,
and Lǎojūnnú, Supreme Military Administrator, was appointed Tìyǐn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Dǎngxiàng tribes were reorganized.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Huíhú came to pay tribute.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the title of Commissioner for Pacification of Fēihú in Yìzhōu was changed to Commissioner for Comfort and Pacification.
In summer, the fourth month, day Bǐngxū,
the Nǚzhí and the Āsàlán Huíhú each sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Tiělí came to pay tribute.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Dǎngxiàng came and invaded.
The fifth month, day Wùshēn (the first day of the month),
Sòng sent Sūn Jǐn and others to celebrate the Huáng Tàihòu’s birthday.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
gold and silk were bestowed upon the families of the officers and soldiers who died in battle.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Gāolì, due to the peace agreement with Sòng,
sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
In the sixth month, day Rénchén,
went to Tàn Shān to escape the heat.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Tiělàlǐ, chief of the Zǔbǔ, sent an envoy to congratulate [us] on the peace with Sòng.
On the day Jǐhài,
nine tribes of Dádàn Guó sent envoys to make a formal visit.
In autumn, the seventh month, day Guǐchǒu,
inquired after the welfare of the Huáng Tàihòu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Dǎngxiàng came to pay tribute.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
sacrifices of a black ox and a white horse were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Rénxū,
the Wūgǔ came to pay tribute.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Nǚzhí sent envoys to pay tribute.
The Āsàlán Huíhú sent envoys requesting that previous envoys be permitted to stay,
but all were dismissed.
In the ninth month, day Jiǎxū,
Grand Commandant Ālǐ and Grand Tutor Yáng Liù were sent to congratulate the Sòng ruler on his birthday.
In winter, the tenth month, day Bǐngzǐ, the first day of the month,
Bǐgǔdé came to pay tribute.
Day Wùzǐ,
held court for the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
Day Jiǎwǔ,
the Imperial Retinue halted at Qīdùhé.
Day Guǐmǎo,
the annual payments (suìbì) from Sòng first arrived,
and thereafter became regular.
In the eleventh month, day Wùshēn,
the Emperor sent Grand Guardian (Tàibǎo) Hèzhù and Distributor (Bāngěi Shǐ) Hán Zhuǒn,
and the Empress Dowager sent Grand Preceptor (Tàishī) Pénnú and Palace Aide for Policy Review (Zhèngshì Shèrén) Gāo Zhèng as envoys to Sòng to celebrate the New Year’s Day (Zhèngdàn).
Day Xīnhài,
observed fishing at the Sānggānhé.
Day Dīngsì,
an edict ordered Grand Chancellor (Dà Chéngxiàng) Yēlǜ Déchāng to be removed from the Palace Register (gōngjí),
and affiliated with the Horizontal Tent (Héngzhàng).
In the twelfth month, day Bǐngshēn,
Sòng sent Zhōu Jiàn and others to congratulate (the Emperor) on the Qiānlíng Festival.
Day Dīngyǒu,
(Sòng) again sent Zhāng Ruògǔ and others to congratulate (the Emperor) on the New Year’s Day.
The 24th year, spring, the first month,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
Summer, the fifth month, day Rén'yín, the first day of the month,
visited Tànshān to escape the summer heat.
Imprisoned Imperial Consort Dowager (Huáng Tàifēi) Hú Liǎn in Huáizhōu,
imprisoned Lady Yí Lǎn in Nánjīng,
and all the rest of the partisans were buried alive.
Autumn, the seventh month, day Xīnchǒu, the first day of the month,
traveled south.
The eighth month, day Bǐngxū,
the Xuānjiào Gate of the Nánjīng Palace was renamed Yuánhé;
the Outer Three Gates were renamed Nánduān;
the Left Flanking Gate (Zuǒ Yè Mén) was renamed Wànchūn;
and the Right Flanking Gate (Yòu Yè Mén) was renamed Qiānqiū.
In this month,
Cáo Shòu, King of Dùnhuáng in Shāzhōu, sent an envoy to present horses from Dàshí Guó and fine jade,
and was rewarded with objects such as robes and silver vessels.
The ninth month,
visited Nánjīng.
Winter, the tenth month, day Gēngwǔ, the first day of the month,
the Emperor led the assembled officials to confer the honorable title of Ruìdé Shénlüè Yìngyùn Qǐhuà Chéngtiān Huáng Tàihòu upon the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu),
and the assembled officials conferred the honorable title of Zhìdé Guǎngxiào Zhāoshèng Tiānfǔ Huángdì upon the Emperor.
A general amnesty was granted.
In this year,
twenty-three successful candidates (jìnshì), including Yáng Jí, were appointed to office.
The 25th year, spring, the first month,
construction of Zhōngjīng began.
The second month,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
Summer, the fourth month,
escaped the summer heat at Tànshān.
The sixth month,
Imperial Consort Dowager Hú Liǎn was granted death at her place of confinement.
Autumn, the seventh month, day Rénshēn,
the mother of Lǐ Dézhāo, Prince of Xīpíng, died.
An envoy was sent to convey condolences and offer sacrifices.
Day Jiǎxū,
an envoy was sent to authorize his return to office (qǐfù).
The ninth month,
Xiāo Túyù, the Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Circuit (Xīběi Lù Zhāotǎo Shǐ), campaigned against the Zǔbǔ,
and defeated them.
Winter, the tenth month, day Bǐngshēn,
the Imperial Retinue halted at Zhōngjīng.
The twelfth month, day Jǐyǒu,
famine relief was distributed to the starving people of Ráozhōu.
The 26th year, spring, the second month,
went to Cháng Luò.
Summer, the fourth month, day Xīnmǎo, the first day of the month,
offered sacrifices at Mùyè Shān.
The fifth month, day Gēngshēn, the first day of the month,
returned to Shàngjīng.
Day Bǐngyín,
Gāolì presented mats woven from dragon’s beard grass.
Day Jǐsì,
an envoy was sent to celebrate the completion of Zhōngjīng.
Day Gēngwǔ,
sacrifices were offered at the Zǔ Líng and Huái Líng Mausoleums.
Day Xīnwèi,
the Imperial Retinue halted at Huáizhōu.
Autumn, the seventh month,
the posthumous titles (shì) of Tàizǔ, Tàizōng, Ràngguó Huángdì, and Shìzōng were augmented,
and the Imperial Younger Brother Lǐ Hú was posthumously titled Qīnshùn Huángdì.
Winter, the tenth month, day Wùzǐ, the first day of the month,
visited Zhōngjīng.
The twelfth month,
Xiāo Túyù reported having campaigned against the Gānzhōu Uighurs (Huíhú),
forcing their king Yēlālǐ to submit,
and then returned after offering comfort and reassurance.
In this year,
thirteen successful candidates (jìnshì), including Shǐ Kèzhōng, were appointed to office.
The 27th year, spring, the first month,
fished in the Tǔhé.
Hunted at Ruìlù Yuán.
Summer, the fourth month, day Bǐngxū, the first day of the month,
the Imperial Retinue halted at Zhōngjīng,
and began construction of the palace buildings.
Day Gēngxū,
the Administration Office (Chǔzhì Sī) of Bàzhōu was abolished.
Autumn, the seventh month, day Jiǎyín, the first day of the month,
continuous heavy rain fell,
and the four rivers—Huáng Hé, Tǔ Hé, Wòlà Hé, and Yīnliáng Hé—all overflowed,
washing away and submerging civilian dwellings.
The eighth month, day Jiǎshēn,
traveled north.
Winter, the eleventh month, day Rénzǐ, the first day of the month,
performed the Chái Cè Rite (ceremony of burnt offering).
The twelfth month, day Yǐyǒu,
traveled south.
The Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) became ill.
Day Wùzǐ,
a general amnesty was widely proclaimed.
Day Xīnmǎo,
the Empress Dowager passed away at the traveling palace (xínggōng).
Day Rénchén,
envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Sòng, Xià, and Gāolì.
Day Wùshēn,
went to Zhōngjīng.
Day Jǐyǒu,
an edict excused the celebration of the Qiānlíng Festival.
In this year,
three people, including Liú Èryí, were tested in the presence of the Emperor.
Basic Annals No. 15, Shèngzōng 6
The 28th year, spring, the first month, day Xīnhài, the first day of the month,
congratulations were not received.
Day Jiǎyín,
went to Qián Líng.
Day Guǐyǒu,
the coffin of the Deceased Empress Dowager (Dàxíng Huáng Tàihòu) was placed and secured at the Zū Tú Hall in Qiánzhōu.
The second month, day Bǐngxū,
Sòng sent Wáng Suí, Wáng Rú, and others to convey condolences and offer sacrifices.
Day Jǐhài,
Gāolì sent Wèi Shǒuyú and others to offer sacrifices.
In this month,
Left General-in-Chief of the Dragon and Tiger Guard (Zuǒ Lónghǔ Wèi Shàng Jiāngjūn) Xiāo Hézhuó was sent to present the relics of the Deceased Empress Dowager to Sòng,

and subsequently, Military Commissioner of Línhǎi Command (Línhǎi Jūn Jiédù Shǐ) Xiāo Xūliè and Left General-in-Chief of the Leader Guard (Zuǒ Lǐngjūn Wèi Shàng Jiāngjūn) Zhāng Chóngjì were sent to thank Sòng for their condolences and sacrifices.
The third month, day Guǐmǎo,
the posthumous title of Shèngshén Xuānxiàn Huánghòu was conferred upon the Deceased Empress Dowager.
In this month,
Sòng and Gāolì sent envoys to attend the funeral.
Summer, the fourth month, day Jiǎzǐ,
the Empress Dowager was buried at Qián Líng.
Grand Chancellor Yēlǜ Déchāng was granted the name Lóngyùn.
Day Gēngwǔ,
(He) was granted a residence and land for a satellite burial.
The fifth month, day Jǐmǎo, the first day of the month,
went to Zhōngjīng.
Day Xīnmǎo,
escaped the summer heat at Qījīn Shān.
Day Yǐsì,
Xiāo Túyù, the Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Circuit, reported attacking the Gānzhōu Uighurs,
capturing Sùzhōu,
and taking all its inhabitants captive.
An edict ordered the repair of the old city wall at Tǔwěikǒu to settle them there.
Day Bǐngwǔ,
Kāng Zhào, Defense Commissioner of Xījīng in Gāolì, assassinated his sovereign, Sòng,
and arbitrarily installed Sòng’s older cousin, Xún;
an edict ordered all circuits to repair their armor and weapons,
in preparation for an eastern expedition.
Autumn, the eighth month, day Wùshēn,
famine relief was distributed to the starving people of Píngzhōu.
Day Xīnhài,
visited Zhōngjīng.
Day Bǐngyín,
paid respects at the Xiǎn Líng and Qián Líng Mausoleums.
Day Dīngmǎo,
personally led the campaign to attack Gāolì,
and sent an envoy to inform Sòng.
Imperial Younger Brother Lóngyòu, Prince of Chǔ, was appointed as Garrison Commander (Liúshǒu) in the capital,
Xiāo Páiyā, Chancellor of the Northern Administration (Běi Fǔ Zǎixiàng) and Commandant-Escort (Fùmǎ Dūwèi), was appointed Supreme Commander (Dūtǒng),
and Sēngnú, Northern Secretary (Běimiàn Línyá), was appointed Inspector-General (Dūjiān).
The ninth month, day Yǐyǒu,
an envoy was sent to invest Lǐ Dézhāo, Prince of Xīpíng, as King of Xià.
Day Xīnmǎo,
Privy Council Academician (Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì) Gāo Zhèng and Reception Commissioner (Yǐnjìn Shǐ) Hán Shí were sent to deliver an imperial message inquiring about Xún, the King of Gāolì.
Winter, the tenth month, day Bǐngwǔ, the first day of the month,
the Nǚzhí presented ten thousand fine horses,
requesting to join the campaign against Gāolì,
which was permitted.
King Xún sent an envoy bearing a memorial requesting the withdrawal of the army,
but this was not granted.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
the great army crossed the Yālù Jiāng.
Kāng Zhào resisted the fight,
but was defeated,
retreating to defend Tóngzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhào emerged again.
The Yòupíshì Xiángwěn, Yēlǜ Dílǔ, captured Zhào and his deputy general Lǐ Lì,
pursuing and killing them for dozens of *lǐ*.
They captured the provisions, supplies, armor, and weapons that had been abandoned.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the prefectures of Tóng, Huò, Guì, Níng, and others all surrendered.
Pái Yā arrived at Núgǔdá Lǐng,
encountered enemy troops,
and defeated them in battle.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wáng Xún sent an envoy submitting a memorial requesting to attend court.
This was permitted.
The army was forbidden from taking captives or engaging in plunder.
Mǎ Bǎoyòu, Secretariat Drafter, was made Resident General of Kāijīng,
and Wáng Bā, Commandant of Ānzhōu, was made Deputy Resident General.
Yǐ Lǐn, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince (Tàizǐ Tàishī), was dispatched with one thousand cavalry
to escort Bǎoyòu and others to the capital.
On the *rénchén* day,
the defending general Zhuó Sīzhèng killed Hán Xǐsūn and ten other Liao envoys.
He led troops out to resist,
causing Bǎoyòu and the others to return.
Yǐ Lǐn was sent leading troops to attack them.
Sīzhèng then fled to Xījīng.
The city was besieged for five days without success,
and the imperial retinue halted west of the city.
Bóhǎi Tuóshī, Director of the Bureau of Rites (Lǐbù Lángzhōng) of Gāolì, came and surrendered.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Pái Yā, Pén Nú, and others were dispatched to attack Kāijīng.
They encountered Gāolì troops
and defeated them.
Wáng Xún abandoned the city and fled.
Subsequently, Kāijīng was burned.
They reached Qīngjiāng
and then returned.
In the twenty-ninth year, spring, the first month, on the *yǐhài* new moon day,
the troops returned to the capital.
All the cities that had previously surrendered mutinied again.
Upon reaching the steep ridge valley south of Guìzhōu,
heavy rain fell for several days continuously.
Horses and camels were all exhausted,
and much armor and weaponry was abandoned.
They were only able to cross once the weather cleared.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
they reached Yālù Jiāng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Empress and the Imperial Brother, Chǔguówáng Lóngyòu, welcomed them at Láiyuǎn Chéng.
On the *rénchén* day,
an imperial decree ordered the disbanding of all armies.
On the *jǐhài* day,
they reached Dōngjīng.
Second month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Qián and Xiǎn Mausoleums were visited.
On the *wùmǎo* day,
the captured Gāolì people were distributed among the various imperial mausoleums and temples,
and the remainder were bestowed upon imperial relatives and high ministers.
Third month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Grand Chancellor and Jìnguówáng, Yēlǜ Lóngyùn, died.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Imperial Brother, Chǔguówáng Lóngyòu, was provisionally put in charge of the affairs of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì).
Gāo Zhèng, Rectifying Scholar of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì), was made Vice Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Nánjīng and Píngzhōu suffered flooding;
relief was provided.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Yēlǜ Shìlǔ, Grand Prince of the Northern Bureau (Běiyuàn Dàwáng), was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs,
and was enfeoffed as Hánwáng.
Yēlǜ Shìliáng, Gentleman of the Northern Bureau (Běiyuàn Lángjūn), was made Grand Prince of the Northern Bureau.

Liú Shènxíng, former Commissioner of the Three Bureaus, was made Participator in Determining Government Affairs and concurrently in charge of the affairs of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì).
Summer, fourth month,
the heat was cleared at Lǎogǔ Guō.
Fifth month, on the *jiǎxū* new moon day,
an imperial decree ordered that matters already memorialized be sent to the relevant department to be appended to the daily calendar.
Another decree stated that if a member of the *zhàng* clans committed a crime,
they should be branded and tattooed according to the precedent for people of the various tribes.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Liú Shènxíng was made Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.
Xíng Bàozhì, Chancellor of the Southern Administration (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng), was put in charge of the affairs of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.
Sixth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Yùzhōu and Lìzhōu were elevated to Inspecting Commissioners' posts.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Hánwáng Yēlǜ Shìlǔ died.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Huàgē, Grand Prince of the Southern Bureau, was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an imperial decree ordered Xiāo Túyù, Northwest Route Pacification Commissioner and Commandant-Escort, to pacify the western borderlands.
Regional Commissioners (Jiédùshǐ) were established for the various Zhǔbǔ tribes.
That autumn,
hunting took place at Píngdì Sōnglín.
Winter, tenth month, on the *gēngzǐ* new moon day,
the imperial retinue halted at Guǎngpíng Diàn.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Grand Chancellor and Jìnguówáng, Yēlǜ Lóngyùn, was posthumously given the title Manager of the Affairs of the Secretariat (Shàngshū Lìng),
with the posthumous name Wénzhōng.
Eleventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* new moon day,
the emperor visited Xiǎnzhōu.
Twelfth month, on the *gēngzǐ* new moon day,
he returned to Guǎngpíng Diàn.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
because Xíng Bàozhì, who was in charge of the affairs of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs, was advanced in years,
an imperial decree permitted him to ride in a small carriage when attending court.
In this month,
the two prefectures of Guī and Níng were established.
In this year,
imperial examinations were held,
and Gāo Chéngyán and one other person passed the examinations (Jí dì).
Kāitài Era, first year, spring, first month, on the *jǐsì* new moon day,
Sòng dispatched Zhào Xiāng and Fú Chénghàn to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the chieftains of thirty Nǚzhí tribes from Chángbáishān came to offer tribute
and begged to be granted noble rank and official position.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the imperial retinue halted at Wángzǐ Yuàn.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a sacrifice was offered to Mùyè Shān from afar.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Pú Niǎn, Grand Protector (Tàibǎo) of the Nǚzhí, and others came to court.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
hunting took place at Mǎihélǔ Lín.
On the *gēngyín* day,
a sacrifice was offered at Mùyè Shān.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Hélǐxǐ, Grand Prince of Hésūguǎn (Hésūguǎn Dàwáng), came to court.
Second month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the imperial retinue halted at Ruìlù Yuán.
Third month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Yùzhōu was made an Inspecting Command
and was no longer subordinate to Wǔdìng Jūn.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the emperor went to Wěi Luò.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an imperial decree enfeoffed eight imperial daughters as Commandery Princesses (Jùnzhǔ).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial decree fixed a day by divination to perform the rites of worshipping the mountains and the Grand Willow Shooting Ceremony (Dà Shèliǔ zhī Lǐ).
Xiāo Níng, Northern Chancellor, Commandant-Escort, and Lánlíng Jùnwáng,
and Xíng Bàozhì, Commissioner of Military Affairs and Minister of Works (Sīkōng), were ordered to supervise the relevant departments in preparing the ritual items.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Imperial Brother, Chǔguówáng Lóngyòu, was transferred and enfeoffed as Qíguówáng,
and was appointed Resident General of Dōngjīng.
Summer, fourth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Gāolì sent Cài Zhōngshùn,
requesting to be allowed to refer to themselves as subjects (chēng chén) as before.
An imperial decree ordered Wáng Xún to personally attend court.
On the *rényín* day,
Xiàguó sent an envoy to present fine horses.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Earl of Wind (Fēng Bó).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Xiāo Fónú, former Chǎngwěn of the Mèngfù Fáng, was made Left Judicial Commissioner (Zuǒ Yílíbì).
Fifth month, on the *wùchén* new moon day,
the emperor returned to Shàngjīng.
An imperial decree appointed Péi Xuángǎn and Xíng Xiáng to manage the Civil Service Examinations of the Board of Rites (Lǐbù Gòngjǔ).
Shǐ Jiǎn and nineteen other Presented Scholars (Jìnshì) passed the examinations.
Commandant-Escort Xiāo Shàozōng was made Defense Commissioner of Zhèngzhōu.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Xíng Bàozhì was made Regional Commissioner of Dàtóng Jūn.
Sixth month,
the imperial retinue halted at Shàngjīng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Suìzhēn was made Regional Commissioner of Liáoxīng Jūn.
Suì Zhèng was made Commissioner of Court Affairs of the Northern Bureau,
Zhāng Zhāoyíng was made Commissioner of Court Affairs of the Southern Bureau,
Yēlǜ Shòuyì was made Deputy Resident General of Shàngjīng,
and Kòu Qīng was made Regional Commissioner of Zhāngdé Jūn.
Yēlǜ Shìshēnnú and Lǐ Cāo were appointed to serve as the chief and deputy envoys (Guóxìn Shǐ Fù) conveying birthday felicitations to Sòng.
Xiāo Niègǔn and Qí Tài were appointed as the chief and deputy envoys conveying New Year felicitations to Sòng.
Presented Scholars Kāng Wénzhāo, Zhāng Sùchén, and Láng Xuándá were implicated for criticizing Péi Xuángǎn and Xíng Xiáng, who were managing the examinations, for alleged partiality.
Lǐ Wàn, Proofreader of the Palace Library (Mìshū Shěng Zhèngzì), submitted a memorial,
the language of which involved resentment and slander.
They were all punished with a flogging and exiled.
Wàn was assigned forced labor at Xiànhé Yě.
Eighth month, on the *bǐngshēn* new moon day,
Tiělí Nàshā and others escorted over one hundred households of Wūyě to Bīnzhōu.
Silk was bestowed upon them.
On that day,
Nàshā requested the bestowal of a Buddha statue and Confucian texts.
An imperial decree granted one Hùguó Rénwáng Buddha statue,
and one copy each of the *Yì*, *Shī*, *Shū*, *Chūnqiū*, and *Lǐ Jì*.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Gāolì King Wáng Xún sent Tián Gǒngzhī with a memorial claiming illness prevented him from attending court.
An imperial decree ordered the reoccupation of the six prefectures' territory.
In this month,
Qíguówáng Lóngyòu died.
Court was suspended for five days.
Winter, tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
the emperor went to Zhōngjīng.
Intercalary month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lóngyòu was posthumously granted the title Acting Grand Preceptor (Shǒu Tàishī),
civil and military officials added the exalted title *Hóngwén Xuānwǔ Zūndào Zhìdé Chóngrén Guǎngxiào Cōngruì Zhāoshèng Shénzàn Tiānfǔ Huángdì*.
A great amnesty was granted,
and the era name was changed to Kāitài.
Yōudū Fǔ was changed to Xījīn Fǔ,
Jìběi Xiàn was changed to Xījīn Xiàn,
Yōudū Xiàn was changed to Wǎnpíng Xiàn,
and favors were extended throughout the court and the regions.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the envoys of the Xià State and the Attendant Officials of the Eastern Head, Cáo Wénbīn, Lǚ Wénguì, Dòu Guīyòu, Shǒuróng, Wǔ Yuánzhèng, and others, were granted varying ranks of nobility.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Zhāng Tíngměi, former Recorder of Liáozhōu, whose family had lived together for six generations,
and Líu Xīngyìn of Yíkūnzhōu, whose family had lived together for four generations,
were each granted three years of tax exemption.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Xiāo Túyù, Commissioner for Northwest Military Operations, reported that the Grand Tutor of the Seven Tribes, Ālǐdǐ, due to the resentment of his tribal people,
had killed Bà'àn, the Military Commissioner of his own tribe, and massacred his family in rebellion;
the Zhǔbǔ captured Ālǐdǐ and presented him,
but the various tribes along the border all rebelled.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the stone statues of the various emperors from Nánjīng were respectfully moved to the Guāndé Hall in Zhōngjīng,
and those of Jǐngzōng and Empress Xuānxiàn were moved to the Wǔluán Hall in Shàngjīng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
relief was distributed to the famine victims in Fèngshèngzhōu.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor’s younger brother, Lóngqìng, the King of Qínjìn State, was granted an iron certificate (iron pass).
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Líu Chén stated that Gāo Kěyuán of the Court of Imperial Affairs and Lǐ Kějǔ, the Investigator of the Zhōngjīng Resident Office, were clear and impartial in handling legal cases.
An imperial decree ordered their exceptional promotion.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial decree stated that for famine victims in the various circuits who suffered from floods and had pawned their children (male or female),
starting from the first month of the following year,
their daily labor should be calculated at ten *wén* of coin,
and when the value (of the pawned child) was exhausted by the labor wages,
they should be sent back to their homes.
Guīzhōu reported that its residents were originally relocated from Xīnluó,
and were not yet skilled in writing;
they requested the establishment of schools to educate them.
An imperial decree approved the request.
In the seven *zhōu*—Guìdé, Lónghuà, Yíkūn, Shuāng, Liáo, Tóng, and Zǔ—
an imperial decree was issued starting the collection of commercial taxes (upon arrival).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered the construction of towers for proclaiming imperial edicts in all garrisons.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the *guǐsì* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Péi Xuángǎn was appointed Director of the Hanlin Academy,
Xíng Xiáng was appointed Attendant Censor,
Shí Yòngzhōng was appointed Hanlin Academician,
Lǚ Détuī was appointed Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs,
Zhāng Jiǎn was appointed Aide to the Bureau of Governmental Affairs,
Xíng Bàozhì was granted the title *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī* and appointed acting Minister of Works (*Sīkōng*) concurrently serving as Palace Attendant (*Shìzhōng*),
Wáng Jìzhōng was appointed Resident of Zhōngjīng and Acting Grand Tutor,
Líu Jīng, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to Minister of Works (*Gōngbù Shàngshū*),
the Imperial Son-in-Law Xiāo Shàozōng was granted the title Acting Grand Tutor,
Yēlǜ Kòngwēn was promoted to Director of Governmental Affairs (*Zhèngshì Lìng*),
and enfeoffed as the King of Yōu.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
[The Emperor] went to Ruìlù Yuán.
Yēlǜ Huàgē, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery, was enfeoffed as the King of Bīn.
Lady Mǎ was appointed *Lìyí*,
Lady Gěng was appointed *Shūyí*,
Lady Bái, Director of Sleeping Quarters, was appointed *Zhāoyí*,
Lady Lǐ, Director of Clothing, was appointed *Shùnyí*,
Lady Ài, Director of Works, was appointed *Fāngyí*,
and Lady Sūn, Director of Ceremonies, was appointed *Héyí*.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
The Wūgǔ and Díliè rebelled.
Yánshòu, the Grand Commandant (*Xiángwěn*) of the Right Pìshì, led troops to suppress them.
In this month,
the troops of the Dádàn State besieged Zhènzhōu.
The garrison firmly held its position,
and [the invaders] soon withdrew.
The second month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an imperial decree changed Màiwù Chuān to Xiàngléi Xiàn,
Nǚhé Chuān to Shénshuǐ Xiàn,
Luójiā Jūn to Lǘshān Xiàn,
Shānzǐ Chuān to Fùshù Xiàn,
Xíjiā Zhài to Lóngshān Xiàn,
Ālǎnyù to Quànnóng Xiàn,
Sōngshān Chuān to Sōngshān Xiàn,
and Jīndiànzǐ to Jīnyuán Xiàn.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Gāo Zhèng, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery, was dispatched to inspect the prisons in the various circuits.
In the third month, on the *rénchén* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Huàgē, having generally pacified the Northwest Route,
left troops to garrison Zhènzhōu
and proceeded to the traveling palace.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Sun Worship Ceremony was performed.
An imperial decree granted Shàngjīng's request
to use the more than 25,400 households registered by Hán Bīn in the *zhōu* of Shànguó, Tàlǔ Hé, Fèng, Háo, and others,
to establish ten counties, including Chángbà, Xīngrén, and Bǎohé.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
[The Emperor] went to Miǎnshān.
The fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Huàgē and others were again ordered to campaign in the west.
The sixth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Yēlǜ Zīzhōng, Imperial Censor, was sent as an envoy to Gāolì
to reclaim the old territory of the six *zhōu*.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Wūgǔ and Díliè were both restored to their former territories.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Xiézhěn, Commissioner for Southwest Military Operations and Director of Governmental Affairs, reported
that all the rebellious Dǎngxiàng tribes had fled north of the Yellow River (*Huáng Hé*) to Múnǎn Shān;
the non-rebellious tribes of Gédǎng and Wūmí then occupied that land,
but now they had moved west again.
When questioned, they claimed they were following water and pasture.
If steps were not taken soon,
it might later cause trouble.
He also heard that many of those who had rebelled previously and subsequently sought refuge in Xī Xià,
but Xī Xià refused to accept them.
An imperial decree ordered that an envoy be sent to inquire again about the reason for the westward migration,
and if they returned to their former territory,
they could then be pacified and persuaded.
The envoy did not return with a report,
and the Emperor was angry,
intending to launch a punitive expedition against them.
He then issued a decree to Lǐ Dézhāo, saying:
"Now the Dǎngxiàng have rebelled.
I intend to campaign in the west;
you must attack in the east,
so as not to lose the strategic advantage of flanking maneuvers."
Furthermore, he ordered all armies to procure stout horses.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Díliè, the Controller of the Imperial Kin (*Tìyǐn*), was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Chancellery,
and Wǔgē, the Grand Commandant (*Tàiwèi*), was appointed Controller of the Imperial Kin.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
[The Emperor] fished at Qūgōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial decree ordered that the interest money of the Dūnmù Palace treasury be used to relieve the poor.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Huàgē and others defeated the forces of Wūbā, the chief of the Zhǔbǔ.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
The Imperial Son Zōngxùn was enfeoffed as the Controller of the Imperial Kin of the Great Palace.
The eighth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Lǐ Yánhóng, the Envoy of Introduction, was dispatched to bestow chariots and horses upon Lǐ Dézhāo, the King of Xià State, and Princess Yìchéng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Zīzhōng returned from his mission to Gāolì.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐwèi* day, the first day of the lunar month,
[The Emperor] hunted north of Biāojǐng.
Yēlǜ Āyíng and others were ordered to serve as envoys to Sòng to offer birthday felicitations.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
The imperial procession halted at Chángluò.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Grand Commandant Zhāng Mǎliú presented a Nǚzhí man who was knowledgeable about Gāolì affairs.
The Emperor questioned him,
and he said:
"Three years ago, I was captured by Gāolì,
and served as a palace official (*lángguān*),
which is why I know these matters.
Traveling east from Kāijīng for seven days on horseback,
there is a large fortress
as large as Kāijīng.
The rare treasures paid as tribute by the surrounding *zhōu*
are all stored here.
South of the *zhōu* of Shèng and Luó, and others,
there are also two large fortresses,
storing similar amounts.
If the main army follows the northern route,
passes north of the Gésū Residence of the Nǚzhí,
crosses the Yālù Jiāng (Yalu River) directly,
and proceeds up the great river,
reaching Guōzhōu where it meets the main road,
then Gāolì can be captured."
The Emperor accepted this advice.
The eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Huàgē, King of Bīn and Commissioner of Military Affairs, was found guilty regarding the western campaign,
stripped of his rank and title,
