and demoted to serve as Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Army.
The twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Shìliáng, Grand Prince of the Northern Chancellery, was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery,
and enfeoffed as the King of Qí.
Chancellor Líu Shèng was appointed Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History,
Niú Lín was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhāngguó Army,
and Xiāo Xiàomù was appointed Commissioner for Northwest Military Operations.
Six candidates, including the successful scholar Xiānyú Màozhāo, passed the imperial examination.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
Wūbā, the chief of the Zhǔbǔ, came to court,
and was enfeoffed as a king.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
[The Emperor] went to Húnhé.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Nǚzhí and the Tiělí each sent envoys to present tribute.
That night,
a comet was seen in the west.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
[The Emperor] hunted along the bank of the Huáng Hé.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
The Emperor and the Empress hunted at Ruìlù Yuán.
The second month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
an imperial decree increased the monthly salaries of the Commissioner of Military Affairs and all officials below that rank.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Zīzhōng, Vice Resident of Shàngjīng, was again sent as an envoy to Gāolì to reclaim the old territory of the six *zhōu*.
Yēlǜ Shìliáng was dispatched to construct a city at Zhāozhōu.
On the day Wùshēn,
Transport Commissioners (Zhuănyùnshĭ) were established in Nánjīng, Fèngshèng, Píngzhōu, Wèizhōu, Yúnzhōu, Yìngzhōu, Shuòzhōu, and other prefectures.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùwŭ,
an imperial edict commanded that criminal cases within the jurisdiction of Nánjīng should not be unduly prolonged,
lest they impede agricultural work.
On the day Guĭhài,
the Wūgŭ rebelled.
On the day Yĭhài,
Cáo Shùn of the Shāzhōu Uighurs sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day Bĭngzĭ,
Xiāo Xiàomù, Director-in-Chief of Pacification and Investigation for the Northwest Circuit (Xīběi Lù Zhāotăo Dūjiān), was appointed Chief Minister of the Northern Administration (Běi Fŭ Zăixiàng).
In the fifth month, on the first day, Yĭyŏu,
[the Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Miănshān.
In the sixth month, on the day Yĭhài,
the two Imperial Maternal Uncle clans, Bálĭ and Yĭshì, were consolidated into one Yizhàng (Tribe/Administration),
and Xiāo Díliè, the Yílíbì of the Yĭshì clan, was made Xiángwĕn (Military Commissioner) to command them all.
On the day Jiăshēn,
the Emperor’s nephew Húdūgŭ was enfeoffed as Prince of Guăngpíng Commandery (Guăngpíng Jùnwáng).
That summer,
an imperial edict commanded the Imperial Maternal Uncle Xiángwĕn Xiāo Díliè, Yēlǜ Tuánshí (Resident General of Dōngjīng), and others to campaign against Gāolì (Goguryeo),
to build a pontoon bridge across the Yālù Jiāng (Yalu River),
and to fortify Bǎozhōu, Xuānyìzhōu, Dìngyuănzhōu, and other prefectures.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, Yĭyŏu,
[the Emperor] went to Píngdì Sōnglín.
On the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict instructed the Department of State Affairs (Zhèngshì Shĕng) and the Bureau of Military Affairs (Shūmì Yuàn) that
appointments or pardons granted while drinking (during banquets)
should not be immediately carried out,
but should be reported back the following day.
In the eighth month, on the first day, Jiăyín,
[the Emperor] visited Shā Lĭng.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngyŏu,
the Eight Tribes of Díliè killed their Xiángwĕn Shāowă,
and all rebelled.
An edict commanded Yēlǜ Wūlàgĕ, Chief Minister of the Southern Administration (Nán Fŭ Zăixiàng), to recruit and pacify them.
On the day Xīnhài,
several individuals of the Díliè were released,
and ordered to persuade their followers.
On the day Rénzĭ,
Yēlǜ Shìliáng sent an envoy to present Díliè captives.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day, Jiăyín,
[the Emperor] visited Zhōngjīng.
On the day Bĭngzĭ,
Tílígū, the Qígŭ Zhuài Là Xiángwĕn, was made Great King of the Six Xī Tribes (Xī Liù Bù Dàwáng).
Thirty-one successful candidates, including the scholar Zhāng Yòngxíng, were granted degrees.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month, on the day Yĭyŏu,
[the Emperor] went to Ruìlù Yuán.
On the day Bĭngxū,
an edict commanded Yēlǜ Shìliáng to launch a second campaign against the Dílièdé.
On the day Wùzĭ,
the Xiángwĕn Bágū was ordered to build a reservoir at Ruìlù Yuán,
in preparation for the spring hunt.
On the day Dīngyŏu,
[the Emperor] hunted at Mălán Diàn.
On the day Rén'yín,
[the Emperor] began the Eastern Campaign.
Shànníng, Resident General of Dōngjīng, and Nièlĭgŭn, Administrator (Píngzhāng), reported
that they had already taken command of the main army and the troops of the various Nǚzhí tribes, and were advancing in separate routes to subdue the enemy.
Thereupon, an envoy was sent bearing a confidential edict to the front lines.
In the second month, on the first day, Rénzĭ,
[the Emperor] went to Sàdī Luò.
The Kingdom of Yútián came to offer tribute.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guĭchŏu,
Jiànfú, the Línyá, was appointed Great King of the Northern Court (Běi Yuàn Dàwáng).
On the day Jiăyín,
Xiāo Díliè and others returned from campaigning against Gāolì.
On the day Bĭngchén,
The Hésūguăn Tribe requested to register the households of the Nǚzhí Wáng Shūzhǐnĭ that were previously undocumented,
and to include their adult males (dīng) in taxation and corvée labor.
This was approved.
Guànníng, Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmìshĭ), reported a great victory over the Eight Tribes of Dílièdé.
An edict commanded Sǎlà, the Palace Attendant (Shìyù), to award and console the troops,
performing the rite of hand-clasping (an expression of high favor) on behalf of the Emperor.
On the day Bĭngyín,
Yēlǜ Shìliáng and others presented the tally of captives and spoils taken from defeating the Zŭbŭ.
On the day Wùchén,
The imperial traveling palace was set up along Yánliŭ Hú.
On the day Jĭsì,
The Nǚzhí sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day Rénshēn,
Yēlǜ Shìliáng campaigned against the Wūgŭ,
and defeated them.
On the day Jiăxū,
an envoy was sent to reward the generals and officers who had rendered meritorious service.
Shìliáng campaigned against the Dílièdé and reached Qīngní Guō.
At this time, the Yújué had already been subdued;
the imperial court debated moving their populace inward.
The Yújué, being attached to their native land and reluctant to move,
consequently rebelled.
Shìliáng, seeking to punish and deter them,
after defeating the Dílièdé,
unilaterally slaughtered their adult males.
He ordered his troops to cross the Hélà Hé (River),
and advanced to attack the remaining faction.
However, the scouts were negligent;
their general Bókuò gathered troops in the dense forest,
and attacked the unprepared Liáo army.
The Liáo army retreated slightly,
forming a battle array at the river bend.
Bókuò launched a night raid.
The following day,
the Liáo rear guard arrived.
Bókuò lured the Yújué populace away, and they all fled.
Shìliáng pursued them,
and the army reached a strategic choke point.
Bókuò was currently resting, blocked by the natural defenses.
The Liáo army scouts found his location,
but Shìliáng did not quickly move to surround him.
Bókuò fled with light cavalry.
[Shìliáng] captured Bókuò's supplies and the Yújué populace he had lured away,
and also moved the people of the Xiámàilĭ Tribe that had been captured by the Dílièdé.
A city was constructed on the Lúqú Hé (River) to settle them.
That month,
Xiāo Yánggē married the Princess of Nánpíng Commandery (Nánpíng Jùnzhŭ).
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Liú Shèng, Chief Minister of the Northern Administration, was appointed Commander-in-Chief (Dūtŏng);
Yēlǜ Shìliáng, Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Deputy Commander;
and Xiāo Qūliè, Grand Inspector of the Palace Guard (Diànqián Dū Diănjiăn), was appointed Director-in-Chief (Dūjiān) to campaign against Gāolì.
Shèng first placed his family in a border commandery,
which delayed the mobilization schedule.
He was recalled.
Shìliáng and Qūliè were therefore put in command of the troops to advance and subdue the enemy.
Yēlǜ Dézhèng was appointed Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Army (Liáoxīng Jūn Jiédùshĭ),
and Xiāo Niángŭliè was appointed Military Commissioner of Tiānchéng Army.
Lĭ Zhòngjŭ died.
An edict provided funds and condolences to his family.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngxū,
The Emperor performed the rite of worshiping the sun according to custom.
Since Mádūgŭ came from a family of hereditary merit,
[the Emperor] presented him with clothing and horses as a sign of favor.
Yēlǜ Bāgē, Resident General of Shàngjīng, was appointed Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Court (Běi Yuàn Shūmì Fùshĭ).
In autumn, the seventh month,
The Emperor again performed the rite of worshiping the sun,
and then visited Qiūshān.
From the eighth month, hunting deer, until the ninth month,
and again from the day Guĭchŏu until the day Xīnyŏu,
[the Emperor] continuously hunted in the mountains of Yŏubăi, Suìshí, Tàibăo, Xiăngyìng, and Sōngshān.
On the day Dīngmăo,
a formal covenant was established with Xiāo Róngníng, the Yílíbì and Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
to strengthen the relationship between sovereign and minister.
On the day Bĭngzĭ,
Tílígū, the Qígŭ Zhuài Là Xiángwĕn, was appointed King of the Six Xī Tribes (Liù Bù Xī Wáng).
In winter, the tenth month,
The imperial traveling palace was set up at Tàlàgē Luò.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngshēn,
an edict ordered the reduction of the number of monks in Dōngjīng,
and commanded that 55,000 elite soldiers be selected from Shàngjīng, Zhōngjīng, and the various palaces to prepare for the Eastern Campaign.
In the twelfth month,
[the Emperor] conducted a southern tour to the coastal regions.
Upon return,
[the Emperor] visited Xiănzhōu.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
[the Emperor] visited the north.
On the day Gēngxū,
Yēlǜ Shìliáng and Xiāo Qūliè fought the Gāolì army west of Guōzhōu,
defeating them,
beheading tens of thousands,
and capturing all their supplies.
On the day Yĭmăo,
the army halted at Nánhăi Jūn,
and Yēlǜ Shìliáng died while on campaign.
On the day Guĭyŏu,
The imperial traveling palace was set up at Xuĕlín.
In the second month, on the day Jĭmăo,
The chieftain of the Zŭbŭ came to court.
On the day Xīnsì,
[the Emperor] went to Sàdī Luò.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yēlǜ Hánliú, formerly Commander of the Dōngjīng Army (Dōngjīng Tŏngjūnshĭ), was appointed Right Yílíbì.
On the day Wùxū,
The Imperial Prince Zōngzhēn was born.
In the third month, on the day Yĭmăo,
Sābǎotè, Sàilà, and other chieftains of the Bígŭdé came to offer tribute.
On the day Xīnyŏu,
the prisons in all circuits were empty.
An edict granted promotion in rank and gifts of goods.
On the day Bĭngyín,
Yēlǜ Jìngwēn, formerly Great King of the Northern Court, was appointed Āzhā Gēzhǐ.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Kĕ, a chief of the Dăngxiàng, surrendered.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yĭhài,
Relief was distributed to the people of Zhāozhōu.
On the day Wùyín,
Xiāo Hézhuó, the Left Yílíbì, was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Court (Běi Yuàn Shūmìshĭ);
Hélŭníng was appointed Deputy Commissioner.
On the day Gēngchén,
[the Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Gūshù Diàn.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiăzĭ,
Xiāo Jīyĭn, Minister (Shàngshū), was punished for being late in returning from his diplomatic mission,
and stripped of his office.
On the day Dīngmăo,
Gĕng Yuánjí was appointed Director of the Board of Revenue (Hùbù Shĭ).
In the sixth month,
Wú Kèchāng, Secretariat Drafter (Zhèngshì Shèrén), was appointed to inspect the judicial cases in Bàzhōu.
On the day Dīngchŏu,
The Uighurs presented peacocks.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
hunting took place at Chìshān.
The eighth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor traveled to Huáizhōu,
and performed rites at the various imperial tombs (*líng*).
On the *wùyín* day,
returned to Shàngjīng.
The ninth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor’s younger brother, Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner) of Nánjīng, Qínjìn Guówáng Lóngqìng, came to court.
The Emperor personally went out to welcome and greet him as far as Shídé Shān,
and subsequently hunted together at Sōngshān.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the imperial procession paused at Xìngguō.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Qínjìn Guówáng Lóngqìng's eldest son, Zhāgē, was enfeoffed as Zhōngshān Jùnwáng,
and his second son, Suìgē, was enfeoffed as Luò'ān Jùnwáng.
The eleventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day (*shuò*),
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Mǎ Bǎozhōng was made Tóngzhī Shūmìyuàn Shì and Jiānxiū Guóshǐ.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Xiāo Wēiwa, the Běimiàn Línyá, was appointed Guójiù Xiángwěn.
The twelfth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Qínjìn Guówáng Lóngqìng returned,
and upon reaching Běi'ān, he died (*hōng*).
When the obituary was heard,
the Emperor grieved deeply,
and suspended court for seven days.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Sòng dispatched Zhāng Xùn and Wáng Chéngdé to offer congratulations for the Qiānlíng Jié.
In this year,
forty-eight men, including *jìnshì* Sūn Jié, were granted the status of passed candidates (*jí dì*).
Sixth year, spring, the first month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
went to Zhuīzǐ Hé.
The second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
because Gōngzhǔ Sàigē killed an innocent maidservant,
and Fùmǎ Xiāo Túyù failed to manage his household,
the Princess was demoted to Xiànzhǔ,
and Túyù was stripped of his title of Tóng Píngzhāngshì.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict commanded Guójiù Zhàng Xiángwěn Xiāo Wěiwā to lead his tribal forces in an eastern campaign against Gāolì (Goryeo).
The affairs of the Guójiù Division were to be administered by a Dūjiān (*ad interim*).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Nèihé, the Nánmiàn Línyá, was appointed Nányuàn Dàwáng.
The third month, on the *yǐsì* day,
went to Xiǎnzhōu,
and buried Qínjìn Guówáng Lóngqìng.
Performed rites at the two imperial tombs, Xiǎn Líng and Qián Líng.
Lóngqìng was posthumously invested as Tàidì (Crown Younger Brother).
Summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Lóngqìng’s youngest son, Xièjiānú, was enfeoffed as Chángshā Jùnwáng.
Shūmìshǐ (Commissioner of Military Affairs), Qīshuǐ Jùnwáng Yēlǜ Zhìxīn, was appointed to provisionally oversee the affairs of the various traveling palaces (Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ Shì).
On the *rénchén* day,
remarriage for noblewomen (*mìngfù*) was prohibited.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
went to Liángxíng.
The fifth month, on the *wùxū* day (*shuò*),
Shūmìshǐ Xiāo Hézhuó was appointed Dūtǒng (Commander-in-Chief),
Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ Wáng Jìzhōng was appointed Deputy Commander,
and Diànqián Dūdiǎnjiǎn Xiāo Qūliè was appointed Dūjiān, to campaign against Gāolì.
The following day,
a sword was bestowed upon Hézhuó,
granting him the authority to execute independently.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
judicial review of prisoners was conducted.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Sǐ Zhàng Dū Xiángwěn (Chief Commandant of the Four Ordos) position was established.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ Xiāo Huì was appointed Yòu Yílíbì.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
sacrifices were made at Mùyè Shān and Huáng Hé.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the imperial procession paused at Jiǔcéng Tái.
The sixth month, on the *wùchén* day (*shuò*),
Défēi Xiāo Shì was granted death,
and buried west of Tù'ér Shān.
A few days later,
a great wind arose over the mound;
day turned dark,
and there was severe thunder and lightning, and the rain did not cease for over a month.
In this month,
Nánjīng and its associated counties suffered from locusts.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
went to Qiūshān.

Lǐbù Shàngshū Liú Jīng, Hànlín Xuéshì Wú Shúdá, Zhīzhìgào Qiú Zhèngjǐ, Qǐjū Shèrén Chéng Zhù, Lìbù Yuánwàiláng Nán Chéngyán, and Lǐbù Yuánwàiláng Wáng Jǐngyùn were dispatched to investigate criminal cases and prisons along separate routes.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
based on the request of the Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎo (Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit),
Níngrén Xiàn was established in Shèngzhōu.
The ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
returned to Shàngjīng.
Due to the birth of the Imperial son Shǔsī,
a general amnesty was granted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,

Fùmǎ Xiāo Lián, Jiédùshǐ Huàgē, Zhīzhìgào Qiú Zhèngjǐ, and Yáng Jí were appointed as envoys and deputies to Sòng to congratulate them on the Emperor's Birthday (*Shēngchén*) and the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Xiāo Hézhuó and others attacked the Xīnghuà Army of Gāolì but failed to conquer it,
and returned the troops.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Nánjīng Circuit suffered famine.
Millet was transported from Yúnzhōu, Yīngzhōu, Shuòzhōu, and Hóngzhōu to relieve them.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
hunting took place at Huázǐ Hé.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the imperial procession paused at Dá lí Shān.
The eleventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Jiànzhōu Jiédùshǐ Shí Kuāngbì died.
The twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to Shàngjīng with a light cavalry escort.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Sòng dispatched Lǐ Xíngjiǎn and Zhāng Xìn to congratulate for the Qiānlíng Jié.
The following day,
Sòng's Féng Yuán and Zhāng Lún came to congratulate for the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*).
Seventh year, spring, the first month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
went to Dá lí Shān.
The second month, on the *yǐchǒu* day (*shuò*),
paid homage to the Sun,
and went to Húnhé.
The third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the five northeastern tribes—Yuèlǐdǔ, Pōuālǐ, Àolǐmǐ, Púnúlǐ, and Tiělí—were commanded to offer an annual tribute of 65,000 sable furs
and 300 horses.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Wūgǔ Bù Jiédùshǐ Xiāo Pǔdá campaigned against the rebellious Mìngdíliè,
and annihilated them.
Summer, the fourth month,
paid homage to the Sun.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
famine relief was provided to Chuānzhōu and Ráozhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
relief was provided to the poor and destitute in Zhōngjīng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
anonymous letters were prohibited.
On the *rénchén* day,
Sānsī Shǐ Lǚ Démào was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
Intercalary month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Xiāo Jìnzhōng was appointed Zhāngwǔ Jūn Jiédùshǐ and concurrently administrator of five prefectures (*wǔzhōu zhìzhì*).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Bìnglǐzūn, the King of Tǔbō (Tibet), submitted a memorial,
requesting that for all tribute missions to court,
permission be granted to pass through Xià Guó (Western Xià).
This was granted.
The fifth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Imperial son Zōngzhēn was enfeoffed as Liángwáng;
Zōngyuán was appointed Yǒngqīng Jūn Jiédùshǐ;
Zōngjiǎn was appointed Yòuwèi Dàjiāngjūn;
Zōngyuàn was appointed Zuǒxiāowèi Dàjiāngjūn;
Zōngwěi was appointed Yòuwèi Dàjiāngjūn;
Imperial nephew Zōngfàn was appointed Zhāoyì Jūn Jiédùshǐ;
Zōngxī was appointed Zhènguó Jūn Jiédùshǐ;
Zōngliàng was appointed Jiàngzhōu Jiédùshǐ;
Zōngbì was appointed Púzhōu Guāncháshǐ;
Zōngyì was appointed Cáozhōu Fángyùshǐ;
Zōngxiǎn and Zōngsù were both appointed Fángyùshǐ.
Zhāng Jiǎn was appointed Shǒu Sītú and concurrently Zhèngshì Lìng.
The sixth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Pǐndǎlǔguī Bù Jiédùshǐ Bólǔlǐ arrived at Bísǎ Hé.
He encountered a light rain,
when suddenly heaven and earth grew dark,
and a great wind swept up forty-three men, spiraling them into the air.
After a long time, they fell several *lǐ* away.
Bólǔlǐ fortunately escaped harm.
A single wine pot on the ground remained unmoved.
The eighth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the ritual of the Great Willow Shoot (*Dà Shèliǔ zhī Lǐ*) was performed.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Yēlǜ Liúníng and Wú Shǒudá were dispatched as envoys to Sòng to congratulate them on the Emperor's Birthday;
Xiāo Gāojiǔ and Mǎ Yímóu were dispatched as envoys to Sòng to congratulate them on the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*).
Píngzhāng Xiāo Hóngyì was promoted to Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Shàngfù, and concurrently Zhèngshì Lìng.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict commanded Hànlín Dàizhào Chén Shēng to paint the Triumphant Southern Campaign map in the Wǔluán Diàn hall in Shàngjīng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Púnúlǐ tribe came to offer tribute.
The ninth month, on the *gēngshēn* day (*shuò*),
an envoy from Púní Guó reported that their country and Wūlǐ Guó shared borders,
and frequent incursions and raids caused unrest.
An imperial edict was issued to admonish (Wūlǐ Guó).
On the *wùchén* day,
an edict instructed officials, both internal and external,
that receiving bribes in relation to their duties,
and claiming upon discovery that the gifts were received by sons, grandsons, servants, or followers,
was strictly prohibited.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
judicial review of prisoners was conducted.
Horses were requisitioned and supplied to the Eastern Expeditionary Army.
In this month,
the imperial procession paused at Tǔhé Chuān.
Winter, the tenth month,
the two newly constructed halls in Zhōngjīng were named Yánqìng
and Yǒng'ān.
On the *rényín* day,
Shí Yòngzhōng, the Shùnyì Jūn Jiédùshǐ, was appointed Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict appointed Dōngpíng Jùnwáng Xiāo Páiyā as Dūtǒng (Commander-in-Chief),
Diànqián Dūdiǎnjiǎn Xiāo Xūliè as Fùtǒng (Deputy Commander),
and Dōngjīng Liúshǒu Yēlǜ Bāgē as Dūjiān, to campaign against Gāolì.
Furthermore, Gāolì officials guarding the cities were instructed:
those who could lead their people to surrender voluntarily
would be heavily rewarded;
those who strongly fortified and resisted
would regret it when it was too late.
On the Rénxū day of the eleventh month,
Lǚ Démào was appointed acting Shàngshū of the Lìbù,
Yáng Yòuxuán was appointed acting Director of the Xiángfùyuàn,
Liú Shèng was made Jiédùshǐ of Bàzhōu,
and the Běifǔ Zǎixiàng, Liú Shènxíng, was made Jiédùshǐ of Zhāngwǔjūn.
On the day Gēngchén,
the wearing of míngjīn (polished gold), lǚjīn (filigree gold), and tiējīn (gold leaf) was prohibited.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor proceeded to Zhōngjīng.
On the Dīngyǒu day of the twelfth month,
Sòng sent Lǚ Yíjiǎn and Cáo Zhāng to offer congratulations on the Qiānlíng Festival.
This month,
Xiāo Páiyā and others fought Gāolì at the Chá and Tuó rivers,
and the Liáo army suffered a setback.
Many soldiers from the Tiānyún and Yòu Píshì armies drowned,
and the Yáoliǎn Zhàng Xiángwěn Āguǒdá, the Kèsěngshǐ Zhuó Gǔ, the Bóhǎi Xiángwěn Gāo Qīngmíng, and the Tiānyún Jūn Xiángwěn Hǎilǐ all died.
Thirty-seven scholars, including Zhāng Kègōng, were passed in the imperial examination (Jí Dì).
In the spring, first month of the eighth year,
Sòng sent Chén Yáozuǒ and Zhāng Qún to offer congratulations.
On the day Rénxū,
the Tiělí came to offer tribute.
The ancestral temple for Jǐngzōng was constructed in Zhōngjīng.
Cáo Shùn, Jiédùshǐ of Shāzhōu, was enfeoffed as the Jùnwáng of Dùnhuáng.
On the Dīngwèi day of the second month,
the former Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ Hán Zhìxīn was made Liúshǒu of Zhōngjīng,
and Wáng Jìzhōng, the Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ, was made Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ.
On the day Bǐngchén,
sacrifices were offered to Fēngbó.
On the Jǐwèi day of the third month,
Hè Shí, the Qìdān Hóngyì Gōngshǐ, was made Dūbùshǔ of Xīngshèng Palace,
Kònggǔlǐ, the former Yáo'ēn Niānbù Jiédùshǐ, was made Dūbùshǔ of Jìqìng Palace,
and the Zuǒ Zhīhòu Lángjūn Yēlǜ Hǎn was made Dūjiān of the Sìjié Army.
On the day Yǐhài,
Dōngpíng Wáng Xiāo Hánníng, Dōngjīng Liúshǒu Yēlǜ Bāgē, Guójìu Píngzhāngshì Xiāo Páiyā, Línyá Yàozhī, and others returned from campaigning against Gāolì.
They were held responsible for operational failure,
had their crimes enumerated, but were then released.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial decree promoted the Bóhǎi generals and officers who had achieved merit in the campaign against Gāolì.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the horses of the Fēilóngyuàn were reviewed.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Tàishī Tàlágě of the Huíbá Tribe came to offer tribute.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the post of Dōngjīng Bóhǎi Chéngfèngguān Dūzhī Yābān was established.
Summer, fourth month, the Wùzǐ day (the first day of the month),
the Emperor proceeded to Miǎn Shān.
On the Rénshēn day of the fifth month,
the Fùmǎ Xiāo Kèzhōng was made Jiédùshǐ of Chángníngjūn.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Bóhǎi households from Níngzhōu were relocated to the area between the Liáo and Tǔ rivers.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Hésūguǎn Tìyǐn Ābùgě and the Zǎixiàng Sàilà came to offer tribute.
On the Wùzǐ day of the sixth month,
the sons and younger brothers of the generals and officers who died in battle during the campaign against Gāolì were registered for preferential treatment.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Zuǒ Yílíbì Xiāo Jiělǐ was made Xīnán Miàn Zhāotǎoshǐ,
and the Yùshǐ Dàfū Xiāo Yàozhī was made Yílíbì.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Tìyǐn Yēlǜ Hégě was made Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng,
and the Nánmiàn Línyá Yēlǜ Hánliú was made Tìyǐn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the prohibition on logging in the Yuán Lǐng of Dàbǎi Shān was relaxed.
On the day Yǐsì,
the officers of the Nán Píshì Army and others who achieved merit in campaigning against Gāolì
were granted gold and silk according to their rank.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
regarding the various generals who died in the Gāolì campaign,
an imperial decree granted additional enfeoffments to their wives.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Dōngběilù Xiángwěn Yēlǜ Dúdié was made Běiyuàn Dàwáng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Yáolǐ and Niègē Xī armies achieved merit in the Gāolì campaign,
and were all granted gold and silk.
On the day Guǐhài,
it was decreed that the Zǔbǔ should continue their annual tribute: 1,700 horses,
440 camels,
10,000 sable skins,
and 25,000 blue squirrel skins.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor inspected the crops.
On the day Jǐsì,
Tàibǎo Má Mén of the Huíbá Tribe came to offer tribute.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor inspected the market,
and granted a partial pardon to the prisoners detained there.
Xiè Níng and Mǎ Yì were ordered to serve as the Envoy and Deputy Envoy to Sòng to congratulate them on the Emperor's birthday.
Eighth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Lángjūn Hébùlǚ and others were sent leading troops from various tribes to join the main army campaigning against Gāolì.
Ninth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Shí Yòngzhōng was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
Sòng sent Cuī Zūndù and Wáng Yìngchāng to offer congratulations on the Qiānlíng Festival.
On the day Rénshēn,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Jiǎxū,
prisoners were reviewed again.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Hésūguǎn Tìyǐn Ābùgē came to offer tribute.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor made a temporary stop at Tǔ Hé Chuān.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
it was decreed to all circuits
that all matters, regardless of their significance,
which have been judged,
must be summarized and reported once every three months.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Yēlǜ Jìchóng and Zhèng Xuánxiá were sent to congratulate Sòng on Zhèngdàn.
On the day Guǐsì,
it was decreed that the Three Branches of the Héngzhàng must not intermarry with clans of lower status;
for any marriage,
they must report it to the throne before proceeding.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the former Běiyuàn Dàwáng Jiànfú was made Āzhāgēzhǐ.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Hàolǐ Tàibǎo City on the Eastern Route was renamed Xiánzhōu,
and a garrison command was established to govern it.
Eleventh month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Xuāndé County was established in Yúnzhōu.
Twelfth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor stayed at Zhōngjīng.
On the day Yǐsì,
Guǎngpíng Jùnwáng Zōngyè was made Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu and Dàdìng Yǐn,
and Hán Zhìxīn was made Tìyǐn.
On the day Xīnhài,
King Xún of Gāolì sent an envoy requesting to offer local tribute,
and an imperial decree accepted it.
In the spring, first month of the ninth year,
Sòng sent Liú Píng and Zhāng Yuánpǔ to offer congratulations.
Second month,
the Emperor proceeded to Yuānyang Luò.
On the Gēngwǔ day of the fifth month,
Yēlǜ Zīzhōng returned from his mission to Gāolì.
King Xún petitioned requesting to acknowledge vassalage and offer tribute,
and returned the captured royal official Zhǐlálǐ.
Zhǐlálǐ had been in Gāolì for six years,
and his loyalty and integrity remained unyielding;
he was appointed Línyá.
On the day Xīnwèi,
an envoy was sent to pardon King Xún's offenses,
and to grant his request.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Yēlǜ Zōngjiào was made Jiǎnxiào Tàifù,
Zōnghuì was made Qǐshèngjūn Jiédùshǐ,
and Liú Shèng was made Tàizǐ Tàifù.
They were also granted the title Bǎojié Gōngchén.
Autumn, seventh month, the Gēngxū day (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial decree ordered close officials to perform the ritual prostrations for "saving the sun" on the Emperor's behalf.
On the day Jiǎyín,
an envoy was sent to bestow clothing and goods upon Cáo Shùn, the Shāzhōu Huíhú Dùnhuáng Jùnwáng.
Chálà, Gěng Yuánjí, Hán Jiǔ, and Sòng Zhāng were appointed as Envoy and Deputy Envoy for the upcoming year's congratulations to Sòng on the Emperor's Birthday and Zhèngdàn.
Ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Fùmǎ Xiāo Shàozōng was appointed Píngzhāngshì.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
all civil and military officials presented a memorial requesting the conferral of an honorific title,
which was refused;
when the memorial was presented a third time,
it was accepted.
On the day Yǐhài,
Cáo Shùn, the Shāzhōu Huíhú Dùnhuáng Jùnwáng, sent an envoy to offer tribute.
The horses owned by Han residents across the circuits were collected and granted to the Dōngzhēng Jūn.
Yílíbì Yánníng was made Bīngmǎ Fù Dūbùshǔ,
to command the entire army in the Eastern Campaign.
This month,
the Emperor stayed at Jīnpíng Luò.
Sòng sent Sòng Shòu and Luò Jìlún to offer congratulations on the Qiānlíng Festival.
Winter, tenth month, the Wùyín day (the first day of the month),
Nièlǐ was made Xī Wáng Dūjiān,
and Tūdiélǐ was made Xiángwěn of the Shèlì Army of the Běi Wángfǔ.
Lángjūn Lǎo returned from his mission to Shāzhōu,
and an imperial decree pardoned his past offenses.
It was the custom of the state that when missions were sent to distant lands,
they often employed those who were condemned to penal servitude but possessed talent and strategy;
upon their return from the mission,
their crimes were immediately remitted.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Xīnán Zhāotǎo memorialized that among the Dǎngxiàng tribes, the Sòngxī Clan failed to deliver tribute punctually
and often harbored ulterior motives,
and that it was advisable to periodically send envoys to supervise them.
The imperial decree stated:
"These small tribes on the frontier
have a fixed annual tribute.
The frontier officials are arrogant and unrestrained,
and their demands and levies are excessive,
causing the tribes to harbor fear and be unable to present themselves.
Only send clean and cautious officials and generals,
show them kindness and sincerity,
and do not permit them to exploit the tribes.
They will naturally comply and submit."
It was further memorialized by the Dìjū and Diélièdé tribes stating that the Jiédùshǐ Hánliú had implemented benevolent governance,
but was now due for replacement,
and they requested that he be retained.
The Emperor ordered the presentation of a report on his administration.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor proceeded to Zhōngjīng.
On the day Rényín,
the Dàshí Guó sent an envoy to present an elephant and local products,
and requested a marriage alliance for his son Cègē.
In the 11th month, on the *dìngsì* day,
Hán Zhìxīn (Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery) was appointed as the Resident Administrator of Nánjīng, Prefect of Xījīn, and Grand Commander of Horse and Foot Armies.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Xiāo Xiàoshùn (the *Yílíbì*) was appointed as the Commissioner of all Southern Traveling Palaces,
and was given the added title of Left Assistant Director (Zuǒ Púyè).
In the 12th month, on the *dīnghài* day,
monks were forbidden from burning their bodies or refining their fingers (self-immolation rituals).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an imperial decree ordered the construction of a Grand Ancestor Temple (Tàizǔ Miào) in Zhōngjīng;
its regulations and sacrificial vessels were all to follow ancient customs.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial decree mandated that the Grand Investiture Ceremony (*Dàcèlǐ*) be held in the winter of the coming year.
Forty-five *jìnshì*, including Zhāng Zhòngjǔ, were released (from examination/service).
Tàipíng 1st Year (1021), Spring, 1st month, on the *dīngchǒu* day (*shòu*),
Sòng envoys Lǔ Zōngdào and Chéng Jí came to offer congratulations.
Went to the Húnhé River.
2nd month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited Bóhé River.
On the *rénxū* day,
hunted in Gāoliǔlín Forest.
3rd month, on the *wùxū* day,
the Imperial Prince Bóyǐzhī was born.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Xiāo Shàoyè, the Commandant-Escort (*Fùmǎ Dūwèi*), established a private city,
which was granted the name Mùzhōu,
and the army stationed there was named Chángqìng.
In this month,
the King of Dàshí again sent an envoy to request a marriage alliance.
The Prince's (Wángzǐ Bān Lángjūn) daughter Kělǎo Húsīlǐ was enfeoffed as a Princess (*Gōngzhǔ*)
and married off (to the Dàshí King).
Summer, 4th month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Resident Administrator of Dōngjīng reported
that the chieftains of thirty Nǚzhí tribes requested that each send their son to the imperial court to serve.
An imperial decree ordered that they all come, along with their fathers, to receive the covenant.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Láizhōu was established.
In this month,
sought relief from the summer heat at Miǎnshān Mountain.
Autumn, 7th month, on the *jiǎxū* day (*shòu*),
autumn clothing was bestowed upon the Nǚzhí people who participated in the hunt.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Gǔlǐ was dispatched to Zhōngjīng to retrieve the Imperial Jade Seal (*Yùxǐ*) that the Shí Jìn had presented (to the Khitan).
The Zǔbǔ came to offer tribute.
On the *xīnsì* day,
went to Shālíng Ridge.
In this month,
hunted along the Huánghé River.
9th month,
the Emperor visited Zhōngjīng.
Winter, 10th month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Pǒbái, the chieftain of the Díliè, came to offer horses and camels as tribute.
On the *wùshēn* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Sòng envoys Lǐ Yì and Wáng Zhòngbīn came to congratulate (the Emperor) on the Thousand-Years Festival (*Qiānlíng Jié*),
and Sū Wéifǔ and Zhōu Dǐng came to congratulate (the Emperor) on the New Year (*Yuánzhēng*) of the coming year.
Xiāo Shàn and Chéng Zhù were immediately dispatched in return to establish diplomatic relations.
Hélǔ, the chief of the Dǎngxiàng, came to offer tribute.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Sàmǐn Jiělǐ was appointed as the Grand Commissioner (*Dū Diǎnjiǎn*),
Gāo Liù as the Deputy Commissioner (*Fù Diǎnjiǎn*),
Yēlǜ Luóhànnú as the Administrator-in-Chief of the Left Guard (*Zuǒ Píshì Xiángwěn*),
Sǎnggū as the Administrator-in-Chief of the Right Guard (*Yòu Píshì Xiángwěn*),
Liáoliǎo as the Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Circuit (*Xīběilù Jīnwú*),
Yēlǜ Sēngyǐn as the Grand Censor (*Yùshǐ Dàfū*),
Qiúgē as Commandant-Escort (*Fùmǎ Dūwèi*),
Xiāo Chōng and Gǔlǐ were both appointed as Grand Generals (*Dà Jiāngjūn*).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor visited the Tōngtiān Temple
to watch the *yúlóng mányǎn* performance (a kind of pageant).
The following day,
the Emperor visited again.
Upon return,
mounted the Imperial Jade Chariot (*Yùlù*),
entered the Wànshòu Hall through the Inner Three Gates (*Nèisānmén*),
performed a libation ceremony for the imperial portraits in the Seven Ancestral Temples (*Qīmiào Yùróng*),
and subsequently held a banquet for the imperial clan members (*zōngshì*).
11th month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
His Majesty resided in Zhāoqìng Hall.

All civil and military officials respectfully presented the imperial scroll, conferring the exalted title *Ruìwén Yīngwǔ Zūndào Zhìdé Chóngrén Guǎngxiào Gōngchéng Zhìdìng Zhāoshèng Shénzàn Tiānfǔ Huángdì* (The Wise, Cultured, Heroic, and Martial Emperor, Who Honors the Way, Achieves Supreme Virtue, Esteems Benevolence, Extends Filial Piety, Perfects Accomplishments, Establishes Order, Manifests Sageliness, Is Divinely Assisted, and Supported by Heaven).
A general amnesty was declared,
the era name was changed to Tàipíng,
and officials inside and outside the capital were promoted according to their rank.
Sòng dispatched envoys to establish diplomatic relations,
and Xià and Gāolì dispatched envoys to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Imperial Prince Zōngzhēn, Prince of Liáng, was invested as the Crown Prince (*Huáng Tàizǐ*).
2nd Year (1022), Spring, 1st month,
went to Nàshuǐ to fish with hooks.
2nd month, on the *xīnchǒu* day (*shòu*),
the Emperor resided at Yúérluò.
3rd month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
went to Chángchūnzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Sòng envoy Xuē Yíkuò arrived to announce the death of the Sòng ruler,
and that his son Zhēn had succeeded to the throne.
Grand Commissioner Yēlǜ Sēngyǐn and others were dispatched as chief and deputy envoys for the Sòng sacrificial rites,
while the *Línyá* Xiāo Rìxīn and the Surveillance Commissioner Fèng Yánxiū were dispatched as chief and deputy envoys to convey condolences to the Sòng Empress Dowager.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Commander-in-Chief Yēlǜ Xiélǐng and the Usher Yáo Jūxìn were dispatched as chief and deputy envoys to convey condolences to the Sòng ruler.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
meals were provided for the monks of the Three Capitals on behalf of the Sòng ruler.
In this month,
there was an earthquake.
In Yúnzhōu and Yìngzhōu, houses were destroyed and the ground collapsed,
Wéibáishān Mountain cracked for several hundred paces,
and springs erupted to form a stream.
Summer, 4th month,
went to Miǎnshān Mountain to seek relief from the summer heat.
5th month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Shí Yòngzhōng, the Auxiliary Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Cānzhī Zhèngshì*), passed away.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Tiělí dispatched envoys to present sixteen households of the Wùrě.
6th month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Sòng dispatched envoys Xuē Yóu and others to present relics of their late Emperor.
Autumn, 7th month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yēlǜ Xìnníng was appointed Military Governor of Fènglín Army (*Fènglín Jūn Jiédùshǐ*),
Wáng Tóngxiǎn, Auxiliary Administrator of Governmental Affairs of Gāolì Kingdom, was appointed Military Governor of Jìnghǎi Army (*Jìnghǎi Jūn Jiédùshǐ*),
Yēlǜ Suìzhōng was appointed Military Governor of Chángníng Army,
Gěng Yányì was appointed Military Governor of Zhāodé Army,
and Gāo Shǒuzhēn was appointed Military Governor of Héxī Army.
9th month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Minister Sēngyǐn and Hán Gé were dispatched to congratulate the Sòng ruler on his ascension.
Winter, 10th month, on the *rényín* day,
Official Zhāng Kègōng of the Inner Department was dispatched as the envoy to congratulate Lǐ Dézhāo, King of the Xià State, on his birthday,
Yēlǜ Sǎogǔ and Hán Wáng were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate the Sòng Empress Dowager on her birthday,
and Yēlǜ Xiānníng and Shǐ Kèzhōng were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*).
In this month,
the Emperor resided at Húlǔgǔsī Diàn (Lake).
On the *guǐmǎo* day,

money and goods, varying according to rank, were bestowed upon Chancellor Lǚ Démào, Auxiliary Administrator Wú Shúdá, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Yáng Yòuxuán, and Right Chancellor Mǎ Bǎozhōng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
arrived at Shàngjīng,
and partially pardoned the prisoners within the capital region (*jīnèi*).
11th month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Sòng dispatched envoys to offer thanks.
12th month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wáng Xún, the King of Gāolì, passed away.
His son Qīn sent an envoy to report the news.
Immediately ordered an envoy to invest Qīn as the King of Gāolì.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Sòng dispatched Liú Yè and Guō Zhìyán to congratulate (the Emperor) on the Thousand-Years Festival (*Qiānlíng Jié*).
In this year,
forty-seven *jìnshì*, including Zhāng Jiàn, were released (from examination/service).
3rd Year (1023), Spring, 1st month, on the *bǐngyín* day (*shòu*),
went to Nàshuǐ to fish with hooks.
Sēngyǐn was appointed Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Píngzhāng Shì*).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Xiāo Táidé was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Prince's Residence (*Nán Wáng Fǔ Dūjiān*),
and the *Línyá* Yēlǜ Xìnníng was appointed Commissioner-General of the Northwest Circuit Pacification Command (*Xīběilù Zhāotǎo Dūjiān*).
On the *xīnsì* day,
the private city of the Princess of Yuè State (*Yuègúo Gōngzhǔ*) was granted the name Yìzhōu,
and the army stationed there was named Qìngyì.
2nd month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Dīng Zhèn was appointed Military Governor of Wǔxìn Army,
and his title was changed to Prince of Lánlíng Commandery (*Lánlíng Jùnwáng*).
On the *wùshēn* day,
Xiāo Páiyā, Prince of Dōngpíng Commandery, was appointed Grand Pacification Commissioner of the Southwestern Front,
and was promoted to be Prince of Bīn (*Bīnwáng*).
Summer, 4th month,
Yēlǜ Shǒuníng was appointed Grand Commissioner (*Dū Diǎnjiǎn*).
5th month,
sought relief from the summer heat at Miǎnshān Mountain.
6th month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Liú Jīng, Commissioner of the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Xuānhuīshǐ*), was appointed Auxiliary Administrator of Governmental Affairs,
Xiāo Xiàohuì was appointed Deputy Commissioner (*Fù Diǎnjiǎn*),
and Xiāo Xiàogōng was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Dōngjīng and concurrently Border Inspector (*Yánbiān Xúnjiǎnshǐ*).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Xiāo Lián was appointed Left *Yílíbì*,
and Xiāo Lín was appointed Administrator-in-Chief (*Xiángwěn*).
Autumn, 7th month, on the *wùyín* day,
Yēlǜ Hégě, Chancellor of the Southern Administration (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*), was appointed Resident Administrator of Shàngjīng,
and enfeoffed as Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Empress's birthday was designated as the Shùntiān Festival.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Miǎnshān Mountain was granted the name Yǒng’ān.
In this month,
hunted at Chìshān Mountain.
Intercalary 9th month, on the *rénchén* day (*shòu*),
Xiāo Bódá and Hán Shàoyōng were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*),
and Táng Gǔdé and Chéng Zhāowén were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday (*Shēngchén*).
Winter, 10th month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Sòng dispatched Xuē Kuí and Guō Shèng to congratulate (the Empress) on the Shùntiān Festival,
and Wáng Zhēn and Mùróng Wéisù to congratulate (the Emperor) on the Thousand-Years Festival (*Qiānlíng Jié*).
The Eastern Expeditionary Army reported:
"The Commanders Xiélǐng and Chánggǔn Kènú led their troops entering from Máomǔguólǐng Ridge,
while *Línyá* Gāo Jiǔ and Deputy General Dàkuāng Yì and others led their troops entering from Gǔshānlǐng Ridge.
Before reaching Tàlíhé River in the intercalary month,
they returned without encountering the enemy.
In this month, they rendezvoused at Hóngpàzhǐlǐng Ridge,
where a great number of camels and horses died."
The Emperor resided by the Liáohé River.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the Imperial Nephew Zōngfàn was made Military Commissioner (*Jiédùshǐ*) of Guīdé Command;
the Chancellor of the Northern Administration (*Běi Fǔ Zǎixiàng*), Xiāo Xiàomù, was made Grand Defender (*Liúshǒu*) of the Southern Capital (*Nánjīng*);
and he was enfeoffed as the Prince (*Wáng*) of Yān.

Hán Zhìxīn, the Grand Defender of the Southern Capital, was made the Great King (*Dà Wáng*) of the Southern Division (*Nán Yuàn*) and Grand Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs (*Bīngmǎ Dū Zǒngguǎn*).
Qiú Zhèng was made Commissioner of Transportation (*Zhuǎnyùnshǐ*) for Yānjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Zōngfàn was made Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Píngzhāng Shì*),
and enfeoffed as the Commandery Prince (*Jùn Wáng*) of Sānhán.
Qiú Dàohéng was made Deputy Grand Defender (*Fù Liúshǒu*) of the Central Capital (*Zhōngjīng*).
Féng Yánxiū was made Prefect (*Cìshǐ*) of Shùn Zhōu.
Láng Xuánhuà was made Commissioner of Transportation for Xī Shān.
Zhào Qí was made Academician Director (*Zhí Xuéshì*) of the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Shūmì*).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Xiāo Yǒng was made Grand Preceptor (*Tàishī*) to the Crown Prince.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Imperial Son Chóngyuán was enfeoffed as the King of Qín State (*Qín Guó Wáng*).
In the fourth year [1015 CE], spring, the first month, on the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng dispatched Zhāng Chuán, Zhāng Shìyǔ, Chéng Lín, and Dīng Bǎohéng to come and offer congratulations.
[The Emperor] went to the Yāzǐ River.
In the second month, on the *jǐwèi* day, the first day of the lunar month,
[The Emperor] hunted at the Tàlǔ River.
An imperial edict commanded that the Yāzǐ River be renamed the Hùntóng River (*Hùntóng Jiāng*),
and the Tàlǔ River be renamed the Chángchūn River (*Chángchūn Hé*).
The third month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the lunar month,
it was the Qiānlíng Festival.
An edict granted food to the elderly in all palace divisions.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Shìhóng, the son of the Right Chancellor (*Yòu Chéngxiàng*) Mǎ Bǎozhōng, was dispatched as envoy to Lǐngbiǎo;
upon reaching Píngdì Sōnglín, he was killed by bandits.
He was posthumously granted the title of Military Commissioner of Zhāoxìn Command.
In the fifth month,
[The Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Yǒng'ān Mountain.
The sixth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Great King of the Southern Division, Hán Zhìxīn, passed away.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhèng Hóngjié was made Bureau Director (*Lángzhōng*) of the Ministry of War (*Bīngbù*).
Liú Shènxíng was made Military Commissioner of Shùnyì Command.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Shùn, the son of the Prince of Yān, Xiāo Xiàomù, was made General (*Jiāngjūn*) of the Qiānniú Guard.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Chágē, the Commandery Prince of Zhōngshān, was made Military Commissioner of Bǎojìng Command.
Suìgē, the Commandery Prince of Luò'ān, was made Military Commissioner of Guǎngdé Command.
Xiāo Jiělǐ was made Military Commissioner of Zhāngdé Command.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Húdūgǔ, the Prince of Zhōu and Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Command, was made Military Commissioner of Línhǎi Command.
Díliè, the Commandery Prince of Qīshuǐ, was made Great King of the Southern Division.
Autumn, the seventh month,
[The Emperor] went to Qiū Mountain.
The eighth month, on the *bǐngchén* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Hán Shàofāng was made Academician Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The Imperial Son-in-Law (*Fùmǎ*) Xiāo Pǐdí was made Grand Inspector (*Dū Diǎnjiǎn*).
In the ninth month,
the Imperial Son-in-Law Xiāo Shàozōng was made Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Command.
Yēlǜ Zōngfú was made Military Commissioner of Ānguó Command.
Winter, the tenth month,
The imperial cortege halted at the Liáo River.
Sòng dispatched Cài Qí and Lǐ Yònghé to come and congratulate on the Qiānlíng Festival.
In the eleventh month,
the Great King of the Southern Division, Hán Zhìxīn, was posthumously enfeoffed as the Prince of Chén (*Chén Wáng*).
In the twelfth month,
Xiāo Cóngzhèng was made Military Commissioner of Guīyì Command.
Kāng Yún was made Guard of the Palace Gates (*Jiānmén Wèi*).
[They were] appointed Envoy and Deputy Envoy to Sòng to celebrate the New Year (*Zhèngdàn*).
In this year,
forty-seven successful candidates, including the presented scholar (*jìnshì*) Lǐ Jiǒng, were released [into official service].
Basic Annals 17: Shèngzōng 8
The fifth year [1016 CE], spring, the first month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
[The Emperor] went to the Hùntóng River.
In the second month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
it was forbidden throughout the realm to wear bright gold or brocades woven with gold thread;
those who were imperial relatives and required to wear them
must petition first before using them.
In this month,
[The Emperor] went to Yú'ér Marsh.
The third month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Left Chancellor (*Zuǒ Chéngxiàng*), Zhāng Jiǎn, was made Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Command and Concurrent Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Tóng Zhèngshì Ménxià Píngzhāng Shì*).
Zhèng Hóngjié was made Vice Prefect (*Shǎoyǐn*) of Línhuáng.
Liú Shènxíng was made Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Command.
Xiāo Pǐdí, Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Command, was made Grand Commissioner of the Qìdān Travelling Palace (*Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ*).

Yáng Yòuxuán, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (*Shūmì Fùshǐ*), was made Minister (*Shàngshū*) of the Ministry of Personnel (*Lìbù*), Concurrent Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Cānzhī Zhèngshì*), and Commissioner of Military Affairs (*Shūmìshǐ*).
In this month,
[The Emperor] went to the Chángchūn River and Yú'ér Marsh.
That night, the water sounded like thunder;
it surged over a forty-mile stretch of sand dunes,
forming a new pond.
Summer, the fifth month,
[The Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Yǒng'ān Mountain.
Xiāo Cóngshùn was made Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
Wú Shūdá was made Academician of the Hànlín Academy.
The Daoist priest Féng Ruògǔ was additionally appointed Internal Adviser (*Zhōngyǔn*) to the Crown Prince.
Yēlǜ Chén was made Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Command.
Zhāng Jiǎn was made Military Commissioner of Zhāngxìn Command.
Lǚ Shìzōng was made Supernumerary Director (*Yuánwàiláng*) of the Ministry of Rites (*Lǐbù*).
Lǐ Kějǔ was made Military Commissioner of Shùnyì Command.
Autumn, the seventh month,
[The Emperor] hunted at Píngdì Sōnglín.
In the ninth month,
The imperial cortege halted at the Southern Capital (*Nánjīng*).
On the *jǐhài* day,
Xiāo Díliè and Lǐ Shàoqí were appointed Envoy and Deputy Envoy to Sòng to celebrate the birthday of the Empress Dowager (*Tàihòu*).
Yēlǜ Shǒuníng and Liú Sìduān were appointed Envoy and Deputy Envoy to Sòng to celebrate the birthday of the Sòng ruler.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the Sòng Empress Dowager dispatched Féng Yuánzōng and Shǐ Fāng to come and congratulate on the Shùntiān Festival.
The eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
[The Emperor] visited the Inner Orchard for a banquet.
The capital residents gathered to watch.
Seventy-two successful presented scholars (*jìnshì*) were found [through examination].
They were ordered to compose poetry;
ranking their skill,
fourteen men, including Zhāng Yù, were made Collators (*Jiàoshūláng*) for the Crown Prince.
Fifty-eight men, including Hán Luán, were made Collators of the Academy for the Veneration of Literature (*Chóngwén Guǎn*).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Xiāo Luóluó, Administrator of the Left Attending Cadets (*Zuǒ Zhīhòu Lángjūn Xiángwěn*), was made Right Grand Minister of Administration (*Yòu Yílíbì*).
The twelfth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Xiāo Xiàoxiān, Grand Commissioner of the Han People’s Travelling Palace, was made Grand Defender of the Supreme Capital (*Shàngjīng Liúshǒu*).
The Imperial Nephew Xièjiānú, Commandery Prince of Chángshā, was made Military Commissioner of Kuāngyì Command.
Yēlǜ Rénjǔ was made Military Commissioner of Xīngguó Command.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Xiāo Shǒuníng was made Inspector (*Diǎnjiǎn*) of the Imperial Bodyguard Cavalry and Infantry.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Northern Division (*Běi Yuàn Shūmìshǐ*), Xiāo Hézhuó, passed away.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Chancellor of the Northern Administration, Xiāo Pǔgǔ, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Northern Division.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Xiāo Xié and Lǐ Qí were dispatched as Envoy and Deputy Envoy to Sòng to celebrate the New Year.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Liú Jīng, Concurrent Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was made Military Commissioner of Shùnyì Command.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sòng envoys Lǐ Wéi and Zhāng Lún came to congratulate on the Qiānlíng Festival.
In this year,
the people of Yān, due to the abundant harvest,
and the presence of the imperial carriage,
vied with each other to present local products.
The Emperor paid respect to the elders,
showed favor to the widowed,
and granted a general feast with drink.
By nightfall,
the lights in the six streets were as bright as day;
officials and commoners celebrated and roamed freely.
The Emperor also secretly toured to observe them.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
artisans were forbidden from melting down gold and silver vessels.
The sixth year [1017 CE], spring, the first month, on the *jǐmǎo* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng dispatched Xú Shì, Péi Jìqǐ, Zhāng Ruògǔ, and Cuī Zhǔn to come and offer congratulations.
On the *gēngchén* day,
[The Emperor] went to Yuānyāng Marsh.
The second month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Mílíjǐ was made Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Tóngzhī Shūmì Yuàn*).
Huáng Piān was made Grand Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Dá Gǔzhǐ was made his Deputy.
Hè Shí was made Grand Inspector (*Dū Jiān*).
They led troops to build a walled city between the Hùntóng River and the Shūmù River.
Huánglóng Prefecture requested the construction of three fortifications and ten beacon towers.
An edict commanded that they be constructed during the farming off-season.
The Grand Defender of the Eastern Capital (*Dōngjīng Liúshǒu*), Bāgē, memorialized that Huáng Piān had led troops into Nǚzhí territory to seize land.
The captured people, horses, cattle, and swine
were countless;
two hundred and seventy households submitted.
An edict commended and encouraged him.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Yēlǜ Yě was made Deputy Inspector (*Fù Diǎnjiǎn*).

Xiāo Liǔshì of the Imperial Maternal Uncle's Division (*Guójiù Zhàng*) and Tú Lǔgǔ were appointed to lead the Twelve-Division Army of the Northwest Circuit and the Shělì Army of the Xī King's Residence.
On the *jǐsì* day,
The Southern Capital was flooded.
An envoy was dispatched to provide relief.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
An edict commanded that the separate Dǎngxiàng tribe of Tāxī be governed by a Qìdān Military Commissioner.
The third month, on the *wùyín* day, the first day of the lunar month,

Zhāng Jiǎn, Military Commissioner of Dàtóng Command, entered the court to become Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Division, Left Chancellor, and concurrently Director of Political Affairs (*Zhèngshì Lìng*).
Wú Shūdá, Concurrent Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was demoted and appointed Vice Supervisor of Palace Buildings (*Jiàngzuò Shàojiān*),
and sent out to serve as Prefect of Dōng Zhōu.
In this month,
the Zǔbǔ came to invade.
The Northwest Circuit Commissioner of Pacification and Punishment (*Zhāotǎoshǐ*), Xiāo Huì, defeated them.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngwèi* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Yēlǜ Hónggǔ, Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Command, was made Tìyǐn.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Púlú Máozēng Tribe had many Wùrě households.
An edict commanded that they be sought out.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
[The Emperor] went to Yǒng'ān Mountain.
The fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Xiāo Zàogǔ, Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Capital, was made Grand Commissioner of the Qìdān Travelling Palace.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Xiāo Huì, Commissioner of Pacification and Punishment for the Northwest Circuit, was dispatched to lead troops to attack the Gān Zhōu Uighurs (*Huíhú*).
The sixth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
An edict commanded that all official livestock must be branded on the left side for identification.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùshēn* day,
[The Emperor] hunted at Hēilǐng.
In the eighth month,
Xiāo Huì attacked Gānzhōu but failed,
and the army returned.
From this time, all the various tribes of the Zǔbǔ rebelled.
The Liáo army fought against them,
but was defeated by them every time.
The Supervising Envoy Nièlǐgū and the Maternal Uncle Account Grand Mentor Hébùlǚ died there.
An imperial edict was issued, sending Tìyǐn Yēlǜ Hónggǔ and Línyá Huàgē, among others, to lead troops to suppress them.
In the ninth month,
the imperial retinue halted on the bank of the Liáohé.
In winter, on the day Bǐngzǐ of the tenth month,
the chieftains of the various Hésūguǎn tribes came to court.
On the day Gēngchén,
an envoy was dispatched to inquire about the reason for the Xià State's engagement in battle with the Sòng in the fifth month.
On the day Xīnsì,
Zhílǔgǔn, the former Grand King of the Southern Department, was made the Grand Administrator of Wūgǔdíliè.
On the day Gēngyín,
Xiāo Xiàoshùn and Xiāo Shàozōng were appointed concurrently as Palace Attendants (Shìzhōng);
Consort-designate Xiāo Shàoyè was made Manager of Governmental Affairs (Píngzhāng Zhèngshì);
Húdǔjǐn, the former Grand King of the Southern Department, was made Co-Administrator of the Supreme Capital Residency (Shàngjīng Liúshǒu);
and Āngē was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of Tōnghuàzhōu.
On the day Yǐchǒu of the eleventh month,
Sòng dispatched Hán Yì and Tián Chéngshuō to congratulate on the Shùntiān Festival.
On the day Wùchén,
Sǎogū, a petty officer of the Northwest Route Pacification and Inspection Commissioner (Zhāotǎo) Office, accused the Pacification and Inspection Commissioner Xiāo Huì of three crimes.
An imperial edict ordered the Military Supervisor (Dūjiān) Àogǔzhēn to investigate the matter.
On the day Gēngchén of the twelfth month,
the Hésūguǎn tribe requested permission to establish flags and drums,
which was granted.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial edict instructed that officials in the northern and southern tribes, inspectors of prefectures and counties, and officials of the Shíliè and Mǐlǐ [accounts],
if incompetent in governance, should be dismissed.
An imperial edict further stated that if any official, high or low, was greedy, violent, or oppressive toward the people,
they should be immediately dismissed,
and never reappointed for life;
if they were not honest and upright,
even if holding an important position,
they should be replaced immediately;
those who could maintain integrity and diligence
should be recommended and promoted even if in a low position;
and if members of the imperial clan accepted bribes,
and the incident was exposed,
they would be subject to the same penalty as common people committing the crime.
On the day Wùxū,
Dù Fáng and Xiāo Yùn were dispatched as the envoy and deputy to congratulate the Sòng Emperor on his birthday.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the imperial retinue halted at the Liáohé.
In the spring of the seventh year, on the first day Rén'yín of the first month,
Sòng dispatched Zhāng Bǎowéi, Sūn Jìyè, Kǒng Dàofǔ, and Mǎ Chóngzhì to offer congratulations.
The Emperor proceeded to the Hùntóngjiāng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Báilǚ of the Nǚzhí was made Tìyǐn,
and Púmǎ was made Grand Mentor (Tàishī) of the Yánmǔ Department.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Púlúmáo 部 tribe dispatched an envoy to present tribute.
In summer, on the day Yǐwèi of the fourth month,
the Emperor hunted at Hēilǐng.
In the fifth month,
the Emperor sought respite from the heat at Yǒng'ānshān.
The Southwest Route Pacification and Inspection Commissioner Office reported that gold and silver were produced in the Yīnshān,
and requested the establishment of a foundry,
which was granted.
Envoys were again dispatched to trace the source of the Liáohé in search of gold and silver mines.
In the sixth month,
the practice of various garrison farms selling official grain without authorization was prohibited.
On the day Guǐsì,
an imperial edict ordered Xiāo Huì to suppress the Zǔbǔ again.
In autumn, on the first day Jǐhài of the seventh month,
an imperial edict ordered the revision and standardization of laws and regulations.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict instructed Consort-designate Xiāo Chúbù and Princess Niánmǐgǔn:
"You regard the Empress as having the same honor as parents.
When the Empress visits,
you perform respectful homage to your ancestors
and bow respectfully to the empty tent,
but you fail to observe the ritual of reverence.
Henceforth, you must set up an image for bowing and paying respects."
On the day Yǐsì,
an imperial edict stated that areas through which the Imperial Carriage Route (Niǎnlù) passed,
within thirty paces on either side, must not be cultivated,
and such cases were not subject to litigation limitations.
In the ninth month,
the imperial retinue halted at the Liáohé.
In winter, on the first day Dīngmǎo of the tenth month,
an imperial edict decreed that concerning the illegitimate children (shùniè) of the various accounts and offices,
their status of nobility or lowliness should be determined based on their mother's status.
In the eleventh month,
Sòng dispatched Shí Zhōnglì and Shí Yísūn to congratulate on the Qiānlíng Festival,
and Wáng Bówén and Wáng Shuāng to congratulate on the Shùntiān Festival.
On the day Xīnhài,
Yáng Yòuxuán and Xíng Xiáng were appointed to manage the civil service examinations (gòngjǔ).
On the day Jǐwèi,
Zhāgě, Prince of Zhōngshān Commandery and Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Kuāngyì Army; Xiè Jiānú, Prince of Chángshā Commandery and Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Bǎoníng Army;
and Suìgē, Prince of Yuè'ān Commandery and Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Guǎngdé Army, submitted a memorial,
requesting that officials leading troops
be allowed to select companions for reading and scribing (bàndú shūshǐ),
which was granted.
On the day Guǐhài,
Qīn, King of Sānhán, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Qǐshèng Army,
and Yáng Jí was made Vice Minister (Shìláng) of the Ministry of Personnel (Xíngbù).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Yēlǜ Gǔyù, Supreme General of the Left Thousand Ox Guard, was made Grand King of the Northern Department.
On the first day Dīngmǎo of the twelfth month,
Yēlǜ Suìyīng and Wáng Yǒngxī were dispatched as envoy and deputy to congratulate the Sòng Empress Dowager on her birthday,
and Xiāo Sùsā and Mǎ Bǎoyǒng as envoy and deputy to congratulate on the New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn).
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Xiāo Gāoliù of the Right Army of Imperial Insignia was made Administrator (Xiángwěn) of the Xīshèlì Army.
In the spring of the eighth year, on the day Jǐhài of the first month,
the Emperor proceeded to the Hùntóngjiāng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Dǎngxiàng invaded the frontier,
and they were defeated.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict commanded the chief administrators of prefectures and counties to encourage agriculture.
In the second month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Xiāo Xiàomù, the Resident of Yānjīng, requested that a garrison commander be established on the border near the Jùmǎhé connecting with Sòng territory to conduct patrols,
and an imperial edict granted this.
In the third month,
the imperial retinue halted at the Chángchūnhé.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the Emperor sought respite from the heat at Yǒng'ānshān.
In the sixth month,
Hán Níng and Liú Xiāng were appointed as the envoy and deputy to congratulate the Sòng Empress Dowager on her birthday,
and Wú Kèhé was appointed as the envoy to congratulate Lǐ Dézhāo, King of the Xià State, on his birthday.
On the day Guǐsì,
Yēlǜ Zhèngliú, Acting Grand King of the Northern Department, submitted a memorial, stating that
in the eleventh month of this year, the Crown Prince would take a consort,
and the various clans were preparing the tents for family gatherings.
An imperial edict ordered that thirty of the wealthiest and most influential households be allocated funds for this purpose.
In autumn, on the day Dīngyǒu of the seventh month,
Chéngē, a young gentleman of the Yáolián Account, was made Patrol Inspector (Xúnjiǎn) of the Northwest Route,
and was to jointly govern the territory of the two Pacification and Inspection Commissioner Offices (Zhāotǎo) with Xiāo Xié.
Yēlǜ Díliè, Grand King of the Southern Department, was made Resident of the Supreme Capital (Shàngjīng Liúshǒu).
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor hunted in the Píngdì Sōnglín.
On the first day Rénchén of the ninth month,
Luóhàn, Chancellor of Bóhǎi, was made Acting General-in-Chief of the Eastern Capital (Dōngjīng Tǒngjūn Shǐ).
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Central Capital (Zhōngjīng).
Yēlǜ Yánshòu, Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Northern Díliè Department, requested to inspect the various tribes,
and was granted flags and drums,
which was permitted by imperial edict.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Hú Lǎn, a chieftain of a separate Zǔbǔ branch, came to surrender.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Chūngǔ, a chieftain of the Zǔbǔ, came to surrender.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Sòng dispatched Táng Sù and Gé Huáimǐn to congratulate on the Shùntiān Festival.
Āguō, the granddaughter-in-law of Yēlǜ Xiézhěn, Grand Mentor (Shūmì Shǐ) and King of Wèi, was accused of insulting the imperial carriage,
and her grandson Gǔyù concealed it.
When the matter was discovered,
they were both charged together,
and their property was confiscated.
An imperial edict instructed the generals and soldiers in Yānchéng that,
if the enemy arrived,
the Governor-General (Zǒngguǎn) should prepare the southeast of the city,
the General-in-Chief (Tǒngjūn) should guard the northwest,
the cavalry and infantry should prepare for field combat,
and the Deputy General-in-Chief (Tǒngjūn Fùshǐ) should repair the defensive walls and stockades,
examine the soldiers,
and each practice their duties.
On the day Bǐngshēn of the eleventh month,
the Crown Prince took Lady Xiāo as his consort.
Yēlǜ Qiúhàn was made Grand King of the Northern Department.
On the first day Xīnyǒu of the twelfth month,
Xiè Fóliú, Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) of the Yáolián, was made Administrator (Xiángwěn) of the Tiānyún Army.
On the day Rénshēn,
Yēlǜ Liúníng, the former Grand King of the Northern Department, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of Shuāngzhōu;
Kāng Yún was made Supreme Commander (Dūbùshǔ) of the Chóngdé Palace;
Xiè Shí was made Supreme Commander of the Yǒngxīng Palace;
Lǚ Fén was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of Yízhōu;
☐ Ān was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of Liáozhōu;
Yēlǜ Yě was made Co-Administrator of the Central Capital Residency;
and Yēlǜ Hélǔtūkuì was made Grand General.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict stated that although illegitimate children (shùniè) had been made commoners,
they were not allowed to participate in hereditary selections.
On the day Dīnghài,
Sòng dispatched Kòu Jiān and Kāng Déqiú to congratulate on the Qiānlíng Festival,
and Zhū Jiàn, Cáo Yīng, Zhāng Yì, and Liú Yǒngzhāo to congratulate on the New Year's Day of the two palaces (Liǎng Gōng Zhèngdàn) in the coming year.
An imperial edict stated that the two maternal uncles, and the Northern and Southern Princely Establishments, were noble clans of the state,
and those of low or illegitimate birth were not permitted to hold office in these departments.
In this year,
fifty-seven advanced scholars, including Zhāng Yòu, were graduated.
In the spring of the ninth year, in the first month,
the Emperor returned from the Central Capital.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
an envoy was dispatched to bestow goods upon Qīn, the King of Gāolì.
The Emperor proceeded to the Wòlǐnhé.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the Emperor sought respite from the heat at Yǒng'ānshān.
On the first day Wùzǐ of the sixth month,
Xiè Jiānú, Prince of Chángshā Commandery, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Guǎngdé Army;
Suìgē, Prince of Yuè'ān Commandery, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Kuāngyì Army;
Zhāgě, Prince of Zhōngshān Commandery, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Bǎodìng Army,
and was advanced in rank to Prince of Lù;
and Tiēbù, Prince of Yùzhāng, was made Commissioner of Jiézhì of the Chángníng Army.

Yēlǜ Sīzhōng, Yēlǜ Hé, Yēlǜ Gǎo, Yáolián Xiè Fóliú, Chén Miǎo, Hán Shàoyī, Hán Zhībái, and Zhāng Zhèn were appointed as the envoy and deputy to congratulate the Sòng two palaces on their birthdays and on the New Year's Day of the coming year.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Wùwǔ (the first day of the month),
went to Hēilǐng.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,

Xiāo Xiàoxiān, the Residential Commissioner and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law (Fùmǎ Dūwèi), and Nányáng Gōngzhǔ were imprisoned by Dà Yánlín, the Xiāngwěn (Chancellor) of the Shèlì Army in Dōngjīng (Eastern Capital).
He killed Hán Shàoxūn, the Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù Shǐ), Wáng Jiā, the Deputy Commissioner, and Xiāo Pōdé, the Commander-in-Chief of the Sìjié Army.
Yánlín then usurped the throne,
naming his state Xīngliáo,
and the era Tiānqìng.
Initially,
the lands of Dōngliáo,
since they came to submit during the Shéncè era,
did not have laws governing the monopoly of liquor, vinegar, salt, and yeast,
and the levies on markets and passes were also very lenient.
Féng Yánxiū and Hán Shàoxūn successively enforced the strict laws of Píngshān in Yāndì (the Yan region) upon them,
and the people could not endure the burden.
The Yan region also suffered severe famine for several years,
and Wáng Jiā, the Deputy Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, again offered a plan to build ships,
sending the people skilled in maritime affairs
to transport grain to relieve the Yan populace.
The water routes were treacherous,
often leading to capsizing and loss.
Though the officials' words were not trusted,
whippings and beatings were used,
causing public resentment and a desire for rebellion.
Therefore, Yánlín seized the opportunity,
first killing Shàoxūn and Jiā,
to satisfy his followers.
Yánlín had previously consulted with Wáng Dàopíng, the Deputy Residential Commissioner, about the affair.
Dàopíng abandoned his family that night,
fled over the wall,
and together with Huáng Piān, whom Yánlín had dispatched to summon from Huánglóng Fǔ,
they both reached the Imperial Traveling Residence (Xíngzài) to report the rebellion.
The Emperor immediately levied troops from all circuits (Zhūdào),
to advance and suppress the rebellion promptly.
At that time, Xiāo Pǐdí, the Imperial Uncle Xiāngwěn, governed near Yánlín.
He first led his own administration's troops and household forces to occupy strategic points,
cutting off Yánlín's plan to cross westward.
Xià Xíngměi, the Bóhǎi Tàibǎo (Grand Protector), was also a former commander of troops,
garrisoned at Bǎozhōu.
Yánlín secretly sent a fast letter,
instructing him to plot against the Commander-in-Chief, Yēlǜ Púgǔ.
Xíngměi instead reported the truth.
Púgǔ received the letter
and consequently killed eight hundred Bóhǎi soldiers,
cutting off Yánlín's eastern route.
Yánlín learned that both Huánglóng and Bǎozhōu were not supporting him,
so he divided his forces to take Shěnzhōu in the west.
Its Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ), Xiāo Wángliù, had just arrived.
His deputy, Zhāng Jié, announced his intention to surrender,
so Yánlín did not attack urgently.
When Yánlín realized the deception,
the defenses were already prepared,
and the attack failed, so he returned.
At that time, the Southern and Northern Nǚzhēn peoples all followed Yánlín,
and Gāolì (Goryeo) also withheld its tribute.
When the troops from all circuits arrived in sequence,
Yánlín defended the city steadfastly.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Bǐngxū (the first day of the month),
Xiāo Xiàomù, Prince of Yan and Residential Commissioner of Nánjīng (Southern Capital), was appointed Dūtǒng (Commander-in-Chief);
Xiāo Pǐdí, the Imperial Uncle Xiāngwěn, was appointed Fùtǒng (Deputy Commander-in-Chief);
and Xiāo Púnú, the Great King of the Six Departments of the Xī, was appointed Dūjiān (Supervisor) to suppress the rebellion.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo (the first day of the month),
went to Xiǎnlíng (Mausoleum).
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāng Jié, the Deputy Military Governor of Shěnzhōu, was promoted to Military Governor.
Twenty-two Imperial City Scholars (Huángchéng Jìnshì), including Zhāng Rénjì and Zhào Mù, came to the court.
They were tested with poetry and rhyming prose (shī fù),
and all were granted degrees.
Xià Xíngměi, the general guarding Bǎozhōu, was exceptionally promoted to Píngzhāngshì (Chancellor).
On the day Rénshēn,
Liú Sìduān, the Imperial Son-in-Law, was given the provisional authority (Quán Zhī) over the Southern Bureau of the Department of Imperial Chancellery (Xuānhuī Nányuàn Shì).
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Sòng (Song Dynasty) sent Qiú Yǒng and Hán Yǒngxī to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival (Qiānlíng Jié).
Yēlǜ Yù, Wú Kèhé, Xiāo Kěguān, and Zhào Lìyòng were ordered to serve as the chief and deputy envoys (Shǐ Fù) to congratulate the Sòng Emperor's birthday.
Yēlǜ Yuánjí, Cuī Rùn, Xiāo Zhāogǔ, and Dòu Zhèn were appointed as the chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn) of the coming year.
Tenth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Yǐmǎo (the first day of the month),
Sòng sent Wáng Yíjiǎn, Dòu Chǔyuē, Zhāng Yì, and Zhāng Shìyí to offer congratulations.
In the second month,
went to Lónghuà Zhōu.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎyín (the first day of the month),
Xiāo Pǐdí, the Xiāngwěn, arrived from Liáodōng,
reporting that the Dūtǒng, Xiāo Xiàomù, had constructed fortresses five *lǐ* (li) away from all four sides of the city
to besiege it.
Yánníng, the Imperial Son-in-Law, and his sister dug a tunnel and fled.
Only Princess Cuī Bā remained behind
and was detected and stopped by the guards on the ramparts.
In the fourth month of summer,
went to Qiánlíng (Mausoleum).
Yēlǜ Xíngpíng was appointed Military Governor of Guǎngpíng Army.
Xià Xíngměi was appointed Military Governor of Zhōngshùn Army.
Lǐ Yánhóng was made Provisional Governor (Zhī) of Yìzhōu.
Xiāo Cóngshùn was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàishī).
In the fifth month, on the day Wùshēn,
cleared the summer heat at Bǎipō.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Rénwǔ,
an imperial edict decreed that the civil service examination (Gòngjǔ Fǎ) would be implemented the following year.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Yáng Xiángshì, the rebel general in Dōngjīng, secretly delivered a letter.
He opened the South Gate at night to admit the Liáo army.
Yánlín was captured,
and Bóhǎi was pacified.
In the tenth month of winter,
stationed the imperial carriage (Zhùbì) at Chángníng Diàn.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnhài,
Xiāo Xiàomù, Prince of Yan and Residential Commissioner of Nánjīng, returned triumphantly with the generals and soldiers of the Eastern Expedition.
He appeared before the Emperor in military attire,
and the Emperor greatly feasted and rewarded them.
The following day,
Xiàomù was made Prince of Dōngpíng and Residential Commissioner of Dōngjīng.
Xiāo Pǐdí, the Imperial Uncle Xiāngwěn and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, was enfeoffed as Prince of Lánlíng Commandery.
Xiāo Púnú, the King of the Xī, was promoted to Shìzhōng (Chamberlain).
Xiāo Huì, provisional Residential Commissioner of Yānjīng (Yan Capital) and concurrently Shìzhōng, was appointed Commander of the Yānjīng Army (Tǒngjūn Shǐ).
The former Commander of the Wēiwā Grand General and Military Governor.
Mǎ Bǎozhōng, Chancellor and concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Shǐ), was made provisional Residential Commissioner of Yānjīng.
Xiāo Āgǔzhěn, Supervisor of the Xī King's Prefecture, was made Commander of the Dōngjīng Army.
An imperial edict ordered that members of the old Bóhǎi aristocracy who possessed merit, labor, talent, or strength should be employed;
the rest were distributed to reside in the prefectures of Lái, Xí, Qiān, Rùn, and others.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Sòng sent Méi Xún and Wáng Lìngjié to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival.
Yēlǜ Díliè, Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery, was promoted to Shàngfù (Imperial Mentor).
Xiāo Pǔdá, Military Governor of the Wūgǔ Department, was made Great King of the Yǐshì Department.
Xiāo Lín, Left Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè), was made Military Governor of the Línhǎi Army.
Eleventh year, in the first month of spring, on the day Jǐyǒu (the first day of the month),
went to the Húntóng Jiāng (River).
In the second month,
went to the Chángchūn Hé (River).
In the third month,
the Emperor became unwell.
In the fifth month of summer,
there was heavy rainfall,
and all rivers flooded,
deviating from their old courses.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngchǒu (the first day of the month),
stationed the imperial carriage north of the Dàfú Hé (River).
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor passed away at the traveling palace,
aged sixty-one,
having reigned for forty-nine years.
In the intercalary tenth month of the first year of Jǐngfú, on the day Rénshēn,
he was honored with the posthumous title Emperor Wénwǔ Dàxiào Xuān,
and the temple name Shèngzōng.
The eulogy says: Shèngzōng succeeded to the throne in his youth,
with government affairs issuing from his merciful mother.
When the Sòng people attacked in two routes,
he personally donned armor and helmet,
and in one campaign recovered Yan and Yun,
and defeated Xìn and Bīn.
In a second campaign, he trod upon Hé and Shuò.
Was this not magnificent!
Subsequently, once his extravagant ambition was aroused,
fondness for military action proved inauspicious.
To the east, there was the defeat at Chá and Tuó;
to the west, the loss of Gānzhōu.
This was the consequence of relying on habitual victories.
However, during his forty-nine years on the throne,
he redressed grievances and injustice,
promoted talented and virtuous conduct,
investigated the greedy and cruel,
suppressed extravagance and usurpation,
recorded the descendants of those who died in service,
relieved the poverty of the various tribes,
reproved the crime of flattering and disloyal compliance,
and refused the return of female musicians from Gāolì.
Among the emperors of Liáo,
who reigned for a long time,
whose excellent reputation is boundless,
was he not Shèngzōng!
Basic Annals XVIII: Xīngzōng I
Xīngzōng, Emperor Shénshèng Xiàozhāng,
taboo name Zōngzhēn,
courtesy name Yībùjǐn,
pet name Zhīgǔ.
He was the eldest son of Shèngzōng,
his mother being Empress Qīn'āi, of the Xiāo clan.
When the Emperor was first born,
Empress Qítiān adopted him and raised him.
He was intelligent in his youth,
and imposing and great in adulthood,
with a dragon countenance and a prominent forehead (rìjiǎo),
being broad-minded and magnanimous.
He was skilled in riding and archery,
fond of Confucian studies,
and versed in musical temperament.
At age three, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liáng.
In the first year of Tàipíng, he was established as Crown Prince.
In the tenth year, in the sixth month, he provisionally managed (Pàn) the Northern and Southern Bureaus of the Department of Military Affairs.
In the eleventh year, summer, the sixth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Shèngzōng collapsed (died).
He ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
On the day Rénwǔ,
his mother, Consort Yuánfēi of the Xiāo clan, was honored as Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
On the day Jiǎshēn,
envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Sòng, as well as Xià and Gāolì.
In this year,
fifty-seven successful candidates, including the presented scholar (jìnshì) Liú Zhēn, were released from Xuānzhèng Diàn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
a general amnesty was granted,
and the reign title was changed to Jǐngfú.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the coffin of the late Emperor (Dàxíng Huángdì) was escorted
and temporarily placed at Tàipíng Diàn on Yǒng'ān Shān.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Empress Dowager granted death to the Princely Son-in-Law (Fùmǎ) Xiāo Chúbulǐ and Xiāo Pǐdí.

Seven people, including the Commander of the Imperial Hunting Ground (Wéichǎng Dū Tàishī), the Nǚzhí Zhùgǔlǐ, and the Right Palace Attendant Gentleman General (Yòu Zhīhòu Lángjūn Xiángwěn) Xiāo Yánliú, were all executed publicly.
Their families were confiscated.
Empress Qītiān was moved to Shàngjīng.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, Bǐngwǔ,
the Empress Dowager led the imperial clan in a great lamentation at Tàipíng Diàn.
Gāolì sent envoys to offer condolences and comfort.
The Emperor summoned the Prince of Jìn, Xiāo Pǔgǔ, and others to drink and gamble,
only dispersing at midnight.
On the day Dīngwèi,
they played polo (jījú).
On the day Wùshēn,
Yēlǜ Hánbā was appointed Left Yílíbì.
Tèmòlǐ was appointed Left Palace Attendant Gentleman General (Zuǒ Zhīhòu Lángjūn Xiángwěn).
The Horizontal Tent Gentleman (Héngzhàng Lángjūn) Lègǔ temporarily held the post of Right Palace Attendant Gentleman General (Yòu Zhīhòu Lángjūn Xiángwěn).
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Yēlǜ Zhèngliú was appointed Yújué Dílièdū Xiángwěn.
Gāobā was appointed Right Píshì Xiángwěn.
On the day Gēngxū,
