relief was provided to the starving populace of Jìzhōu.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an edict was issued to paint the portrait of the late Emperor.
On the day Jiǎyín,
prisoners were reviewed.
The Intendant (Guānchá) Yáo Jūxìn was appointed Supreme General (Shàng Jiāngjūn).
Qìngzhōu was established south of Qìng Líng (the mausoleum).
People were relocated to populate it,
serving as the city dedicated to the mausoleum service.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
because the harvest had been abundant in recent years,
the provision of grain to the Commander-in-Chief's Office (Tǒngjūn Sī) of Dōngjīng was halted.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor visited the late Emperor’s portrait,
grieving deeply for a long time.

Consequently, he ordered the portraits of the Chancellor (Zǎixiàng) of the Northern Administration (Běifǔ), Xiāo Xiàoxiān, and the Chancellor of the Southern Administration (Nánfǔ), Xiāo Xiàomù, to be painted in the Imperial Portrait Hall (Yùróng Diàn).
Xiāo Āgūzhěn was appointed Defense Commissioner (Liúshǒu) of Dōngjīng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
he visited Tàipíng Diàn,
burning the bows and arrows formerly used by the preceding Emperor.
He visited the residence of the Prince of Jìn, Pǔgǔ, to check on his illness.
On the day Xīnwèi,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor visited the spirit tablet tent (shénzhǔ zhàng).
At this time, Lady Xiāo of Àowēi first entered the palace,
and she was also commanded to bow before it.
The eighth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the coffin of the late Emperor was moved to Zōutú Diàn.
The ninth month, on the day Wùshēn,
he personally inspected Qìng Líng.
On the day Gēngxū,
he inquired after the welfare of the Empress Dowager.
On the day Xīnhài,
Sòng sent Wáng Suí and Cáo Yí to offer sacrifices.
Wáng Pì, Xǔ Huáixìn, Méi Xún, and Zhāng Lún came to comfort the Two Palaces.
Fàn Fèng and Sūn Jìyè offered congratulations on the ascension to the throne.
Kǒng Dàofǔ and Wèi Zhāowén offered congratulations on the Empress Dowager's official conferment ceremony (cè lǐ).
On the day Wùwǔ,
bows, arrows, saddles, and bridles were burned at Zōutú Diàn.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the state of Xià sent envoys to offer comfort.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
owing to the sacrificial condolences offered by the Sòng envoys,
the Emperor, in mourning attire, went to Zōutú Diàn.
On the day Jiǎxū,

the Emperor sent Vice Director of the Censorate (Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng) Yēlǜ Zhù, Minister of Agriculture (Sīnóng Qīng) Zhāng Què, General (Xiángwěn) Yēlǜ Lì, and Envoy for the Four Directions Residence (Sìfāng Guǎn Shǐ) Gāo Wéihàn to thank Sòng for their condolences and comfort.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
the Chancellor (Zǎichén) Lǚ Démào passed away.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Mílènú and Guānyīnnú, partisans of Chúbulǐ, and others were killed.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor sent Minister of Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū) Gāo Déshùn and Minister of Ceremonies (Chónglù Qīng) Lǐ Kěfēng to deliver the preceding Emperor’s relics to Sòng.

Supreme General of the Right Leader of the Army Guard (Yòu Lǐngjūn Wèi Shàng Jiāngjūn) Yēlǜ Xùn and Director of the Imperial Less Palace (Shàofǔ Jiān) Mǎ Dàn served as the Empress Dowager’s envoys to thank Sòng.
Supreme General of the Right Palace Guard (Yòu Jiānmén Wèi Shàng Jiāngjūn) Yēlǜ Yuánzài and Usher (Yǐnjìn Shǐ) Wèi Yǒng served as the Emperor’s envoys to thank Sòng.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the state of Xià sent envoys to offer funeral gifts (fù).
On the day Wùxū,
Xiāo Gé, Zhào Wéiguǒ, Yēlǜ Yù, and Mǎ Bǎoyè were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to Sòng for the New Year (Zhēngdàn) celebration the following year.
Intercalary month, on the day Xīnhài,
he visited Zōutú Diàn,
and inspected the sacred funerary objects (bì qì) of the Mysterious Palace (Xuán Gōng).
The appropriate authorities requested that the Emperor’s birthday be designated Yǒngshòu Jié,
and the Empress Dowager’s birthday be designated Yìngshèng Jié.
This was approved.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
new armor and mail were inspected.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
relief was provided to the starving populace of Huánglóng Fǔ.
The eleventh month, on the day Rénchén,
the Emperor led the assembled officials in offering sacrifice at Zōutú Diàn.
The late Emperor’s clothing, personal effects, and cherished belongings were taken out and burned.
The hawks and falcons from the Five Aviaries (Wǔ Fāng) were released.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Emperor Wénwǔ Dàxiào Xuān Huángdì was buried at Qìng Líng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
He inquired after the welfare of the Empress Dowager.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
he visited Qìng Líng.
Relics were bestowed upon the various officials.
The mountain was named Qìngyún,
and the palace was named Wàngxiān.
The twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
he arrived back from Qìng Líng.
The Empress Dowager managed the government affairs,
and the Emperor did not personally handle administrative matters.
The assembled officials submitted petitions regarding this,
but he did not follow their advice.
In this year,
Princess Xīngpíng was married off to Yuánhào, the son of Lǐ Dézhāo, King of Xià.
Yuánhào was appointed Duke of Xià (Xiàguó Gōng) and Princely Son-in-Law Commandant (Fùmǎ Dūwèi).
Chóngxī, the first year, spring, the first month, on the first day, Rénshēn,
the Empress Dowager attended the main palace (Zhèng Diàn),
receiving the court audience from the Emperor and the assembled officials.
Sòng sent Rèn Bù, Wáng Zūnfàn, Chén Yǎn, and Wáng Kèshàn to offer congratulations.
On the day Yǐhài,
Sòng sent Zhèng Xiàng and Guō Zūnfàn to congratulate on Yǒngshòu Jié.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
he went to Xuělín.
The second month,
a great hunting expedition (Dà Sōu) took place.
The third month, on the first day, Rénshēn,
Shàngfǔ, Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery (Qīshuǐ Jùnwáng) Díliè, was restored as Tìyǐn.
This spring,
the Empress Dowager falsely accused Empress Qītiān of a crime,
and sent men to Shàngjīng to carry out the murder.
The Empress requested a full bath before facing death,
which was permitted.
A short while later,
the Empress collapsed (died).
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐsì,
he visited Qīngshǔ Biéniǎndǒu.
Autumn, the seventh month,
hunting took place at Píngdì Sōnglín.
Xiāo Dápǔ, Wáng Yīngxiù, Xiāo Lù, and Zhāng Sùyǔ were appointed as envoys to Sòng for the New Year and birthday celebrations the following year.
The eighth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial procession stopped at Lāhé Yuán.
Imperial Prince Hóngjī was born.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
he visited Zhōngjīng.
The eleventh month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor led the assembled officials in offering the Empress Dowager the honorific title: Empress Dowager Fǎtiān Yìngyùn Réndé Zhāngshèng.
The assembled officials offered the Emperor the honorific title: Emperor Wénwǔ Rénshèng Zhāoxiào.
A general amnesty was granted,
and the reign title was changed to Chóngxī.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Sòng sent Liú Suí and Wáng Déběn to congratulate on Yìngshèng Jié.
Yáng Jí was appointed Academican (Hànlín Chéngzhǐ).
On the day Bǐngxū,
the state of Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the chiefs of the Five Nations (Wǔ Guó) came to pay tribute.
Lǐ Dézhāo, King of Xià, passed away (hōng).
His son, Yuánhào, Duke of Xià, was enfeoffed as King of Xià (Xiàguó Wáng).
The twelfth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Sòng sent Xū Yǎn, Wáng Cóngyì, Cuī Jì, and Zhāng Huáizhì to offer congratulations on the New Year of the coming year.
They also sent Yáng Rìyán and Wáng Kèzuǎn to congratulate on Yǒngshòu Jié.
Yēlǜ Qiúhàn, Prince of Běidà, was appointed to serve as Associate Administrator (Tóng Píngzhāng Shì).
In this year,
fifty-seven presented scholars, including Liú Shīzhēn, were released (passed the examination).
The second year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor proceeded eastward.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the state of Xià sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day Rénchén,
Tái Yā, General (Xiángwěn) of the Nǚzhí, led his subordinates to pay tribute.
Sòng sent Cáo Cóng to announce the mourning for their Empress Mother, Lady Liú.
Zhāng Déxiàng and Ān Jìchāng came to deliver relics of the Empress Mother.

Immediately, the Emperor sent Envoy of Xīngshèng Gōng, Yēlǜ Shòuníng, and Drafting Official in the Imperial Secretariat (Jǐshì Zhōng Zhī Zhìgào), Lǐ Kuí, to serve as envoys for sacrifices and libations.

Military Commissioner of Tiāndé Army (Tiāndé Jūn Jiédù Shǐ) Yēlǜ Qīngníng, Minister of the Court of Judicial Review (Dàlǐ Qīng) Hé Dàohēng, Military Commissioner of Héxī Army (Héxī Jūn Jiédù Shǐ) Yēlǜ Sōng, and Usher (Yǐnjìn Shǐ) Mǎ Shìqīng served as envoys to offer condolences and comfort to the Two Palaces.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, Jiǎzǐ,
Yēlǜ Shí, Gāo Shēng, Yēlǜ Dí, and Wáng Wéiyǔn were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng's Two Palaces on their birthdays.
Yēlǜ Shīgǔ and Liú Wǔcháng were appointed as chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year of the coming year.
The eighth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
he visited Wēnquán Gōng (Hot Springs Palace).
On the day Yǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to inspect the crops in various circuits (lù).
Winter, the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Sòng sent Liú Bǎo, Fú Zhōng, Lǐ Zhāoshù, Zhāng Màoshí, and others to offer thanks for the comfort and libations.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Sòng sent Dīng Dù and Wáng Jìníng to offer congratulations for Yìngshèngjié (The Festival of Responding to the Sage).
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the envoys of Xià Guó (The State of Xià) were forbidden from privately trading gold and iron along the route.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Sòng sent Zhāng Pín, Lǐ Yì, Wáng Chōngmù, Zhāng Wěi, Lǐ Hóng, and Lǐ Jìyī to offer congratulations for Yǒngshòujié and the New Year's Day (Zhēngdàn) of the coming year.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Xiāo Xiàoxiān, the Prime Minister (Zǎixiàng) of the Northern Administration (Běi Fǔ), was appointed as Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmìshǐ).
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Sòng envoy Zhāng Pín died.
An imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to provide burial stipends and gifts,
and commanded close attendants to escort the funeral back.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
[the Emperor] went to the Spring Hunting Ground (Chūnshuǐ).
The second month, on the first day Rénchén,
Xiāo Pǔgǔ, the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department (Běi Yuàn Shūmìshǐ), was appointed as Resident General (Liúshǒu) of Dōngjīng.
On the day Wùshēn,
because Yēlǜ Dàshīnǔ had the favor of having attended [the Emperor] in infancy,
an imperial edict commanded him to be entered into the official register.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
relief was provided to the Yēmízhī tribe.
The fifth month, on the first day Gēngshēn,
[the Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat along Liǔ Hú (Willow Lake).
In this month,
the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) returned the administration to the Emperor,
and personally guarded Qìng Líng.
The sixth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xiāo Pǔgǔ was appointed as Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Department (Nán Yuàn Shūmìshǐ).
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor began to personally govern.
Yēlǜ Shùzhēng, Liú Liùfú, Yēlǜ Mù, and Bó Kějiǔ were appointed as the chief envoy and deputy envoy to congratulate Sòng on the New Year's Day of the coming year.
On the day Rénchén,
[the Emperor] went to Qiūshān (Autumn Mountain).
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the imperial carriage halted at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
The twelfth month,
Sòng sent Duàn Shǎolián and Dù Rénzàn to offer congratulations for the New Year's Day of the coming year,
and Yáng Xié and Lǐ Shǒuzhōng came to offer congratulations for Yǒngshòujié.
The fourth year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngyín,
[the Emperor] went to Yēmízhī Lǐ.
The third month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
Empress Xiāo Shì was established.
Summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jiǎyín,
[the Emperor] went to Liángxíng.
The fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
[the Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Sǎnshuǐ Yuán.
The sixth month, on the first day Guǐchǒu,
the Imperial Prince Bǎoxìnnú was born.
Yēlǜ Xìn, Lǚ Shìzōng, Xiāo Gǔn, and Guō Kuí were appointed as the chief envoy and deputy envoy to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday (Shēngchén) and the New Year's Day of the coming year.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Rénwǔ,
[the Emperor] hunted at Hēilǐng.
The ninth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage halted at Chángníng Diàn.
Winter, the tenth month,
[the Emperor] went to Wángzǐ Chéng.
The eleventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Nánjīng Commander-in-Chief's Office (Zǒngguǎnfǔ) was renamed to Marshall's Office (Yuánshuàifǔ).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Cháicè Ceremony was performed at Báilǐng,
and a general amnesty was granted.

Grand Preceptor (Shàngfù) Yēlǜ Xìnníng and Director of Political Affairs (Zhèngshì Lìng) Yēlǜ Qiúhàn were given the title of Qísù Zànyì Gōngchén (Meritorious Elder Statesman Who Assists and Supports).
The twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial edict commanded all armies' artillery, crossbowmen, archers, and swordsmen to practice regularly.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Sòng sent Zhèng Jiǎn, Chái Yífàn, Yáng Rìhuá, and Zhāng Shìyǔ to offer congratulations for Yǒngshòujié and Zhèngdàn.
The fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
[the Emperor] went to Yú'ér Luò.
Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiāo Yánníng requested that the Chamberlain (Chǎngshǐ) of the Imperial Uncle Yǐshì Xiǎogōng Zhàng be changed to General (Jiāngjūn).
This was granted.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Zhāgě, the Prince of Lù (Lù Wáng), was appointed as the Prime Minister of the Southern Administration (Nán Fǔ Zǎixiàng).
Yēlǜ Mǎliù, the Director of Chóngdé Palace, was appointed as Tìyǐn.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
[the Emperor] visited the residence of the Empress's younger brother, Xiāo Wúqǔ.
They performed the Qūshuǐ Fànshāng (Floating Cups on Winding Streams) ceremony and composed poetry.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
newly established regulations and institutions were promulgated.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor and the high ministers divided into teams to play polo (Jījú).
The fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
[the Emperor] traveled south (Nán Xìng).
On the day Dīngwèi,
[the Emperor] went to Hútǔ Báishān to escape the summer heat.
On the day Gēngshēn,
[the Emperor] visited the traveling tent of Gāo Shí, the Prince (Dàwáng) of the Northern Department (Běi Yuàn), where he paid respects to the inner sanctum (bài ào),
and bestowed silver and silk.
On the day Rénxū,
an imperial edict commanded the renovation of the palace and official residences in Nánjīng.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
prisoners were reviewed.
Yēlǜ Bǎbā falsely accused his younger brother Hángē of plotting to murder him.
The authorities reported that Bǎbā should be punished under the law of false accusation (fǎnzuò).
Just before the execution,
his younger brother tearfully pleaded:
"I only have one elder brother,
I beg that his life be spared."
The Emperor took pity and granted the request.
The ninth month, on the day Guǐsì,
[the Emperor] hunted at Huánghuā Shān,
catching thirty-six bears,
and rewarded the hunters according to rank.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
[the Emperor] visited Nánjīng.
On the day Xīnhài,
a partial amnesty was granted to the prisoners within Xījīn Fǔ.
On the day Rénzǐ,
[the Emperor] presided over Yuánhé Diàn,
and tested the presented scholars (Jìnshì) in court with essays on the thirty-six bears shot that day and poems about the visit to Yān (Xìng Yān Shī);
Fény Lì, Zhào Huī, and forty-nine others were granted the Jìnshì degree.
Féng Lì was appointed as Right Reminder (Yòu Bǔquē),
and Zhào Huī and all those below him were made Palace Interns of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Zhōngshě).
They were granted scarlet robes and silver fish ornaments,
followed by a grand banquet.
The imperial examination of presented scholars began from this point.
Sòng sent Sòng Jiāo and Wáng Shìwén to offer congratulations for Yǒngshòujié.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Prime Minister (Zǎichén) Zhāng Jiǎn and others requested [the Emperor] to visit the Examination Hall (Gòngyuàn) of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù).
They drank merrily until dusk before concluding,
and rewards were bestowed according to rank.
Yēlǜ Xiáng, Zhāng Sùmín, Yēlǜ Fǔ, and Wáng Zé were appointed as the chief envoy and deputy envoy to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday and New Year's Day.
The sixth year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
[the Emperor] traveled west (Xī Xìng).
The third month, on the day Wùyín,
Xiāo Xiàomù, the Prince of Qín (Qín Wáng), was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department,
and his title was changed to Prince of Wú (Wú Wáng);
Xiāo Xiàoxiān, the Prince of Jìn (Jìn Wáng), was appointed Resident General of Nánjīng.
Summer, the fourth month,
[the Emperor] hunted at Yěhú Lǐng.
Intercalary month,
[the Emperor] hunted on the Western Mountain of Lóngmén County.
The fifth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
[the Emperor] sought refuge from the summer heat at Tànshān.
Yēlǜ Hánbā was appointed as Prince of the Northern Department;
Xiāo Bǎgē as Left Yílíbì;
Wángzǐ Lángjūn Xiángwěn Bígūdélínyá;
and Yēlǜ Niègē, who oversaw affairs of the Northern Facade (Qiān Běimiàn Shì), was concurrently appointed to the Commission of Inspection (Qiān Diǎnjiǎn Sī).
On the day Jiǎyín,
prisoners were reviewed.
Yēlǜ Xìnníng, the Prince of the South (Nán Dàwáng), was charged with willfully hiding a serious prisoner and for improper conduct with a serving maid involving stolen goods (zāngwū).
He was ordered to be beaten with the flat of a sword and stripped of his office.
The Area Commander (Dūjiān) was convicted of complicity and the crime concerning the serving maid.
Both were sentenced to death,
but an imperial edict pardoned them.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yēlǜ Xìnníng was appointed Commissioner of Pacification of the Southwest Route (Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ).
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Fēilóng Pīnmǎ (Flying Dragon Thoroughbred Horses) were brought out
and bestowed upon the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán and the attendants of the Northern and Southern Facades according to rank.
On the day Guǐhài,
Yēlǜ Húdǔgǔn, the Resident General of Shàngjīng, was appointed as Prince of the South.
Xiāo Chálàníng, Director of Affairs (Píngzhāng Shì), was appointed Resident General of Shàngjīng.
Guǎn Níng, Attendant Consultant (Shìzhōng), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Temporary Palace (Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ).
Yēlǜ Púnú was appointed Supreme General (Dū Xiángwěn) of the Wūgǔdílièdé.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Yēlǜ Hónggǔ, the Resident General of Shàngjīng, was appointed Prince of the Northern Department.
The sixth month, on the first day Rénshēn,
Shànníng was appointed Supreme Inspector of the Palace Guard (Diànqián Dūdiǎnjiǎn).
Yēlǜ Hézhù, Grand Guardian of the Imperial Guard (Hùwèi Tàibǎo), was concurrently appointed Director of Chángníng Palace.
Xiāo Ālàlǐ, Yēlǜ Wūlǔwò, Yēlǜ Héshàng, Xiāo Hánjiānú, Xiāo Tèlǐ, and Xiāo Qiúhàn were appointed as Commanders-in-Chief (Dūbùshǔ) of various palaces.
The Emperor, intoxicated with wine, composed poetry.
Xiāo Xiàomù, the Prince of Wú Guó, and Xiāo Sābā, the Northern Prime Minister, and others all joined in composing complementary verses.
They stopped only in the middle of the night.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the imperial mandate was bestowed upon Yēlǜ Húdǔgǔn, the Prince of the Southern Department.
The Emperor personally composed the edict,
and also bestowed a poem to honor him.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Hóu Shěn, the Prince of the Northern Department, was appointed Commissioner of Military Administration of Nánjīng (Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ).
Autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Xīnchǒu,
because the prisons of the Northern and Southern Departments of Military Affairs were empty,
rewards were granted according to rank.
On the day Rén'yín,
because the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán had a son,
[the Emperor] bestowed a poem and precious artifacts,
and granted a partial amnesty to those sentenced to death or lesser punishments.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
[the Emperor] went to Qiūshān.
The eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Northern Department of Military Affairs reported that the people of the Yuèjí tribe suffered under the unlawful rule of their tribal leader Kūncháng,
and many had fled.
An imperial edict dismissed the tribal leaders of Yuèjí and four other nations,
and commanded that one Khitan Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) be appointed to oversee them.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage halted at Shíbǎo Gāng.
On the first day (xuò) of the eleventh month, Jǐhài,
the chieftain of the Zǔbǔ came to pay tribute.
On Xīnhài,
Xiāo Huì, the General Commandant (Dū bùshǔ) of the Khìdān Traveling Palace, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ).
On Rénzǐ,
Guǎn Níng was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery,
Xiāo Sǎogǔ was made General Commandant of all Traveling Palaces,
Yēlǜ Niǎolǐ was made Acting Deputy Commandant (Fù bùshǔ) of the Southern Traveling Palace,
Xiāo Ālàlǐ was made Xiāngwěn of the Left Gentry Guard (Zuǒ zhīhòu lángjūn xiāngwěn),
and Yēlǜ Hézhǔ was made Xiāngwěn of the Right Gentry Guard (Yòu zhīhòu lángjūn xiāngwěn).
On Gēngshēn,
the Emperor visited the tent of the Princess of Jìnguó to check on her illness.
Hóngjī, the Imperial Son, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Liáng (Liángwáng).
In the twelfth month,
Yáng Jí was made Jìedùshǐ of the Zhōngshùn Army.
Yēlǜ Wò, Qín Jiàn, Yēlǜ Dé, and Cuī Jìfāng were sent to the Sòng court to congratulate them on the Emperor's birthday and the New Year (Zhèngdàn).
In the spring of the seventh year, on the first day (xuò) of the first month, Wùxū,
Sòng sent Gāo Ruònè, Xià Yuánzhèng, Xiè Jiàng, and Zhāng Màoshí to offer congratulations on the New Year and the Yǒngshòu Festival.
On Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor went to the Hùntóng River (Hùntóngjiāng).
In the second month, on Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor went to Chūnzhōu.
On Yǐhài,
the imperial procession stopped at Dōngchuān.
On Dīngchǒu,
Gāolì sent envoys to pay tribute.
On Rénwǔ,
the Emperor visited the Five Parks (Wǔfāng) to inspect eagles and falcons.
On Yǐyǒu,
envoys were sent to Qìngzhōu to inquire after the health of the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu).
In the third month, on the first day (xuò), Wùxū,
the Emperor visited the tent of the Imperial Younger Brother, Chóngyuán.
On Rén'yín,
the Emperor went to Púhé Lake (Púhédìan).
On Xīnhài,
the state of Xià sent envoys to pay tribute.
On Jiǎyín,
prisoners were reviewed.
In summer, the fourth month, on Jǐsì,
due to the death of the Princess of Xīngpíng,
Yēlǜ Shùchéng, Assistant Administrator of the Northern Chancellery (Běiyuàn Chéngzhǐ), was sent with an imperial decree to question Lǐ Yuánhào, King of Xià,
stating that the Princess was estranged from Yuánhào during her life,
and now that she had died,
to interrogate him about the reason for the estrangement.
On Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor hunted at Báimǎguō.
On Jiǎshēn,
rabbits were shot at Xīndìngjǐng.
On Yǐwèi,
the Emperor hunted at Jīnshān,
and sent Yáng Jiā to present deer tails and antlers to the Dà'ān Palace.
In the sixth month, on Yǐhài,
the Emperor held the metropolitan examination for Presented Scholars (Jìnshì) at the Qīngliáng Hall,
and granted degrees to fifty-five people, starting with Xíng Péngnián.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Jiǎchén,
prisoners were reviewed.
On Yǐsì,
Túntǔgǔsī, the chieftain of the Zǔbǔ, came to court.
On Wùshēn,
the Emperor went to Hēilǐng.
In the ninth month, on Dīngwèi,
the imperial procession stopped at Píngdiàn.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day (xuò), Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor crossed the Liáohé River.
On Bǐngyín,
the imperial procession stopped at Báimǎdiàn.
On Rénshēn,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the eleventh month, on the first day (xuò), Guǐsì.
Yēlǜ Yuánfāng, Zhāng Ní, Hán Zhìdé, and Xiāo Fù were appointed as envoys and deputies to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday and the New Year (Zhèngdàn).
On Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor inquired after the health of the Empress Dowager,
and presented precious curios.
On Gēngshēn,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the twelfth month,
several dozen skilled polo players were summoned to Dōngjīng,
and commanded to compete against high officials;
the Emperor personally observed the event.
On Jǐsì,
the Imperial Younger Brother, Chóngyuán, was appointed Acting Commissioner of Military Affairs of both Northern and Southern Chancellery (Pàn Běi Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì).
Sābānìng, Chancellor of the Northern Administration, was reinstated, concurrently supervising Dōngjīng Prefecture;
Yēlǜ Yīngwěn was made Chancellor of the Southern Administration;
Zhāgēzhé was made Imperial Tìyǐn;
Xiāo Hàn of the Yǐshìyǐ Tribe was made Jìedùshǐ of Qiánzhōu;
Liú Liùfú was made Advisor to the Government (Cānzhī Zhèngshì);
Guàngē of the Imperial Clan Tribe was made Xiāngwěn of the Imperial Clan Gentry Guard;
Chújiǒng, the Great King, was made Jìedùshǐ of Píngzhōu;
Zhāng Kègōng, the Chief Minister, was made acting Minister of Works (Sīkōng);
Hán Shàofāng, the Chief Minister, was given the additional title of Grand Counselor (Shìzhōng);
Yēlǜ Mǎliù, the Tìyǐn, was made Commissioner of Palace Affairs of the Northern Chancellery (Běiyuàn Xuānhuīshǐ);
and Yēlǜ Xǐsūn, the Tutor (Fùfù), was made Chancellor of the Southern Administration.
On Guǐwèi,
Sòng sent Wáng Jǔzhèng and Zhāng Shìyǔ to offer congratulations on the Yǒngshòu Festival.
On Jiǎshēn,
an order was given to present wine daily at the Dà'ān Palace
and offer sacrifices at Qìnglíng.
On Dīnghài,
prisoners were reviewed.
Those who had committed unintentional homicide had their penalties reduced.
Zhuànggǔlǐ, an Attendant Censor of the Southern Circuit, fraudulently acquired Jurchen tribute goods
and was sentenced to death;
however, because the Emperor recognized his administrative ability,
he was branded and exiled.
In the spring of the eighth year, the first month, on the first day (xuò), Rénchén,
Sòng sent Hán Qí and Wáng Cóngyì to offer congratulations.
On Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor went to the Hùntóng River to observe fishing.
On Wùxū,
the Pǐnbù Department was reorganized.
On Gēngxū,
fish were speared in the Shuàimòlǐ River.
On Dīngsì,
Sùzhōu was prohibited from selling sheep to Sòng.
In the second month, on Bǐngzǐ,
the imperial procession stopped at the Chángchūn River.
In summer, the sixth month, on Yǐchǒu,
an edict was issued to register households and population.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Dīngsì,
the Emperor visited Qìnglíng,
offering sacrifices at the Wàngxiān Hall;
the Empress Dowager was welcomed to Xiǎnzhōu,
where she visited the mausoleum,
and then returned to the capital.
In winter, the tenth month,
the imperial procession stopped at Dōngjīng.
In the eleventh month, on Jiǎwǔ,
an edict stated that anyone who claimed the Northern Chancellery handled affairs unfairly,
by striking the bell or stopping the imperial carriage to make an accusation,
should have their case fully reported to the throne.
On Wùxū,
the Emperor paid respects to the Empress Dowager,
and summoned monks to discuss Buddhist doctrine.
On Wùshēn,
the Empress Dowager performed the Rebirth Ceremony (Zàishēng Lǐ),
and a general amnesty was granted.
On Jǐyǒu,
Chángchūn was walled.
In the intercalary twelfth month, on Rénchén,
the Emperor checked on the illness of Xiāo Xiàomù, Prince of Wúguó.
Sòng sent Páng Jí and Dù Zàn to offer congratulations on the Yǒngshòu Festival.
In the spring of the ninth year, the first month, on the first day (xuò), Bǐngchén,
the Emperor presented wine at the Palace of the Empress Dowager,
and presided over the Main Hall (Zhèngdiàn).
Sòng sent Wáng Gǒngchén and Péng Zàisī to offer congratulations.
On Gēngshēn,
the Emperor went to the Yāzǐ River.
In the second month,
the imperial procession stopped at Yú'ér Lake (Yú'érluò).
In the third month, on Xīnwèi,
due to the Yìngshèng Festival,
a general amnesty was granted.
In the fifth month, on the first day (xuò), Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor avoided the heat at Yǒng'ān Mountain.
In the sixth month,
willow-shooting was performed to pray for rain.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Guǐyǒu,
Sòng sent Guō Zhēn to report on the punitive expedition against Xià,
and Commissioner of Military Affairs Dù Fáng was sent in return.
On Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor went to Qiūshān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day (xuò), Guǐwèi,
the imperial procession stopped at Zhōnghuì River (Zhōnghuìchuān).
In the eleventh month, on Jiǎzǐ,
the Jurchen (Nǚzhí) invaded the border.
Troops from the Tiělí Army of Huánglóng Prefecture were dispatched to resist them.
Sòng sent Sū Shēn and Xiàng Chuánfàn to congratulate them on the Yìngshèng Festival.
In the twelfth month, on Gēngyín,
the Gentry Guard of the Bùwěizhàng (Bùwěizhàng Lángjūn) of the Northern Great King's Residence declared that his ancestors had intermarried with the imperial family.
Permission was granted to establish the position of Chǎngshǐ (Registrar),
and Xiāo Húdǔ of that tribe was appointed to the post.
On Xīnmǎo,
the Jurchen households captured were used to establish Sùzhōu.

Xiāo Dí, Liú Sāngǔ, Yēlǜ Yuánfāng, Wáng Wéijí, Yēlǜ Shùzhōng, Sūn Wénzhāo, Xiāo Shàoyún, and Qín Déchāng were appointed as envoys and deputies to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday and the New Year (Zhèngdàn) of the coming year.
An edict prohibited
all those who had committed crimes from becoming officials.
All officials, unless for weddings or sacrifices,
were forbidden from heavy drinking that caused them to neglect their duties.
Anyone who possessed strategies for governing the people and securing the borders
was to report them fully to the throne.
Basic Annals 19: Xīngzōng II
In the spring of the tenth year, the first month, on the first day (xuò), Xīnhài,
Sòng sent Liáng Shì, Zhāng Cóngyī, Fù Bì, and Zhào Rìxuān to offer congratulations.
On Jiǎzǐ,
Wú Yù and Féng Dài were again sent to congratulate on the Yǒngshòu Festival.
In the second month, on the first day (xuò), Gēngchén,
an edict ordered that the confiscated households of the Hésūguǎn Tribe, belonging to the Púlú Máochū Tribe, be returned to their former occupations.
On Jiǎshēn,
the Northern Chancellery reported:
The Gentry Guard (Zhīhòu Lángjūn) of the Military Commissions (Jìedù Shìwèi) of the Northern and Southern Princely Residences and various tribes,
all originate from noble clans (Zúzhàng).
Since they are already exempt from border duty alongside commoners,
they requested that for their guard duties,
they also be permitted to use their retainers (Bùqǔ) to perform the service in their stead.
An edict was issued granting their request.
In the fourth month of summer,
an edict ordered the cessation of the project to repair the floating bridge over the Yālù Jiāng and the duties of the Hàn soldiers stationed there.
Furthermore, based on the words of Xiāo Sāba, the Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner) of Dōngjīng,
the ban on *jījú* (polo) in Dōngjīng was lifted.
On the first day of the sixth month, *wùyín* (55),
Xiāo Níng, Yēlǜ Tǎn, Cuī Yǔchēng, Mǎ Shìliáng, Yēlǜ Rénxiān, and Liú Liùfú were appointed as envoys and deputy envoys to offer congratulations on the Sòng Emperor's birthday;
Yēlǜ Shùchéng, Zhào Chéng, Yēlǜ Liè, and Zhāng Dàn were appointed as envoys and deputy envoys to offer congratulations on the Sòng New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn) the following year.
In the seventh month of autumn, on *rénxū* (59),
an edict stated that all officials who privately took state property,
should be judged as committing serious theft.
Anyone who dared to bring accusations regarding matters already settled by the previous court (Xiāncháo),
should be punished.
If various Zhàng Lángjūn and their peers shot deer in prohibited areas,
they would be beaten three hundred strokes,
and no compensation would be sought.
Xiǎo Jiāngjūn (Minor Generals) would receive two hundred strokes or fewer;
If common people committed the offense,
their punishment would be judged the same as the Lángjūn.
In the eighth month, on *bǐngxū* (23),
because the physician Dèng Yánzhēn had successfully treated the illness of the Xiángwěn Xiāo Liúníng,
official titles were posthumously granted to his parents as an award.
In the ninth month, on *xīnhài* (48),
the Emperor paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu (Empress Dowager).
The Guójiù (Imperial Uncle) Liúníng died.
On *gēngshēn* (57),
the Huáng Tàihòu shot and captured a bear,
and the Emperor offered wine for her longevity.
On *guǐhài* (60),
the Emperor hunted on Mǎyú Shān.
Because the vegetation was thick and dense,
fearing that hunters might accidentally shoot and injure people,
he ordered Yēlǜ Dígū to have everyone write their names on their arrows to mark them.
On *bǐngyín* (3),
the Xià state presented captives taken from the Sòng.
Guō Sān, the Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) of Shíyìng Zhài (Stone Hard Stockade), was dismissed from office
because he retreated from a tiger without shooting it.
In the tenth month of winter, on *bǐngxū* (23),
an edict ordered Xiāo Xiàozhōng, the Liúshǒu of Dōngjīng, to observe officials who were honest, capable, clean, and vigorous,
and report their names in detail.
On *gēngyín* (27),
Tái Yā, the Tàishī (Grand Preceptor) of the Nǚzhí, was appointed as the Dū Dàwáng (Great King of the Metropolis) of Hésū Guǎn.
On *xīnmǎo* (28),
because the Imperial Prince Húlúwòlǐ was born,
Sābaníng, the Chancellor of the North and Fùmǎ (Son-in-law of the Emperor), welcomed the Emperor to his residence for a banquet,
and the Emperor ordered his imperial guards to engage in wrestling (*jiǎodǐ*) with Hàn people for entertainment.
On *rénchén* (29),
they again drank at the Huáng Tàihòu's palace hall,
and because of the birth of the Imperial Prince,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the evening,
the Emperor again brought in princesses, imperial sons-in-law, and ministerial officials of the inner clan into the private sleeping chamber for heavy drinking.
On *jiǎwǔ* (31),
the Emperor visited Zhōngjīng.
On *gēngzǐ* (37),
Xiāo Hūliè, the Fùmǎ Dūwèi (Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law), was appointed Guójiù Xiángwěn.
In the eleventh month, on *bǐngchén* (53),
the Huíhú (Uyghurs) dispatched envoys to present tribute.
On the first day of the twelfth month, *bǐngzǐ* (13),
the Sòng dispatched Liú Hàng and Wáng Zhěng to offer congratulations on the Yìngshèng Jié (Imperial Birthday).
On *yǐwèi* (32),
Chiefs of the Tàzhúbùgū were established.
Hú Tàlá was appointed Píngzhāng Shì (Administrator).
The Emperor, hearing that the Sòng had established border barriers and rivers,
and constructed trenches,
feared they might cause border trouble.

He consulted with the Nan and Bei Shūmì (Chief Military Commissioners), the King of Wú, Xiāo Xiàomù, and the King of Zhào, Xiāo Guànníng, about reclaiming the ten counties south of the pass (Guānnán) previously ceded by the Sòng.
Consequently, he sent Xiāo Yīng and Liú Liùfú as envoys to the Sòng.
On *gēngyín* (27),

the Sòng dispatched Zhāng Miǎn, Hóu Zōngliàng, Xuē Shēn, Shìqí Jùn, Shī Chāngyán, and Pān Yǒngzhào to offer congratulations on the Yǒngshòu Jié (Longevity Festival) and the upcoming New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn).
Yáng Jí, Academician of the Xuānzhèng Diàn, was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū) and acting Jìdùshǐ (Regional Military Governor) of the Shùnyì Army.
On *dīngyǒu* (34),
a discussion was held regarding the punitive expedition against the Sòng,
and an edict was issued to instruct the various circuits (Zhū Dào).
In the first month of spring of the eleventh year, on *wùshēn* (45),
the Huáng Tàihòu was welcomed to the inner palace hall.
On *gēngxū* (47),
Xiāo Tèmò, the Commissioner of the Southern Chancery (Nányuàn Xuānhuīshǐ), and Liú Liùfú, Academician of the Hanlin, were sent as envoys to the Sòng,
to demand the return of Jìnyáng and the ten counties south of Wǎqiáo.
They were also to inquire about the Sòng raising troops to attack Xià, the dredging of swamps along the border,
and the reason for increasing garrison troops.
In the second month, on *rényín* (39),
the Emperor traveled to Yuānyang Luò.
On the first day of the fourth month of summer, *jiǎxū* (11),
the regulations for rewards and punishments for the Southern Expedition were promulgated.
In the sixth month, on *yǐhài* (12),
the Sòng dispatched Fù Bì and Zhāng Màoshí carrying a letter to establish friendly relations,
and the Emperor replied to them with a letter.
On *rénwǔ* (19),
the Emperor held court at the Hánliáng Diàn,
and conferred the *Jìnshì* degree upon Wáng Shí and sixty-three others.
The sale of felt and silver into Sòng territory was prohibited.
On the first day of the seventh month of autumn, *rényín* (39),
an edict stated that those who stole and exchanged official horses would have their capital punishment reduced.
Officials in external circuits (Wàilù) who were diligent, exhausted, and upright,
would be replaced upon completion of their term evaluation;
those who failed to manage their duties would be replaced immediately.
In the eighth month, on *bǐngshēn* (33),
the Sòng again dispatched Fù Bì and Zhāng Màoshí carrying a letter to establish friendly relations,
requesting an increase in the annual payment of silver and silk.
The Emperor replied to them with a letter.
In the ninth month, on *rényín* (39),
Yēlǜ Rénxiān, Vice Commissioner of the Northern Shūmì Yuàn, and Liú Liùfú, Deputy Director of the Hàn People’s Traveling Palace, were sent as envoys to the Sòng to negotiate peace.
At this time,
Fù Bì had spoken to the Emperor,
stating that the general meaning was: if Liáo made peace with Sòng,
and passively received the annual payment,
the benefit would accrue to the state (Guójiā),
and the officials would gain nothing;
if Liáo engaged in conflict with Sòng,
the benefit would accrue to the officials,
but the state would suffer harm.
The Emperor was moved by his words,
and friendly relations were finally established.
In the intercalary month, on *guǐwèi* (20),
Yēlǜ Rénxiān sent a messenger to report
that the Sòng would annually increase the silver and silk payment by one hundred thousand *liǎng* and pieces,
and the documents would refer to it as
“tribute” (*gòng*),
delivered to Báigōu.
The Emperor was delighted,
and hosted a banquet for the assembled officials at the Zhāoqìng Diàn.
On that day,
relief was given to the poor among the Sānfù Clans.
On *xīnmǎo* (28),
Rénxiān and Liú Liùfú returned,
and presented the Sòng state's sworn covenant.
In the eleventh month of winter, on *dīnghài* (24),

the assembled officials conferred the honorific title: Cōngwén Shèngwǔ Yīnglüè Shéngōng Ruìzhé Rénxiào Huángdì (The Wise and Cultivated, Sagely and Martial, Heroic and Strategic, Spiritually Meritorious, Enlightened and Judicious, Benevolent and Filial Emperor).
Empress Xiāo was formally invested with the title Zhēnyì Xuāncí Chóngshèng Huánghòu (The Chaste and Righteous, Manifestly Kind, Highly Sacred Empress).
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
Hóngjī, the Prince of Liáng, was promoted in rank to King of Yān.
In the twelfth month, on *guǐmǎo* (40),
the Emperor paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
On *jiǎchén* (41),
Nièlǔgǔ, the son of the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Āndìng Commandery.
On *jǐyǒu* (46),
because it was the anniversary of the death of Empress Xuānxiàn,
the Emperor and the Huáng Tàihòu wore simple attire,
and fed monks at the three monasteries: Yánshòu, Mǐnzhōng, and Sānxué.
On *xīnhài* (48),
an edict exempted the taxes and rents of all tribes that had prepared for the punitive expedition against the Sòng for one year.
On *rénzǐ* (49),
because the Tǔhún and Dǎngxiàng frequently sold horses to the Xià state,
an edict was issued to strengthen border defenses.
On *jǐwèi* (56),
when the Sòng envoys for the New Year (Zhèngdàn) and the Yǒngshòu Jié were residing in the guesthouse,
the Emperor went in plain clothes to observe them.
On *dīngmǎo* (4),
The killing of oxen and horses and the burying of treasures during funeral rites were prohibited.
In the first month of spring of the twelfth year, on *xīnwèi* (8),

Yēlǜ Díliè, Concurrent Administrator of Xījīn Fǔ, and Wáng Wéijí, Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Shūmì Yuàn Dū Chéngzhǐ), were sent to instruct the Xià state to make peace with the Sòng.
On *rénshēn* (9),
Xiāo Xiàomù, King of Wú, was appointed Chief Military Commissioner of the Southern Bureau (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ).
Xiāo Xiàozhōng, Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng), was appointed Chief Military Commissioner of the Northern Bureau (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ);
he was enfeoffed as the King of Chǔ.
Xiāo Huì, King of Hán, was appointed Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture and Concurrent Administrator of the Field Marshal's Office (Yuánshuàifǔ Shì).
Hán Bā was appointed Great King of the Southern Bureau (Nányuàn Dàwáng).
Yēlǜ Hóushěn was appointed Resident Commissioner of Dōngjīng (Dōngjīng Liúshǒu).
Yēlǜ Rénxiān, Vice Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Concurrent Administrator of Dōngjīng Liúshǒu Affairs.
Xiāo Gé, Běimiàn Línyá (Northern Director of Writing), was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
On *jiǎxū* (11),
the Emperor traveled to the reed marshes of Wǔqīng Zhài.
In the second month, on *rényín* (39),
Hàn civilians south of the pass (Guānnán) were forbidden to possess bows and arrows.
On *jǐyǒu* (46),
the Xià state, because of the conferring of the honorific title (on the Emperor),
dispatched envoys to offer congratulations.
On *jiǎyín* (51),
Yēlǜ Díliè and his colleagues returned from their mission to the Xià state,
reporting that Yuánhào had ceased military operations,
and envoys were immediately sent to inform the Sòng.
In the third month, on *xīnmǎo* (58),
the Emperor visited Nánjīng.
On *rénchén* (59),
the state of Gāolì, because of the conferring of the honorific title,
dispatched envoys to offer congratulations.
In the fourth month of summer, on *jǐhài* (36),
Xiángwěn and Dūjiān (Military Inspectors) were established for the Huíbá tribe.
On *gēngzǐ* (37),
the Xià state dispatched envoys to present horses and camels.
In the fifth month, on *xīnmǎo* (58),
two envoys from the Wòlǔ and Púlú Máozēng tribes arrived late with their tribute,
but they were pardoned and sent back.
On *yǐwèi* (32),
an edict was issued to re-establish and fix the regulations concerning rites.
In this month,
the Emperor visited Shānxī.
In the sixth month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
an edict allowed families belonging to the established lineages of Zǎixiàng (Chancellors) and Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioners), and families where the head was currently a Jiédùshǐ,
to use silver utensils for funerals;
simultaneously prohibiting the slaughter of animals for sacrifice.
On the gēngxū day,
an edict decreed that if Hànrén (Han people) Gōngfēn households died out without heirs (hùjué),
their permanent property (héngchǎn) should be inherited by their relatives (qīnzú).
On the xīnhài day,
Sāgélǐ (撒葛里), the Tàiwèi (Grand Commandant) and younger brother of the Zhǔbǔ (Zǔbǔ) Dàwáng (Great King) Tún Tūgǔsī (屯禿古斯), came to court.
On the bǐngchén day,
Huíhú (Uygurs) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
Xiāo Xiàomù (蕭孝穆), the Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ (Southern Chancellery Commissioner) and King of Wú (Wúguówáng), was made Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ (Northern Chancellery Commissioner),
and his title was changed to King of Qí (Qíguówáng).
Autumn, 7th month, on the bǐngyín day (the first day of the month),
the Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Xiāo Xiàozhōng (蕭孝忠) died (hōng);
a special pardon was issued for prisoners.
On the gēngyín day,
Xiàguó (Xixia) sent envoys presenting a memorial,
requesting (Liao) attack Sòng (Song dynasty).
This was not followed.
8th month, on the bǐngshēn day,
(the Emperor) visited Qìnglíng (Qìng Mausoleum).
On the xīnchǒu day,
Hóngjī (洪基), the King of Yān (Yānguówáng), was additionally appointed Shàngshū Lìng (Director of the Department of State Affairs),
took charge of the affairs of the Northern and Southern Chancellery Commissioners,
and was promoted to King of Yān and Zhào (Yānzhàoguówáng).
On the wùwǔ day,
Xiāo Tǎliègé (蕭塔烈葛), formerly the Xīběilù Zhāotǎoshǐ (Northwestern Circuit Pacification Commissioner), was appointed Yòu Yílíbì (Right Yílíbì).
On the gēngshēn day,
Yúyuè Yēlǜ Hónggǔ (耶律洪古) died (hōng).
On the jiǎzǐ day,
Zhǔbǔ (Zǔbǔ) came to offer tribute.
9th month, on the rénshēn day,
(the Emperor) paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu (Empress Dowager),
and visited Wàngxiāndiàn (Wàngxiān Palace Hall).
On the rénwǔ day,
(the Emperor) visited Huáiling (Huái Mausoleum).
Winter, 10th month, on the dīngyǒu day,
the imperial procession stopped at Zhōnghuìchuān (Zhōnghuì River).
On the jǐhài day,
the Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Xiāo Xiàomù (蕭孝穆) died (hōng),
and was posthumously granted the titles Dà Chéngxiàng (Grand Chancellor) and King of Jìn (Jìnguówáng).
On the gēngzǐ day,
an edict ordered officials be sent
to thoroughly review the cases of severe prisoners in all circuits.
On the xīnhài day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Policy Advisor) Hán Shàofāng (韓紹芳) was made Guǎngdéjūn Jiédùshǐ (Guǎngdé Army Military Commissioner),
and Sānsīshǐ (Commissioner of Finance) Liú Liùfú (劉六符) was made Chángníngjūn Jiédùshǐ (Chángníng Army Military Commissioner).
On the rénzǐ day,
because the Xià people (Xixia) had invaded the Dǎngxiàng (Tangut) tribes,
Yánchāng Gōngshǐ (Palace Commissioner of Yánchāng) Gāo Jiānú (高家奴) was sent to admonish them.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
Běifǔ Zǎixiàng (Northern Administration Chancellor) Xiāo Huì (蕭惠) was made Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ,
the King of Bīn (Bīngwáng) Suìgē (遂哥) was made Tìyǐn,
the Tìyǐn Díluǔgǔ (敵魯古) was enfeoffed as Lord of Qīshuǐ Commandery (Qīshuǐ Jùnwáng) and Xīběilù Zhāotǎoshǐ (Northwestern Circuit Pacification Commissioner),
and Shūmì Fùshǐ (Vice Commissioner of the Chancellery) Xiāo Ālà (蕭阿剌) was appointed Concurrent Administrator of Northern Chancellery Palace Affairs.
Fēilóng (Flying Dragon) horses were brought out,
and distributed as gifts to the various ministers.
11th month, on the dīngchǒu day,
Xiāo Xiàozhōng (蕭孝忠), the Prince of Chǔ (Chǔwáng), was posthumously elevated to King of Chǔ (Chǔguówáng).
On the dīnghài day,
because the harvests were poor in Shàngjīng (Supreme Capital),
the rent and taxes for its people were remitted.
On the guǐsì day,
(the Emperor) paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
12th month, on the wùshēn day,
the Zhèngshì Shěng (Department of State Affairs) was renamed the Zhōngshū Shěng (Chancellery).
13th year, Spring, 1st month, on the jiǎzǐ day (the first day of the month),
(the Emperor) paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
On the wùchén day,
(the Emperor) went to Hùntóngjiāng (Hùntóng River).
On the xīnwèi day,
(the Emperor) hunted at Wūlǔguǎngāng (Wūlǔguān Hill).
2nd month, on the gēngxū day,
(the Emperor) went to Yúérluò (Yú'ér Lake).
On the bǐngchén day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Dù Fáng (杜防) was made Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng (Southern Administration Chancellor).
3rd month, on the dīnghài day,
Gāolì (Goryeo) sent envoys to offer tribute.
Xuānzhèngdiàn Xuéshì (Scholar of the Xuānzhèng Hall) Yáng Jí (楊佶) was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In this month,
the Qìdān Jǐngxúnyuàn (Qìdān Security and Patrol Office) was established.
Summer, 4th month, on the jǐyǒu day,

Yēlǜ Hóushěn (耶律侯哂), the Dōngjīng Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner of the Eastern Capital), and Yēlǜ Ōulǐsī (耶律歐里斯), the Administrator of Huánglóng Fǔ (Huánglóng Prefecture), were dispatched to lead troops to attack the Púlú Máojiǎnbù (Púlú Máojiǎn tribe).
On the jiǎyín day,
Nányuàn Dàwáng (Great King of the Southern Chancellery) Yēlǜ Gāoshí (耶律高十) reported that the Dǎngxiàng and other tribes had rebelled and defected to Xiàguó (Xixia).
On the bǐngchén day,
Luóhànnú (羅漢奴), the Xīnánmiàn Zhāotǎo Dūjiān (Director-General of Pacification and Mobilization of the Southwestern Front), and Xiángwěn Wòlǔmǔ (斡魯母) and others reported that
Qūliè (屈烈), the Shānxī Bùzú Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioner of the Shānxī Tribes), had defected to Xīxià (Western Xià) with five tribes,
and requested that troops from the Northern and Southern Administrations be sent to reinforce and settle the households of Wēisàizhōu (Wēisài Prefecture).
An edict ordered that the wealthy among them should be sent off,
while the rest should remain to form military colonies at Tiāndéjūn (Tiāndé Army).
5th month, on the rénxū day (the first day of the month),
Luóhànnú reported that the tribal troops that had been mobilized fought unsuccessfully against the Dǎngxiàng;
Zhāotǎoshǐ Xiāo Pǔdá (蕭普達) and Sijiejūn Xiángwěn (Xiángwěn of the Four Victory Army) Zhāng Fónú (張佛奴) died in battle.
Lǐ Yuánhào (李元昊) came to reinforce the rebel faction.
On the wùchén day,
an edict ordered the mobilization of troops from all circuits to assemble on the southwestern border to suppress Yuánhào.
6th month, on the jiǎwǔ day,
Wūbā (烏八), the chieftain of Zhǔbǔ (Zǔbǔ), sent his son, who had captured Wāyìgǎi (窊邑改), the envoy sent by Yuánhào to request aid,
and requested to use his troops to assist in the war.
This was granted.
The imperial procession stopped at Yǒng'ānshān (Yǒng'ān Mountain).
Since (Liao) was about to attack Xià (Xixia),
Yēlǜ Gāojiānú (耶律高家奴), the Yánchāng Gōngshǐ, was sent to inform Sòng.
On the bǐngshēn day,

an edict ordered former Nányuàn Dàwáng Yēlǜ Gǔyù (耶律谷欲) and Hànlín Dū Línyá (Chief Scholar of the Hànlín Academy) Yēlǜ Shùchéng (耶律庶成) and others to compile the history of the achievements of the Dynasty since its founding generations.
On the bǐngwǔ day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the dīngwèi day,
prisoners were reviewed.
Autumn, 7th month, on the xīnyǒu day,
Lǐ Yí'ér (李宜兒), a commoner of Xiānghé Xiàn (Xiānghé County), confused the masses with heterodox teachings,
and was executed.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the Ceremony of Rebirth was performed.
On the gēngchén day,
Xiàguó sent envoys to court.
8th month, on the yǐwèi day,
because the Xià envoy's answers were insincere,
he was detained.
On the dīngsì day,
Xiàguó sent another envoy,
who was questioned about the situation.
Since he again did not answer truthfully,
he was flogged.
9th month, on the wùchén day,
Sòng, regarding the upcoming personal campaign against Xiàguó,
sent Yú Jìng (余靖) to deliver farewell gifts.
On the rénshēn day,
the main army assembled at Jiǔshíjiǔ Quán (Ninety-Nine Springs).
Huáng Tàidì (Imperial Younger Brother Heir Apparent) Chóngyuán (重元) and Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ, King of Hán (Hánguówáng), Xiāo Huì (蕭惠) were appointed to lead the vanguard troops on the western campaign.
Winter, 10th month, on the gēngyín day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
On the bǐngshēn day,
Dǎngxiàng scouts were captured,
and an archery ritual was performed.
On the dīngyǒu day,
Lǐ Yuánhào presented a memorial apologizing for his offense.
On the jǐhài day,
Yuánhào sent envoys to report
that he wished to capture the rebel faction and present them (to the Liao court).
This was permitted.
On the xīnhài day,
Yuánhào sent envoys to present local products.
An edict ordered Běiyuàn Shūmì Fùshǐ (Vice Commissioner of the Northern Chancellery) Xiāo Gé (蕭革) to receive them.
On the rénzǐ day,
the army encamped at Héqu (River Bend).
Gé reported that Yuánhào had personally led three Dǎngxiàng tribes to arrive.
An edict ordered Gé to reproach him for harboring rebels and violating the treaty.
Yuánhào submitted to the charge,
was granted wine,
was permitted to reform himself,
and was sent away.
The various ministers were summoned for deliberation;
all considered that since the main army was already assembled,
a punitive expedition should be launched.
On the guǐchǒu day,
troops from several routes were commanded to launch a surprise attack,
killing several thousand people.
Fùmǎ Dūwèi (Cavalry Commandant and Imperial Son-in-Law) Xiāo Húdǔ (蕭胡覩) was captured by the Xià people.
On the dīngsì day,
Yuánhào sent envoys to return those previously captured.
An edict ordered that the detained Xià envoys also be returned to their country.
11th month, on the xīnyǒu day,
meritorious officers and commanders were granted rewards according to their rank.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
the army returned to the capital.
On the dīngmǎo day,
Yúnzhōu (Yún Prefecture) was renamed Xījīng (Western Capital).
On the xīnsì day,
(the Emperor) paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
12th month, on the jǐchǒu day,
(the Emperor) proceeded to Xījīng.
On the wùxū day,
Yēlǜ Díliè (耶律敵烈), the Běiyuàn Shūmì Fùshǐ, was appointed Yòu Yílíbì.
On the jǐhài day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the wùshēn day,
Xiāo Húdǔ returned from Xià.
14th year, Spring, 1st month, on the gēngshēn day,
Shìzhōng (Palace Attendant) Xiāo Xūliè (蕭虛烈) was appointed Nányuàn Tǒngjūnshǐ (Commander of the Southern Chancellery),
and was enfeoffed as Lord of Liáoxī Commandery (Liáoxī Jùnwáng).
On the gēngwǔ day,
(the Emperor) went to Yuānyāngluò (Yuānyāng Lake).
On the rénwǔ day,
Díluǔgǔ (敵魯古), the Jīnwú Wèi Dà Jiāngjūn (Grand General of the Jinwu Guard), was appointed Yǐshì Dàwáng (Great King of the Yǐshì).
On the jiǎshēn day,
Xiàguó sent envoys to present gyrfalcons (hú).
Since Chángshì (Attendant Counselor) Wògǔdé (斡古得) had died in battle,
his son Xíluō (習羅) was appointed commander.
2nd month, on the gēngzǐ day,
(the Emperor) paid respects to the Huáng Tàihòu.
The imperial procession stopped at Sǎlàluò (Sǎlà Lake).
3rd month, on the jǐmǎo day,
Sòng sent envoys to offer congratulations
because the army that attacked Xià had returned.
In the fourth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
(He) spent the summer at Yǒng'ān Shān.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
(He) visited the Qìng Líng (tomb).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
The Great King of Zǔbǔ, Tún Tūgǔsī, led the various chieftains to court.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Xià Guó sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Since Xiāo Pǔdá, the Commissioner of Pacification for the Southwest Circuit, had died in battle,
He was posthumously granted the title of *Tóng Zhōngshū Ménxià Píngzhāngshì*.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùshēn* day,
The imperial temporary residence was established at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
The *wàng* sacrifice was performed at Mùyè Shān.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénwǔ* day (the first day of the month),
The Uighur Āsàlán sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Xiāo Ālà, the Associate Administrator of the Northern Palace Affairs, was appointed Northern Chancellor (*Běifǔ Zǎixiàng*).
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
(He) observed the Hàn troops practicing cannon fire, shooting, and stabbing.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Delayed lawsuits were judged.
In the fifteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
(He) went to the Hùntóng Jiāng.
The Qìdān were forbidden from selling slaves to the Hàn people.
In the second month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
(He) went to the Chángchūn Hé.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Households from the Púlú Máowǔ boundary of the Hélǎn Hé came to submit,
and an imperial edict commanded that they be placated.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
(He) paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
In celebration of the Emperor’s birthday (*Shèng Jié*),
death sentences were reduced,
and those serving penal servitude and lesser sentences were released.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
(He) paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
An edict commanded that all circuits annually report on lawsuits and prisons.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnhài* day (the first day of the month),
Officials and common people in the Five Capitals were forbidden from playing *jījú* (polo).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
The garrison troops of the Yáoniǎn *Zhàng* were dismissed.
On the *rénxū* day,
Xiāo Gāoliù, the Commissioner of the Northern Nǚzhí, was appointed Great King of the Six Xī Tribes.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
(He) spent the summer at Yǒng'ān Shān.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
180 households from the Púlú Máowǔ Hélǎn Hé submitted.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Mǎliù, the Defense Commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Hàn People’s Traveling Palace (*Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ*);
Yáng Jí, the Associate Administrator, was sent out to be the Military Governor of Wǔdìng Jūn.
On the *wùchén* day,
(He) attended the Qīngliáng Diàn,
and released 68 *jìnshì* (advanced scholars), including Wáng Táng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yēlǜ Dí lǔgǔ, the Commissioner of Pacification for the Northwest Circuit, was stripped of his office for corruption.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Suìgē, Prince of Bīn, passed away.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
(He) observed the harvest.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zú Fén, the Commissioner of Northern Palace Affairs, was appointed Chief Justice of the Left (*Zuǒ Yílíbì*);
and Yēlǜ Xǐsūn, the former Southern Chancellor (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*), was appointed Commissioner of the Northeast Circuit.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Troops from all circuits were registered.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
(He) went to Qiū Shān.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
The retinues were prohibited from trampling the people's fields.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Because Zhēmǔ, the chieftain of the Nǚzhí, led his people to submit,
he was promoted to Grand Preceptor (*Tàishī*).
In the eighth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Qīn, the King of Gāolì, passed away,
and sent envoys to report (the death).
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
The use of snares and nets to catch foxes and rabbits was prohibited.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
The imperial temporary residence was established at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Xiāo Xiàoyǒu, the Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Southern Chancellery, was appointed Northern Chancellor (*Běifǔ Zǎixiàng*);
Yēlǜ Rénxiān, the Commander-in-Chief of the Qìdān Traveling Palace, was appointed Great King of the Southern Chancellery;
Xiāo Gé, the Northern Chancellor, was appointed Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs for the Northern Chancellery;
Yēlǜ Xìnxiān, Administrator of Justice, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Hàn People’s Traveling Palace;
Lǚ Fén, the Chief Justice of the Left, was appointed *Tìyǐn*;
and Yēlǜ Díliè, the Commander-in-Chief of the Hàn People’s Traveling Palace, was appointed Chief Justice of the Left.
On the *jǐhài* day,
The Bóhǎi tribal division used the census standard of Qìdān households to generally count military horses.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Relief was distributed to the poor people of the Southern Capital (*Nánjīng*).
In the twelfth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
A partial amnesty was granted for crimes involving penal servitude and lesser sentences.
This day was the birthday of Shèngzōng when he was alive.
Basic Annals, Volume 20: Xīngzōng 3
In the sixteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
(He) went to the Hùntóng Jiāng.
In the second month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
(He) went to the Yú'ér Luò.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Officials were prohibited from presenting private requests during banquets and celebrations.
An edict commanded that hereditary offices,
should be filled by selecting competent individuals from among the elders of the various tribes.
In the third month, on the *dīnghài* day,
(He) went to the Hēishuǐ Luò.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Envoys were dispatched to review and decide cases for prisoners in Shuāng Zhōu.
On the *rényín* day,
There was heavy snow.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐsì* day (the first day of the month),
The Empress Dowager was unwell,
and the Emperor quickly went to examine her illness.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
The Empress Dowager recovered,
and (the Emperor) returned to Hēishuǐ Luò.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the sixth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
(He) spent the summer at Yǒng'ān Shān.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Tún Tūgǔsī, the Great King of Zǔbǔ, came to court,
and presented local products.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
An edict commanded that scholars and common people submit memorials regarding affairs (of state).
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
(The Emperor) visited Qìng Zhōu.
From this month until the ninth month,
(He) hunted daily in the mountains of Chǔbùgōu Xiáliè, Jìlún, and Shítǎ.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
(He) visited the Central Capital (*Zhōngjīng*) and paid respects at the Ancestral Temple.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
The ritual procedures for princesses performing marriage rites for their parents-in-law (*jiùgū*) were established.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Tiělí Xiānmén came to court.
As it was the first time they offered tribute,
(He) was granted the title Grand General of the Right Inspectorate Guards (*Yòu Jiānmén Wèi Dàjiāngjūn*).
In the eleventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
A sacrifice was offered at Mùyè Shān.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
(He) visited the Central Capital (*Zhōngjīng*),
and paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
On the *rénchén* day,
The leaking of palace affairs was prohibited.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day (the first day of the month),
The Nǚzhí sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *xīnhài* day,
(He) visited the temple of Tàizǔ,
and observed the depiction of Tàizōng conquering Jìn.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
(He) inquired about the Empress Dowager's health.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Because the Empress Dowager had recovered,
capital crimes of various offenses were reduced by one degree in sentencing,
and those sentenced to penal servitude and lesser sentences were pardoned.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Dù Fáng and Hán Shàoróng, the Southern Chancellors, made errors in reporting affairs,
and were each punished with heavy caning.
Dù Fáng was sent out to be the Military Governor of Wǔdìng Jūn.
On the *rénxū* day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the seventeenth year, spring, the first month, on the *dīnghài* day,
(He) went to the Spring Waters (*Chūnshuǐ*).
In the intercalary month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
(He) hunted tigers at Hòulǐjí.
In the second month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Relief was distributed to the Yáowěn and Cháowěn divisions.
In this month,
an edict commanded that scholars and common people, when discussing state benefits,
must not mention their own affairs;
what slaves and maidservants saw,
they were permitted to inform their masters,
but they were not allowed to report directly (to the court).
Lǐ Yuánhào, the King of Xià Guó, passed away.
His son, Liàngzuò, sent envoys to report (the death).

(The Emperor) immediately dispatched Yēlǜ Niǎolǐ, the Commissioner of Yǒngxīng Palace; Yēlǜ Xīnglǎo, the Grand Guardian of the Right Guards; and Wáng Quán, the Vice Minister of Construction, to offer condolences and sacrifices.
In the third month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Xiāo Tǎliègě, the Associate Defense Commissioner of the Southern Capital (*Nánjīng*), was appointed Chief Justice of the Left (*Zuǒ Yílíbì*);
and Tánggǔ, the Administrator of Justice of the Right, was appointed Chief Justice of the Right (*Yòu Yílíbì*).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Lǐ Liàngzuò of Xià Guó sent envoys to present artifacts left behind by his father Yuánhào.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Envoys from the Tiěbùdé Guó arrived,
requesting to use their tribal troops to assist in attacking Xià Guó,
but this was not permitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Dù Fáng, the Military Governor of Wǔdìng Jūn, was reinstated as Southern Chancellor (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*).
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Pú Liǎn, the Great King of the Púlú Máowǔ tribe, brought shipbuilders to present (to the court).
In the sixth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Zǔbǔ offered twenty thousand horses and camels.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Cháigě, Grand Preceptor (*Tàishī*) of Chángbái Shān, and Sālàdū, Grand Preceptor of the Huíbá tribe, came to offer local tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *Dīngwèi* day,
Bùgěyī (son of Yúyuè Mó Méiyù) and the *Yílíjǐn* Hǔtǔ of the eight Bólí tribes, along with others, submitted internally (came to join the court).
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
prisoners were reviewed,
and death sentences for miscellaneous crimes were reduced.
Eighth month, on the *Bǐngxū* day,
rental taxes were restored for the poor households in Nánjīng.
On the *Wùzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Yìxiān (Dianqian Dū Diǎnjiǎn) was appointed as the Xíngjūn Dū Bùshǔ (Area Army Commander-in-Chief),
Xià Xíngměi (Jiedushi of the Zhōngshùn Army) as the Deputy Commander,
and Yēlǜ Zhúzhe (Xiángwěn of the Northeast Front) as the Supervisor of the Army,
to campaign against Táo Délǐ, the chieftain of Púnúlǐ.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Nányuàn Dàwáng Yēlǜ Hánbā died.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Dúlújīn.
Eleventh month, on the *Yǐwèi* day (the first day of the month),
envoys were dispatched to inventory horses.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
the Imperial Younger Brother Zhòngyuán was granted a gold certificate.
The Imperial Son Hélǔwò was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yuè;
Āliǎn as the Prince of Xǔ;
Xiè Jiānú (Jiedushi of the Zhōngshùn Army) as the Prince of Chén;
Tiēbù (Xījīng Liúshǒu) as the Prince of Hàn;
Lǚfén (Tìyǐn) as the Prince of Liáoxī Commandery;
Biégǔdé (Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ) as the Prince of Liǔchéng Commandery;
Hóugǔ (Jiedushi of the Fènglín Army) as the Prince of Ráolè Commandery;
Nièlǔgǔ (Prince of Āndìng Commandery) was promoted to Prince of Chǔ.
The eighteenth year, Spring, the first month, on the *Jiǎwǔ* day (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *Wùxū* day,
the envoy from the Xià State who came to congratulate the New Year was detained and not sent back.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
Xiāo Wéixìn (Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the North Court) was dispatched to inform Sòng of the campaign against Xià.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
(the Emperor) went to Yuānyāng Luò.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
(the Emperor) hunted at Bàtè Shān.
Yēlǜ Yìxiān reported a victory over Púnúlǐ.
Second month, on the *Gēngchén* day,
(the Emperor) visited Hóngjī, the King of Yānzhào, at his camp to check on his illness.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Yìxiān and others captured Táo Délǐ and presented him (to the court).
Third month, on the *Yǐsì* day,
the Guó of Gāochāng sent an envoy to pay tribute.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
because Hóngjī recovered from his illness,
amnesty was granted for crimes up to and including miscellaneous capital offenses.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
Wūgǔ sent an envoy to offer submission.
Summer, fourth month, on the *Guǐyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Gāoshí (Chancellor of the Southern Prefecture) was appointed Tǒngjūn Shǐ of Nánjīng.
Fifth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
the chieftains of the Five States (Wǔguó) each led their tribes to submit.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Wùdiētáizhā, the chief of the Huíbá tribe, and others came to court.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
Yēlǜ Xiāntóng (Jiedushi of the Five States), due to his surrender of Wūgǔ rebels,
was granted the title of Superior General of the Zuǒ Jiānmén Guard.
Sixth month, on the *Rénxū* day (the first day of the month),
Xiāo Huì (King of Hánguó) was appointed Xíngjūn Dūtǒng of Hénán Circuit,
assisted by Xiāo Xiàoyǒu (Prince of Zhào) and Tiēbù (Prince of Hàn).
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
the Rite of the Twelve Divine Standards was performed.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
since the Liáo forces were campaigning against Xià,
Sòng dispatched Qián Yì to deliver congratulatory gifts.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
Zǔbǔ came to pay tribute with horses, camels, and precious trinkets.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
an envoy from the Xià State came to pay tribute,
but he was detained and not sent back.
On the *Dīnghài* day,
the Rite of Rebirth was performed.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *Wùxū* day,
(the Emperor) personally led the expedition.
Eighth month, on the *Xīnyǒu* day (the first day of the month),
(the army) crossed the river.
The Xià people fled,
so (the army) returned.
Ninth month, on the *Dīngwèi* day,
Xiāo Huì and others were defeated by the Xià people.
Winter, the tenth month,
Yēlǜ Dílǔgǔ (Xíngjūn Dūtǒng of the Northern Circuit) led the Zǔbǔ armies to Hèlán Shān,
where they captured Lǐ Yuánhào's wife and the families of his officials and subordinates.
They encountered three thousand Xià soldiers who came to fight,
and they were annihilated;
Xiāo Císhìnú (Dū Xiángwěn of the Wūgǔ Díliè Tribe) and Yēlǜ Wòlǐ (Nánkè) died there.
Twelfth month, on the *Wùyín* day,
the trees at Qìng Líng caught fire.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
In cases where a younger brother followed an elder brother in becoming a bandit,
and both brothers were without sons,
the younger brother was specially pardoned.
The nineteenth year, Spring, the first month, on the *Gēngyín* day,
the monk Huìjiàn was promoted to Assistant Grand Commandant (Jiǎnxiào Tàiwèi).
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Dílǔgǔ was re-enfeoffed as the Prince of Qīshuǐ Commandery.
Various generals, officers, and chieftains of the Zǔbǔ and other tribes were promoted in rank according to their degree of merit.
Xiāo Císhìnú was posthumously granted the title of Minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery (Tóng Zhōngshū Ménxià Píngzhāngshì).
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
an envoy was dispatched to condemn the Xià State for its crimes.
On the *Rényín* day,
(the Emperor) went to Yú'ér Luò.
Second month, on the *Dīnghài* day,
Xià generals Wāpǔ, Wěihuò, Yǐlíngjì, and others came to attack Jīnsù Chéng.
Yēlǜ Gāojiānú (Línyá of the Southern Front) and others defeated them.
Wāpǔ was wounded and fled,
while Wěihuò and Yǐlíngjì were killed.
Third month, on the *Wùxū* day,
Xiāo Diélǐdé (Dianqian Dū Diǎnjiǎn) fought against Xià at Sānjiǎo Chuān,
and defeated them.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
Xiāo Púnú (Southwest Recruiting Commissioner), Yíxīn (Nányuàn Dàwáng), Xiāo Sāmǒ (Línyá), and others were ordered to lead an army to campaign against Xià,
with Biégǔdé (Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ) supervising the battle.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
Xiāo Gé (Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs of the North Court) was dispatched to inspect the troops in the border city,
in order to serve as support.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Xī Jī Diàn.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
(the Emperor) visited Xiāo Diélǐdé (Dianqian Dū Diǎnjiǎn) and Xiāo Húdǔ (Fùmǎ Dūwèi) at their camps to check on their illnesses.
Summer, fourth month, on the *Bǐngyín* day,
(the Emperor) went to Yú'ér Luò.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
Xìndǔ (Tìyǐn of the Púlú Máotǔ Tribe) came to pay tribute.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the Guó of Gāolì sent an envoy to pay tribute.
Fifth month, on the *Jǐchǒu* day,
(the Emperor) went to Liángxíng.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
Xiāo Púnú and others entered Xià territory,
but did not encounter the enemy.
They allowed the troops to capture and plunder, and then returned.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
Wāpǔ of the Xià State came to surrender.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
the distant Yi tribe Bāsīmǔ sent an envoy to pay tribute.
Sixth month, on the *Bǐngchén* day (the first day of the month),
the Office of the Dǎotā Lǐng Dūjiān (Supervisor of Dǎotā Ridge) was established.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
(the Emperor) visited Qìng Líng.
On the *Gēngwǔ* day,
(the Emperor) visited Qìngzhōu,
and visited the Dà'ān Diàn.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
an edict was issued stating that physicians, diviners, butchers, vendors, slaves, those who disobeyed their parents, or those who committed crimes and fled,
were not permitted to be recommended as *Jìnshì* (advanced scholars).
The Huíbá, Hésūguǎn, and Púlú Máotǔ tribes each sent envoys to present horses.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
Sòng dispatched an envoy to congratulate (the Liáo) on the victory against Xià;
the Gāolì envoy arrived concurrently.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
the *Jìnshì* examination was held in the Jīnluán Diàn.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *Rénchén* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Kuòlǐ Púwǎn.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
Hóngjī (King of Yānzhào) was appointed to oversee the Bureaus of Military Affairs, both North and South.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
Wòdé, the younger brother of Huòdélà, chief of Zǔbǔ, came to court,
was promoted to Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), and then sent away.
On the *Wùxū* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
Xiāo Tánggǔ (Left Yílíbì) was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the North Court.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
(the Emperor) hunted at Hòulǐjí.
Eighth month, on the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Chuǎnzhǐgě Bálǐsī, the chieftain of Zǔbǔ, came to court.
Ninth month, on the *Rényín* day,
the Xià people invaded the border.
Dílǔgǔ dispatched Hǎilǐ, a general of the Six Court Armies, to defeat them.
Winter, tenth month, on the *Gēngwǔ* day,
(the Emperor) returned to Shàngjīng.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
the mother of Lǐ Liàngzuò, the King of the Xià State, sent an envoy requesting to resume vassal status as before.
When the envoy returned,
an imperial edict was issued instructing (Xià) to send a different trusted official to the Imperial Court,
stating that the matter would be considered slowly.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
laborers in Línhuáng Fǔ were released.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
(the Emperor) went to Zhōnghuì Chuān.
Huōdélá, the chief of the Zǔbǔ, sent an envoy to present tribute.
Gēngxū day,
Reviewed prisoners.
Rénzǐ day,
Dismissed Hán Zhībái, Chancellor of the Southern Administration (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng), to become Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) of Wǔdìngjūn;
Yáng Jì, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Fùshǐ), as Military Governor of Chángníngjūn;
Wáng Gāng, Academician of the Hànlín Academy, as Prefect (Cìshǐ) of Zézhōu;
Zhāng Yòu as Prefect of Huīzhōu;
and Zhōu Bái, Drafting Official (Zhī Zhìgào), as Prefect of Hǎiběizhōu.
Intercalary month, yǐmǎo day,
Appointed Tiēbù, Prince of Hàn (Hànwáng), as Viceroy (Liúshǒu) of the Central Capital (Zhōngjīng).
Xīnwèi day,
Appointed Xiāo Gé, Acting Commissioner of the Northern Military Council (Tóng Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì), as Commissioner of the Southern Military Council (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ);
Yēlǜ Rénxiān, Great King of the Southern Administration (Nányuàn Dàwáng), as Commissioner of the Northern Military Council (Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì);
and enfeoffed him as Prince of Sòng (Sòngwáng).
Twelfth month, dīnghài day,
Xiāo Xiàoyǒu, Chancellor of the Northern Administration (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng) and Prince of Zhào (Zhàowáng), was dismissed to become Viceroy of the Eastern Capital (Dōngjīng);
Xiāo Tǎliègé, Viceroy of the Eastern Capital, became Chancellor of the Northern Administration;
and Chágé, Commissioner of the Southern Military Council and Prince of Lù (Lùwáng), became Great King of the Southern Administration.
Gēngxū day,
Xiāo Huì, King of Hán (Hán'guówáng), was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Wèi (Wèiwáng),
and retired from office.
Rénzǐ day,
Lǐ Liàngzuò of the Xià state sent an envoy to present a memorial,
requesting to revert to the status of a former vassal state.
Spring, first month of the 20th year, wùxū day,
The Imperial Retinue halted at Hùntóng Jiāng.
Second month, jiǎshēn day,
Sent Xiāo Yǒukuò, former Military Inspector of the Northern Council (Běiyuàn Dūjiān), and others as envoys to the Xià state,
demanding the return of the rebel households of the Dǎngxiàng.
Jǐchǒu day,
Went to Cāng'ěrluò.
Jiǎchén day,
The Tǔfān sent an envoy to present tribute.
Third month, the first day (Shuò) rénzǐ,
Visited Hēishuǐ.
Summer, fifth month, guǐchǒu day,
Xiāo Yǒukuò and the other envoys returned from Xià.
Lǐ Liàngzuò’s mother presented a memorial requesting permission, according to the Dǎngxiàng custom, to temporarily present items like horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
Jǐsì day,
The Xià state sent an envoy requesting (the return of) Tánglóng Zhèn and asking for the dismantling of the cities and towns that had been constructed.
The response was given by imperial edict.
Sixth month, bǐngxū day,
An edict commanded that Lǐ Yuánhào's wife, who had been captured, and the Xià people previously taken captive,
be resettled in Sūzhōu.
An envoy was sent to Sòng, bearing goods acquired during the campaign against Xià.
Autumn, seventh month,
Went to Qiūshān.
Ninth month,
An edict revised the regulations and statutes.
The Imperial Retinue halted at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
Winter, tenth month, the first day jǐmǎo,
Compiled the military registers of all circuits.
Eleventh month, gēngshēn day,
Appointed Xiāo Mólǔ, Imperial Guard Inspector (Tìyǐn Dūjiān), as Chief Justice of the Left (Zuǒ Yílíbì).
Jiǎzǐ day,
Ordered the Dōngjīng Viceroyalty Office to oversee the affairs of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù) and the Inner Secretariat (Nèishěng).
Dīngmǎo day,
Discontinued the practice of the Censors (Zhōngchéng) recording the transgressions of officials;
Ordered the Grand Academician (Chéngzhǐ) to take overall charge of this duty.
Twelfth month, yǐyǒu day,
Because the Empress Dowager performed the "rebirth ritual" (zàishēng lǐ),
a great amnesty was proclaimed.
Spring, first month of the 21st year, xīnhài day,
Went to Hùntóng Jiāng.
Second month,
Went to Yú'ěrluò.
Summer, fourth month, guǐwèi day,
Appointed Xiāo Ālà, Imperial Maternal Uncle and Governor (Guójìu Xiángwěn), as Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Route (Xīběilù Zhāotǎoshǐ);
and enfeoffed him as Prince of Xīpíng Commandery (Xīpíngjùnwáng).
Sixth month, bǐngzǐ day,
The Imperial Retinue halted at Yǒng'ān Shān.
Autumn, seventh month, the first day jiǎchén,

Summoned Xiāo Tǎliègé, Chancellor of the Northern Administration; Tiēbù, Chancellor of the Southern Administration and Prince of Hàn; Xiāo Gé, Commissioner of the Southern Military Council; Rénxiān, Commissioner of the Northern Military Council; and others.
They were granted seats,
and discussed the principles of governance from ancient times to the present.
Wùshēn day,
Sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
Jǐyǒu day,
An edict was issued to the Northern and Southern Military Councils,
requiring them to report on affairs twice daily.
Rénzǐ day,
Posthumously honored the grandfather of Tàizǔ as Emperor Jiǎnxiàn (Jiǎnxiàn Huángdì);
his temple name was Xuánzǔ;
his grandmother as Empress Jiǎnxiàn (Jiǎnxiàn Huánghòu);
Tàizǔ's father as Emperor Xuānjiǎn (Xuānjiǎn Huángdì);
his temple name was Dézǔ;
and his mother as Empress Xuānjiǎn (Xuānjiǎn Huánghòu).
Posthumously enfeoffed Tàizǔ’s paternal uncle Yánmù, the Yílíjǐn, as King of Shǔ (Shǔguówáng);
and Shìlǔ, the Yúyuè, as King of Suí (Suíguówáng).
Appointed Hóngjī, King of Yān and Zhào (Yānzhàoguówáng), as Grand Marshal of Military Affairs Under Heaven (Tiānxià Bīngmǎ Dàyuánshuài) and Overseer of the Imperial Guard (Zhī Tìyǐn Shì);
and granted him an imperial edict of instruction.
Guǐhài day,
Lú Bǎo, a palace attendant (Xiǎodǐ), falsely imitated the imperial handwriting.
He was spared death,
but sentenced to forced labor for life.
Jiǎzǐ day,
Went to Qiūshān.
Wùchén day,
Visited Qìng Líng (Mausoleum).
Appointed Xiāo Gé, Commissioner of the Southern Military Council, as Commissioner of the Northern Military Council;
and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wú (Wúwáng).
Xīnwèi day,
Went to Qìngzhōu.
Rénshēn day,
Posthumously enfeoffed Tàizǔ's younger brother Yīndǐshí as King of Xǔ (Xǔguówáng).
Eighth month, wùzǐ day,
Wūzhě, the Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), passed away.
An edict commanded that he be included in the sacrifices at Shèngzōng Miào (Temple).
Ninth month, yǐmǎo day,
Píngzhōu presented a white rabbit.
Jǐwèi day,
Visited Huái Líng (Mausoleum).
Gēngshēn day,
Posthumously conferred the honorary posthumous titles of Emperor Sìshèng (Sìshèng Huángdì) and Emperor Tiānshùn (Tiānshùn Huángdì);
and changed the posthumous title of Empress Zhāngdé (Zhāngdé Huánghòu) to Jìng'ān.
Guǐhài day,
Conferred the posthumous title Empress Réndé (Réndé Huánghòu) upon Empress Qítiān (Qítiān Huánghòu).
Jiǎzǐ day,
Visited Zǔ Líng (Mausoleum).
Increased Tàizǔ's posthumous title to Emperor Dàshèng Dàmíng Shénliè Tiān (Dàshèng Dàmíng Shénliè Tiānhuángdì);
changed the posthumous title of Empress Zhēnliè (Zhēnliè Huánghòu) to Chúnqīn;
Emperor Gōngshùn (Gōngshùn Huángdì) to Zhāngsù;
