and the Empress of the Xiāo clan to Héjìng.
Winter, tenth month, wùyín day,
The Imperial Retinue halted at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
Dīnghài day,
Lǐ Liàngzuò of the Xià state sent an envoy requesting the relaxation of border defenses.
Xiāo Yǒukuò was immediately sent with an imperial edict to instruct him.
Wùzǐ day,
Visited the two prefectures of Xiǎnzhōu and Yìzhōu.
Jiǎwǔ day,
Xiāo Xūliè, Military Governor of Liáoxīngjūn, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhèng (Zhèngwáng);
Chágé, Great King of the Southern Administration and Prince of Lù, became Commissioner of the Southern Military Council;
and promoted to King of Yuè (Yuèguówáng).
Wùxū day,
Hunted tigers at Nánsàgěbǎi.
Xīnchǒu day,
Visited Qián Líng (Mausoleum).
Eleventh month, the first day rényín,
Increased the posthumous title of Emperor Wénxiàn (Wénxiàn Huángdì) to Emperor Wénxiàn Qīnyì (Wénxiàn Qīnyì Huángdì);
and conferred posthumous titles upon the two Empresses as Duānshùn,
and Róuzhēn.
Furthermore, changed the posthumous title of Empress Xiàoliè (Xiàoliè Huánghòu) of Shìzōng to Huáijié.
Dīngwèi day,
Increased the posthumous title of Emperor Xiàochéng (Xiàochéng Huángdì) to Emperor Xiàochéng Kāngjìng (Xiàochéng Kāngjìng Huángdì);
and changed the posthumous title of Empress Shèngshén Xuānxiàn (Shèngshén Xuānxiàn Huánghòu) to Ruìzhì.
Jiǎzǐ day,
Encamped at Zhōnghuì Chuān.
Āsàlán of the Huíhú (Uighurs) sent an envoy to present famous horses and spotted leopards as tribute.
Bǐngyín day,
Reviewed prisoners.
Twelfth month, wùxū day,
Appointed Tǎliègé, Chancellor of the Northern Administration, as Supreme Commander of the Southern Capital (Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ);
Prince of Zhèng, Xūliè, as Chancellor of the Northern Administration;
and Yēlǜ Yìxiān, Chief Administrator of the Qìdān Traveling Palace (Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ), as Tìyǐn (Overseer of the Imperial Guard).
Released convicts sentenced to limited terms of penal servitude.
22nd year, Spring, first month, yǐsì day,
Went to Hùntóng Jiāng.
Second month, bǐngzǐ day,
Āsàlán of the Huíhú, having been invaded by a neighboring country,
sent an envoy seeking aid.
Gēngchén day,
Went to Chūnshuǐ.
Third month, guǐhài day,
Lǐ Liàngzuò, having received the imperial edict permitting his surrender,
sent an envoy to express his gratitude.
Bǐngyín day,
Went to Hēishuǐ Luò.
Summer, fourth month, wùzǐ day,
Hunted at Hèdiàn.
Fifth month, rényín day,
An edict commanded the planting of fruit trees in the prefectures and counties of the interior.
Sixth month, rénshēn day,
The Imperial Retinue halted at Húlǚ Shān.
Guǐwèi day,
Gāolì (Koryŏ) sent an envoy to present tribute.
Autumn, seventh month, jǐyǒu day,
Tún Tūgǔsī, the Great King (Dàwáng) of the Zǔbǔ, led the various chiefs to present horses and camels.
Gēngshēn day,
Went to Hēilǐng.
Intercalary month, gēngwǔ day,
The Wūgǔ presented tribute.
Guǐsì day,
Established the Bureau of Money and Silk (Qiánbósī) in Chángchūnzhōu.
Ninth month, rénchén day,
Lǐ Liàngzuò of the Xià state sent an envoy to present an instrument of surrender.
Jiǎwǔ day,
Sent Gāo Jiānú, Minister of the Southern Administration (Nánmiàn Línyá), and others, bearing an imperial edict to reassure and instruct them.
Winter, tenth month, the first day bǐngshēn,
There was a solar eclipse.
Eleventh month, xīnmǎo day,
An edict commanded that all officials who retired ceremoniously or were dismissed due to crimes should have their records maintained;
these records were to be reported annually to the Military Council (Shūmìyuàn).
In the twelfth month, on the day *Bǐngshēn* (the new moon),
an edict ordered the Vice Envoy of the Huíhú department to be filled by a Qìdān person.
On *Gēngzǐ*,
corresponding to the Shèngjié festival,
a partial amnesty was granted for crimes of penal servitude and lesser offenses.
On *Rénzǐ*,
the Emperor addressed his ministers, saying:
"I and the Lord of Sòng are pledged as brothers.
Our joyful amity has lasted for many years,
and I wish to see his painted likeness.
Instruct the incoming envoy (to provide it)."
In the spring, the first month of the twenty-third year (of *Chóngxī*), on *Jǐsì*,
(the Emperor) went to the Hùntóng Jiāng.
On *Guǐyǒu*,
he hunted at Shuāngzǐ Diàn.
On *Wùzǐ*,
the state of Xià sent an envoy to offer local tribute.
On *Rénchén*,
he went to the spring hunting grounds.
On *Jiǎwǔ*,
he hunted at Pánzhípō.
In the third month, on *Dīnghài*,
he visited the camp of the Imperial Younger Brother, *Zhòngyuán*.
In summer, the fourth month, on *Guǐmǎo*,
Gāolì sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On *Guǐchǒu*,
he hunted at Hézhǐhūlǐ.
In the fifth month, on *Jǐsì*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò requested permission to present horses and camels,
and an edict allowed this as annual tribute.
On *Gēngyín*,
the Imperial entourage stopped at Yǒng'ān Shān.
On *Rénchén*,
the state of Xià sent an envoy to offer tribute.
In the sixth month, on *Bǐngshēn*,
he went to Qìngzhōu.
On *Jǐhài*,
he paid respects at Qìng Líng.
On *Rényín*,
Huī, the King of Gāolì, requested an official post for his son,
and an edict granted him the title of *Jiǎnxiào Tàiwèi*.
On *Xīnhài*,
Tǔbō sent an envoy to offer tribute.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *Jǐsì*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò of the state of Xià sent an envoy to request marriage alliance.
On *Jiǎxū*,
he went to the autumn hunting grounds.
On *Jǐmǎo*,
an edict mandated headcloths for the Eight Lineages.
In the ninth month, on *Gēngyín*,
while hunting,
he encountered three tigers,
loosed the dogs, and captured them.
In winter, the tenth month, on *Dīngyǒu*,
the Imperial entourage stopped at Zhōngjīng.
On *Wùxū*,
he visited the newly constructed Secretariat.
On *Xīnchǒu*,
rituals were held at the Ancestral Temple.
On *Guǐchǒu*,
because the Kāitài Sì temple had cast a silver Buddha image,
a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners in the capital.
On *Bǐngchén*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò sent an envoy to present a sworn memorial.
In the eleventh month, on *Yǐchǒu*,
a chief of the Zǔbǔ came to offer tribute.
On *Rénshēn*,
the Emperor led his officials in presenting the Empress Dowager with the venerable title *Réncí Shèngshàn Qīnxiào Guǎngdé Ānjìng Zhēnchún Yìhé Kuānhòu Chóngjué Yītiān Huángtàihòu*.
A general amnesty was declared.
Internal and external officials were promoted according to their ranks.
On *Guǐwèi*,
prisoners were reviewed.
On *Jiǎshēn*,
the officials presented the Emperor with the venerable title *Qīntiān Fèngdào Yòushì Xīnglì Wǔdìng Wénchéng Shèngshén Rénxiào Huángdì*.
Empress Xiāo Shì was invested with the title *Zhēnyì Cíhé Wénhuì Xiàojìng Guǎng'ài Chóngshèng Huánghòu*.
In the twelfth month, on *Bǐngshēn*,
he went to Zhōnghuì Chuān.
In the spring, the first month of the twenty-fourth year, on *Guǐhài*,
he went to the Hùntóng Jiāng.
On *Wùchén*,
he paid court to the Empress Dowager.
On *Xīnsì*,
Sòng sent an envoy to offer congratulations,
presenting trained elephants.
In the second month, on *Jǐchǒu* (the new moon),
the Sòng envoy was summoned to fish and compose poetry.
On *Guǐsì*,
he went to the Chángchūn Hé.
On *Jiǎyín*,
the state of Xià sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
In the third month, on *Guǐhài*,
the Imperial Younger Brother *Zhòngyuán* had a son,
and a partial amnesty was granted for crimes of penal servitude and lesser offenses in the temporary residence and the two prefectures of Chángchūn and Zhènběi.
In summer, the fifth month,
the Imperial entourage stopped at Nányá.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *Rénwǔ*,
he went to the autumn hunting grounds.
Stopping next at the northern valley of Nányá,
he fell ill.
In the eighth month, on *Dīnghài*,
the illness worsened significantly,
and he summoned Hóngjī, King of Yān and Zhào,
instructing him on the essentials of governing the state.
On *Wùzǐ*,
a general amnesty was declared;
the hawks and falcons of the Five Directorates were released,
and the fishing equipment was burned.
On *Jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor died at the temporary palace,
aged forty.
The posthumous edict ordered Hóngjī, King of Yān and Zhào, to succeed to the throne.
In the tenth month of the first year of *Qīngníng*, on *Gēngzǐ*,
the honorable posthumous name *Shénshèng Xiàozhāng Huángdì* was conferred,
with the temple name *Xīngzōng*.
A eulogy says: *Xīngzōng* ascended the throne at the age of sixteen.
He failed to first honor the Empress Dowager but honored his own mother,
which led to her ruling the court and monopolizing power,
causing the wrongful killing of innocents.
Furthermore, he failed to use rites and gentle persuasion to admonish her,
causing *Qítiān* to die by regicide and rebellion.
This was a deficiency in the filial piety expected of a sovereign.
What a pity!
As for how, while the deceased Emperor lay in the coffin,
(he) drank wine and played ball games,
repeatedly recorded in the historical records.
Yet, when paying respects to the departed Emperor's portrait, he was deeply mournful,
and upon receiving condolences from Sòng, he wore mourning clothes.
His actions seemed to belong to two different persons.
Why was this so?
Furthermore, he was moved by the words of Fù Bì and renewed good relations with the Southern Sòng;
he allowed Lǐ Liàngzuò's covenant and withdrew troops from Xī Xià.
The frontiers were not alarmed,
and internal governance was repaired.
He personally tested the presented scholars,
greatly revised the statutes and regulations,
and allowed everyone, from scholars down to commoners,
to present beneficial suggestions.
Thus, his desire for good governance was intense.
However, among the ministers at court at that time,
there was never mention of one worthy person being promoted
or one instance of remonstrance being offered.
How could he have hoped to attain the conduct of ancient sovereigns?
Nevertheless,
compared to *Shèngzōng* and those who followed him,
he can be called a worthy ruler.
Annals Twenty-One: Dàozōng (1)
Dàozōng Xiàowén Huángdì,
whose taboo name was Hóngjī,
courtesy name Nièlín,
and milk name Chálà.
He was the eldest son of Emperor Xīngzōng;
his mother was Rén Yì Huánghòu Xiāo Shì.
At the age of six, he was enfeoffed as King of Liáng.
In the eleventh year of *Chóngxī*, he was promoted to King of Yān,
and was appointed to oversee the affairs of the Central Secretariat.
The following year,
he was appointed to oversee the affairs of the Chancellery of Military Affairs for both the Northern and Southern Courts,
granted the title *Shàngshū Lìng*,
and promoted to King of Yān and Zhào.
In the twenty-first year, he was made Grand Marshal of the Armies of the World,
appointed to manage the affairs of the *Tìyǐn*,
and participated in court politics.
The Emperor's temperament was calm, serious, and resolute.
Whenever he attended court,
*Xīngzōng* would assume a solemn expression because of him.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day *wùyín*,
the imperial retinue halted at Zhōnghuì Chuān (中會川).
On the day *dīnghài*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚) of Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to request the relaxation of border defenses.
An imperial edict was immediately dispatched with Xiāo Yǒukuò (蕭友括) to convey it.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
the Emperor visited Xiǎn (顯) and Yì (懿) prefectures.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Xiāo Xūliè (蕭虛烈), Jìedùshǐ (節度使) of Liáoxīng Jūn (遼興軍), was enfeoffed as Zhèng Wáng (鄭王).
Zhāgě (查葛), Nányuàn Dàwáng (南院大王) and Lù Wáng (潞王), was made Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ (南院樞密使),
and further enfeoffed as Yuèguó Wáng (越國王).
On the day *wùxū*,
a tiger was shot at Nánsāgěbǎi (南撒葛柏).
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
the Qīan Líng (乾陵) was visited.
In the eleventh month, on the first day, *rényín*,
the posthumous title of Wénxiàn Huángdì (文獻皇帝) was augmented to Wénxiàn Qīnyì Huángdì (文獻欽義皇帝).
The posthumous titles of the two empresses were:
Duānshùn (端順) and Róuzhēn (柔貞).
The posthumous title of Shìzōng Xiàoliè Huánghòu (世宗孝烈皇后) was changed again to Huáijié (懷節).
On the day *dīngwèi*,
the posthumous title of Xiàochéng Huángdì (孝成皇帝) was augmented to Xiàochéng Kāngjìng Huángdì (孝成康靖皇帝),
and the posthumous title of Shèngshén Xuānxiàn Huánghòu (聖神宣獻皇后) was changed to Ruìzhì (睿智).
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the imperial retinue camped at Zhōnghuì Chuān (中會川).
Āsàlán (阿薩蘭) of Huíhú (回鶻) sent an envoy to offer famous horses and spotted leopards as tribute.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the twelfth month, on the day *wùxū*,
Tǎliègě (塔烈葛), Běifǔ Zǎixiàng (北府宰相), was made Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ (南京統軍使).
Zhèng Wáng (鄭王) Xūliè (虛烈) was made Běifǔ Zǎixiàng (北府宰相),
and Yēlǜ Yìxiān (耶律義先), Qìdān Xínggōng Dōubùshǔ (契丹行宮都部署), was made Tìyǐn (惕隱).
Prisoners with limited terms of corvée labor were released.
In the twenty-second year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *yǐsì*,
the Emperor went to Húntóng Jiāng (混同江).
In the second month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Āsàlán (阿薩lán) of Huíhú (回鶻) was invaded by a neighboring state,
and sent an envoy to request aid.
On the day *gēngchén*,
the Emperor went to the spring hunting ground.
In the third month, on the day *guǐhài*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚), having been permitted to surrender by an imperial edict,
sent an envoy to express gratitude.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
the Emperor went to Hēishuǐ Luò (黑水濼).
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
the Emperor hunted at Hè Diàn (鶴淀).
In the fifth month, on the day *rényín*,
an imperial edict ordered fruit trees to be planted in prefectures and counties of the interior.
In the sixth month, on the day *rénshēn*,
the imperial retinue halted at Húlǚ Shān (胡呂山).
On the day *guǐwèi*,
Gāolí (高麗) sent an envoy to offer tribute.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
Túntūgǔsī (屯禿古斯), Dàwáng (大王) of Zǔbù (阻卜), led various tribal chiefs to offer horses and camels.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the Emperor went to Hēilǐng (黑嶺).
In the intercalary month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
Wūgǔ (烏古) offered tribute.
On the day *guǐsì*,
a Qíánbó Sī (錢帛司) was established in Chángchūn Zhōu (長春州).
In the ninth month, on the day *rénchén*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚) of Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to present a memorial of surrender.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Gāo Jiānú (高家奴), Nánmiàn Línyá (南面林牙), and others were dispatched with an imperial edict to appease and instruct him.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day, *bǐngshēn*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month, on the day *xīnmǎo*,
an imperial edict ordered that records be kept of all officials who received transfer according to ritual or were dismissed due to offenses,
and these records were to be reported to the Shūmìyuàn (樞密院) annually.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, *bǐngshēn*,
an imperial edict stipulated that the Fùshǐ (副使) of the Huíhú (回鶻) department should be filled by a Qìdān (契丹) person.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
in celebration of the Emperor's birthday,
a partial amnesty was granted for crimes of corvée labor and below.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
the Emperor instructed his ministers, saying:
“I and the Sòng (宋) ruler are sworn brothers,
and our good relations have lasted for many years.
I wish to see his painted portrait,
so you may convey this to his envoy.”
In the twenty-third year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *jǐsì*,
the Emperor went to Húntóng Jiāng (混同江).
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
the Emperor hunted at Shuāngzǐ Diàn (雙子淀).
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to offer local products as tribute.
On the day *rénchén*,
the Emperor went to the spring hunting ground.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
the Emperor hunted at Pánzhípō (盤直坡).
In the third month, on the day *dīnghài*,
the Emperor visited the tent of the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán (重元).
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Gāolí (高麗) sent an envoy to offer tribute.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
the Emperor hunted at Hézhǐhūlǐ (合只忽里).
In the fifth month, on the day *jǐsì*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚) requested to present horses and camels,
and an imperial edict allowed him to offer them as annual tribute.
On the day *gēngyín*,
the imperial retinue halted at Yǒng'ān Shān (永安山).
On the day *rénchén*,
Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to offer tribute.
In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor went to Qìng Zhōu (慶州).
On the day *jǐhài*,
the Qìng Líng (慶陵) was visited.
On the day *rényín*,
Wáng Huī (王徽) of Gāolí (高麗) requested official titles for his sons,
and an imperial edict granted them the additional title of Jiǎnxiào Tàiwèi (檢校太尉).
On the day *xīnhài*,
Tǔbō (吐蕃) sent an envoy to offer tribute.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *jǐsì*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚) of Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to seek a marriage alliance.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
the Emperor went to the autumn hunting ground.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
an imperial edict ordered the eight branches of the imperial clan to wear khăn xắc (巾幘).
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
the Emperor hunted,
encountered three tigers,
and released dogs to catch them.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
the imperial retinue halted at Zhōngjīng (中京).
On the day *wùxū*,
the Emperor visited the newly built Mìshūjiān (祕書監).
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
rites were performed at the ancestral temple.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
because the Kāitàisì (開泰寺) cast a silver Buddha statue,
a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners in the capital.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
Lǐ Liàngzuò (李諒祚) sent an envoy to present a memorial of oath.
In the eleventh month, on the day *yǐchǒu*,
a chief of Zǔbù (阻卜) offered tribute.
On the day *rénshēn*,

the Emperor, leading his officials, conferred the honorific title Réncí Shèngshàn Qīnxiào Guǎngdé Ānjìng Zhēnchún Yìhé Kuānhòu Chóngjué Yítiān Huángtàihòu (仁慈聖善欽孝廣德安靜貞純懿和寬厚崇覺儀天皇太后) upon the Empress Dowager,
and a general amnesty was declared.
Officials inside and outside the court were promoted with varying grades.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
all officials conferred the honorific title Qīntiān Fèngdào Yòushì Xīnglì Wǔdìng Wénchéng Shèngshén Rénxiào Huángdì (欽天奉道祐世興曆武定文成聖神仁孝皇帝) upon the Emperor,
and Empress Xiāo (蕭) was formally titled Zhēnyì Cíhé Wénhuì Xiàojìng Guǎng'ài Chóngshèng Huánghòu (貞懿慈和文惠孝敬廣愛崇聖皇后).
In the twelfth month, on the day *bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor went to Zhōnghuì Chuān (中會川).
In the twenty-fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *guǐhài*,
the Emperor went to Húntóng Jiāng (混同江).
On the day *wùchén*,
the Empress Dowager was paid respects.
On the day *xīnsì*,
Sòng (宋) sent an envoy to offer congratulations,
and presented trained elephants.
In the second month, on the first day, *jǐchǒu*,
the Sòng (宋) envoy was summoned to fish and compose poetry.
On the day *guǐsì*,
the Emperor went to Chángchūn Hé (長春河).
On the day *jiǎyín*,
Xià (夏) Kingdom sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
In the third month, on the day *guǐhài*,
the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán (重元) had a son,
and a partial amnesty was granted for crimes of corvée labor and below in the temporary imperial residence and in Chángchūn (長春) and Zhènběi (鎮北) prefectures.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the imperial retinue halted at Nányá (南崖).
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *rényǐn*,
the Emperor went to the autumn hunting ground.
Upon reaching the northern valley of Nányá (南崖),
he became unwell.
In the eighth month, on the day *dīnghài*,
his illness worsened considerably.
Hóngjī (洪基), Yānzhào Guówáng (燕趙國王), was summoned,
and instructed on the essentials of governing the country.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
a general amnesty was declared,
the falcons and eagles of the five falconries were released,
and fishing equipment was burned.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor passed away at the imperial temporary palace,
at the age of forty.
His dying edict named Yānzhào Guówáng (燕趙國王) Hóngjī (洪基) as his successor.
In the first year of Qīngníng (清寧), in the tenth month, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
the honorific posthumous title Shénshèng Xiàozhāng Huángdì (神聖孝章皇帝) was conferred,
and the temple name was Xīngzōng (興宗).
In the 24th year, in the autumn, eighth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day (day 26),
Xīngzōng collapsed (died).
He immediately ascended the imperial throne before the coffin,
grieving deeply and refusing to attend to government affairs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day (day 28),
all the officials presented memorials firmly requesting him (to rule),
and he permitted it.
An imperial edict stated:
"We, due to Our meager virtue,
are entrusted to reside above the scholars and common people.
We are greatly afraid that Our wisdom and understanding are insufficient,
and that the multitude below may lack trust;
that taxes and levies may be wrongly instituted,
and that rewards and punishments may be inaccurate;
that the grace of the sovereign cannot reach the people below,
and that the feelings of the people below cannot reach the sovereign.
Therefore, you, the scholars and common people,
speak directly without concealment.
If [your words] are acceptable, they will be selected and used;
if not, they will not be considered a fault.
All you ministers must embody Our intention."
On the *rénchén* day (day 29),
the Imperial Younger Brother Chóngyuán was made Imperial Elder Uncle (Huáng Tàishū),
exempted from the Hàn style of kneeling,
and not addressed by his personal name.
On the *guǐsì* day (day 30),
envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Sòng, as well as Xià, and Gāolì.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day (day 31),
Chóngyuán was dispatched to pacify the soldiers and common people of Nánjīng.
On the *wùxū* day (day 35),
according to the posthumous edict,
Xiāo Ālà, the Prince of Xīpíng Commandery and Commissioner of Pacification for the Northwest Circuit, was appointed Chancellor of the Northern Administration (Běi Fǔ Zǎixiàng),
and concurrently authorized to oversee the affairs of the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery (Nán Yuàn Shūmìshǐ);
and Xiāo Xūliè, Chancellor of the Northern Administration, was made Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of Wǔdìng Prefecture.
On the *xīnchǒu* day (day 38),
the era name was changed to Qīngníng,
and a great amnesty was proclaimed.
In the ninth month, on the *wùwǔ* day (day 55),
an edict decreed that areas outside the hunting grounds habitually favored [by the Emperor] were not to be restricted.
On the *gēngshēn* day (day 57),
an edict decreed that except for the guardsmen,
others were not permitted to wear blades when entering the palace;
those who were not descendants of meritorious relatives or officials of the ranks *Yílíjǐn*, Deputy Commissioner (Fùshǐ), or *Chéngyīng* were not permitted to wear caps.
On the *rénxū* day (day 59),
an edict decreed that the families of *Yílíjǐn* and Deputy Commissioners, along with commoners treated as base persons,
were not permitted to wear camel felt or otter furs;
knife handles, hunting eagles, saddles and bridles, or pendants were not permitted to be made using rhino horn, jade, or carved rhino horn;
only Grand Generals (Dà Jiāngjūn) were exempted from this prohibition.
On the *yǐchǒu* day (day 62),
ranks and rewards were differentially bestowed upon inner and outer officials.
On the *gēngwǔ* day (day 67),
the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) was honored as Grand Empress Dowager (Tài Huáng Tàihòu).
On the *xīnwèi* day (day 68),
Xiāo Móulǔ, Left *Yílíbì*, and Hán Yùn, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, were sent to present the late emperor's artifacts to Sòng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day (day 70),
an envoy was sent to inform Sòng of the enthronement.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day (day 73),
the Empress (Huánghòu) was honored as Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu),
and a banquet was held at the Zōutú Hall.
Chén Liú, Prince of Sù State and Resident Administrator of Shàngjīng, was made Resident Administrator of Nánjīng.
On the *rénwǔ* day (day 79),
envoys were dispatched to bestow artifacts of the late emperor upon Gāolì and the state of Xià.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *dīnghài* day (day 84),
the relevant authorities requested that the Emperor's birthday be designated the Tiān'ān Festival,
and this was approved.
Rénxiān, Prince of Wú, was made Acting Joint Resident Administrator of Nánjīng,
and Túpōtè, Prince of Chén, was made Chancellor of the Southern Administration (Nán Fǔ Zǎixiàng),
and promoted to be the Prince of Wú.
On the *rényín* day (day 99),
Shíshénnú, Military Commissioner of the Shùnyì Army, was made Great Prince of the Southern Chancellery (Nán Yuàn Dàwáng).
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day (day 101),
Emperor Xīngzōng was interred at Qìnglíng.
Sòng and Gāolì sent envoys to attend the ceremony.
The mountain there was named Yǒngxīng.
On the *bǐngyín* day (day 103),
Hóugǔ, Great Prince of the Southern Chancellery, was made Resident Administrator of Zhōngjīng,
and Xiāo Ālà, Chancellor of the Northern Administration and Prince of Xīpíng Commandery, was promoted to be the Prince of Hán.
On the *rénshēn* day (day 109),
[The Emperor] stopped at Huáizhōu.
Sacrifices were offered at the temples of Tàizōng and Mùzōng.
On the *jiǎxū* day (day 111),
[The Emperor] visited the ancestral mausoleum (Zǔlíng).
On the *wùyín* day (day 115),
it was the Winter Solstice (Dōngzhì).
Sacrifices were offered at the temples of Tàizǔ, Jǐngzōng, and Xīngzōng,
and the congratulations of the assembled officials were not accepted.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngxū* day (day 123),
an edict instructed the Left *Yílíbì*, saying:
"We, due to Our slight youth and immaturity,
have succeeded to the great position.
Morning and night We are worried and fearful,
afraid We are unable to bear the responsibility.
We desire to hear forthright words,
so as to correct Our errors.
Now several months have passed,
but We have not yet seen actions that fulfill Our intention of entrusting important officials to act as Our limbs, eyes, and ears.
Therefore, command all inner and outer officials,
before their term of office is completed,
to each speak on one matter.
Furthermore, relay this command to all jurisdictions,
that regardless of noble or base status, old or young,
all may speak directly without concealment."
On the *wùzǐ* day (day 125),
marking the Yìngjié festival (the Empress Dowager's birthday),
a longevity celebration was held for the Grand Empress Dowager,
and a banquet was given for the assembled officials and their titled wives.
Consort Xiāo was formally invested as Empress (Huánghòu).
The Imperial Younger Brother Hélǔwò, Prince of Yuè, was promoted to be Prince of Lǔ State,
Āliǎn, Prince of Xǔ, was made Prince of Chén State,
and Nièlǔgǔ, Prince of Chǔ, was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Wú.
On the *xīnmǎo* day (day 128),
an edict instructed the Dùshǔ Yuàn (Deployment Office) that,
if matters contained state secrets, they should be immediately reported [to the Emperor].
Regarding those who cast forth slanderous and defamatory writings,
anyone who dared to receive or read them would also be executed in the marketplace.
On the *guǐsì* day (day 130),
ten dukes of the imperial clan defied their mother,
and were executed.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day (day 131),
Yáo Jǐngxíng, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs, was made Associate Administrator of Governmental Affairs (Cānzhī Zhèngshì),
Wú Zhàn, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was made Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs,
and Hán Shàowén, Associate Administrator of Governmental Affairs and Acting Joint Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Resident Administrator of Shàngjīng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day (day 133),
Sòng dispatched Ōuyáng Xiū and others to come and congratulate [the Emperor] on his enthronement.
On the *wùxū* day (day 135),
an edict decreed the establishment of schools to foster scholars,
distributed the commentaries and sub-commentaries on the Five Classics,
and established one position each for an Erudite (Bóshì) and an Assistant Instructor (Zhùjiào).
On the *guǐmǎo* day (day 140),
Yáng Jì, Magistrate of Zhuōzhōu, was made Associate Administrator of Governmental Affairs and Acting Joint Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *gēngxū* day (day 147),
due to the birthday of Shèngzōng when he was alive,
the prisoners in Shàngjīng were pardoned.
In this year,
in the Qīngliáng Hall, the Emperor personally conferred the *Jìnshì* degree upon Zhāng Xiàojié and forty-three other men.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the *bǐngchén* day (day 153),
an edict decreed that officials and their subordinates in prefectures and commanderies who determined the fates of prisoners,
should follow the precedents set for various tribal groups.
On the *jǐsì* day (day 156),
an edict exempted those from the Èrgǔ tribe whose families had historically participated in the selection of chancellors and military commissioners from service in the *Píshì* Army.
In this month,
[The Emperor] visited Yú'er Luò.
In the second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day (day 162),
Xiāo Móulǔ, Left *Yílíbì*, was made Administrator of the Pacification Commission for the Southwest Region.
On the *yǐsì* day (day 172),
due to the birthday of Xīngzōng when he was alive,
a banquet was held for the assembled officials,
and they were ordered to each compose a poem.
In the third month, on the *dīngsì* day (day 184),
marking the Yìngjié festival,
a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners within a hundred *lǐ*.
On the *jǐmǎo* day (day 186),
the Emperor personally composed the *Fàng Yīng Fù* (Rhapsody on Releasing the Falcon) and bestowed it upon his officials,
illustrating his intention to employ ministers.
In the intercalary month, on the *jǐhài* day (day 198),
the coins minted in Dōngjīng were first put into circulation.
On the *yǐsì* day (day 204),
the prisons in Nánjīng were empty,
and the Resident Administrator and subordinate officials were promoted.
Summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day (day 211),
an edict stated:
"Since it is now summer,
the time for raising birds and beasts and for reproduction,
fires must not be started in the countryside."
In the fifth month, on the *wùxū* day (day 225),
[The Emperor] visited Qìnglíng.
On the *jiǎchén* day (day 231),
sacrifices were offered at Xīngzōng's temple.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngsì* day (day 244),
an edict instructed the Chancellors to recommend talented and capable men.
On the *wùwǔ* day (day 245),
the relevant authorities were ordered to register soldiers to replenish the border garrisons.
On the *xīnyǒu* day (day 248),
the chieftain of the Zǔbǔ came to court,
presenting local tribute.
On the *dīngmǎo* day (day 254),
Gāolì sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *xīnwèi* day (day 258),
the historians were dismissed from participating in court deliberations,
and were instructed to write only after consulting the Chancellors.
On the *yǐhài* day (day 262),
Zhōngjīng suffered a plague of locusts.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day (day 263),
an edict decreed that cases of proven serious banditry,
could be determined (judged) by the various circuits.
On the *dīngchǒu* day (day 264),
Zhāgě, Prince of Zhào State and Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery, was made Resident Administrator of Shàngjīng,
and Rénxiān, Prince of Wú and Acting Joint Resident Administrator of Nánjīng, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery.
On the *yǐyǒu* day (day 272),
envoys were dispatched to various circuits to equalize taxes and levies,
repair military equipment,
encourage agriculture and sericulture,
and prohibit banditry.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnwèi* day (day 288),
[The Emperor] went to the Autumn Mountain.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day (day 307),
[The Emperor] visited Zhōngjīng,
and offered sacrifices to Shèngzōng and Xīngzōng at the Huì'ān Hall.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
went to Zhōnghuìchuān.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùxū,
Yēlǜ Huàlǐ, who was managing the affairs of the Left Yílíbì, was appointed Yílíbì,
and the Northern Court Grand King Yēlǜ Xiāntóng was appointed to manage the affairs of Huánglóngfǔ.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the civil and military officials offered the Emperor an honorific title, saying, “Tiānyòu Huángdì” (Emperor Tiānyòu);
the Empress was titled “Yìdé Huánghòu” (Empress Yìdé).
A general amnesty was granted.
On the day Yǐsì,
Chóngyuán, the Imperial Grand Uncle, was appointed Grand Marshal (Dà Yuánshuài) of the troops and horses of all under Heaven.
Zhāgě, the King of Zhào State, was transferred and enfeoffed as King of Wèi State; Hélǔwò, the King of Lǔ State, as King of Sòng State; and Ālián, the King of Chén State, as King of Qín State.
Nièlǔgǔ, the King of Wú, was advanced in rank to King of Chǔ State.
All officials were promoted with varying differences.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Wùshēn,
Xiāo Ālà, the King of Hán, was appointed Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmìshǐ);
Chénliú, the Metropolitan Commandant of Dōngjīng and King of Sù State, was appointed Northern Prefecture Chancellor (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng);
Hélǔwò, the King of Sòng State, was appointed Metropolitan Commandant of Shàngjīng;
and Ālián, the King of Qín State, was appointed to manage the affairs of the Central Censorate (Zhōngchéng Sī).
On the day Jiǎyín,
an honorific title was offered to the Empress Dowager, saying, “Cíyì Rénhé Wénhuì Xiàojìng Guǎng'ài Zōngtiān Huáng Tàihòu.”
In the third year, spring, in the first month, on the day Gēngchén,
went to the Yāzihé River.
On the day Bǐngxū,
a Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) for Dǎotā Lǐng was established.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the tribal chiefs of the Five Nations (Wǔ Guó) came to offer tribute of local products.
In the second month, on the day Jǐwèi,
went to Dàyú Luò (Great Fish Lagoon).
In the third month, on the day Xīnsì,
Nièlǔgǔ, the King of Chǔ State, was appointed Military Governor of Wǔdìngjūn.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
cleared the heat at Yǒng'ān Shān.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
went to Qìng Líng (Qìng Mausoleum),
and offered ritual wine (Zhòu) at the Jīndiàn Hall and Tóngtiāndiàn Hall.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Zhāgě, the King of Wèi State, was appointed Tìyǐn;
Xiāo Tánggǔ, Joint Manager of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Tóngzhī Shūmìyuàn Shì), was appointed Southern Prefecture Chancellor;
and Tiēbù, the King of Wèi State, was appointed Metropolitan Commandant of Dōngjīng.
Autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
there was an earthquake in Nánjīng,
and an amnesty was granted within that territory.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
went to Qiūshān (Autumn Mountain).
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor presented the Empress Dowager with a poem titled “Jūnchén Tóngzhì Huáyí Tóngfēng” (Sovereign and Ministers Share the Same Aspiration, Huá and Yí Share the Same Custom).
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
proceeded to Zhōnghuìchuān.
Winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
paid respects at the Ancestral Mausoleum (Zǔ Líng).
On the day Gēngshēn,
paid respects at the temple of Ràngguó Huángdì and Shìzōng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
offered ritual wine at the Yùdiàn Hall.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Xiāo Mólǔ, the Left Yílíbì, was appointed Commissioner-in-Chief of the Khitan Traveling Palace (Qìdān Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ).
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Gāolì dispatched an envoy to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngxū,
officials were prohibited from engaging in lending or trading within their jurisdiction.
On the day Wùchén,
as the Grand Empress Dowager was unwell,
a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners within five hundred *lǐ* of the temporary residence.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Grand Empress Dowager passed away.
In the fourth year, spring, in the first month, on the first day Rénshēn,
envoys were dispatched to inform Sòng and Xià of the mourning.
Went to the Yāzihé River to fish.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Sòng dispatched an envoy bearing a painted portrait of the Sòng ruler.
On the day Dīnghài,
Yēlǜ Pōdé, who managed the affairs of Yìzhōu, completed his term of office;
the local people pleaded for him to remain,
and permission was granted.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
an imperial edict instructed the Yílíbì: regarding all capital cases tried across the circuits,
even if the judgment was complete,
another prefecture or county must be ordered to review the case again;
if there were no wrongs,
then the execution should proceed;
if the person claimed a wrong,
the case must be reported immediately to the throne.
On the day Gēngxū,
went to Yú'ér Luò.
In the third month, on the day Wùyín,
brave and swift individuals from Tiāndé, Zhènwǔ, Dōngshèng, and other locations were recruited
and registered as soldiers.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
paid respects at Qìng Líng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Sòng dispatched an envoy to offer condolences and sacrifices.
In the fifth month, on the first day Gēngwǔ,
the posthumous honorific title “Qīn'āi Huánghòu” (Empress Qīn'āi) was conferred upon the deceased Grand Empress Dowager.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
she was interred at Qìng Líng.
Xià State and Gāolì dispatched envoys to attend the ceremony.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
went to Yǒng'ān Shān to clear the heat.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Xiāo Gé, the King of Zhèng and Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs
and transferred and enfeoffed as King of Chǔ;
Rénxiān, the King of Wú and Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
a regulation was enacted: officials in charge of the imperial treasuries who stole more than two strings of cash
could be reported by their slaves or bondservants.
On the day Rénwǔ,
hunted at Hēilǐng.
Winter, in the tenth month, on the first day Wùxū,
Hóugǔ, who was Joint Manager of the Metropolitan Commandant of Dōngjīng, was appointed Southern Court Grand King;
Xīdì, the Military Governor of Bǎo'ānjūn, was appointed Khitan Six Tribes Grand King (Xī Liùbù Dà Wáng).
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the Rebirth (Zàishēng) and Kindling-Wood Ceremony (Cháicè Lǐ) were performed,
and a feast was held for the officials at Bāfāng Pō.
On the day Gēngchén,
resided at Qīngfēngdiàn Hall to receive the Grand Investiture Ceremony (Dà Cè Lǐ).
A general amnesty was granted.
Rénxiān, the King of Wú, was appointed Vice Marshal of the troops and horses of Nánjīng
and transferred and enfeoffed as King of Suí.
On the day Rénwǔ,
paid respects at the palaces of Tàizǔ and the various emperors.
On the day Bǐngxū,
sacrificed at Mùyè Shān.
The manufacture of jade artifacts was prohibited.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the ban on camel hair (Tuóní) and otter fur coats was lifted.
On the day Yǐsì,
the gentry and commoners were permitted to keep eagles.
On the day Xīnhài,
Xiāo Gé, the King of Chǔ and Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, was reinstated as Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐsì,
Chóngyuán, the Imperial Grand Uncle, was granted a metal plaque (Jīn Quàn).
In this year,
the Imperial Prince Jùn was born.
In the fifth year, spring,
went to Chūnzhōu.
Summer, in the sixth month, on the first day Jiǎzǐ,
the imperial retinue halted at Nàgě Luò.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Xiāo Āsù, the Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Northern Prefecture Chancellor;
Yēlǜ Yǐxīn, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs;
Zhāgě, the Tìyǐn, was appointed Military Governor of Liáoxīngjūn;
Xiè Jiānú, the King of Lǔ, was appointed Military Governor of Wǔdìngjūn;
Tiēbù, the King of Wú and Metropolitan Commandant of Dōngjīng, was appointed Metropolitan Commandant of Xījīng.
Autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Xiāo Mólǔ, the Xiāngwěn of the Wūgǔ Dìliè, was appointed Left Yílíbì.
Winter, in the tenth month, on the first day Rénzǐ,
proceeded to Nánjīng
and sacrificed to Xīngzōng at Jiāníngdiàn Hall.
In the eleventh month,
hunting was prohibited.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénxū,
Xī Mǎliù, the Northern Court Línyá, was appointed Right Yílíbì.
Wú Zhàn, the Participant in Determining Governmental Affairs (Cānzhī Zhèngshì), was stripped of his rank and made a commoner
for fraudulently listing his younger brother, Xún, in the official registers.
In this year,
the Emperor presided over Bǎifúdiàn Hall,
and conferred degrees on one hundred and fifteen Jinshì candidates, including Liáng Yuán.
In the sixth year, spring,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
Summer, in the fifth month, on the first day Wùzǐ,
Yēlǜ Bái, the Supervising Compiler of the National History (Jiānxiū Guóshǐ), requested the compilation and arrangement of the Emperor’s imperial poems and *fù* (rhapsodies),
and Bái was also ordered to write the preface.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the imperial retinue halted at Nàgě Luò.
In the sixth month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
Gāo Jiānú, the Xiāngwěn of the Nǚzhēn of the Northeast Route, was appointed Tìyǐn.
On the day Rénxū,
envoys were dispatched to record and review prisoners.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Imperial Academy (Guózǐ Jiān) was established in Zhōngjīng,
and orders were given to sacrifice to the former Sages and former Teachers at the appropriate times.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Rénxiān, the King of Suí, was appointed Northern Court Grand King,
and was granted the imperial edict written by the Emperor.
Winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the imperial retinue halted at Ǒusī Diàn.
In the seventh year, spring, in the third month, on the day Gēngxū,
went to Chūnzhōu.
Yēlǜ Yǐxīn was appointed to manage the affairs of the Northern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
officials and common people were prohibited from keeping the Hǎidōngqīng falcon.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
cleared the heat at Yǒng'ān Shān.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
paid respects at Qìng Líng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Xiāo Ālà, the King of Chén and Metropolitan Commandant of Dōngjīng, was executed.
Sixth month, Rénzǐ *shuò* (first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
Jiǎzǐ (day),
Xiāo Mólǔ was made Jìedùshǐ of the Shùnyì Army.
Dīngmǎo (day),
the Emperor proceeded to the Hóngyì, Yǒngxīng, and Chóngdé Palaces to perform sacrifices.
Willow shooting was held,
a feast was granted,
and rewards were bestowed according to rank.
Wùchén (day),
the Rebirth Ceremony was performed,
and the ministers were again ordered to divide into teams and shoot the willow.
Dīngchǒu (day),
Nièlǔgǔ, King of Chǔ Guó, was put in charge of the Southern Chancellery of Military Affairs (Zhī Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì).
Autumn, ninth month, Dīngchǒu (day),
the imperial carriage halted at Ǒusī Diàn.
Winter, twelfth month, Rénwǔ (day),
Yēlǜ Ālǐzhī, who was in charge of Huánglóng Fǔ affairs, was made Great King of the Southern Department (Nányuàn Dàwáng).
Basic Annals Twenty-two: Dàozōng (II)
Eighth Year. Spring, first month, Guǐchǒu (day),
went to the Yāzǐ Hé (River).
Second month,
the imperial carriage halted at Nàgě Luò.
Third month, Wùshēn *shuò* (day),
Xiāo Gé, King of Chǔ, retired from office,
and was promoted and enfeoffed as King of Zhèng Guó.
Summer, fifth month,
Wúdúwǎn Tìyǐn Tún Tūgě and others requested to present annual tribute of horses and camels,
which was permitted.
Sixth month, Bǐngzǐ *shuò* (day),
the imperial carriage halted at Tuōgǔliè.
Xīnchǒu (day),
Xī Mǎliù, the Right Yílíbì, was made Great King of the Six Xī Departments.
In this month,
at the Qīngliáng Hall, the Emperor approved Wáng Dǐng and ninety-two other successful *jìnshì* candidates.
Autumn, seventh month, Jiǎzǐ (day),
shot a bear at Wàishìlà.
Winter, tenth month, Jiǎxū *shuò* (day),
the imperial carriage halted at Dúlújīn.
Twelfth month, Gēngchén (day),
Xiāo Túgǔcí, who was in charge of the Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs, was made Northern Chancellor of Military Affairs (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ).
Guǐwèi (day),
the Emperor proceeded to Xījīng (Western Capital).
Wùzǐ (day),
the Empress Dowager performed the Rebirth Ceremony,
and a limited amnesty was granted to prisoners in Xījīng.
Ninth Year. Spring, first month, Xīnhài (day),
the Emperor proceeded to Yuānyāng Luò.
Xīnwèi (day),
the private sale of copper by the populace was forbidden.
Third month, Xīnwèi (day),
Zhēn, the Ruler of Sòng, died,
and his nephew Shǔ succeeded to the throne as his adopted son.
Summer, fifth month, Bǐngwǔ (day),
Rénxiān, Prince of Suí, was made Southern Chancellor of Military Affairs (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ),
and was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince Xǔ.
In this month,
the Emperor sought refuge from the summer heat at Hélǐjué.
Autumn, seventh month, Bǐngchén (day),
went to Tàizǐ Shān (Prince Mountain).
Wùwǔ (day),

Huáng Tàishū Chóngyuán, along with his son Nièlǔgǔ, King of Chǔ Guó, Chén Liù, King of Chén Guó, Xiāo Húdǔ (Assistant Official of the Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs), Tiēbù, Prince of Wèi, Nièlàpǔgǔ (Línyá), Xiāo Diélǐdé (Commander of Armies), Fùmǎ Dūwèi Cān and his younger brothers Zhúzhě and Túgǔ, Yēlǜ Guōjiǔ (Xiángwěn of the Banner and Drum Yèlà), Xī Shū (Wénbān Tàibǎo), Wūgǔ (Tídiǎn of the Inner Treasury), Díbùgǔ and Àndá (Huìwèi Zuǒ Tàibǎo), Hánjiānú and Bǎoshénnú (Vice Palace Commissioners), totaling four hundred people,
incited and coerced the crossbow army to attack the temporary imperial residence.

At that time, Rénxiān, Prince Xǔ and Southern Chancellor of Military Affairs, Yēlǜ Yǐxīn, Prince Zhào and Official in Charge of the Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs, Xiāo Tánggǔ, Southern Premier, Xiāo Hánjiānú, Northern Commissioner of the Department of the Court, Xiāo Wéixìn, Northern Vice Chancellor of Military Affairs, Yēlǜ Liáng, Commissioner of the Dūnmù Palace, and others led several thousand Palace Guards and soldiers to defend against them.
Nièlǔgǔ leaped forward on his horse,
intending to fight,
but was shot and killed by Bóhǎi Āsī, the Xiángwěn of the Imperial Attendants,
and Hùwèi Sū.
Jǐwèi (day),
the families of the rebel faction were executed (by wiping out the clan).
Gēngshēn (day),
Chóngyuán fled into the Great Desert,
and committed suicide.
Xīnyǒu (day),
edicts were issued to soothe all circuits.
Rénxū (day),
Rénxiān was made Northern Chancellor of Military Affairs,
promoted and enfeoffed as Prince Sòng,
and given the additional title Shàngfù.
Yēlǜ Yǐxīn was made Southern Chancellor of Military Affairs.
Xiāo Hánjiānú was made Supreme Commander of the Palace Guards (Diànqián Dū Diǎnjiǎn),
and enfeoffed as Prince Jīng.
Xiāo Wéixìn and Yēlǜ Fēngjiānú were both promoted to Crown Prince’s Grand Tutor (Tàizǐ Tàifù).

The Palace Guard officials Xiāo Yǐxīn, Huíhú Hǎilín, Niǎolǐ, Yēlǜ Tàbùyě, and Āsī, along with the Palace Servants Jílǐgē, Xiámò, Yǐxīn, and Zhǐlǔ, were all granted the rank of Upper General (Shàng Jiāngjūn).
The various guards, soldiers, cooks, crossbowmen, umbrella bearers, and others, totaling over three hundred people,
were each granted official posts according to their differences in rank.
Yēlǜ Liáng, who had secretly informed about Chóngyuán’s rebellion,
was ordered to take charge of the Yílíjǐn Fáng (Chancellery) of the Lateral Tents,
and was made Chief Commander (Dū Bùshǔ) of the Chinese (Hàn Rén) Temporary Palace.
Guǐhài (day),
Tiēbù petitioned, claiming he had been coerced by Chóngyuán and the others.
An edict stripped him of his title and reduced him to a commoner,
banishing him to Zhènzhōu.
Wùchén (day),
black and white sheep were used to sacrifice to Heaven.
Eighth month, Gēngwǔ *shuò* (day),
envoys were dispatched to comfort the officials and people of Nánjīng (Southern Capital).
Guǐyǒu (day),
Yēlǜ Tàbùyě, Commissioner of the Yǒngxīng Palace, having distinguished service in suppressing the rebellion,
was made Assistant Official of the Diǎnjiǎn Directorate (Tóng Zhī Diǎnjiǎn Sī Shì).
Winter, tenth month, Wùchén *shuò* (day),
the Emperor proceeded to Xīngwáng Sì (Temple).
Gēngwǔ (day),
Yēlǜ Héshù, Grand Tutor (Tàibǎo) of the Six Departments, was put in charge of the affairs of the Southern Great King.
In this month,
the imperial carriage halted at Ǒusī Diàn.
Eleventh month, Xīnchǒu (day),
Xiāo Jiǔgē, Southern Commissioner of the Department of the Court, was made Northern Premier (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng).
Jǐwèi (day),
the deceased Yēlǜ Yìxiān, formerly Prince of Fùchūn Commandery, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Xǔ.
In this year,
the Imperial Son Jùn was enfeoffed as Prince Liáng.
Tenth Year. Spring, first month, Jǐhài (day),
the Emperor proceeded north.
Second month,
the people of Nánjīng were forbidden from drawing water to plant *jīngdào* (early-maturing rice).
Autumn, seventh month, Rénshēn (day),
an edict ordered the judgment of prisoners throughout all circuits.
Xīnsì (day),
monks and nuns were forbidden from privately going to the temporary imperial residence [Xíngzài],
and falsely predicting misfortune or fortune to obtain wealth.
Ninth month, Rénwú (day),
the Emperor proceeded to Huáizhōu,
and paid respects at the temples of Tàizōng and Mùzōng.
Winter, tenth month, Rénchén *shuò* (day),
the imperial carriage halted at Zhōngjīng (Central Capital).
Wùwǔ (day),
the private carving and printing of documents by the populace was forbidden.
Eleventh month, Jiǎzǐ (day),
the regulations for the clothing of officials and commoners were established.
Xīnwèi (day),
slaughtering was forbidden on the six vegetarian fast days.
Dīngchǒu (day),
an edict ordered the search for missing classics and records from the Qiánwén Pavilion,
and scholar officials were appointed to collate them.
Gēngchén (day),
Hán Xièshí, Jìedùshǐ of the Zhāngguó Army, was made Tìyǐn.
An edict forbade Nánjīng from privately manufacturing imperial colored satin,
privately trading iron,
or drinking alcohol at inappropriate times.
It was ordered that the Three Directorates of Nánjīng
hold feasts for the officers and soldiers every spring and autumn using public funds.
Twelfth month, Guǐsì (day),
Xiāo Wūgǔnì, Northern Great King, was made Chief Commander of the Qìdān Temporary Palace.
In this year,
Nánjīng and Xījīng had great harvests.
Xiányōng First Year. Spring, first month, Xīnyǒu *shuò* (day),
the civil and military officials conferred the honorary title "Shèngwén Shénwǔ Quán Gōng Dàlüè Guǎngzhì Zǒngrén Ruìxiào Tiānyòu Huángdì."
The reign title was changed,
and a general amnesty was declared.
Jùn, Prince Liáng, was formally designated Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ),
and officials, both internal and external, were granted differing promotions in rank.
Jiǎzǐ (day),
went to Yúér Luò.
Gēngyín (day),
an edict ordered that whenever the holidays Zhēngdàn, Chóngwǔ, and Dōngzhì occurred,
separate memorials of congratulations should be presented to the Eastern Palace [Dōnggōng, the Crown Prince].
Third month, Dīnghài (day),
Yáng Jì, who was in charge of Xīngzhōng Fǔ affairs, was put in charge of the Chancellery of Military Affairs (Zhī Shūmìyuàn Shì).
Summer, fourth month, Xīnmǎo (day),
because Zhāng Sìfù, who was in charge of the Chancellery of Military Affairs, was ill,
he was transferred to be in charge of Xīngzhōng Fǔ affairs.
Gēngzǐ (day),
the Emperor sought refuge from the summer heat at Tuōgǔliè.
Fifth month, Xīnsì (day),
Xià Guó sent envoys to present tribute.
Autumn, seventh month, Bǐngzǐ (day),
because the Empress Dowager shot and captured a bear,
rewards were bestowed upon the hundred officials according to rank.
Eighth month, Bǐngshēn (day),
a guest star trespassed into the Tìanmiào constellation.
An edict ordered all circuits to guard against bandits and thieves,
and strictly enforce fire prohibitions.
Ninth month, Yǐhài (day),
the imperial carriage halted at Ǒusī Diàn.
Dīngchǒu (day),
Zàogǔ, the Left Yílíbì, was made Mèngfù Chǎngwěn.
Winter, tenth month, Dīnghài *shuò* (day),
the Emperor proceeded to Yīwūlǘ Shān.
Jǐhài (day),
the Empress Dowager shot and captured a tiger,
a great banquet was held for the assembled ministers,
and they were ordered to compose poems.
Eleventh month, Rénxū (day),
there was a star, large as a measure (*dǒu*),
moving retrograde,
with a faint sound.
Twelfth month, Jiǎwǔ (day),
Rénxiān, Prince of Liáo, was made Resident Grand Marshal of Nánjīng (Nánjīng Liúshǒu),
and was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince Jìn.
Xīnhài (day),
Xiāo Wéixìn, Resident Grand Marshal of Nánjīng, was made Left Yílíbì.
Rénzǐ (day),
Yínghuò (Mars) traveled alongside the moon,
from dawn until noon.
went to the Yāzǐ Hé.
Sòng envoy Wáng Yán, who was offering New Year congratulations, died.
He was sent back with proper rites.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
visited Shānyú Diàn.
The second month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict commanded Yáo Jǐngxíng, Military Governor (*Jiédùshǐ*) of Wǔdìng Prefecture,
inquiring about governance,
and appointed him Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ*).
The second month, on the *xīnsì* day,
appointed Yēlǜ Hánfú'nú, the Commander (*Xiángwěn*) of the Northeast Circuit, as Prince of the Northern Chancellery (*Běiyuàn Dàwáng*).
On the *rénwǔ* day,
a comet was seen in the west.
Summer, the fourth month,
continuous heavy rain fell.
The fifth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Tuōgǔliè.
On the *xīnsì* day,
appointed Liú Shēn, Administrator of the Ministry of Revenue (*Hùbù Shǐ*), as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (*Shūmì Fùshǐ*).
The sixth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Huíhú (Uyghurs) came to offer tribute.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Zǔbǔ came to offer tribute.
Autumn, the seventh month, the first day (*guǐchǒu*),
appointed Xiāo Shùzhě, Commissioner of Pacification (*Zhāotǎoshǐ*) of the Northwest Circuit, as Chancellor of the Northern Administration (*Běifǔ Zǎixiàng*);
Xiāo Wéixìn, the Left *Yílíbì*, as Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ*);
and Yēlǜ Báitìyǐn as Concurrent Administrator of the Affairs of the Southern Chancellery (*Tóngzhī Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì*).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Yáo Jǐngxíng, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery, retired.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
reviewed the prisoners.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Jǐngxíng was restored to his former post.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
went to Ǒusī Diàn.
Due to the drought that year,
envoys were sent to relieve the poor people in Shānhòu.
The ninth month, the first day (*rénzǐ*),
there was a solar eclipse.
Appointed Hán Fú, Participating Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Cānzhī Zhèngshì*), as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Winter, the twelfth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
appointed Yáng Jì, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Zhī Shūmì Yuàn Shì*), as Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery;
and Liú Shēn, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, as Participating Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the monk Shǒu Zhì was granted the title of Acting Minister of Education (*Shǒu Sītú*).
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
appointed Héshù, Resident Administrator (*Liúshǒu*) of Xījīng, as Prince of the Southern Chancellery (*Nányuàn Dàwáng*).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
appointed Xiāo Shùzhě as Military Governor of Wǔdìng Prefecture.
That year,
degrees were granted to 101 successful candidates, including *Jìnshì* Zhāng Zhēn, at the Yǒng'ān Diàn.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *xīnhài* day,
went to the Yāzǐ Hé.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
fished at the Ānliú Diàn.
The third month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the Sòng ruler Zhù died;
his son Xū succeeded to the throne,
and sent an envoy to announce the mourning;
immediately sent Xiāo Tàbùyě, Grand Guardian (*Tàibǎo*) of the Right Palace Guard, and Chén Jué, Academician of the Hanlin Academy (*Hànlín Xuéshì*), and others to offer condolences and sacrifices.
The intercalary month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the camp of the Imperial Guard caught fire.
Money, grain, and horses were granted in varying amounts.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at the Northern Diàn of Chūnzhōu.
On the *yǐsì* day,
appointed Xiāo Wùgǔnì as Chancellor of the Northern Administration.
Summer, the fifth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Nàgě Luò.
On the *rényín* day,
granted horses to the officials and various laborers accompanying the imperial carriage.
The sixth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the relevant officials reported that Yáng Cóng, a civilian from Xīnchéng County, had plotted rebellion,
and had illicitly appointed officials.
The Emperor said:
“These common people are ignorant.
This is merely child’s play.”
Only the ringleader was banished;
the rest were released.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Sòng sent an envoy to present posthumous gifts from their former Emperor.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Sòng, having installed the new Emperor,
sent Chén Xiāng to report the enthronement;
immediately sent Xiāo Túgǔcí, Administrator of Huánglóng Prefecture (*Zhī Huánglóngfǔ Shì*), and Mǎ Xuàn, Secretariat Drafter (*Zhōngshū Shèrén*), to offer congratulations.
On the *rénxū* day,
Xiāo Tánggǔ, Prince of Hán and Chancellor of the Southern Administration (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*), retired.
On the *rénshēn* day,
appointed Yēlǜ Ruǐnú, Military Governor of Guǎngdé Prefecture, as Chancellor of the Southern Administration;
and Zhào Huī, Administrator of Finance (*Dùzhī Shǐ*), as Participating Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) was visible during the day,
for a total of thirty-five days.
The ninth month, on the *wùxū* day,
an edict ordered grain rations to be given to prisoners throughout the circuits.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
visited Nánjīng.
Winter, the eleventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
Xià State sent envoys to present a Huíhú monk, a gold Buddha, and Buddhist scriptures (*Fànjué Jīng*).
The twelfth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
appointed Liú Shēn, Participating Administrator of Governmental Affairs, as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs;
Gāo Bā, Commander of the Northeast Circuit, as Prince of the Southern Chancellery;
and Zhāng Xiàojié, Academician Directly Serving in the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì*), as Participating Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
appointed Zhāng Xiàojié as Concurrent Administrator of the Affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *dīngsì* day,
performed the Rite of Rebirth (*Zàishēng Lǐ*),
and granted amnesty to those sentenced to death or lesser punishments.
That month,
Lǐ Liàngzuò, King of Xià State, died.
That year,
Nánjīng suffered drought and locusts.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month, the first day (*jiǎxū*),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
On the *xīnsì* day,
changed the title of Yi Prefecture Commissioner of Military Affairs (*Bīngmǎ Shǐ*) to Commissioner of Pacification (*Ānfǔ Shǐ*).
On the *dīnghài* day,
hunted at Tàn Shān.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
sent envoys to relieve the starving people of Xījīng.
The second month, the first day (*jiǎchén*),
an edict commanded the Office of the Marshal (*Yuánshuài Fǔ*) to recruit soldiers.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Bǐngcháng, son of Lǐ Liàngzuò, King of Xià State, sent an envoy to announce the mourning.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
promulgated the Imperial Exegesis on the *Huáyán Jīng*.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
traveled north.
The third month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
sent envoys to Xià State to offer condolences and sacrifices.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
relieved the starving people of Yìngzhōu.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an edict decreed that in Nánjīng, excluding land designated for military use,
the rest of the land could be used to plant rice.
On the *gēngyín* day,
relieved the starving people of Shuòzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Bǐngcháng of Xià State sent an envoy to present posthumous objects of his father, Liàngzuò.
Summer, the fourth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Āsàlán Huíhú (Uyghurs) sent envoys to offer tribute.
The fifth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Tuōgǔliè.
The sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Northwest Circuit experienced a rain of grain,
covering an area of thirty *lǐ* square.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
appointed Yēlǜ Zhàosān, *Línyá* of the Northern Chancellery, as Prince of the Northern Chancellery;
and Xiāo Sùsà, the Right *Yílíbì*, as Resident Administrator of Zhōngjīng.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
established the Headquarters of the General Commander (*Dūtǒng Jūnsī*) for the Wūgǔ Díliè Tribe.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
hunted at Hēilǐng.
That month,
Nánjīng experienced continuous heavy rain,
and an earthquake.
The ninth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Ǒusī Diàn.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
granted partial amnesty to prisoners in Nánjīng sentenced to banishment or lesser crimes.
Yǒngqīng, Wǔqīng, Āncì, Gù'ān, Xīnchéng, Guīyì, and Róngchéng counties suffered floods,
and were exempted from one year’s tax (*zū*).
On the *wùchén* day,
Lǐ Bǐngcháng was invested as King of Xià State.
The twelfth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Xià State sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month,
the Zǔbǔ rebelled;
appointed Rénxiān, Prince of Jìn, as Commissioner of Pacification of the Northwest Circuit,
leading the Forbidden Army to suppress them.
Summer, the sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Tuōgǔliè.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Tǔbō (Tibetans) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *rénxū* day,
appointed Xiāo Wéixìn, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery, to concurrently administer the affairs of the Northern Chancellery (*Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì*).
Autumn, the seventh month, the first day (*yǐchǒu*),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùchén* day,
Xià State sent envoys to express gratitude for the investiture.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict prohibited imperial relatives from relying on their power to oppress and exploit the common people.
The eighth month,
paid homage at Qìng Líng.
The ninth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Rénxiān sent someone to report the victory over the Zǔbǔ.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage stopped at Ǒusī Diàn.
The eleventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict stipulated that the Vice Commissioners of the Four Quarters Office (*Sìfāng Guǎn Fùshǐ*) must only be filled by Qìdān people.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Pōu'ālǐ Tribe of the Five States rebelled;
commanded Xiāo Sùsà to suppress them.
On the *wùshēn* day of the intercalary month,
Lǐ Bǐngcháng (李秉常), King of the Xià (夏) State, sent an envoy to beg for the conferral of seals and ribbons.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the monk Zhìfú (志福) was promoted to Acting *Sītú* (司徒).
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the ceremony for the Crown Prince's rebirth was performed,
reducing the penalty for all criminals (*tú* and below) in all circuits by one degree.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered all officials to discuss state affairs in court.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Five Tribes (Wǔguó, 五國) came to submit,
and presented local products.
The sixth year, spring, first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
went to Qiān'é Luò (千鵝濼).
Second month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Zǔbǔ (阻卜) came to pay homage at court,
and offered local tribute.
Summer, fourth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Northwest Circuit Pacification and Patrol Office (Xīběilù Zhāotǎo Sī, 西北路招討司) brought the surrendered Zǔbǔ chieftains to the temporary imperial residence (*xíngzài*).
Fifth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
sought respite from the heat at Tuōgǔliè (拖古烈).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Bureaucratic Examination for the Worthy and Good (Xiánliáng Kē, 賢良科) was established.
An edict commanded that all those who applied for this examination
must first submit 100,000 words on their field of study.
Sixth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the Zǔbǔ came to court.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Bái (耶律白), the *Tìyǐn* (惕隱), was appointed Administrator of Zhōngjīng (中京 Liúshǒu).
In this month,
at the Yǒng'ān Diàn (永安殿), the Emperor conferred degrees upon 138 *jìnshì* (進士), including Zhào Tíngmù (趙廷睦).
Autumn, seventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
hunted at Hélǔniètè (合魯聶特).
Eighth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Bái died.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as the Prince of Liáoxī Commandery (Liáoxī Jùnwáng, 遼西郡王).
Ninth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
visited Ǒusī Diàn (藕絲淀).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
because Mǎ Xībái's (馬希白) poetic talent was brilliant and marvelous,
such that ten clerks could not keep up with his dictation,
he was summoned for an examination.
Winter, tenth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Five Tribes' (Wǔguó) chiefs came to court.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Northwest Circuit Pacification and Patrol Office captured Zǔbǔ chieftains and presented them.
Eleventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the sale of raw and finished iron to the territory of the Huíhú (回鶻), the Zǔbǔ, and other groups was prohibited.
Twelfth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the two monks Yuánshì (圓釋) and Fǎjūn (法鈞) were both promoted to Acting *Sīkōng* (司空).
On the *jǐwèi* day,
on account of the Kūnníng Jié (坤寧節),
an amnesty was granted to those sentenced to death and below.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Hàn (漢) people were forbidden from hunting.
The seventh year, spring, first month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
went to Yāzǐ Hé (鴨子河).
Second month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Nǚzhí (女直) presented horses.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yáo Jǐngxíng (姚景行), Grand Counselor of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ, 南院樞密使), was appointed to Govern Xīngzhōng Fǔ (興中府).
Third month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
for their meritorious service in punishing the Five Tribes (Wǔguó),

Pú Yán (蒲延, Governor of Huánglóng Fǔ), Gāo Yuánjì (高元紀, Military Commissioner of Huáihuà Jūn), and Gāo Zhèng (高正, Surveillance Commissioner of Yì Zhōu) were all promoted to Senior General of the Left Guard of a Thousand Oxen (Qiānniú Wèi Shàngjiāngjūn, 千牛衞上將軍);
Xiāo Táosuō (蕭陶蘇斡, Military Commissioner of the Five Tribes) and Dà Róng (大榮, Defense Commissioner of Níngjiāng Zhōu) were both promoted to Military Commissioner of Jìngjiāng Jūn.
Visited Hēishuǐ (黑水).
Summer, fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
went to Nàgě Luò (納葛濼).
On the *yǐhài* day,
the making of short or narrow cloth or silk that did not meet the standard measurements was prohibited.
Sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Tǔbō (吐蕃) came to present tribute.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Gāo Bā (高八), Grand Prince of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Dàwáng), retired.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day (the first day of the month),
Hélǐzhī (合里只), the *Xiángwěn* (詳穩) of the Northeast Circuit, was appointed Grand Prince of the Southern Chancellery;
Shídénú (拾得奴), the Pacification and Patrol Commissioner of the Southwest Sector, was appointed Grand Prince of the Six Xī (奚) Tribes.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
envoys were dispatched to investigate and interrogate prisoners in the Five Capitals (Wǔjīng).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
went to Ǒusī Diàn.
Eighth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the Buddha's relics (bones) were placed in the Zhāoxiān (招仙) Pagoda;
hunting was halted,
and slaughtering was prohibited.
Winter, tenth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
went to Yīwūlǘ Shān (醫巫閭山).
On the *rénxū* day,
Yēlǜ Ruǐnú (耶律蘂奴), Prime Minister of the Southern Chancellery (Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Nánjīng (南京 Tǒngjūnshǐ).
On the *wùchén* day,
visited the Qián Líng (乾陵) mausoleum.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered all officials to discuss military and state affairs in court.
Eleventh month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
remitted the rent for displaced people in Nánjīng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
relieved the famine victims in Ráozhōu (饒州).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Gāolì (高麗, Koryŏ) sent envoys to present tribute.
Twelfth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Yēlǜ Húdǔ (耶律胡覩), Grand Commissioner of the Qìdān (契丹) Temporary Palace, was appointed to Govern the Northern Chancellery (Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì);
Xiāo Wéixìn (蕭惟信), who Governed the Northern Chancellery, was made Prime Minister of the Southern Chancellery,
concurrently serving as Grand Commissioner of the Qìdān Temporary Palace.
On the *dīngsì* day,

Lǐ Zhòngxǐ (李仲禧, Hàn People Temporary Palace Grand Commissioner), Liú Mù (劉霂, Northern Chancellery Commissioner of Imperial Edicts), Wáng Guān (王觀, Vice Grand Counselor), and Yáng Xīnggōng (楊興工, Director of Palace Secretariat) were each granted the imperial surname.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Huíhú (回鶻) came to present tribute.
In this year,
a *dǒu* of grain in Chūnzhōu (春州) cost six *qián*.
Basic Annals 23, Dàozōng (道宗) (3)
The eighth year, spring, first month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Yēlǜ Cháo (耶律巢), *Xiángwěn* of the Wūgǔdíliè (烏古敵烈) Tribe, and others reported a victory on the northern frontier.
Because many people were killed in the battle,
monks were fed in Nánjīng and Zhōngjīng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
went to Yú'ér Luò (魚兒濼).
On the *rén'yín* day,
dim fog persisted for several days.
Second month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Northern and Southern Chancellery reported that there were no matters requiring discussion.
On the *rénxū* day,
for meritorious service in punishing the Northern Tribes,
Yēlǜ Cháo, *Xiángwěn* of the Wūgǔdíliè Tribe, was appointed to Govern the Northern Grand Prince's Office (Zhī Běiyuàn Dàwáng Shì);
Xiāo Ālǔdài (蕭阿魯帶), the Commander (Dūjiān), was appointed *Xiángwěn* of the Wūgǔdíliè Tribe,
and promoted to Senior General of the Left Gate Guard (Zuǒ Jiānmén Wèi Shàngjiāngjūn).
On the *wùchén* day,
due to famine,
taxes and rents in Wǔ'ān Zhōu (武安州) were remitted,
and relief was provided to the people of Ēn (恩), Wèi (蔚), Shùn (順), Huì (惠), and other prefectures.
Third month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the relevant authorities reported that over 3,000 people in the three prefectures of Chūnzhōu, Tàizhōu (泰州), and Níngjiāng Zhōu (寧江州) wished to become monks and nuns
and receive the full monastic precepts;
permission was granted.
Summer, fourth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided to the people of Yì (義) and Ráo (饒) prefectures.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the imperial temporary residence was established at Tǎlǐshě (塔里捨).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
sought respite from the heat at Tuōgǔliè.
Fifth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Rénxiān (仁先), Prince of Jìn (晉王), died.
Sixth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
relief was provided to the poor people of Yì Zhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
relief was provided in Zhōngjīng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
relief was provided in Xīngzhōng Fǔ.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yáng Jì (楊績), Prime Minister of the Northern Chancellery (Běifǔ Zǎixiàng), was enfeoffed as Prince Zhào (趙王);
Yēlǜ Guān (耶律觀), Vice Grand Counselor, was appointed Grand Councilor Participant (Cānzhī Zhèngshì) concurrently Governing the Southern Chancellery.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Gāolì (高麗) sent envoys to present tribute.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
because Jìn Wéngāo (靳文高) of Qìngzhōu (慶州) lived together with eight generations of his family,
an edict granted him a noble rank.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
relief was provided to the famine victims in Ráozhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
visited Hēilǐng (黑嶺).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the five verses of the *Huáyán Jīng* (華嚴經, Avataṃsaka Sūtra) personally copied by the Emperor were shown to the assembled officials.
Intercalary month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
shot a bear at Gǔyáng Shān (羖羊山).
Eighth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Hóugǔ (侯古), Prince of Húntóng Commandery (混同郡王), died.
Envoys were sent to offer sacrifices.
Ninth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the imperial temporary residence was established at Ǒusī Diàn.
Winter, tenth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Guān, Grand Councilor Participant, falsely issued an edict to build a private residence;
he was demoted to commoner status.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Huíhú came to present tribute.
Eleventh month, on the *gēngxū* day,
taxes in Zǔzhōu (祖州) were remitted.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
due to heavy snow,
people were permitted to gather firewood in restricted areas.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
money was granted to the poor households of the Yánchāng Gōng (延昌宮) Palace.
Twelfth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Yēlǜ Zhòngxǐ (耶律仲禧, Hàn People Temporary Palace Grand Commissioner) was enfeoffed as Duke of Hánguó (韓國公);
Zhào Huī (趙徽, Vice Grand Counselor and Grand Councilor Participant) was sent out as Military Commissioner of Wǔdìng Jūn (武定軍);
Chái Dézī (柴德滋, Vice Grand Counselor) was appointed Grand Councilor Participant;
Yēlǜ Dàbēinú (耶律大悲奴, Hàn People Temporary Palace Vice Commissioner) was promoted to Grand Commissioner;
Xiāo Hánjiānú (蕭韓家奴, Assistant Governing Official of the Southern Chancellery) was appointed to Govern the Office of the Left *Yílíbì* (夷離畢).
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
on account of the Kūnníng Jié,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *gēngyín* day,
one complete Buddhist canon was bestowed upon Gāolì.
The ninth year, spring, first month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
went to Shuāng Luò (雙濼).
Summer, fourth month, on the *rénchén* day,
went to Wàngguó Yá (旺國崖).
In the autumn, the seventh month, day *Jiǎchén*,
hunted at Dàxióng Shān.
On day *Wùshēn*,
the commander of Wūgǔ Díliè reported
that the people of Bāshíliè Díliè had killed their *Jiédùshǐ* (Military Commissioner) and rebelled.
On day *Jǐyǒu*,
an edict ordered the forces of the Wěi Wūgǔ Department to attack them from different routes.
On day *Bǐngyín*,
Nánjīng reported that locusts from Guīyì and Láishuǐ counties had flown into Sòng territory,
and the remainder were eaten by bees.
In the eighth month, day *Bǐngshēn*,
Yēlǜ Zhòngxī was appointed Nányuàn Shūmìshǐ (Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery).
In the ninth month, day *Guǐmǎo*,
stopped the imperial carriage at Dúlújīn.
In winter, the tenth month,
went to Yīnshān,
and then proceeded to Xījīng (Western Capital).
The eleventh month, day *Wùwǔ*,
an edict exempted lands visited by the imperial retinue from rent for one year.
On day *Jiǎzǐ*,
Hélǐzhī, the Nányuàn Dàwáng (Great King of the Southern Chancellery), retired from office.
In the twelfth month, day *Xīnwèi*,
Yēlǜ Yíxīn, who handled affairs of the Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ (Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery), was made Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu (Resident General of the Central Capital);
Yēlǜ Sālā, the Nányuàn Xuānhuīshǐ (Grand Herald of the Southern Chancellery), was made Nányuàn Dàwáng.
On day *Rénchén*,
Gāolì and Xiàguó both sent envoys to offer tribute.
The tenth year, spring, the first month, day *Yǐmǎo*,
went to Yuānyāng Luò.
The second month, day *Guǐwèi*,
remitted the rents and taxes for residents of Píng Zhōu who had returned to their occupations.
On day *Wùzǐ*,
Zǔbǔ came to offer tribute.
The third month, day *Jiǎzǐ*,
went to Tuōgǔliè.
Yēlǜ Cháo was appointed Běiyuàn Dàwáng (Great King of the Northern Chancellery).
Summer, the fourth month,
there was a drought.
On day *Xīnwèi*,
because the Xī man Dálǔ had three generations living together,
he was bestowed an official post and honored.
The fifth month, day *Bǐngyín*,
reviewed prisoners.
The sixth month, day *Wùchén*,
personally set the examination questions for the Presented Scholars (*Jìnshì*).
On day *Rénshēn*,
an edict ordered officials and commoners to speak about successes and failures.
On day *Bǐngzǐ*,
presided over the Yǒngdìng Diàn (Yongding Palace),
questioning the virtuous and competent.
Autumn, the seventh month, day *Bǐngchén*,
went to Qiūshān.
On day *Guǐhài*,
paid respects at Qìnglíng (Qing Mausoleum).
The ninth month, day *Gēngxū*,
visited Dōngjīng (Eastern Capital),
and paid respects at the Èryí and Wǔluán Diàn (Palaces).
On day *Guǐhài*,
performed sacrifice at Mùyè Shān.
Winter, the tenth month, day *Dīngmǎo*,
stopped the imperial carriage at Ǒusī Diàn.
On day *Dīngchǒu*,
an edict ordered the relevant authorities to distribute the *Shǐjì* (Records of the Grand Historian) and the *Hànshū* (Book of Han).
The eleventh month, day *Wùwǔ*,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer tribute.
The twelfth month, day *Xīnsì*,
the name of the next year was changed to Dàkāng,
and a general amnesty was declared.
Dàkāng, the first year, spring, the first month, day *Yǐwèi*,
went to Hùntóng Jiāng.
On day *Rényín*,
provided relief to the famine victims in Yún Zhōu.
The second month, day *Dīngmǎo*,
a fire occurred in Xiáng Zhōu,
and an envoy was dispatched to provide disaster relief.
On day *Yǐyǒu*,
stopped the imperial carriage at Dàyú Luò.
On day *Dīnghài*,
because geese were captured,
the title of the Yīngfángshǐ (Director of the Eagle Falconry), Yēlǜ Yángliù, was raised to Gōngbù Shàngshū (Minister of Works).
The third month, day *Yǐsì*,
commanded the Crown Prince to copy Buddhist scriptures.
Summer, the fourth month, day *Bǐngzǐ*,
provided relief to the famine victims in Píng Zhōu.
On day *Yǐyǒu*,
went to Dú Shān.
Intercalary month, day *Bǐngwǔ*,
provided relief to the famine victims in Píng and Luán two prefectures.
On day *Gēngxū*,
the Imperial Grandson Yánxǐ was born.
The fifth month, day *Jiǎzǐ*,
titles were granted, varying according to rank, to the relatives of the Consort and the staff of the Eastern Palace (*Dōnggōng*).
The sixth month, day *Guǐsì*,
Xī Xièjiānú, the Xīngshèng Gōngshǐ (Director of Xingsheng Palace), was put in charge of the affairs of the Xī Liùbù Dàwáng (Great King of the Six Xī Tribes).
On day *Wùxū*,
Hán Cāo, who handled the affairs of the Sānsīshǐ (Commissioner of the Three Bureaus), was promoted to Sānsīshǐ
because of the increase in funds and grain reserves.
On day *Guǐmǎo*,
envoys were dispatched to investigate the prisoners in all circuits.
Tìyǐn Dàbēinú was appointed Shǐpíngjūn Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioner of Shiping Command),
and Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Adviser to the Government) Chái Dezī was appointed Wǔdìngjūn Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioner of Wuding Command).
On day *Yǐmǎo*,
Tǔfān came to offer tribute.
On day *Bǐngchén*,
an edict commanded the Crown Prince to take overall charge of court affairs,
and simultaneously admonished and instructed him.
Zhào Huī, the Wǔdìngjūn Jiédùshǐ, was appointed Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng (Chancellor of the Southern Administration);
Shūmì Fùshǐ (Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs) Yáng Zūnxù was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
Autumn, the seventh month, day *Xīnyǒu* (first day of the lunar month),
hunted in Píngdì Sōnglín (Pine Forest of Flat Land).
On day *Bǐngyín*,
provided relief to the poor residents of Nánjīng.
The eighth month, day *Gēngyín* (first day of the lunar month),
there was a solar eclipse.
The ninth month, day *Yǐhài*,
stopped the imperial carriage at Ǒusī Diàn.
On day *Jǐmǎo*,
because of the famine in Nánjīng,
rent and taxes were exempted for one year,
and money and grain were also issued for relief.
Winter, the tenth month,
the chiefs of the Northwest Circuit, Xiátā, Chūtā, Shuānggǔ, and others, came to surrender.
The eleventh month, day *Xīnyǒu*,
the Empress was falsely accused,
and ordered to commit suicide;
the entertainers Zhào Wéiyī and Gāo Chángmìng were killed,
and their families and property were confiscated.
The twelfth month, day *Jǐchǒu* (first day of the lunar month),
Yēlǜ Ruǐnú, the Nánjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ (Nanjing Commander), was made Tìyǐn (Uncle-in-Law/Tribal Head);
Yēlǜ Mù, the Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ (Chief Commissioner of the Han People's Traveling Palace), was made Shūmì Fùshǐ;
Xiāo Duólà, who jointly managed the affairs of the Dōngjīng Liúshǒu (Resident General of the Eastern Capital), was made Yílíbì (Liaison Officer).
On day *Gēngyín*,
Zhāng Xiàojié was bestowed the Imperial Surname.
On day *Rénchén*,
Xiāo Yànliù, the Xījīng Liúshǒu, was appointed Zuǒ Yílíbì (Left Liaison Officer).
The second year, spring, the first month, day *Jǐwèi*,
went to the Spring Water (*Chuānshuǐ*).
On day *Gēngchén*,
stopped the imperial carriage at Shuāng Luò.
The second month, day *Wùzǐ*,
provided relief to the famine victims in Huánglóng Fǔ.
On day *Guǐchǒu*,
because Nánjīng Lù (Nanjing Circuit) suffered famine,
rent and taxes were exempted for one year.
The third month, day *Xīnyǒu*,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
On day *Rénxū*,
Diànqián Fùdiǎnjiǎn (Vice Inspector of the Palace Guard) Yēlǜ Xiágǔ was dispatched to announce the mourning to Sòng.
On day *Guǐhài*,
envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Gāolì and Xiàguó.
On day *Dīngmǎo*,
a general amnesty was declared.
On day *Wùyín*,
envoys were dispatched to Sòng and Xià, bringing relics left by the Empress Dowager.
Summer, the sixth month, day *Yǐyǒu* (first day of the lunar month),
the posthumous honorary title Rén Yì Huánghòu (Empress Renyi) was conferred upon the deceased Empress Dowager.
