On the *guǐhài* day,
went to Húntóngjiāng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor passed away at the traveling palace,
aged seventy.
The last will decreed Yānguówáng Yánxǐ to succeed to the throne.
In Winter, the tenth month, day Jǐhài, the first day of the lunar month.
Gāolì Wáng Yóng (高麗王顒) sent an envoy to request investiture and official recognition.
Day Dīngsì.
Wòtèlā (斡特剌) reported a victory in the campaign against Yědǔguā (耶覩刮).
Day Bǐngyín.
Xiāo Délǐdǐ (蕭得里底), Associate Administrator of the Southern Capital Garrison (Nánjīng Liúshǒu Shì), was appointed Administrator of the Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs (Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì).
Day Dīngmǎo.
Sòng (宋) sent Guō Zhīzhāng (郭知章) and Cáo Píng (曹平) to present gifts.
Day Wùchén.
Relief was distributed in Liáozhōu (遼州), where there was a famine.
Furthermore, rents and taxes were exempted for one year.
The eleventh month, day Jiǎxū.
Relief was distributed to the two Jiū (糺) areas, Southern and Northern.
Day Yǐyǒu.
The state of Xiàguó (夏國), upon Sòng (宋) stopping military action,
sent an envoy to express thanks.
The twelfth month, day Jiǎzǐ.
Zhào Xiàoyán (趙孝嚴), Administrator of Governmental Affairs (Cānzhī Zhèngshì), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Provisional Palace (Hànrén Xínggōng Dūbùshǔ).
Liáng Yuán (梁援), Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Provisional Palace, was appointed Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Jūn (遼興軍 Jiédùshǐ).
Sixth year, Spring, the first month, day Guǐyǒu.
Yēlǜ Wúyě (耶律吾也), Prince of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Dàwáng), died.
Day Rénwǔ.
Tū Kǎiqǐ (禿開起), who had retired as Grand Preceptor (Tàishī), was recalled and appointed Prince of the Six Xī (奚) Tribes (Xī Liùbù Dàwáng).
Day Dīnghài.
Went to the Spring Waters (Chūnshuǐ).
Day Xīnmǎo.
Wòtèlā (斡特剌) captured Mógǔsī (磨古斯) and brought him to court.
Day Bǐngshēn.
An edict was issued inquiring about the suffering of the people.
The second month, day Dīngwèi.
Chén Jiānú (陳家奴), Military Commissioner of the Wūgǔ (烏古) Tribe, was appointed Prince of the Southern Chancellery.
Day Jǐyǒu.
Mógǔsī (磨古斯) was executed by dismemberment in the marketplace.
Day Guǐchǒu.
Silk was distributed to the poor citizens of the Five Chancelleries (Wǔyuàn).
Day Xīnyǒu.
Sòng (宋) sent an envoy to announce that the Sòng (宋) ruler Xǔ (煦) had died.
His younger brother Jí (佶) succeeded to the throne.
On the same day, an envoy was dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices.
The third month, day Jiǎshēn.
The restrictions on mountains and forests in Shuòzhōu (朔州) were relaxed.
Summer, the fourth month, day Dīngyǒu, the first day of the lunar month.
There was a solar eclipse.
Day Guǐmǎo.
Went to Tànshān (炭山).
The fifth month, day Rénwǔ.
The Wūgǔ (烏古) tribe attacked Cházhálá (茶扎剌).
They defeated them.
Day Yǐyǒu.
Zhào Xiàoyán (趙孝嚴), Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Provisional Palace, died.
Day Bǐngxū.
The imperial carriage halted at Nàgě Luò (納葛濼).
Day Xīnmǎo.
Sòng (宋) sent an envoy to present posthumous objects of the former emperor.
Day Yǐwèi.
Hélǔ Sàogǔ (何魯掃古), Garrison Administrator of the Eastern Capital (Dōngjīng Liúshǒu), was appointed Tìyǐn (惕隱).
Xiāo Chánggē (蕭常哥), Commissioner of the Southern Chancellery (Nányuàn Xuānhuīshǐ), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Provisional Palace.
The sixth month, day Gēngzǐ.
An envoy was dispatched to congratulate the Sòng (宋) ruler.
Day Xīnchǒu.
Because the official document written by the proper department referred to the Sòng (宋) Emperor
succeeding to the throne (sìwèi)
as
ascending the precious seat (dēng bǎowèi),
an edict was issued stripping the Chancellor Zhèng Zhuān (鄭顓) and others below him of their posts.
Zhuān (顓) was sent out to administer Xīngzhōng Fǔ (興中府) affairs.
Hán Zīràng (韓資讓) was made Military Commissioner of Chóngyì Jūn (崇義軍 Jiédùshǐ).
Hán Jūnyì (韓君義), Vice Censor-in-Chief (Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng), was made Military Commissioner of Guǎngshùn Jūn (廣順軍 Jiédùshǐ).
Day Guǐchǒu.
The chief of the Zǔbǔ (阻卜) came to pay tribute.
Day Wùwǔ.
An envoy was dispatched to review and decide pending prison cases in the Five Capitals (Wǔjīng).
Day Jǐwèi.
Liáng Yuán (梁援), Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Jūn, was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmì Fùshǐ).
Autumn, the seventh month, day Gēngwǔ.
Went to Shālǐng (沙嶺).
Day Rénshēn.
The various tribes of Yědǔguā (耶覩刮) raided the Northwest Circuit (Xīběi Lù).
The eighth month.
Wòtèlā (斡特剌) used troops to defeat them.
An envoy was sent to present the victory report.
The ninth month, day Guǐwèi.
A distance sacrifice (wàngcí) was offered at Mùyè Shān (木葉山).
Day Wùzǐ.
The imperial carriage halted at Ǒusī Diàn (藕絲淀).
Winter, the tenth month, day Rén Yín.
Wáng Shīrú (王師儒), Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Supervisor of National History Compilation (Jiānxiū Guóshǐ).
Day Guǐmǎo.
The various chiefs of the Five Nations (Wǔguó) came to pay tribute.
Day Jiǎyín.
Because of the famine in Píngzhōu (平州),
their rents and taxes were remitted for one year.
The eleventh month, day Rénshēn.
Because Tián Shìróng (田世榮), a citizen of Tiāndé Jūn (天德軍), had three generations living together,
an edict granted him an official post.
He ordered one of his sons to be a Retainer in the Court of the Three Ranks (Sānbānyuàn Zhīhòu).
Day Bǐngzǐ.
The monk Zhìdá (志達) from Yīwūlǘ Shān (醫巫閭山) was summoned to establish an altar in the inner palace.
Day Wùzǐ.
Lǐ Qiánshùn (李乾順), King of Xiàguó (夏國), sent an envoy to request marriage to a princess.
The twelfth month, day Yǐwèi.
The Nǚzhí (女直) sent an envoy to pay tribute.
Day Jǐhài.
Hǎo Jiānú (郝家奴), Administrator of the Affairs of the Right Yílíbì (Yòuyi Lí bì Shì), was appointed Northern Administrator (Běimiàn Línyá).
Day Xīnhài.
An edict commanded Yān Guówáng Yánxǐ (燕國王延禧) to nominate officials for posts below that of Grand General (Dàjiāngjūn).
Day Gēngshēn.
The Tiělí (鐵驪) came to pay tribute.
Sòng (宋) sent an envoy to express thanks.
The Emperor was unwell.
In this year,
Yǔ (俁), the eldest son of Gāolì Wáng Yóng (高麗王顒), was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Hán States (Sānhán Guógōng).
Eighty-seven scholars, including Kāng Bǐngjiǎn (康秉儉), who had passed the imperial examination (Jìnshì), were released [into official service].
Seventh year, Spring, the first month, day Rénxū, the first day of the lunar month.
Despite his illness, [the Emperor] held court in the Qīngfēng Diàn (清風殿) to receive congratulations from all officials and envoys from various states.
That night,
a white vapor, like silk,
descended from the sky.
Black clouds arose in the northwest,
flying swiftly and making noise.
In the north, there were blue, red, black, and white vapors,
mingling together as they fell.
Day Guǐhài.
Went to the Húntóng Jiāng (混同江).
Day Jiǎxū.
The Emperor collapsed and died at the provisional palace,
at the age of seventy.
The testamentary edict named Yān Guówáng Yánxǐ (燕國王延禧) as successor.
The sixth month, day Gēngzǐ.
The honorable posthumous title Rénshèng Dàxiào Wénhuángdì (仁聖大孝文皇帝) was conferred,
and the temple name Dàozōng (道宗) was given.
Appraisal: When Dàozōng (道宗) first ascended the throne,
he sought honest criticism,
inquired about governing principles,
encouraged agriculture and promoted education,
provided disaster relief and cared for the suffering—
all brilliant and observable achievements.
However, after the decree against slander and libel was implemented,
the rewards for informants and accusers grew heavier daily.
All manner of wicked elements arose together,
and crafty slanderers aggressively advanced.
Rebellions afflicted his own kin,
and the imperial foundation gradually fell into peril.
Upright officials were dragged down together,
and the various tribes became rebellious.
There was no year of peace from the use of arms and armor.
In one year, three hundred sixty thousand monks were fed.
In one day, three thousand people shaved their heads [to become monks].
He merely dedicated himself to small favors,
and disregarded the great foundation [of government].
How can he still be discussed in terms of good governance?
Basic Annals Twenty-seven: Tiānzuò Huángdì (天祚皇帝) I
Tiānzuò Huángdì (天祚皇帝),
whose taboo name was Yánxǐ (延禧),
whose courtesy name was Yánníng (延寧),
and whose infant name was Āguǒ (阿果).
He was the grandson of Dàozōng (道宗).
His father was Shùnzōng Dàxiào Shùnshèng Huángdì (順宗大孝順聖皇帝).
His mother was Empress Zhēnshùn (貞順皇后) of the Xiāo (蕭) clan.
He was born in the first year of Dàkāng (大康).
At the age of six, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liáng (Liáng Wáng).
He was additionally awarded the nominal title of Grand Commandant (Shǒu Tàiwèi),
and concurrently Central Secretariat Director (Zhōngshū Lìng).
Three years later,
he was promoted and enfeoffed as King of Yān (Yān Guówáng).
In the seventh year of Dà'ān (大安),
he oversaw the affairs of the Military Chancelleries of both the Northern and Southern Courts.
He was additionally awarded the title Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Lìng),
and was made Grand Marshal of All Military Forces (Tiānxià Bīngmǎ Dàyuánshuài).
Shòulóng (壽隆) seventh year, the first month, day Jiǎxū.
When Dàozōng (道宗) died,
he received the testamentary edict and ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
The officials conferred upon him the honorable title Tiānzuò Huángdì (天祚皇帝).
The second month, day Rénchén, the first day of the lunar month.
The reign era was changed to Qiántǒng (乾統).
A general amnesty was granted.
An edict stated that those who had been falsely implicated by Yēlǜ Yǐxīn (耶律乙辛)
should have their official posts and titles restored.
Those whose property was confiscated should have it returned.
Those who were exiled should be recalled.
Day Yǐwèi.
Envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Sòng (宋), Xīxià (西夏), and Gāolì (高麗).
Day Yǐsì.
Xiāo Wùnà (蕭兀納), Chancellor of the Northern Administration (Běi Fǔ Zǎixiàng), was appointed Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Jūn.
He was additionally awarded the nominal title of Grand Tutor (Shǒu Tàifù).
The third month, day Dīngmǎo.
An edict commanded the proper department to distribute the household members of Zhāng Xiàojié (張孝傑) among the various officials.
Day Jiǎxū.
The monk Fǎyí (法頤) was summoned to administer the precepts in the inner court.
Summer, the fourth month.
There was a drought.
The sixth month, *gēngyín* (first day of the lunar month)
. Went to Qìngzhōu.
*Jiǎwǔ*
, Sòng sent Wáng Qián and others to offer condolences and sacrifices.
*Bǐngshēn*
, Gāolì and Xiàguó each sent envoys to express sympathy and offer sacrifices.
*Wùxū*
, appointed the Southern Palace Chancellor Wòtèlà concurrently as the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery.
*Gēngzǐ*
, posthumously honored Empress Yìdé Huánghòu as Xuānyì Huánghòu.
*Rényín*
, appointed Hélǔwò, King of Sòng Wèiguó, as the Grand Marshal of the Armies of the Realm (Tiānxià Bīngmǎ Dàyuánshuài).
*Yǐsì*
, Chún, Prince of Běipíng Commandery, was promoted to Prince of Zhèng (Zhèng Wáng).
*Dīngwèi*
, Yēlǜ Āsī, Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery, was promoted to Yúyuè.
*Xīnhài*
, buried Emperor Rénshèng Dàxiào Wénhuángdì and Empress Xuānyì Huánghòu at Qìnglíng.
Autumn, the seventh month, *guǐhài*
, the Zǔbǔ and Tiělí came to offer tribute.
The eighth month, *jiǎyín*
, visited Qìnglíng.
The ninth month, *rénshēn*
, visited Huáilíng.
*Yǐhài*
, the imperial carriage stopped at Ǒusīdàin.
Winter, the tenth month, *rénchén*
, visited Qiánlíng.
*Jiǎchén*
, conferred the posthumous title Dàxiào Shùnshèng Huángdì upon the late Imperial Father, Crown Prince Zhāohuái
. His temple name was Shùnzōng
, and the late Imperial Mother was titled Zhēnshùn Huánghòu.
The twelfth month, *wùzǐ*
, appointed Zhāng Lín, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, to supervise the Bureau of Military Affairs (Zhī Shūmì Yuàn Shì)

, and Zhāng Fèngguī, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, to participate in governmental affairs (Cān Zhī Zhèngshì) concurrently holding the position of Assistant Supervisor of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Tóng Zhī Shūmì Yuàn Shì).
*Guǐsì*
, Sòng sent Huáng Shí to congratulate the accession.
*Dīngyǒu*
, Gāolì and Xiàguó both sent envoys to offer congratulations.
*Yǐsì*
, issued an edict
forbidding reporting or petitioning concerning matters already settled by the previous court.
Formerly
, Yánggē was appointed Military Governor (Jiédùshǐ) of the raw Nǚzhí tribes
. By their custom, he was called Tàishī.
In this year, Yánggē died
, and the title was passed to his elder brother’s son, Wūyǎshù
. When Shù died
, his younger brother Āgǔdǎ succeeded.
The second year, spring, the first month
, went to Yāzǐhé.
The second month, *xīnmǎo*
, went to Chūnzhōu.
The third month
, there was great cold
, and the ice reformed.
Summer, the fourth month, *xīnhài*
, issued an edict executing Yǐxīn’s faction
and relocating their descendants to the borders;
the tombs of Yǐxīn and Délǐtè were opened
, their coffins split
, and their corpses exposed;
Their household dependents were distributed among the families of those whom they had killed.
The fifth month, *yǐchǒu*
, Wòtèlà presented a report of victory over the Yēdǔguā and other tribes.
The sixth month, *rénchén*
, the hunt was suspended due to rain
, and the imperial carriage stopped at Sǎnshuǐyuán.
*Bǐngwǔ*
, Lǐ Qiánshùn, King of Xiàguó, again sent an envoy requesting marriage to a princess.
*Dīngwèi*
, Chénjiānú, Grand King of the Southern Chancellery, retired from office.
*Rénzǐ*
, Lǐ Qiánshùn, being attacked by Sòng
, sent Lǐ Zàofú and Tián Ruòshuǐ to request aid.
Intercalary month, *gēngshēn*
, examined outstanding scholars.
*Rénshēn*
, demoted Consort Huìfēi to a commoner.
Autumn, the seventh month
, hunted at Hēilǐng
. Due to continuous rain
, horses were distributed to the hunters.
The Zǔbǔ came to invade
, Wòtèlà and others defeated them in battle.
Winter, the tenth month, *yǐmǎo*
, Xiāo Hǎilǐ rebelled
, seizing weapons and armor from the arsenal of Qiánzhōu.
Ordered Hǎo Jiānú, the North Face Lingu (Línyá), to capture him
. Xiāo Hǎilǐ fled into the Ādiǎn tribe at Péizhúshuǐ.
*Bǐngyín*
, appointed Yēlǜ Wòtèlà, Chancellor of the Southern Palace, as Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery
, and Niú Wēnshū, Participant in Governmental Affairs, to supervise the Bureau of Military Affairs of the Southern Chancellery.
The eleventh month, *yǐwèi*
, Hǎo Jiānú was removed from office
for failing to capture Xiāo Hǎilǐ.
*Rényín*
, appointed Yēlǜ Shènsī, Protector of Shàngjīng, as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Chancellery.
Officials requested that the Emperor's birthday be designated the Tiānxīng Festival.
The third year, spring, the first month, *xīnsì* (first day of the lunar month)
, went to Hùntóng Jiāng.
The Nǚzhí boxed the head of Xiāo Hǎilǐ
and sent an envoy to present it.
*Wùshēn*
, went to Chūnzhōu.
The second month, *gēngwǔ*
, because Wǔqīng County experienced severe flooding

Second year, spring, the first month, on the first day, *Jǐwèi*,

the chiefs of the Five Tribes came to pay tribute.
they went to Chūnzhōu.
The Emperor visited Hùntóng Jiāng to fish.
The chieftains of the "Raw Nǚzhí" (Shēng Nǚzhí) outside the border, who resided within a thousand *lǐ*,
all came to court according to established practice.
It happened to coincide with
the "First Fish Banquet" (*Tóuyú Yàn*).
When the wine was halfway through,
the Emperor approached the railing (balcony),
and ordered the various chieftains to rise and dance in turn;
only Āgǔdǎ declined, citing inability.
He was urged repeatedly,
but he ultimately refused to comply.
Another day,
the Emperor secretly said to the Grand Councilor of Military Affairs, Xiāo Fèngxiān,
"During the banquet the day before yesterday,
Āgǔdǎ's spirit was vigorous and heroic,
and his gaze was unusual.
We should use a pretext concerning border affairs to execute him.
Otherwise,
he will certainly cause future trouble."
Fèngxiān replied:
"Barbarians (*jū* rén) do not understand ritual propriety,
and killing him without a major fault
might damage the desire of others to submit.
Even if he has rebellious intent,
what can he possibly achieve?"
His younger brothers Wúqǐmǎi, Zhānhǎn, Húshè, and others once followed the Emperor on a hunt,
capable of calling deer,
spearing tigers,
and wrestling bears.
The Emperor was pleased,
and immediately granted them official titles and rank.
In summer, the sixth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
they rested from the summer heat at Nányá.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Huíhú (Uighurs) of Hézhōu came to present tribute.
On the *wùxū* day,
Princess Chéng'ān came to court.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Zǔbǔ came to present tribute.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
they hunted at Nánshān.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
a bear was shot and captured.
A banquet was held for the officials.
The Emperor personally played the *pípá*.
Previously,
when Āgǔdǎ returned from the Hùntóng Jiāng banquet,
he suspected the Emperor knew of his rebellious intent,
and subsequently raised troops,
first annexing nearby tribes.
The Nǚzhí men Zhào Sān and Āhúchǎn resisted him,
and Āgǔdǎ captured their family members.
The two men fled and reported this to Xiánzhōu,
and the Xiángwěn Office sent the matter to the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs (Běi Shūmìyuàn).
The Grand Councilor of Military Affairs, Xiāo Fèngxiān, reported it to the Emperor as a routine matter,
and also sent a message to Xiánzhōu to reprimand and question [Āgǔdǎ],
hoping he would reform himself.
Later, he was summoned several times,
but Āgǔdǎ finally claimed illness and did not come.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
the mother of Wáng Yǔ, the Duke of Three Hàn Nations of Gāolì (Goryeo), died.
He sent a notification.
An envoy was immediately dispatched to offer sacrifice
and grant dispensation from mourning (*qǐfù*).
In this month,
the imperial cortege stopped at Fèngshèngzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited Nánjīng (Southern Capital).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
he paid respects at the temple of Tàizǔ.
In this year,
seventy-seven *jìnshì* (presented scholars), including Hán Fǎng, were passed.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
money was bestowed upon the poor people of Nánjīng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
they went to Dàyú Luò.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
monks and nuns breaking their vows were forbidden.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
they hunted at Gǒuyá Shān.
Due to the intense cold,
many hunters died.
In the third month,
the households of the various circuits (*dào*) were registered.
The residents in the hunting ground area of Dàláogǔ Shān were moved to other land.
One day, Āgǔdǎ led five hundred cavalry in a sudden arrival at Xiánzhōu,
greatly alarming the officials and populace.
The next day,
he went to the Xiángwěn Office
and confronted Zhào Sān and the others face-to-face in the courtyard.
Āgǔdǎ was unyielding,
and he was sent to the relevant office for questioning regarding the circumstances.
He escaped overnight.
He sent someone to appeal to the Emperor,
stating that the Xiángwěn Office intended to kill him,
and therefore he dared not remain.
From then on, when summoned, he never came again.
In summer, the intercalary fourth month,
Lǐ Hóng gathered a crowd and caused trouble using heterodox doctrines.
He was dismembered
and pieces were displayed in the Five Capitals.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the State of Wòlǎng Gǎi sent an envoy to present fine dogs as tribute.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the State of Xià sent an envoy to present tribute.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Emperor visited Qiūshān.
In the ninth month,
the imperial cortege stopped at Ǒusī Diàn.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yú Róng, the Commissioner of the Three Bureaus (*Sānsī Shǐ*), was made Acting Grand Councilor of Military Affairs for the Southern Bureau,
and Xiāo Lègǔ, the Pacification Commissioner for the Southwest Region, was made Chancellor of the Southern Administration (*Nánfǔ Zǎixiàng*).
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Gāolì sent an envoy to express gratitude for the sacrifice offered.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Huíhú sent an envoy to present tribute.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Mǎ Rénwàng, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Manager of Governmental Affairs (*Cānzhī Zhèngshì*).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Yēlǜ Yǎn, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, died.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Gāolì sent an envoy to express gratitude for the dispensation from mourning.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month,
they went to Chūnzhōu.
Earlier,
when the Nǚzhí raised troops,
they viewed Āshū, a man of the Hēshíliè tribe, as non-compliant.
They sent Sāgǎi of his own tribe to punish him.
Āshū's younger brother, Dígùbǎo, came to report this.
An imperial decree was issued instructing them not to attack,
but they did not listen,
so Āshū came to seek asylum.
At this time, the Nǚzhí sent an envoy to demand his return,
but he was not released.
In summer, the fifth month,
they rested from the summer heat at Sǎnshuǐ Yuán.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Nǚzhí again sent an envoy to retrieve Āshū,
but he was not released.
Therefore, the Assistant Censor Āxībǎo was sent to inquire about the reason for the extensive construction of fortresses along the border.
The Nǚzhí responded with discourteous words, saying:
"If Āshū is returned,
tribute shall be paid to court as before;
otherwise,
the construction of fortresses cannot be stopped."
Subsequently, the various armies north of the Húnhé River were mobilized
to reinforce the Northeast Route Military Command (Dōngběilù Tǒngjūnsī).
Āgǔdǎ then conspired with his younger brothers Zhānhǎn, Húshè, and others,
appointing Yínzhúgē, Yíliè, Lóushì, Shémǔ, and others as commanders,
gathering the troops of the various Nǚzhí tribes,
and capturing the Liáo officials responsible for falconry in the border defenses.
When they attacked Níngjiāngzhōu,
the Northeast Route Military Command reported this.
At that time, the Emperor was hunting deer in Qìngzhōu,
and upon hearing the report, he barely paid it any mind.
He sent Gāo Xiānshòu, the Prefect of Hǎizhōu, to command the Bóhǎi army for reinforcement.
Xiāo Tàbùyě encountered the Nǚzhí
and fought east of Níngjiāng,
suffering a crushing defeat.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day, *rén'yín*,
Shǒu Sīkōng Xiāo Sìxiān was made Commander-in-Chief of the Northeast Route (*Dōngběilù Dūtǒng*),
and Xiāo Tàbùyě, the Military Governor (*Jiédùshǐ*) of Jìngjiāng Commandery, was made Deputy Commander.
Three thousand Qìdān and Xī troops were mobilized,
along with two thousand Imperial Guards from Zhōngjīng (Central Capital) and local gentry militias,
and separately selected brave warriors numbering over two thousand from various circuits.
Cuī Gōngyì, the Usher (*Yúhòu*), was made Chief Commander of the Guards (*Dūyā Guān*),
and Xíng Yǐng, the Commander of the Kònghè Corps, was made his deputy.
They led the army to camp at Chūhédiàn.
The two armies faced each other,
but the Nǚzhí army secretly crossed the Hùntóng Jiāng
and launched a surprise attack on the Liáo forces.
Xiāo Sìxiān's army was routed,
and Cuī Gōngyì, Xíng Yǐng, Yēlǜ Fóliú, Xiāo Gěshí, and others died.
Only seventeen men escaped.
Xiāo Fèngxiān feared that his younger brother, Sìxiān, would be punished;
he preemptively reported that the routed Eastern Expedition troops were pillaging wherever they went,
and if a general pardon was not granted,
they might band together and cause disaster.
The Emperor agreed,
and Sìxiān was merely stripped of his office.
The various armies said among themselves:
"If we fight, we die without merit;
if we retreat, we survive without penalty."
Consequently, the soldiers had no will to fight,
and scattered upon merely seeing the enemy.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
Commander-in-Chief Xiāo Dílǐ and others camped east of Wòlín Luò,
but were again attacked by the Nǚzhí,
and very many soldiers died.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Xiāo Dílǐ was also dismissed from office for his failure.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Wòlǐwù, the Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Route, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Expeditionary Forces (*Xíngjūn Dūtǒng*).
Xiāo Yǐxuē, the Deputy Grand Inspector (*Fù Diǎnjiǎn*), and Yēlǜ Zhāngnú, the Acting Grand Councilor of Military Affairs for the Southern Bureau, served as his deputies.
In the twelfth month,
the three prefectures of Xián, Bīn, and Xiáng, along with Tiělí and Wùrě, all rebelled and joined the Nǚzhí.
Yǐ Xuē went to reinforce Bīnzhōu,
while the Southern Army generals Shílóu, Tèliè, and others went to reinforce Xiánzhōu,
but they were all defeated by the Nǚzhí.
Basic Annals, Volume 28, Tiānzuò Huángdì (2)
In the fifth year, in spring, the first month,
an edict was issued for a personal campaign (qīnzhēng).
Sēng Jiānú was dispatched carrying a letter to propose peace,
but it denounced Āgǔdǎ by name.
Āgǔdǎ sent Sàilá with a reply,
stating that if the defector Āshū was returned
and Huánglóng Fǔ was moved to another location,
then negotiations could proceed.
The Commandant-in-Chief Yēlǜ Wòlǐjūn and others fought the Nǚzhí forces at the city of Dálǔgǔ Chéng,
and were defeated.
In the second month,
Bóhǎi Gǔyù and others in Ráozhōu revolted,
proclaiming themselves the Great King (Dàwáng).
In the third month,
Xiāo Xièfóliú and others were assigned to suppress them.
Yēlǜ Zhāngjiānú and five others were sent carrying a letter as envoys to the Nǚzhí,
denouncing their ruler by name,
hoping to hasten their surrender.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Xiāo Xièfóliú and others were defeated by Bóhǎi Gǔyù.
Xiāo Táosūwò, the Vice Commander of the Southern Front, was made Commandant-in-Chief (Dūtǒng)
and dispatched to the scene.
In the fifth month,
Táosūwò fought Gǔyù
and was defeated.
Zhāngjiānú and others returned with a letter from Āgǔdǎ;
they were sent back again.
In the sixth month, on the first day Jǐhài,
they observed the summer retreat ritual at Tèlǐ Lǐng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Zhāngjiānú and others returned.
Āgǔdǎ replied in a letter,
also denouncing [the Liao Emperor] by name and urging him to surrender.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the plan for the personal campaign was announced to all circuits.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Táosūwò recruited and captured Gǔyù and his followers.
On the day Guǐhài,
Yēlǜ Mòlǐ, the Tìyǐn, was made Prince (Dàwáng) of the Northern Administration (Běi Yuàn).
In this month,
Xiāo Cílà was sent as an envoy to the Nǚzhí.
Due to the uncompromising language in his letter, he was detained.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Song sent envoys bearing silver and silk to aid the army.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
they hunted east of the ridge.
In this month,
Commandant-in-Chief Wòlǐjūn and others fought the Nǚzhí at Báimǎ Luò
and were defeated.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the hunt was called off,
and they hurried to the camp.
Because Wòlǐjūn’s army had been defeated,
he was stripped of his office.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Ābù, the Wéichǎng Envoy, was appointed Commandant-in-Chief of the Central Army (Zhōngjūn Dūtǒng),
and Yēlǜ Zhāngjiānú was made Commander (Dūjiān),
leading 100,000 Fān and Hàn soldiers.
Xiāo Fèngxiān was appointed Commandant-in-Chief of the Imperial Camp (Yùyíng Dūtǒng),
with Yēlǜ Zhāngnú, the Commander-in-Chief of the various mobile camps, as his deputy,
leading 20,000 elite troops as the vanguard.
The remainder were divided into five divisions forming the main force,
a thousand noble youths formed the resolute force,
and officials from the various escorting bureaus formed the guard force.
They advanced north out of Luòtuo Kǒu.
Xiāo Húdǔgū, the Chief Inspector (Dūdiǎnjiǎn), was made Commandant-in-Chief,
with Zhái Yì, the Secretarial Academician (Shūmì Zhí Xuéshì), as his deputy,
leading 30,000 Hàn infantry and cavalry,
advancing south out of Níngjiāng Zhōu.
They divided their routes and advanced from Chángchūn Zhōu,
deploying several months’ worth of rations,
determined to annihilate the Nǚzhí.
In the ninth month, on the first day Dīngmǎo,
the Nǚzhí army captured Huánglóng Fǔ.
On the day Jǐsì,
Xiāo Délǐdǐ, who managed the affairs of the Chief of the Northern Chancellery (Běi Yuàn Shūmìshǐ), was transferred out to become the Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Front.
Cílà returned.
The Nǚzhí again sent Sàilá with a letter in reply: If you return our defectors Āshū and others,
we will immediately withdraw our troops.
The Emperor personally led the campaign.
Zhānhǎn, Wùzhú, and others sent a letter to the Emperor,
outwardly using humble and mournful language,
but actually seeking battle.
When the letter was presented,
the Emperor was enraged
and issued an edict containing the phrase:
"The Nǚzhí have committed offenses;
the great army will utterly destroy them."
The Nǚzhí ruler gathered his followers,
slashed his face, looked up to Heaven, and wept bitterly, saying:
"When I first raised troops with you all,
it was because we suffered under the brutality of the Qìdān
and wished to establish our own state.
Now the ruler himself is leading the campaign.
What shall we do?
Unless men fight to the death,
no one can withstand them.
It would be better to kill my entire clan,
and for you all to welcome them and surrender,
thereby turning calamity into fortune."
All the armies responded:
"Since the situation has reached this point,
we shall only obey your command."
On the day Yǐsì,
Yēlǜ Zhāngnú rebelled,
fleeing to Shàngjīng
and plotting to welcome and enthrone Chún, the King of Wèi.
The Emperor dispatched the imperial son-in-law Xiāo Yù leading troops to Guǎngpíng Diàn to guard the empresses and concubines.
Yǐ Xìn, a small attendant of the temporary palace, carried a letter and raced to inform the King of Wèi.
At that time, Zhāngnú had already sent his wife’s younger brother, Xiāo Dìlǐ, to persuade the King of Wèi with the plot.
The King said:
"This is no small matter.
The Emperor already has various princes who should be enthroned.
If the great ministers of the Northern and Southern Administrations have not come,
why do you speak of this?
What is your intention?"
He secretly ordered his attendants to restrain Xiāo Dìlǐ.
A short while later,
Yǐ Xìn and others arrived bearing the Imperial Rescript,
fully detailing the plot by Zhāngnú and others to depose and enthrone.
The King of Wèi immediately beheaded Xiāo Dìlǐ and his followers and presented their heads.
He rode alone by a side path to Guǎngpíng Diàn to await punishment.
The Emperor treated him as before.
Zhāngnú, knowing the King of Wèi would not listen,
led his subordinates to plunder Qìng, Ráo, Huái, Zǔ, and other prefectures.
He allied with Bóhǎi bandit groups;
his forces swelled to tens of thousands.
He rushed toward Guǎngpíng Diàn to attack the temporary palace.
Āhúchǎn, a Nǚzhí from Shuṅguó, used 300 cavalry to defeat them in a single battle,
capturing over 200 of their nobles,
and executing them all and displaying their heads publicly.
Their wives and children were assigned labor in the Embroidery Bureau,
or dispersed among the imperial attendants as maids.
The remainder who managed to escape all fled to the Nǚzhí.
Zhāngnú disguised himself as an envoy,
attempting to flee to the Nǚzhí,
but was captured by scouts.
He was bound and sent to the Imperial residence,
where he was cut in half at the waist in the marketplace,
his heart was cut out and offered to the Ancestral Temple,
and his body was dismembered and displayed across the five routes.
In winter, the eleventh month,
the imperial son-in-law Xiāo Tèmò and the Chancellor (Línyá) Xiāo Chálá, among others, were dispatched leading 50,000 cavalry, 400,000 infantry, and 700,000 imperial guards to Tuómén.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Yēlǜ Zhāngjiānú rebelled.
On the day Wùshēn,
[The Emperor] personally fought at Hùbùdágāng,
was defeated,
and lost all his baggage train.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Yēlǜ Zhúzhě, the Governor (Cìshǐ) of Jǐnzhōu, rebelled and supported Zhāngjiānú.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Yēlǜ Mǎgē, the Chancellor of the Northern Front, suppressed Zhāngjiānú.
On the day Guǐhài,
Xiāo Hánjiānú, the Commissioner of the Northern Administration, was appointed to manage the affairs of the Chief of the Northern Chancellery,
and Xiāo Tèmò, the Commissioner of the Southern Administration, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Temporary Palace for the Hàn people.
In the sixth year, spring, the first month, on the first day Bǐngyín,
at night in Dōngjīng, more than ten wicked youths,
drunk and wielding blades,
scaled the wall and entered the Office of the Resident General.
They asked for the Resident General Xiāo Bǎoxiān, stating:
"There is a military upheaval now.
We request you prepare for it."
Xiāo Bǎoxiān emerged
and they stabbed him to death.
Dà Gōngdǐng, the Minister of Revenue, heard of the disturbance
and immediately took charge of the affairs of the Resident General.
He, along with Gāo Qīngmíng, the Vice Resident General, assembled 1,000 Xī and Hàn soldiers,
captured all the perpetrators,
executed them,
and pacified the populace.
Dōngjīng was formerly Bóhǎi territory,
which Tàizǔ had obtained only after fighting vigorously for more than twenty years.
However, Xiāo Bǎoxiān was harsh and cruel,
and the Bóhǎi people suffered under him,
hence this upheaval occurred.
His subordinate general, Gāo Yǒngchāng of Bóhǎi, usurped the title,
proclaiming the first year of Lóngjī.
Xiāo Yǐxuē and Gāo Xīngshùn were dispatched to recruit him,
but he refused.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xiāo Hánjiānú and Zhāng Lín were sent to suppress him.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Yēlǜ Yúdǔ, the garrison commander of Guìdé Zhōu, led the Bóhǎi people of Guǎngzhōu to rebel and join Yǒngchāng.
Our army attacked and defeated them.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
the Shìyù Sītú, Tàbùyě, and others attacked Zhāng Jiānú,
fighting at Zǔzhōu.
They were defeated.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Hánrén Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ, Xiāo Tèmò, was dispatched to lead the generals to attack Zhāng Jiānú.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Zhāng Jiānú lured the Bóhǎi people of Ráozhōu and the bandits Hóugài and others from Zhōngjīng, totaling more than ten thousand men,
and attacked and captured Gāozhōu.
In the third month,
the Dōngmiàn Xíngjūn Fùtǒng, Chóu Wò, and others captured Hóugài at Chuānzhōu.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor personally campaigned against Zhāng Jiānú.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
he defeated him.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the rebel faction was executed,
and the Bóhǎi people of Ráozhōu were pacified.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the generals and soldiers who had pacified the bandits were rewarded according to their rank;
however, Xiāo Hánjiānú, Zhāng Lín, and others were again defeated by the bandits.
In the fifth month,
the heat was cleared at Sǎnshuǐyuán.
The Nǚzhí army attacked and captured Shěnzhōu,
then again captured Dōngjīng,
and captured Gāo Yǒngchāng.
Thirteen members of the imperial clan from the prefectures and counties of Dōngjīng—Hénbó, Duólà, Wúshí, Tàbùyě, Dàolà, Chóu Wò, and others—all surrendered to the Nǚzhí.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the troops of all circuits were registered.
Those who possessed ten or more heads of livestock were all required to join the army.
On the day Gēngchén,
Chún, the King of Wèiguó, was promoted and enfeoffed as the King of Qínjìn Guó,
and made Dū Yuánshuài (Commander-in-Chief);
Xiāo Tàbùyě, the Liúshǒu of Shàngjīng, was made the Qìdān Xínggōng Dū Bùshǔ concurrently Fù Yuánshuài (Vice Commander-in-Chief).
On the day Dīnghài,
Xiāo Hánjiānú, who managed the affairs of the Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ (Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs), was made the Liúshǒu of Shàngjīng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
there was a hunt on Qiūshān.
More than two thousand Bóhǎi households in Chūnzhōu rebelled.
The Tǒngjūnshǐ of the Northeast Circuit led troops in pursuit, caught up with them,
and returned with all of them captured.
In the eighth month,
the Wūgǔ tribe rebelled.
The Zhōngchéng Yēlǜ Tàbùyě and others were dispatched to recruit them back.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Huáilíng mausoleum was visited.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
because Zhāng Lín’s army was defeated,
he was stripped of his office.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Wūgǔ tribe came and surrendered.
In the eleventh month,
the Dōngmiàn Xíngjūn Fùtǒng Mǎgē and others attacked Hésūguǎn,
and were defeated.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài,
a commoner woman of the Xiāo clan was enfeoffed as Tàihuáng Tàifēi (Grand Empress Dowager).
On the day Xīnsì,
the Fùtǒng Yēlǜ Mǎgē was stripped of his office.
In the seventh year (1117), spring, the first month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the horse rations (millet) were reduced,
and distributed to various offices.
In this month,
the Nǚzhí army attacked Chūnzhōu.
The armies on the Northeast Front scattered without fighting.
The Nǚgǔ and Píshì four tribes, as well as the Bóhǎi people, all surrendered.
Tàizhōu was captured again.
In the second month,
Dǒng Páng'ér, a bandit from Láishuǐ County, gathered a crowd of more than ten thousand.
Xiāo Yǐxuē, the Liúshǒu of Xījīng, and Chálà, the Tǒngjūn Dūjiān of Nánjīng, fought against him at Yìshuǐ,
and defeated him.
In the third month,
Páng'ér's faction gathered again.
Yǐxuē again attacked and defeated them at Fèngshèngzhōu.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
the generals of the Northeast Front Army—Nièlǐ, Hélǔ, Niègē, Xūgǔ, and others—were publicly executed in the marketplace.
On the day Yǐsì,
the unused land in all the hunting preserves
was opened up for the common people to gather firewood and forage.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Yúlǐyě, who shared management of the Shūmìyuàn (Chancellery of Military Affairs), was made the Běiyuàn Dàwáng (Great King of the Northern Court).
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
there was a hunt on Qiūshān.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
there was a hunt on Juésīnàlǐshān.
The Dū Yuánshuài, the King of Qínjìn, was ordered to proceed to the border areas,
to gather the troops and cavalry from the four circuits to defend against autumn raids.
In the ninth month,
the Emperor traveled from Yān to Yīnliáng Hé,
and established eight camps of discontented troops (Yuànjūn): those recruited from Yízhōu were named Qiányí and Hòuyí;
those from Jǐnzhōu were named Qiánjǐn and Hòujǐn;
those from Qiánzhōu and Xiǎnzhōu were named Qián and Xiǎn;
there were also the Qiánxiǎn Dàyíng (Grand Camp) and the Yánzhōu Yíng (Camp),
totaling more than twenty-eight thousand men,
stationed at Jílìshān in Wèizhōu.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
there was a hunt on Wǎngzishān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day, Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor arrived at Zhōngjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the Dū Yuánshuài, Chún, the King of Qínjìn Guó, encountered the Nǚzhí army,
and fought at Jílìshān.
He was defeated.
The Nǚzhí again captured Xiǎnzhōu and the nearby prefectures and commanderies.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict was issued criticizing himself.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Yílìbì Chálà and Dàgōngdǐng were dispatched to recruit soldiers throughout the circuits.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Xiāo Yǐxuē, the Liúshǒu of Xījīng, was made the Běifǔ Zǎixiàng (Chancellor of the Northern Administration).
Xī Xiámò, the Xíngjūn Dūtǒng of the Northeast Circuit, was given charge of the affairs of the Xī Liù Bù Dàwáng (Great King of the Six Xī Tribes).
In this year,
Agǔdǎ of the Nǚzhí, employing the strategy of Yáng Pǔ from Tiězhōu,
ascended the imperial throne,
established the reign name Tiānfǔ,
and named his state Jīn (Gold).
Yáng Pǔ further stated,
“Since ancient times, when a hero founds a state or receives the abdication,
he must first seek investiture and acknowledgement from a great power.”
Consequently, an envoy was dispatched to discuss peace,
and to request investiture.
In the eighth year (1118), spring, the first month,
the Emperor visited Yuānyāng Luò.
On the day Dīnghài,
Yēlǜ Núgē and others were dispatched as envoys to Jīn to discuss peace.
On the day Gēngyín,
Zhāng Chóng, the Jiédùshǐ of Bǎo'ānjūn, surrendered to Jīn with two hundred households from Shuāngzhōu.
Bandits and thieves swarmed up in the prefectures of the Eastern Circuit,
plundering the populace and taking them along to serve as food supply.
In the second month,
Yēlǜ Núgē returned from Jīn.
The Jīn sovereign replied in a letter, saying:
“If you can serve Us as an elder brother,
present annual tribute of local products,
return the prefectures and counties of the three circuits of Shàngjīng, Zhōngjīng, and Xīngzhōng Fǔ to Us;
offer the sons and grandsons of princes, princesses, imperial sons-in-law, and high ministers as hostages;
return Our envoy and the original credentials given to him;
and hand over the exchanged documents, imperial edicts, memorials, and communications between your court and Sòng, Xià, and Gāolì (Koryŏ),
then the agreement can be fulfilled.”
In the third month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Núgē was again dispatched as envoy to Jīn.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Xiāo Délǐdǐ, the Zhāotǎoshǐ of the Southwest Front, was made the Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ (Northern Chancellery of Military Affairs).
In the fifth month, on the first day, Rénwǔ,
Núgē returned with a letter,
stipulating that a reply must be given before the end of this month.
On the day Wùxū,
Núgē was again dispatched as envoy to Jīn,
demanding a more moderate proposal.
In this month,
the Emperor arrived at Nàgě Luò.
The bandits Ān Shēng'ér and Zhāng Gāo'ér gathered a crowd of two hundred thousand.
Yēlǜ Mǎgē and others executed Shēng'ér at Lónghuàzhōu.
Gāo'ér fled into Yìzhōu,
and joined up with Huò Liùgē.
The Jīn sovereign dispatched Hú Tūgǔn to carry a letter with Núgē,
replying according to the previous agreement.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Núgē and others were sent, carrying the exchanged documents, imperial edicts, memorials, and communications with Sòng, Xià, and Gāolì, to Jīn.
Huò Liùgē captured Hǎiběizhōu,
and hastened toward Yìzhōu.
The military commander Huílǐbǎo and others attacked and defeated him.
More than eight hundred households of the populace from the four prefectures of Tōngzhōu, Qízhōu, Shuāngzhōu, and Liáozhōu surrendered to Jīn.
In autumn, the seventh month,
there was a hunt on Qiūshān.
Jīn again dispatched Hú Tūgǔn to come,
agreeing to waive the requirement for hostages and the prefectures and commanderies belonging to Shàngjīng and Xīngzhōng Fǔ,
and reducing the amount of the annual indemnity.
“[If you can serve Us as an elder brother,
and employ Hàn rites for the investiture ceremony,
the agreement can be fulfilled.”
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Núgē and Tūdié were dispatched as envoys to Jīn,
to discuss the investiture ceremony.
In the ninth month,
Tūdié was detained,
and Núgē was sent back.
He was told:
“If their word is not compliant,
do not send another envoy again.”
In the intercalary month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Núgē was again dispatched as envoy to Jīn.
Meanwhile, Xiāo Bǎo, Érǐ, and fifteen others each led their households to surrender to Jīn.
In winter, the tenth month,
Núgē and Tūdié returned carrying the Jīn sovereign’s letter.
Zhāng Yìnggǔ and four others from Lónghuàzhōu led their crowds to surrender to Jīn.
In the eleventh month,
the Fù Yuánshuài, Xiāo Tàbùyě, died.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the investiture ceremony was definitively agreed upon,
and Núgē was sent as envoy to Jīn.
Liú Hóng, the Jiédùshǐ of Níngchāngjūn, surrendered to Jīn with three thousand households from Yìzhōu.
At that time, the circuits in the region south of the mountains suffered a severe famine.
In the circuits of Qiánzhōu, Xiǎnzhōu, Yízhōu, Jǐnzhōu, Xīngzhōng, and others,
a *dǒu* of millet was worth several bolts of silk.
The people scraped elm bark and ate it.
Later, cannibalism occurred.
In this year,
one hundred and three *Jìnshì*, including Wáng Huī, were released (commissioned).
In the first month of the spring of the ninth year,
Jīn sent Wūlíndá Zànmó bearing a letter to welcome the imperial patent (of investiture).
In the second month,
reached Yuānyāng Luò.
The bandit Zhāng Sābā seduced the provisioning troops of Zhōngjīng,
usurped a title,
but Yú Dǔ, the military commander of the Southern Circuit, captured Sābā.
On the *Dīngwèi* day, the first day of the third month,
sent Xiāo Xíníliè, acting Right *Yílíbì*, and others, to invest the Jīn ruler as the Emperor of the State of Dōnghuái.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
Wūlíndá Zànmó, Núgē, and others reported back first with a letter.
In the fifth month of summer,
the Zǔbǔ (Tatars), including Bǔshūzhǐ, rebelled,
capturing the Commissioner of Pacification Yēlǜ Wòlǐwù,
and the Commandant Xiāo Xiélǐdé died.
In the seventh month of autumn,
hunted at Nánshān.
Jīn again sent Wūlíndá Zànmó,
who criticized the imperial patent because it lacked
the phrase
"to serve as an elder brother,"
did not say
"Great Jīn"
but instead said
"Dōnghuái,"
which implied a small state cherishing their virtue;
moreover, the patent contained
the two characters
"Qú Cái,"
which were deemed contemptuous;
and phrases such as
"Yáo Fēn Duō Jiǎn,"
were all malicious,
and greatly inappropriate in style.
Only if it follows what was stipulated in the previous letter
can it be accepted.
Yáng Xúnqīng and Luó Zǐwéi led their followers to surrender to Jīn.
In the eighth month,
made Xíníliè, the Prince of Zhào, the Defender-in-chief of Xījīng.
In the ninth month,
arrived at Xījīng.
Again sent Xíníliè and Yáng Lìzhōng ahead, bearing a patent (of investiture) to act as envoys to Jīn.
On the *Jiǎxū* day, the first day of the tenth month of winter,
Yēlǜ Chéntúnú and over twenty others plotted rebellion
and were executed.
In this month,
sent an envoy to escort Wūlíndá Zànmó back with the letter.
In the second month of the spring of the tenth year,
visited Yuānyāng Luò.
Jīn again sent Wūlíndá Zànmó bearing a letter and a duplicate of the imperial patent,
and furthermore criticized (Liao) for requesting troops from Gāolì.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day of the third month,
for those among the populace who owned herds of horses,
one out of ten was taken
to supply the troops of the Eastern Circuit.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
as the two characters
"Dà Shèng"
designated by the Jīn people
were the same as the titles of previous emperors,
Xíníliè was again sent to negotiate.
The Jīn ruler grew angry
and consequently broke off relations.
In the fourth month of summer,
hunted at Hútǔ Báishān.
Upon hearing that the Jīn army had mobilized again,
Yēlǜ Báishībù and others selected three thousand elite soldiers to aid the Liáo army.
In the fifth month,
the Jīn ruler personally attacked Shàngjīng,
conquering the outer city wall.
Tàbùyě, the Defender-in-chief, led his followers out to surrender.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,

Xiāo Yǐxuē, the Chancellor of the Northern Administration, was made Defender-in-chief of Shàngjīng, concurrent Director of the Salt and Iron and Inner Ministries, and Director of the Northeast Command.
In autumn,
hunted at Shālíng.
In winter,
returned to Xījīng.
Annals Twenty-Nine: Emperor Tiānzuò (3)
On the *Dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the first month of the spring of the first year of Bǎodà,
the reign era was changed,
and a great amnesty was granted.
Initially,
when the Jīn people raised troops,
nearly half of the prefectures and counties were lost.
The Emperor had four sons: the eldest, the Prince of Zhào,
whose mother was Zhào Zhāoróng;
the second, the Prince of Jìn,
whose mother was Consort Wén;
followed by the Prince of Qín and the Prince of Xǔ,
both born of the Principal Consort (Yuánfēi).
The people of the state knew the Prince of Jìn was worthy
and greatly pinned their hopes on him.
Xiāo Fèngxiān, the Commissioner of Military Affairs and elder brother of the Principal Consort, feared that the Prince of Qín would not be established (as heir),
and secretly plotted against (the Prince of Jìn).
Consort Wén had three sisters: the eldest married Yēlǜ Tàgélǐ,
the second was Consort Wén herself,
and the youngest married Yú Dǔ.
One day,
when her elder and younger sisters were both meeting at the military camp,
Fèngxiān incited someone to falsely accuse the Imperial Son-in-law Xiāo Yù and Yú Dǔ of plotting to enthrone the Prince of Jìn.
When the matter was discovered,
Yù, Tàgélǐ, and others were executed.
Consort Wén was also granted death (forced to commit suicide);
only the Prince of Jìn was spared punishment for the time being.
Yú Dǔ was among the troops;
upon hearing this, he became greatly frightened
and immediately led over a thousand cavalry to defect to Jīn.

The Emperor sent Xiāo Xiámǎi, acting Prince of Xī, Xiāo Dégōng, Chancellor of the Northern Administration, Yēlǜ Dìlǐgū, Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Xiāo Héshangnú, Surveillance Commissioner of Guīzhōu, and Xiāo Gàn, Grand Tutor of the Four Armies, leading their respective troops to pursue him,
reaching Zhūlǘ Shān County.
The generals discussed, saying:
"The sovereign trusts Xiāo Fèngxiān's words,
and Fèngxiān treats our colleagues with utter contempt.
Yú Dǔ is a heroic talent of the imperial clan,
unwilling to serve under Fèngxiān.
If we capture Yú Dǔ,
one day we will all become Yú Dǔ!
It is better to let him go."
They returned,
and immediately lied, saying:
"We pursued him but did not catch up."
Since Fèngxiān had witnessed Yú Dǔ's flight,
fearing that the various officers would also rebel later,
he consequently advised rapidly increasing titles and rewards
to win the hearts of the people.
Xiāo Xiámǎi was made Prince of Xī;
Xiāo Dégōng was appointed Acting Grand Counselor (of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery), concurrent Administrator of the Affairs of the Defender-in-chief of Shàngjīng;
Yēlǜ Dìlǐgū was made General-in-chief of the Dragon and Tiger Guard;
Xiāo Héshangnú was made General-in-chief of the Metropolitan Guard;
Xiāo Gàn was made Grand General Who Guards the State.
In the second month,
visited Yuānyāng Luò.
In the fifth month of summer,
arrived at Gélǐ Yuè.
In the seventh month of autumn,
hunted at Tànshān.
In the ninth month,
arrived at Nánjīng.
On the *Guǐhài* day of the eleventh month of winter,
Xíníliè, the Prince of Zhào and Defender-in-chief of Xījīng, was made *Tìyǐn*.
On the *Yǐhài* day of the first month of the spring of the second year,
Jīn conquered Zhōngjīng,
and advanced to capture Zézhōu.
The Emperor went out through Jūyōng Pass
and reached Yuānyāng Luò.
Hearing that Yú Dǔ had led the Jīn people, Lóushì Bójǐn, in a surprise arrival,
Xiāo Fèngxiān said:
"Yú Dǔ is a descendant of Wángzǐ Bān;
he has come only to enthrone his nephew, the Prince of Jìn.
If we consider the interests of the state,
we should not spare one son.
If we clearly state his crime and execute him,
Yú Dǔ will retreat without a fight."
The Emperor consequently granted the Prince of Jìn death (forced him to commit suicide),
wore mourning clothes for three days,
and Yēlǜ Sābā and others were all executed.
The Prince had long enjoyed popular support.
When the various armies heard of his death,
none failed to weep,
and consequently, morale collapsed.
Yú Dǔ led the Jīn people to press upon the Emperor's temporary palace.
The Emperor led over five thousand cavalry guards to Yúnzhōng,
abandoning the Imperial Seal of State in the Sānggān River.
On the *Gēngyín* day, the first day of the second month,
there was a solar eclipse,
which ended.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Yēlǜ Mǎgē, acting Grand Prince of the Northern Administration, and the Han Chinese Grand Commissioner of the Temporary Palace, Xiāo Tèmò, were both made Grand Commanders,
with Yēlǜ Bǔdé, Envoy of the Tàihé Palace, as their deputy,
leading troops to garrison Yuānyāng Luò.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
the Jīn army defeated Xiámò, the Prince of Xī, at Běi'ān Prefecture,
and consequently took the surrender of that city.
the Emperor
heard that the Jīn army was about to emerge west of the ridge (Lǐngxī),
and consequently hastened to Báishuǐluò.
Yǐchǒu day,
Móluwò, the Director of the Imperial Herds (Qúnmùshǐ), surrendered to Jīn.
Bǐngyín day,
the Emperor arrived at Nǚgǔdǐcāng.
Hearing that the Jīn troops were approaching,
and unable to devise a plan,
he took light cavalry and entered Jiāshān.
It was only then that he realized Fèngxiān's disloyalty.
He said angrily:
"You father and son have misled me to this point!
Although I wish to execute you now,
what help would it be to the situation?
I fear that the military heart will be resentful and bitter.
If you people evade the enemy seeking temporary safety,
the disaster will surely reach me.
Do not follow my retinue."
Fèngxiān dismounted,
wept, bowed, and departed.
Before they had travelled a few *lǐ*,
his attendants seized the father and son,
bound them, and sent them to the Jīn troops.
The Jīn people beheaded his eldest son, Āng,
and shackled Fèngxiān and his second son, Yù, sending them to the Jīn ruler.
On the road, they encountered Liáo troops,
who seized them and brought them back to the country,
and subsequently granted them both death.
(The Emperor) expelled the Commissioner of Military Affairs (Shūmìshǐ), Xiāo Délǐdǐ.
He summoned Tàbùyě to take charge of the Imperial Guard (Jìnwèi).
Dīngmǎo day,

Xiāo Sēngxiàonú, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department (Běiyuàn Shūmì Fùshǐ), was appointed to manage the affairs of the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department (Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmìshǐ Shì),
and Xiāo Chálà, who jointly managed the affairs of the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department, was made Zuǒ Yílíbì.
Wùchén day,
Yēlǜ Gāobā, who jointly managed the affairs of the Palace Inspectorate (Diànqián Diǎnjiǎn), led the guards to surrender to Jīn.
Jǐsì day,
the scout Xiāo Héshàng and the Imperial Edict Gentleman (Páiyìn Lángjūn) Yēlǜ Shěnsī were captured by the Jīn army.
Guǐyǒu day,
because many artisans (bǎigōng) from the various bureaux had deserted,
all those following the retinue, regardless of whether they were officials or commoners,
were granted official ranks.
Previously,
an edict had commanded the Grand Councillors (Zǎixiàng) Zhāng Lín and Lǐ Chùwēn, along with Chún, King of Qín and Jìn (Qínjìn Guówáng), to remain and guard Yān.
Chùwēn heard that the Emperor had entered Jiāshān,
and for several days, communication of orders ceased.
He immediately, along with his younger brother Chùnéng and son Shì,
externally used the pretext of the mutinous army (Yuàn Jūn),
and internally allied with the Commandant (Dūtǒng) Xiāo Gàn,
plotting to enthrone Chún.

Consequently, he, along with various high ministers—Yēlǜ Dàshí, Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Yú Zhòngwén, Cáo Yǒngyì, and Kāng Gōngbì—assembled tens of thousands of barbarian and Han officials, soldiers, and elders to go to Chún's residence.
Chùwēn invited Zhāng Lín to come
and informed him of the plan.
Lín said:
"Acting as regent would be acceptable."
Chùwēn said:
"The will of Heaven and the hearts of the people are already set.
We request that he be immediately enthroned."
Chùwēn and the others requested Chún to receive the ceremony.
As Chún emerged,
Lǐ Shì held a reddish-brown robe and draped it over him,
ordering the officials to bow, dance, and shout "Ten Thousand Years" (shānhū).
Chún was startled and alarmed,
refusing repeatedly,
but having no choice, he complied.
He appointed Chùwēn as Acting Grand Commandant (Shǒu Tàiwèi),
Zuǒ Qǐgōng as Acting Minister of Education (Shǒu Sītú),
Cáo Yǒngyì as Manager of the Affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Zhī Shūmìyuàn Shì),
Yú Zhòngwén as Participation in Deliberations on Governmental Affairs (Cānzhī Zhèngshì),
Zhāng Lín as Acting Grand Preceptor (Shǒu Tàishī),
Lǐ Chùnéng as Administrator in the Bureau of Military Affairs (Zhí Shūmìyuàn),
Lǐ Shì as Vice Supervisor of the Privy Treasury (Shǎofǔ Shàojiān) and Director of Hanlin Imperial Physicians (Tíjǔ Hànlín Yīguān).
Lǐ Shuǎng, Chén Mì, and more than ten others who had participated in the major deliberation (dàjì),
were all granted the degree of *Jìnshì* (advanced scholar),
and appointed to various offices accordingly.
Xiāo Gàn was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the North (Běi Shūmìshǐ),
and Xiāo Dàn, the Commandant Son-in-Law (Fùmǎ Dūwèi), was made Manager of the Affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The Mutinous Army (Yuàn Jūn) was renamed the Ever Victorious Army (Chángshèng Jūn).
Thereupon, a general amnesty was declared.
He proclaimed himself Tiānxī Huángdì (Emperor Tiānxī),
changed the reign title to Jiànfú,
and demoted Tiānzuò, enfeoffing him as the Prince of Xiāngyīn (Xiāngyīn Wáng).
He thus occupied Yān, Yún, Píng, as well as Shàngjīng and Liáoxī (six circuits total).
What Tiānzuò possessed
was only the area north of the desert (Shāmò Yǐ Běi),
the two offices of the Supreme Commander (Dū Zhāotǎofǔ) of the Southwest and Northwest Circuits, and various foreign tribes.
Summer, fourth month, Xīnmǎo day,
Yēlǜ Fódǐng, the Supreme Commander of the Southwest Region (Xīnánmiàn Zhāotǎoshǐ), surrendered to Jīn,
and Yúnnèi, Níngbiān, Dōngshèng, and other prefectures all surrendered.
Āshū was captured by the Jīn troops.
Jīn had already taken Xījīng (Western Capital),
and the tribes south of the desert all surrendered.
The Emperor consequently fled to Ésuōliè.
At that time, Móɡěshī of the Northern Tribe presented horses, camels, and sheep for sustenance.
Fifth month, Jiǎxū day,
the Commandant Mǎgē gathered the scattered remnants
and assembled them at Ōulǐjǐn.
Bǐngzǐ day,
Mǎgē was appointed to manage the affairs of the Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Department,
and concurrently served as Commandant.
Sixth month,
Chún fell ill.
He heard that the Emperor had issued a proclamation to Tiāndé, Yúnnèi, Shuò, Wǔ, Yìng, Wèi, and other prefectures,
to assemble five myriad elite cavalry troops from various foreign tribes,
promising that they would enter Yān in the eighth month;
and furthermore, the Emperor had sent someone to inquire about his well-being,
requesting clothing, furs, tea, and medicine.
Chún was greatly alarmed,
and ordered the Southern and Northern Department ministers to deliberate.
Lǐ Chùwēn, Xiāo Gàn, and others advocated the policy of welcoming the Prince of Qín (Qín) and resisting the Prince of Xiāngyīn (Xiāng).
They assembled barbarian and Han officials to discuss it.
Those who agreed with the proposal
stood to the east;
only Yēlǜ Níng, the Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Region Travelling Headquarters (Nánmiàn Xíngyíng Dū Bùshǔ), stood to the west.
Chùwēn and the others asked the reason.
Níng replied:
"If Tiānzuò can indeed successfully use the troops of the foreign tribes in a large-scale campaign to recapture Yān,
then his mandate (tiān shù) has not yet ended,
how can we resist him?
If not,
Qín and Xiāng
are father and son.
If we resist, we must resist both.
Since ancient times, how has there been anyone who welcomed the son but resisted the father?"
Chùwēn and the others looked at each other and smiled dismissively.
They considered Níng to be inciting chaos in the army's morale
and intended to kill him.
Chún leaned against his pillow and sighed deeply, saying:
"He is a loyal subject;
how can he be killed?
If Tiānzuò truly comes,
I only have death,
and what face would I have to meet him again!"
Soon thereafter, Chún died.
The officials then deliberated and established his wife, Lady Xiāo (Xiāo Shì), as the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu),
to preside over military and state affairs.
Following the posthumous order,
they welcomed and enthroned Dìng, the Prince of Qín (Qín Wáng), Tiānzuò’s second son, as emperor.
The Empress Dowager subsequently assumed control of the government (chēng zhì),
and changed the reign title to Déxīng.
Chùwēn and his son, fearing disaster,
communicated with Tóng Guàn in the south,
wishing to coerce Empress Dowager Xiāo into ceding territory to Sòng;
they also communicated with Jīn in the north,
hoping to act as an internal contact,
and externally claimed great merit for supporting the enthronement.
Empress Dowager Xiāo cursed them, saying:
"Those who misled the King of Qín and Jìn
were all you father and son!"
She fully recounted their dozens of faults,
granted them death,
dismembered and publicly displayed the remains (zhé) of his son Shì;
and confiscated their household property.
Seven myriad *mín* of cash were recovered,
with gold, jade, and precious vessels matching that value.
These were all acquired during the few months they served as Grand Councillors.
Móɡěshī brought troops to provide aid,
but was defeated by the Jīn people at Hónghuīshuǐ.
His son Tuóɡǔ and his subordinate Ādíyīn were captured.
Reinforcements from the Xià kingdom arrived,
but were also defeated by Jīn.
Autumn, seventh month, Dīngsì day (the first day of the month),
Píshì of the Díliè Tribe rebelled.
Yēlǜ Tánggǔ, the Military Commissioner (Jiédùshǐ) of the Wūgǔ Tribe, suppressed the rebellion,
and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo).
Yǐchǒu day,
Máo Bāshí of Shàngjīng led two thousand households to surrender to Jīn.
Xīnwèi day,
the Xià kingdom sent Cáo Jià to inquire about (the Emperor's) well-being.
Eighth month, Wùxū day,
(The Emperor) personally encountered the Jīn army
and fought at Shíliǎn Yì (Post Station).
(He) suffered a crushing defeat.
The Commandant Xiāo Tèmò and his nephew Sāgǔ were captured.
Xīnchǒu day,
(The remaining forces) rendezvoused at Huāntà Xīnchálà.
The Jīn troops pursued them relentlessly,
and (they) abandoned their baggage train and fled.
Ninth month,
the Díliè Tribe rebelled.
The Commandant Mǎgē subdued them.
Winter, tenth month,
the Jīn troops attacked Wèizhōu,
which surrendered.
Eleventh month, Yǐchǒu day,
hearing that the Jīn troops had reached Fèngshèngzhōu,
(The Emperor) led the guard troops to encamp at Luòkūnsuǐ.
Xiāo Défēi, the consort of Chún, King of Qín and Jìn, sent five memorials to Jīn,
requesting the enthronement of the Prince of Qín.
(Jīn) did not permit it,
and instead used elite troops to guard Jūyōng.
When the Jīn troops approached the pass,
the cliff stones spontaneously collapsed,
many garrison soldiers were crushed to death,
and the defense collapsed without a fight.
Défēi exited Gǔběikǒu,
and hastened to Tiāndé Jūn (Military Prefecture).
Twelfth month,
learning that the Jīn ruler had pacified Nánjīng (Southern Capital),
the Emperor consequently left through Sǎolǐ Guān and resided in the home of the *Xiángwěn* (Chief) of the Four Tribes.
In the first year of Bǎo Dà (1128), spring, first month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the reign title was changed,
and a general amnesty was declared.
Originally,
when the Jīn people raised an army,
nearly half of the commanderies and counties were lost.
The Emperor had four sons: the eldest, Zhào Wáng,
whose mother was Zhào Zhāoróng;
the second, Jìn Wáng,
whose mother was Wén Fēi;
the third and fourth, Qín Wáng and Xǔ Wáng,
both born of Yuán Fēi.
The people of the country knew of Jìn Wáng's virtue
and deeply placed their hopes in him.
Yuán Fēi's elder brother, the Grand Counselor Xiāo Fèngxiān, fearing that Qín Wáng would not be established as heir,
secretly plotted.
Wén Fēi had two sisters: the eldest married Yēlǜ Táhélǐ,
the second was Wén Fēi,
and the third married Yú Dǔ.
One day,
when both her elder and younger sisters were assembled at the army front,
Fèngxiān instigated someone to falsely accuse the Imperial son-in-law Xiāo Yù and Yú Dǔ of plotting to establish Jìn Wáng.
When the matter came to light,
Yù, Táhélǐ, and others were executed;
Wén Fēi was also granted death.
Only Jìn Wáng was spared immediate punishment, as the Emperor was reluctant to condemn him.
Yú Dǔ, who was in the army,
was greatly alarmed when he heard of this,
and immediately led over a thousand cavalry to rebel and defect to Jīn.

The Emperor dispatched Xiāo Xiámǎi, who was in charge of the affairs of the Xī King's mansion, the Northern Administration Chancellor Xiāo Dégōng, the Grand Registrar of the Grand Court Yēlǜ Dìlǐgū, the Guī Prefecture Inspector Xiāo Héshàngnú, and the Four Armies Grand Tutor Xiāo Gàn, to lead their respective troops in pursuit.
They caught up with them at Zhūlǘ Shān Xiàn.
The generals deliberated, saying:
"Our Lord believes Xiāo Fèngxiān's words,
and Fèngxiān treats us as nothing.
Yú Dǔ is a valiant and outstanding member of the imperial clan;
he is unwilling to be subservient to Fèngxiān.
If we capture Yú Dǔ,
then one day, all of us will become Yú Dǔ!
It would be better to let him go."
Upon their return,
they fabricated a report, saying:
"We pursued but could not catch up."
Once Fèngxiān saw Yú Dǔ's flight,
he feared that other commanders would also rebel in the future,
so he advised a sudden increase in titles and rewards
to win the hearts of the multitude.
Xiāo Xiámǎi was made Xī Wáng;
Xiāo Dégōng was appointed Acting Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Administrator of Shàngjīng Prefecture;
Yēlǜ Dìlǐgū was made Commander-in-chief of the Dragon and Tiger Guard;
Xiāo Héshàngnú, Commander-in-chief of the Golden Armor Guard;
and Xiāo Gàn, Grand General Who Guards the State.
In the second month,
the Emperor visited Yuānyāng Luò.
In summer, fifth month,
he reached Hélǐjuè.
In autumn, seventh month,
he hunted at Tàn Shān.
In ninth month,
he reached Nánjīng.
In winter, eleventh month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Zhào Wáng Xíníliè, the Administrator of Xījīng, was made Tìyǐn.
In the second year (1129), spring, first month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Jīn conquered Zhōngjīng
and then captured Zézhōu.
The Emperor exited Jūyōng Guān
and arrived at Yuānyāng Luò.
Upon hearing that Yú Dǔ was leading the Jīn people Lóushì Bólǐn to arrive unexpectedly,
Xiāo Fèngxiān said:
"Yú Dǔ is a descendant of Wángzǐ Bān.
He comes now only to establish his nephew, Jìn Wáng.
If we consider the welfare of the state,
and do not begrudge one son,
clearly accuse and execute him,
then Yú Dǔ will turn back without a battle."
The Emperor then granted Jìn Wáng death.
He wore plain mourning clothes for three days.
Yēlǜ Sābā and others were all executed.
The Prince had always enjoyed popular support,
and when the armies heard of his death,
there was no one who did not shed tears;
consequently, morale disintegrated.
Yú Dǔ led the Jīn people to press upon the traveling palace.
The Emperor led five thousand cavalry of his guard to Yúnzhōng,
abandoning the Imperial Seal of State at the Sānggān Hé.
Second month, on the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yēlǜ Mǎgē, who was in charge of the affairs of the Northern Division Great King, and Xiāo Tèmò, the Han Chinese Grand Commissioner of the Traveling Palace, were both appointed Grand Commanders;
Yēlǜ Bǔdé, the Superintendent of Tàihé Palace, served as their deputy.
They led troops to garrison at Yuānyāng Luò.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Jīn army defeated Xī Wáng Xiámò at Běi'ān Zhōu,
and then captured the city.
Third month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor, hearing that the Jīn army was about to emerge from west of the mountains,
then rushed to Báishuǐ Luò.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Mólǔwò, the Superintendent of Herds, surrendered to Jīn.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor arrived at Nǚgǔdǐ Cāng.
Hearing that the Jīn army was approaching,
and not knowing what to do,
he rode lightly into Jiā Shān.
Only then did he realize Fèngxiān's disloyalty.
He angrily said:
"Your father and son have led me to this pass;
now I wish to execute you,
but what good would it do for the situation!
I fear the army's resentment,
and if you evade the enemy and seek temporary safety,
disaster will surely befall me.
Do not follow me."
Fèngxiān dismounted,
cried, bowed, and departed.
Before he had traveled a few *lǐ*,
his attendants seized his father and son,
bound them, and sent them to the Jīn army.
The Jīn people beheaded his eldest son, Áng,
and sent Fèngxiān and his second son, Yù, in chains to the Jīn ruler.
On the way, they met Liáo troops,
who seized them and returned them to their country,
and then both were granted death.
The Grand Counselor Xiāo Délǐdì was banished.
Tābùyě was summoned to command the Imperial Guard.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Xiāo Sēngxiàonú, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Division, was appointed acting Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Division;
Xiāo Chálà, who was concurrently in charge of the affairs of the Northern Division Commissioner of Military Affairs, was made Left Yílíbì.
On the *wùchén* day,
Yēlǜ Gāobā, who was concurrently in charge of the affairs of the Palace Guard Commander, led the palace guards to surrender to Jīn.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the scout Xiāo Héshàng and the seal-holding officer Yēlǜ Shǎnsī were captured by the Jīn army.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
because many artisans from various bureaus had fled,
all followers, regardless of whether they were officials or commoners,
were granted official positions.
Originally,
an edict had commanded the Chancellors Zhāng Lín and Lǐ Chǔwēn, along with Qín Jìn Guówáng Chún, to guard Yān.
Chǔwēn, hearing that the Emperor had entered Jiā Shān,
and that communication of orders had been cut off for several days,
immediately conspired with his younger brother Chǔnéng and his son Shì,
outwardly feigning to join the rebellious troops,
and inwardly forming a pact with the Grand Commander Xiāo Gàn,
to enthrone Chún.

Consequently, he, along with other high officials Yēlǜ Dàshí, Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Yú Zhòngwén, Cáo Yǒngyì, Kāng Gōngbì, assembled tens of thousands of Qīdān and Han officials, various army units, and elders at Chún's residence.
Chǔwēn invited Zhāng Lín to attend
and explained the matter to him.
Lín said:
"Acting as regent would be acceptable."
Chǔwēn replied:
"Heaven's will and the people's hearts are already decided;
please establish him."
Chǔwēn and others asked Chún to receive the ceremony.
As Chún came out,
Lǐ Shì held a crimson robe and draped it over him,
ordering the officials to bow, dance, and shout "Long live!"
Chún was shocked and alarmed,
and repeatedly declined,
but was compelled to comply.
Chǔwēn was appointed Grand Commandant;
Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Grand Minister of Education;
Cáo Yǒngyì, Commissioner of Military Affairs;
Yú Zhòngwén, Vice Chancellor;
Zhāng Lín, Grand Tutor;
Lǐ Chǔnéng, Administrator of Military Affairs;
Lǐ Shì, Vice Director of the Imperial Household, and concurrent Supervisor of the Hanlin Academy Medical Officials;
Lǐ Shuǎng, Chén Mì, and over ten others who had participated in the grand plan
were all granted the *jìnshì* degree,
and given various official positions.
Xiāo Gàn was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Division;
the Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Xiāo Dàn, Commissioner of Military Affairs.
The 'Rebellious Army' was renamed the 'Ever Victorious Army'.
Thereupon, a general amnesty was declared,
Chún proclaimed himself Tiānxī Huángdì,
changed the reign title to Jiànfú,
and demoted Tiānzuò to Xiāngyīn Wáng.
He then took control of Yān, Yún, Píng, and the six routes of Shàngjīng and Liáoxī.
What Tiānzuò still possessed
was only the desert northwards,
the Southwest and Northwest Route Pacification Commissions, and various tribal groups.
Summer, fourth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Yēlǜ Fódǐng, the Southwest Pacification Commissioner, surrendered to Jīn;
Yúnnèi, Níngbiān, Dōngshèng, and other prefectures all surrendered.
Āshū was captured by the Jīn army.
Jīn had already taken Xījīng,
and the tribal groups south of the desert all surrendered.
The Emperor then fled to Éshāliè.
At this time, the Northern Division's Mógéshī presented horses, camels, and sheep for food.
Fifth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Grand Commander Mǎgē gathered the dispersed and dead [troops],
and they assembled at Oūlǐjǐn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Mǎgē was made Commissioner of Military Affairs of the Northern Division,
and concurrently Grand Commander.
In the third year, in spring, the first month, on the day *dīngsì*,
Hé King Huílíbǎo usurped the title,
calling it the first year of Tiānfù.
He ordered the Supreme Commander, Mǎ Gē, to attack him.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
Initially,
Zhāng Jué was the Deputy Military Commissioner of Liáoxīng Jūn.
The people elected Jué to manage the affairs of the prefecture.
After Qín-Jìn Wang Chún died,
Empress Xiāo Dèfēi sent Shí Lì'ài to take charge of Píngzhōu.
Juél knew that the Liáo dynasty would certainly fall,
so he trained troops and raised horses,
registering the able-bodied men for defense.
When Lì'ài arrived,
Juél did not admit him.
The Jīn commander, Nián Hǎn, entered Yān,
and first inquired about the affairs of Píngzhōu from the former Participating Official in Political Affairs, Kāng Gōngbì.
Gōngbì said:
“Jué is wild and reckless with few strategies.
Although he has local troops,
what can he achieve?
Show him that we have no suspicion,
and it will not be too late to plan later.”
The Jīn people summoned Shí Lì'ài to come to the front of the army,
and promoted Jué to Military Commissioner of Línhǎi Jūn,
still overseeing Píngzhōu.
Subsequently, they again wanted to dispatch three thousand elite soldiers to take Píngzhōu first
and capture Zhāng Jué.
Gōngbì said:
“If you increase the troops,
this is urging him to rebel.”
Gōngbì requested to go himself to observe him.
Juél said to Gōngbì:
“Of the eight circuits of Liáo,
seven circuits have already surrendered;
the only reason Píngzhōu has not disarmed
is to guard against Xiāo Gàn.”
He heavily bribed Gōngbì, who then returned.
Gōngbì reported back to Nián Hǎn, saying:
“He is not worth worrying about.”
The Jīn people then changed Píngzhōu to Nánjīng,
and promoted Jué to Provisional Chief Minister of the Department of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery (*Shì Zhōngshū Ménxià Píngzhāngshì*),
and concurrently Judicial Prefectural Governor (*Pàn Liúshǒushì*).
On the day *gēngchén*,
Yí, Jǐn, Gān, Xiǎn, Chéng, Chuān, Háo, Yì, and other prefectures all subsequently surrendered.
At Shàngjīng, Lú Yànlún rebelled,
killing the Qìdān people.
The second month, on the day *yǐyǒu* (the first day of the month),
Xīngzhōng Fǔ surrendered to Jīn.
Tián Hào, Military Commissioner of Láizhōu Guīdé Jūn; Dù Shīhuí, Acting Prefect of Xízhōu; Gāo Yǒngchāng, Acting Prefect of Qiānzhōu; and Zhāng Chéng, Acting Prefect of Rùnzhōu,
all registered the households under their jurisdiction and surrendered to Jīn.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
Empress Xiāo Dèfēi was executed,
Chún was demoted to commoner,
and all his partisans were released.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Xīngzhōng and Yízhōu resumed defending the cities.
In the third month,
the Emperor made a temporary residence south of Yúnnèizhōu.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day *jiǎshēn* (the first day of the month),
Yēlǜ Dàshí was made Administrator of the Northern Chancellery (*Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmì*).
On the day *wùxū*,
the Jīn army surrounded the supply train at Qīngzhǒng.
The Supreme Tutor (*Tàibǎo*) Tè Mǔgē of Yìngzhài stole Liáng Wang Yǎlǐ and fled.
The Prince of Qín, the Prince of Xǔ, the imperial consorts, princesses, and accompanying officials were all captured and lost.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
the Grand Princess of Liáng and Sòng, Tèlǐ, escaped and returned.
On the day *rènyín*,
Jīn sent a person to invite surrender.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
a reply was given requesting peace.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the Jīn army sent the imperial relatives and supply train eastwards.
So, troops were sent to intercept them and fight at Báishuǐ Luò.
Zhào Wang Xíníliè and Xiāo Dàoníng were both captured.
The Emperor sent the Palace Tablet and Seal Officer (*Pái Yìn Lángjūn*) Móu Lúwǎ to deliver a counterfeit gold seal made of rabbit bone and feign surrender,
then fled west to Yúnnèi.
The Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant (*Fùmǎ Dūwèi*) Rǔ Nú went to Jīn and surrendered.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
Jīn again sent a letter inviting surrender,
and a reply was made to the letter.
On the day *rènzǐ*,
the Jīn commander's letter arrived,
refusing the request for peace.
In this month,
Tè Mǔgē brought Yǎlǐ to the Emperor.
The Emperor was angry that he could not save all his sons,
and interrogated him.
The fifth month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Lǐ Qiánshùn, the King of Xià Guo, sent an envoy requesting the Emperor to visit his state.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the army commander Yēlǜ Díliè and others raided and took Liáng Wang Yǎlǐ at night, fleeing to the Northwest Department,
and installed him as Emperor,
changing the era name to Shénlì.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor crossed the river,
stopping north of Jīnsù Jūn.
Huílíbǎo was killed by the masses.
The sixth month,
an envoy was sent to invest Lǐ Qiánshùn as Emperor of Xià Guó.
Autumn, the ninth month,
Yēlǜ Dàshí returned from Jīn.
Winter, the tenth month,
the Emperor crossed the river again, returning east,
and resided in the Tūlǚbù Department.
Liáng Wang Yǎlǐ died,
and Yēlǜ Zhúliè succeeded him.
The eleventh month,
Zhúliè was killed by the masses.
The fourth year, spring, the first month,
the Emperor hastened to the army of Supreme Commander Mǎ Gē.
The Jīn people came to attack,
and the camp was abandoned, and the Emperor fled north.
Mǎ Gē was captured.
Mógēshī came to welcome him,
presenting horses, camels, and sheep,
and also led his tribesmen to provide defense.
At that time, the attendants had lacked provisions for several days,
and exchanged clothing for sheep.
Upon reaching the Wūgǔ Díliè Department,
the Emperor appointed the Grand Inspector General (*Dū Diǎnjiǎn*) Xiāo Yǐxuē to manage the affairs of the Northern Chancellery (*Zhī Běiyuàn Shūmì Shǐ Shì*),
and enfeoffed Mógēshī as Shényúyuè Wáng.
Tè Mǔgē surrendered to Jīn.
The second month,
Yēlǜ Yáoshè and ten others plotted rebellion,
and were executed.
In the fifth month of summer,
the Jīn people had already conquered Yān,
drove the wealthy families of Yān eastward,
and gave the empty city of Yān and Zhuō, Yì, Tán, Shùn, Jǐng, and Jì prefectures to Sòng to seal the alliance.
Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Kāng Gōngbì, Cáo Yǒngyì, and Yú Zhòngwén all relocated eastward.
The people of Yān wandered the roads,
unable to bear their suffering.
They entered Píngzhōu,
and said to the Garrison Commander Zhāng Jué:
"Chancellor Zuǒ Qǐgōng did not plan to defend Yān,
causing our people to wander,
with nowhere to settle.
You now govern a great strategic point,
command strong troops,
and are fully loyal to Liáo;
you will surely be able to enable us to return to our native lands,
and the hearts of the people look solely to you."
Jué then summoned the generals to deliberate.
All said:
"We hear that Tiānzuò's military strength is reviving,
appearing and disappearing south of the desert.
If you uphold righteousness and serve the Emperor,
welcome Tiānzuò,
and plan for restoration,
first charge Zuǒ Qǐgōng and the others with the crime of rebellion and surrender and execute them,
return all the people of Yān,
enabling them to resume their livelihoods,
and turn Píngzhōu over to Sòng,
then Sòng will surely accept it,
and Píngzhōu will consequently become a border commandery.
Even if the Jīn people send troops later,
internally we will use the forces of Píngshān,
and externally we will gain Sòng as a supporter,
so what is there to fear!"
Jué said:
"This is a major undertaking;
it cannot be done carelessly.
The Hanlin Academician Lǐ Shí is wise and resourceful;
he should be summoned to deliberate."
Shí arrived,
and his words concurred with theirs.
He then dispatched Zhāng Qiān with over five hundred cavalry,
conveying the order of the Garrison Commander,
summoning Chancellor Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Cáo Yǒngyì, Commissioner of Military Affairs Yú Zhòngwén, and Assistant Administrator Kāng Gōngbì to the west bank of the Luánhé River.
He sent the official for consultation, Zhào Mìxiào, to list ten crimes,
saying:
"Tiānzuò was exiled to Jiāshān,
and you did not immediately welcome him—
this is the first (crime);
persuading the Imperial Uncle, the Prince of Qín and Jìn, to assume the title illegally—
this is the second;
slandering the sovereign father,
demoting and enfeoffing Xiāngyīn—
this is the third;
Tiānzuò sent Wáng Yǒuqìng, the Palace Attendant, to discuss matters and you killed him—
this is the fourth;
when the declaration first arrived,
