Soup and tea are served.
The attendants step out of the hall gate,
bow to the officials and envoys and deputies to rise,
and bow.
The Qìdān Shèrén and Hàn-Chinese Géshǐ together announce,
all bow,
exclaiming
"Long live!"
The announcer bids each to attend.
First, the Sòng envoys and deputies are led down the hall via the western steps,
and exit through the western side-gate.
Next, the officials are bowed to to exit.
Report to the court gate that all is concluded.
The Huáng Tàihòu rises.
Protocol for Sòng envoys meeting the Huángdì: Sòng envoys offer congratulations for the birthday or the New Year (zhèngdàn).
When the day arrives,
the ministerial officials (chénliáo) enter the court before dawn (mèishuǎng),
the envoys arrive at the reception quarters (mùcì).
A report is made:
"The ranks are complete (bān qí),"
the signal is sounded,
and the Huángdì ascends the hall (diàn) and sits.
The Xuānhuīshǐ leads the officials in the ranks before the hall to complete the greeting (qǐjū),
then they withdraw from the ranks.
After the Qìdān ministerial officials complete their ranked greeting,
the officials who are entitled to seats are led up to the hall,
taking their positions to stand;
the remaining officials who are not entitled to seats,
all withdraw to the north side to stand in attendance (shìlì).
Next, the Hànrén ministerial officials are led in through the northern side gate (běi dòngmén),
bowing toward the hall (miàn diàn jūgōng).
The Shèrén bows,
announcing the greeting (qǐjū) from a certain official (mǒu guān mǒu) and those below him,
and all complete seven prostrations (bài),
leading the officials entitled to seats up to the hall,
taking their positions to stand.
The Prime Minister (xiàngshǒu) is led up to the hall via the southern steps (nán jiē),
reporting the roster (bǎngzi) of the Sòng envoys and their attendants,
taking his position to stand.
The ministerial officials all withdraw to the south side to stand in attendance.
The Music Department (Jiàofāng) enters,
completes their greeting,
and the Sòng chief envoy (nán shǐ) and deputy (fù) are led in through the northern side gate,
standing in the Dānchí (vermilion courtyard) facing the hall.
The Hěshǐ descends the hall via the northern steps,
to receive the letter box (shūxiá).
The attendant carrying the letter box kneels,
the Hěshǐ stands holding his tablet (hù) tucked in his belt,
and receives it at the northern steps.
He ascends the hall,
bows inside the railing (lán),
reports:
"The seal is intact (fēng quán),"
after which,
he hands it to the Shūmì (Grand Councilor) to be opened.
After the Zǎixiàng (Chancellor) reads it aloud to the Huángdì,
the Shèrén leads the chief envoy and deputy up the hall via the northern steps,
standing inside the railing.
The envoy (dàshǐ) celebrating the birthday is ushered slightly forward,
prostrates himself and kneels (miǎnfú guì),
and offers the greeting (qǐjū).
He rises from the prostration,
and returns to his position to stand.
The chief envoy prostrates himself and kneels,
completes his report (zòu),
rises from the prostration,
and withdraws;
he is led down the hall via the northern steps,
the chief envoy and deputy are bowed toward the north,
and they bow facing south.
The Shèrén bows,
announcing the presence (zhīhòu xiàn) of the Nán Cháo Guóxìnshǐ (Southern Court Envoy bearing Credentials), a certain official (mǒu guān mǒu) and those below him,
who offer the greeting (qǐjū),
completing seven prostrations;
The head of the ranks (bānshǒu) is bowed toward, and steps out of the ranks,
offering thanks for seeing the Heavenly Countenance (Tiānyán),
performing the ceremonial dance (wǔdǎo),
completing five prostrations;
he steps out of the ranks,
offering thanks for the long journey reception (yuǎnjiē), the Imperial Feast (Yùyán), the expressions of sympathy (fǔwèn), and the medicine (tāngyào),
performing the ceremonial dance,
completing five prostrations,
and is prompted (zàn) to stand by for attendance (gè zhīhòu).
They are led out,
returning to the reception quarters.
The Hěshǐ conveys the imperial decree (chuán xuān) granting audience robes (duì yī) and a golden belt (jīndài).
The attendants (cóngrén) and those below them are summoned to enter for an audience.
The Shèrén prompts the head of the ranks (bānshǒu) by name, and those below him,
to perform a repeated prostration (zàibài);
without stepping out of the ranks,
they report:
"May the Sage Person (Shèng Gōng) receive ten thousand blessings (wàn fú),"
and are prompted to perform a repeated prostration,
shouting:
"Wànsuì (Ten Thousand Years)!"
They are prompted to stand by for attendance.
They are led out.
The Shèrén conveys the imperial decree granting robes.
After the chief envoy, deputy, and attendants put on the granted robes,
the Shèrén leads the chief envoy and deputy in,
bowing in the Dānchí facing the hall.
The Shèrén prompts them to offer thanks for the grace (xiè ēn),
prostrate,
perform the ceremonial dance,
completing five prostrations,
and are prompted to ascend the hall for attendance.
The chief envoy and deputy are led up the hall via the southern steps,
taking their positions to stand.
The attendants are summoned to enter,
prompted to offer thanks for the grace,
prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted:
"There is an Imperial Edict granting a banquet (cì yàn),"
perform a repeated prostration,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to stand by for attendance.
The Chéngshòuguān leads them to stand beneath the northern corridor (běi láng).
The imperial table (yù chuáng) is brought in,
the high ministers (dàchén) present wine,
and the Huángdì drinks the wine.
The Qìdān Shèrén and the Hànrén Hěshǐ jointly prompt a prostration,
all officials entitled to seats and those standing in attendance prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to stand by for attendance.
When the drinking is finished,
a prostration is prompted,
all officials entitled to seats prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to take their respective seats and serve wine.
The Imperial Princes (Qīnwáng), Envoys-Chancellor (Shǐxiàng), chief envoys, and deputy share music (gòng yuèqǔ).
If an imperial decree commands them to drain their cups,
they all rise and finish drinking.
They set down their cups (fàng zhǎn),
and offer thanks in position.
A prostration is prompted,
and all follow in prostration,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to take their respective seats.
Next, wine is served to the officials and others sitting on the ground mats (fāng yīn) below.
If an imperial decree commands them to drain their cups,
the thanks are prompted as before.
After the first round of wine in the hall is complete,
the attendants beneath the corridor are prompted to prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to take their respective seats.
If the imperial decree commands them to drain their cups,
they all prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to take their respective seats.
Three rounds of wine are served in the hall,
followed by servings of tea (chá), dishes (xiáo), and meals (shàn).
After five rounds of wine,
waiting until the music piece (qǔ) ends,
the attendants beneath the corridor are bowed toward and rise,
prompted to prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to stand by for attendance,
and led out.
When the final piece (qǔ pò) is played,
the ministerial officials, the chief envoy, and the deputy all rise,
and bow.
A prostration is prompted,
all officials entitled to seats, the chief envoy, and the deputy all prostrate,
shouting:
"Wànsuì!"
They are prompted to stand by for attendance.
The chief envoy and deputy are led down the hall via the southern steps,
perform the ceremonial dance in the Dānchí,
completing five prostrations,
and are prompted to stand by for attendance.
They are led out.
Next, all the ministerial officials are led down the hall and exit,
and the Hě Mén (Palace Gate) reports that the affairs are concluded (wú shì).
The Huángdì rises,
and the warning signal (bì) is sounded.
Regulations for the Casual Banquet for the Sòng Envoys: Before dawn,
the ministers and officials enter the court.
The Sòng envoys arrive at their temporary residence (mù cì).
The emperor ascends the hall (diàn).
The regulations for the attendants (diàn qián), the Music Bureau (Jiàofāng), and the Khitan (Qìdān) civil and military ranks
are all the same as for the first audience (chū jiàn zhī yí).
The Sòng chief envoy and vice envoy join the ranks of the Hanlin Academicians (Hànlín Xuéshì bān).
They enter through the East Cave Gate (Dōng Dòngmén),
bow facing west.
The Attendant-in-Waiting (Shèrén) bows,
and announces the greetings (qǐ jū) from all civil and military officials, ministers (chén), and subordinates (mǒu yǐ xià).
They perform seven kowtows (bài).
They offer thanks for the summons (xuān zhào) to the banquet (yàn).
When the address (cí) is finished,
they perform a dance (wǔ dǎo).
When the five kowtows are completed,
the Usher (Zàn) directs everyone to ascend the hall for attendance (zhī hòu).

The Attendant-in-Waiting (Shèrén) leads the great ministers (dà chén), the chief envoys (shǐ xiāng), the officials (chén liáo), the vice envoys (shǐ fù), and the officials who should be seated on the square mats (fāng yīn yīng diàn) onto the hall via the west steps (xī jiē).
They take their positions and stand.
The remaining officials who are not required to be seated exit through the West Cave Gate (Xī Dòngmén).
The Usher calls for the followers (cóng rén) to enter.
They offer greetings (qǐ jū),
and thank the emperor for granting the banquet (cì yàn).
They stand along the two corridors (liǎng láng),
following the regulations for the first audience.
Two officials supervise the wine cups (jiān zhǎn).
The Music Bureau (Jiàofāng) performs a double kowtow (zài bài).
The Usher directs everyone to ascend the hall for attendance.
The Imperial Couch (Yùchuáng) is brought in.
The great ministers present wine.
The Attendants-in-Waiting (Shèrén) and Palace Gate Attendants (Gěhé Shǐ) direct the kowtows (zàn bài) and serve the wine (xíng jiǔ).
All follow the regulations for the first audience.
Next, wine is served to the officials seated on the square mats.
An imperial decree (chuán xuān) orders them to drink it all (yǐn jǐn),
following the usual regulations (cháng yí).
When the first round of wine on the hall is completed,
wine is served to the followers along the two corridors, as before.
When the serving of pastries (bǐng) and tea (chá) on the hall is completed,
the Music Bureau (Jiàofāng) delivers a congratulatory speech (zhì yǔ).
They bow (yī) and the officials, the envoys and vice envoys, and the followers beneath the corridors all stand up.
They wait for the improvised chant (kǒu hào) to finish.
They bow to the officials, who all bend at the waist (jū gōng).
The Usher directs the kowtows.
The officials who should be seated on the hall and those attending while standing all kowtow,
and proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!" (Wànsuì).
The Usher directs everyone to return to their seats.
Next, the Usher directs the followers beneath the corridors to kowtow.
They also follow the same procedure.
The banquet pauses (xiē yàn).
They bow to the officials, who stand up.
The Imperial Couch is removed.
The emperor rises,
and enters the inner chamber (gé).
The officials are led down the hall via the east and west steps.
They return to their temporary residence (mù cì), where flowers are bestowed internally (nèi cì huā).
The Receiving Official (Chéngshòu Guān) leads the followers out.
Flowers are bestowed.
They also follow the same procedure.
When the wearing of flowers (zān huā) is completed,
the followers are led back to stand in their positions along the two corridors.
Next, the officials and the envoys and vice envoys are led in through the two cave gates.
They return to stand in their positions on the hall.
The emperor exits the inner chamber.
He resumes his seat.
The Imperial Couch is brought in.
They bow (yī) to the officials who should be seated, the envoys and vice envoys, and the officials attending while standing, who all bend at the waist.
The Usher directs the kowtows,
and they proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs everyone to return to their seats.
The Usher directs the followers along the two corridors.
They also follow the same procedure.
Single-serving tea (dān chá) is served.
Wine is served.
Food (shàn) is served.
Fruits (guǒ) are served.
Wine is served nine times on the hall.
Music (yuè qǔ) is played for the chief envoys (shǐ xiāng).
When the sound stops,
they bow (yī) and the followers along the two corridors stand up.
The Usher directs the kowtows,
and they proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs them
"May you all depart happily" (gè hǎo qù).
The Receiving Official leads them out.
When the musical suite (qǔ pò) ends,
the officials and the envoys and vice envoys on the hall all stand up.
The Usher directs the kowtows,
and they proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs everyone to attend.
The officials and the envoys and vice envoys are led down the hall via the east and west steps.
The Khitan (Qìdān) ranks thank the emperor for the banquet and exit.
The Han (Hàn Rén) ranks, along with the envoys and vice envoys, thank the emperor for the banquet.
They perform a dance,
and when the five kowtows are completed,
the Usher directs them
"May you all depart happily."
When the exit is complete,
it is reported to the Palace Gate (Gěhé Mén) that there is nothing more to attend to.
The emperor rises.

Regulations for the Sòng Envoys' Farewell Audience (Cháo Cí) with the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) for the Emperor's Birthday (Shēngchén) and New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn): The ranks of the officials and the envoys and vice envoys are assembled
as per the regulations for the casual banquet (qǔ yàn yí).
The Empress Dowager ascends the hall and sits.
The Khitan (Qìdān) civil and military officials before the hall offer greetings and ascend the hall and finish.
The Chief Minister (Zǎichén) presents the memorial tablet (bǎng zi) for the farewell audience of the Sòng envoys, vice envoys, and followers, and finishes.
They take their positions and stand.
The Attendant-in-Waiting leads the envoys and vice envoys in through the North Cave Gate (Běi Dòngmén).
They bow facing south.
The Attendant-in-Waiting bows,
and announces the attendance and farewell (zhī hòu cí) from the Southern Court's (Nán Cháo) Credentials Envoy (Guóxìn Shǐ), official (mǒu guān), and subordinate (mǒu yǐ xià).
They perform a double kowtow.
Without leaving their ranks,
they present
"May the Sacred Person (Shèng Gōng) receive Ten Thousand Blessings."
They perform a double kowtow.
They leave their ranks,
express longing for the court (liàn què),
and when the address is finished,
they perform another double kowtow.
The Usher directs everyone to ascend the hall for attendance.
They are led up the hall via the south steps.
They take their positions and stand.
The followers are led in.
The Usher announces their names.
They perform a double kowtow.
They present
"May the Sacred Person receive Ten Thousand Blessings."
They perform a double kowtow,
and proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs
"May you all depart happily."
They are led out.
On the hall, they bow (yī) to the officials who should be seated, and the envoys and vice envoys take their positions and bend at the waist.
The Usher directs the kowtows,
and they proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs everyone to return to their seats.
When the serving of rinse water (tāng) and tea is completed,
they bow (yī) to the officials and the Southern Envoys (Nán Shǐ), who stand up.
They bend at the waist with the officials who should be seated.
The Usher directs the kowtows,
and they proclaim
"Ten Thousand Years!"
The Usher directs everyone to attend,
and they stand.
Six envoys and vice envoys are led to kneel and kowtow within the railing (lán nèi).
When they have received the letter box (shū xiá),
they stand up straight.
They bow (yī) and move slightly forward,
bend at the waist,
and when they have received the transmitted reply (chuán dá yǔ),
they withdraw.
They descend the hall via the north steps.
Within the vermilion steps (dān chí nèi), they bow facing the hall.
The Attendant-in-Waiting directs
"May you all depart happily."
They are led out.
The officials exit.
The Rites for the Sòng [Sòng] Envoys' Morning Departure from the Emperor's Court for the Emperor's Birthday and the Winter Solstice: Court officials enter the court according to the usual rites.
The Sòng [Sòng] envoys arrive at the receiving chamber.
Clothing and objects are bestowed upon the followers outside.
The Emperor ascends the Hall.
The Xuān Huī [Xuān Huī] and the Khitan civil and military officials rise, pay their respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]), and ascend the Hall,
following the rites for a casual banquet (qū yàn [qū yàn]).
After the Zhōng Shū Lìng [Zhōng Shū Lìng] finishes presenting the memorial (băng zi [băng zi]) announcing the morning departure of the Sòng [Sòng] Chief and Deputy Envoys and their followers,
all court officials stand waiting facing south.
The Bureau of Music (Jiào Fāng [Jiào Fāng]) finishes paying respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]).
The Attendants (Shè Rén [Shè Rén]) lead the six Chief and Deputy Envoys to enter through the North Cave Gate.
They face south,
and bow (jū gōng [jū gōng]) in the northern part of the Vermilion Steps (Dān Chí [Dān Chí]).
The Attendant bows (jū gōng [jū gōng])
and announces: "The Official X [Mǒu Guān [Mǒu Guān] Mǒu [Mǒu]] and his subordinates, Envoys of the Southern Court (Nán Cháo [Nán Cháo]), are here to pay their respects (zhī hòu cí [zhī hòu cí])."
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]).
They pay respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]),
show their reluctance to leave the Palace (liàn què [liàn què]),
following the rites for bidding farewell to the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tài Hòu [Huáng Tài Hòu]).
The Announcer (Zàn [Zàn]) says: "Let all subordinates pay respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
They stand up straight (píng shēn lì [píng shēn lì]).
They bow to the Chief and Deputy Envoys.
The Xuān Huī [Xuān Huī] announces:
"There is an Imperial Edict (Yǒu Chì [Yǒu Chì])."
The Chief and Deputy Envoys make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]),
bow (jū gōng [jū gōng]),
and stand up straight (píng shēn lì [píng shēn lì]).
The Xuān Huī Shǐ [Xuān Huī Shǐ] announces:
"Each of you is granted an official robe (duì yī [duì yī]), a gold belt, bolts of silk (pǐ duàn [pǐ duàn]), bows and arrows, saddles and horses, etc.
You should be aware of this."
The Chief and Deputy Envoys stand up straight (píng shēn lì [píng shēn lì]).
The Announcer gestures to the three Chief Envoys to step slightly forward.
They bow down, prostrate, and kneel.
They tuck in their tablets (hù [hù]).
The Gate Guardian (Gé Mén Shǐ [Gé Mén Shǐ]) hands over the separate list of bestowed items (bié lù cì wù [bié lù cì wù]).
After the passing is completed,
they rise from their prostration
and return to their positions to stand.
The Announcer gestures to the three Deputy Envoys to receive the bestowal,
and they also follow the same procedure.
The Announcer says: "Express gratitude for the grace."
They perform the ritual dance (wǔ dǎo [wǔ dǎo]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
The Announcer says: "Let the subordinates ascend the Hall and pay their respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
The Attendant leads the Chief and Deputy Envoys up the south steps to the Hall
and positions them to stand.
The followers are led in.
The Announcer says: "Express gratitude for the grace."
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]).
They pay respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]).
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]).
The Announcer says: "A banquet is granted."
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]).
All call out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!" ("Ten Thousand Years!").
The Announcer says: "Let the subordinates pay respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
The Receivers (Chéng Shòu [Chéng Shòu]) lead them to stand in the two corridors (liăng láng [liăng láng]).
The Emperor's couch (yù chuáng [yù chuáng]) is brought in.
The Emperor drinks wine.
The Attendants (Shè Rén [Shè Rén]) and the Gate Guardians (Gé Shǐ [Gé Shǐ]) announce, and the court officials and the Chief and Deputy Envoys prostrate (bài [bài]),
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
All follows the rites for a casual banquet (qū yàn [qū yàn]).
The court officials who are permitted to sit prostrate (bài [bài]),
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
They take their seats, serve wine, and play music.
The same procedure is followed in the square mat area (fāng yīn [fāng yīn]) and the two corridors (liăng láng [liăng láng]).
Serving preserved meats (xiáo [xiáo]), serving tea, and serving meals (yàn [yàn]) also follow the same procedure.
After the serving of steamed buns (mán tóu [mán tóu]) is complete,
the followers rise,
following the rites for the envoys upon ascension to their position (dēng wèi shǐ [dēng wèi shǐ] zhī yí [zhī yí]).
When the music is interrupted (qū pò [qū pò]),
the court officials and the Chief and Deputy Envoys all rise and stand,
prostrate (bài [bài]),
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
It follows the rites for bidding farewell to the Empress Dowager (Tài Hòu [Tài Hòu]).
The Chief and Deputy Envoys descend the Hall,
perform the ritual dance (wǔ dǎo [wǔ dǎo]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
The Announcer says: "Let the subordinates ascend the Hall and pay their respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
They are led up the north steps to the Hall
and stand inside the railing (lán nèi [lán nèi]).
The Announcer gestures to the two Chief Envoys for the Emperor's Birthday (Shēng Chén [Shēng Chén]) and the Winter Solstice (Zhèng Dàn [Zhèng Dàn]) to step slightly forward.
They kneel together,
and after receiving the document (shū [shū]),
they rise and stand.
The Announcer gestures to them, they bend deeply at the waist (qìng zhé [qìng zhé]), receive the respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]),
and withdraw.
They are led down the north steps from the Hall,
all bowing (jū gōng [jū gōng]) within the Vermilion Steps (Dān Chí [Dān Chí]).
The Attendant announces:
"May you all have a good journey (hǎo qù [hǎo qù])."
They are led out through the South Cave Gate.
Next, the court officials on the Hall are led out through the North and South Cave Gates. When this is completed,
the Gate Guardians are informed that there are no further duties.
The Rites for the Gāolì [Gāolì] Envoys' Audience: Court officials wear their ordinary attire (cháng fú [cháng fú]),
pay their respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]),
and the court officials who are supposed to ascend the Hall line up and stand on the Hall.
The Gate Guardians present the memorial (băng zi [băng zi]).
The Gāolì [Gāolì] Chief and Deputy Envoys are led to stand facing the Hall.
They are led up to the exposed platform (lù tái [lù tái]), prostrate and kneel.
After concluding the message reporting respects (fù zòu qǐ jū [fù zòu qǐ jū]),
they prostrate (bài [bài]),
rise and stand.
The Gate Guardians relay the Imperial Announcement (Xuān Chuán [Xuān Chuán]):
"Has the King inquired about the Emperor's well-being (ān fǒu [ān fǒu])?"
The Chief and Deputy Envoys all kneel.
The Chief Envoy reports:
"When we left, your humble servants inquired about the well-being [of the King]."
They are led down from the Hall,
and stand facing the Hall.
The tribute items (jìn fèng wù [jìn fèng wù]) are brought in
and arranged in front of the Hall.
After the Kuàng Hè Guān [Kuàng Hè Guān] finishes paying respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]),
the Official Leading the Introduction (Yǐn Jìn Shǐ [Yǐn Jìn Shǐ]) bows (jū gōng [jū gōng])
and announces: "The King of Gāolì [Gāolì] inquires and presents tribute (jìn fèng [jìn fèng])."
The Xuān Huī Shǐ [Xuān Huī Shǐ] announces from the Hall that the tribute should be sent to the storehouse (fù kù [fù kù]).
The horses are led out.
When the stretcher beds (dān chuáng [dān chuáng]) are brought out and completed,
the Chief and Deputy Envoys are led to withdraw,
bowing (jū gōng [jū gōng]) facing west.
The Attendant bows (jū gōng [jū gōng])

and announces: "The Official X [Mǒu Guān [Mǒu Guān] Mǒu [Mǒu]] and his subordinates, Envoys of Gāolì [Gāolì] for Presenting Tribute and Expressing Gratitude (Xiè Ēn Jìn Fèng Shǐ [Xiè Ēn Jìn Fèng Shǐ]), are here to pay their respects (zhī hòu jiàn [zhī hòu jiàn])."
They perform the ritual dance (wǔ dǎo [wǔ dǎo]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
They do not step out of the line (chū bān [chū bān]),
and report:
"May the Sacred Person (Shèng Gōng [Shèng Gōng]) enjoy ten thousand blessings (wàn fú [wàn fú])."
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]).
They step out of the line,
and express gratitude for seeing the Heavenly Countenance (Tiān Yán [Tiān Yán]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
They step out of the line,
and express gratitude for the distant reception and medicines (tāng yào [tāng yào]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
The Announcer says: "Let the subordinates pay respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
The private offerings (sī xiàn [sī xiàn]) of the Chief and Deputy Envoys are brought in
and arranged in front of the Hall.
The Kuàng Hè Guān [Kuàng Hè Guān] pays respects (qǐ jū [qǐ jū]).
The Official Leading the Introduction (Yǐn Jìn Shǐ [Yǐn Jìn Shǐ]) bows (jū gōng [jū gōng])
and announces: "The Official X [Mǒu Guān [Mǒu Guān] Mǒu [Mǒu]] and his subordinates, Envoys of Gāolì [Gāolì] for Presenting Tribute and Expressing Gratitude, present tribute (jìn fèng [jìn fèng])."
The Xuān Huī Shǐ [Xuān Huī Shǐ] announces from the Hall as before (rú chū [rú chū]).
The Chief and Deputy Envoys are led up the west steps to the Hall and line up to stand.
The Emperor does not enter the couch (yù chuáng [yù chuáng]).
The court officials accompany the wine service (bàn jiǔ [bàn jiǔ]).
The Khitan Attendant (Shè Rén [Shè Rén]) announces.
The Han Gate Guardian (Gé Shǐ [Gé Shǐ]) announces.
They make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]),
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
Each takes their seat.
Wine is served three times.
There are two flavors of preserved meat and meals (xiáo shàn [xiáo shàn]).
If an order is announced for them to drink all the wine,
they prostrate in their positions,
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
The Announcer says: "Each take your seat."
The preserved meat and meals are not announced.
They rise,
make a second prostration (zài bài [zài bài]),
crying out
"Wàn Suì [Wàn Suì]!"
They are led down from the Hall,
perform the ritual dance (wǔ dǎo [wǔ dǎo]),
making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]).
The Announcer says: "Let the subordinates pay respects (zhī hòu [zhī hòu])."
They are led out.
Within the receiving chamber (mù cì [mù cì] nèi), a separate official (shǐ chén [shǐ chén]) is dispatched to accompany the banquet (bàn yàn [bàn yàn]).
They rise.
After the announcement of the granted clothing and objects (yī wù [yī wù]) is completed,
they express gratitude from afar (yáo xiè [yáo xiè]).
After making five prostrations (wǔ bài [wǔ bài]),
they return to their lodging (guǎn [guǎn]).
Regulations for the Casual Banquet for the Kāo Lì Envoys: When the ministers enter the court,
the ranks are aligned,
and the Huángdì ascends the Hall.
The Xuān Huī, Jiào Fāng, Kòng Hè, and civil and military officials perform the daily salutations (qǐ jū),
all according to the usual regulations;
they thank the emperor for announcing the banquet,
as per the regulations for the Sòng Envoys.
The Zàn (Masters of Ceremony) each ascend the Hall to wait.
The Qì Dān ministers thank the emperor for announcing the banquet.
The Kāo Lì Envoys are guided to enter,
facing south, bowing deeply (jū gōng).
The Shè Rén (Palace Aides) bow deeply,
announcing the Kāo Lì Guó Envoys for Giving Thanks and Presenting Tribute, such-and-such official Mǒu and below, to perform the daily salutation (qǐ jū),
and thank the emperor for announcing the banquet,
making a total of twelve bows.
The Zàn each ascend the Hall to wait,
and the ministers and the main and deputy envoys take their places standing.
A great minister advances wine,
the Qì Dān Shè Rén announces it,
and the Hàn Rén Hé Shǐ (Palace Gate Envoys) officiate;
the ministers who have ascended the Hall all bow.
The Zàn each wait,
and the wine is advanced.
The great minister returns to his standing position,
the Zàn announces that the seated ministers bow,
and the Zàn each take their seats to serve the wine.
If an order to drink it all is announced,
the Zàn bows twice,
and the Zàn each take their seats.
The Jiào Fāng delivers the opening address (zhì yǔ),
and the ministers all stand up.
When the improvised verse (kǒu hào) is finished,
the Zàn bows twice,
and the Zàn each take their seats.
In all bows,
the cry
"Wàn Suì" is uttered.
When the musical suite (qǔ pò) ends,
the ministers rise
and descend the Hall.
The Qì Dān ministers thank the emperor for the banquet,
and after the Zhōng Shū Lìng and those below him have thanked the emperor for the banquet,
the main and deputy envoys are led to express thanks,
making seven bows.
The Zàn says,
"May all depart well."
The Kòng Hè officials wait outside the gate,
reporting that there is nothing happening at the Hé Mén (Palace Gate).
The Gōng Fèng officials (court attendants) leave by folding their ranks.
The next day, inquiries about the Shèng Tǐ (Emperor's health) are made.
Regulations for the Kāo Lì Envoys’ Morning Farewell: The ministers perform the daily salutation (qǐ jū) and ascend the Hall as per the usual regulations.
The Hé Mén reports the memorial (bǎng zi) of the Kāo Lì Envoys' morning farewell,
and they perform the daily salutation (qǐ jū) and express their yearning for the palace (liàn què),
according to the regulations for the Sòng Envoys.
The Zàn each ascend the Hall to wait,
and they are led to ascend the Hall by the western steps and stand.
The Qì Dān Shè Rén officiates the bow,
uttering
"Wàn Suì."
The Zàn each take their seats,
the Zhōng Shū Lìng and those below him accompany them with three rounds of wine,
and two flavors of food and delicacies (yáo shàn),
all according to the regulations of the initial audience.
After they have expressed thanks,
the Zàn says,
"There is an imperial decree for a banquet,"
and they make five bows.
The Zàn says,
"May all depart well,"
and they are led out,
and outside the curtained area (mù cì nèi), a different envoy is specially assigned to accompany the banquet.
When finished,
clothing and goods are bestowed,
which they receive kneeling,
expressing thanks from afar,
making five bows.
They return to the Gŭan (guest house).
Regulations for the Xī Xià Guó Envoys Presenting Tribute in a Morning Audience: After the ministers' usual morning court is finished,
the envoy is led in from the left,
arriving at the crimson terrace (dān chí),
and stands facing the Hall.
The envoy is led up to stand on the elevated platform (lù tái).
He bows (yī) and moves slightly forward,
bows and kneels,
and having submitted the report of the daily salutation (qǐ jū),
he rises, bending low,
and returns to his position.
The Hé Shǐ announces the inquiry,
"How is Mǒu?"
He bows deeply (jū gōng) to listen to the imperial instructions,
kneels, and reports,
"Mǒu is well."
He bows low, prostrates, and rises,
withdraws,
and returns to his position.
He is led down on the left,
arriving at the crimson terrace,
and stands facing the Hall.
The ceremonial gifts enter from the right and exit from the left,
and when finished,
the Hé Shǐ bows deeply,
announcing that the envoy of such-and-such country presenting tribute, N.N., waits for audience,
making a total of seventeen bows.
The Zàn officiates the waiting,
and they stand upright.
If there is a private presentation,
after it is passed,
the envoy is bowed to (yī) and bows deeply (jū gōng),
and the Zàn announces,
"The tribute presentation has been received."
The Zàn officiates the waiting,
they are led up the Hall on the left,
and stand in their positions.
The ministers and the envoy simultaneously utter a respectful sound (nuò).
Three rounds of wine are served,
the envoy is led down on the left,
and arrives at the crimson terrace to thank the emperor for the banquet,
making five bows.
When finished,
the Zàn announces,
"There is an imperial decree for a banquet,"
making five bows.
Waiting,
they are led out on the right.
The ceremony is complete.
A banquet is bestowed outside,
with the Kè Shěng (Bureau of Guests) accompanying the banquet,
and clothing and goods are also bestowed.
Regulations for the Xī Xià Envoy's Morning Farewell: After the usual morning court is finished,
the envoy is led in from the left,
announcing that the envoy Mǒu of such-and-such country waits to take his leave,
making two bows.
Without leaving the ranks (chū bān),
he performs the daily salutation (qǐ jū),
making two more bows.
Leaving the ranks,
he expresses yearning for the palace (liàn què) and presents his address (zhì cí),
then makes two more bows.
Clothing and goods are bestowed,
and he expresses thanks for the grace as per the usual regulations.
If a banquet is bestowed,
five bows are made.
When finished,
the Zàn says,
"Depart well,"
and he is led out on the right.
Zhì Volume Twenty-one: Lǐ Zhì Five: Jiā Yí Shang (Auspicious Rites, Part 1)
the *Shàng Shè Fèng Yù*
sets up an awning below the northern wall of the main hall,
facing south, and sets up the imperial seat (*Yù Zuò*);
the *Fèng Lǐ Láng* sets up temporary resting places (tents) for the officials and foreign envoys in the eastern and western audience halls (*Cháo Táng*);
the *Tài Yuè Lìng* sets up the suspended orchestra (*Gōng Xuán*) in the hall courtyard;
the position for raising the banner (*Jǔ Huī Wèi*) is on the upper section of the western steps of the second layer of the hall,
facing east;
the *Chéng Huáng Lìng* arrays the imperial carriages and chariots (*Chē Lù*);
the *Shàng Niǎn Fèng Yù* arrays the sedan chairs and palanquins (*Yú Niǎn*);
the *Shàng Shè Fèng Yù* sets up mats for removing swords (*Jiě Jiàn Xí*) at the eastern and western steps.
The seats for civilian officials (*Wén Guān*) of the sixth rank and above are arranged south of the transverse street (*Héng Jiē*),
on the east side, facing west;
the seats for military officials (*Wǔ Guān*) of the fifth rank and above are arranged south of the transverse street,
on the west side, facing east.
All face north in stacked rows,
with separate positions for each rank.
The generals and officers instruct their divisions of the Six Armies (*Liù Jūn*) to station troops and arms at the various gates.
The *Jīn Wú Zhàng* (Golden Crow Guards) and the *Huáng Huī Zhàng* (Yellow Banner Guards) are arrayed in the hall courtyard.
On the designated day,
the official escorting the patent (*Yā Cè Guān*) leads the patent in through the Western Side Gate (*Xī Biàn Mén*),
and places the patent on the patent stand (*Cè Àn*) atop the western steps.
The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the retinue class (*Shì Cóng Bān*) in,
and they take their positions.
The *Shì Zhōng* descends the eastern steps,
removes his sword and shoes,
ascends the hall,
kneels prostrate outside the balustrade,
and reports,
“The mid-preparations are complete.”
He descends the hall,
puts on his sword and shoes,
and returns to his standing position.
The *Gé Shǐ* (Palace Gate Messenger) ascends the hall via the western steps,
kneels outside the balustrade to request the wooden tally (*Mù Qì*);
bows facing the hall,
and reports,
“I report the imperial decree to summon the guards.”
The *Diàn Zhōng Jiān*, *Shǎo Jiān*, *Diàn Zhōng Chéng*, and others escort the *Jīn Wú* Four-Color Guards (*Sì Sè Zhàng*) in,
and they stand behind the officials.
The *Xié Lǜ Láng* enters,
and proceeds to the position for raising the banner.
The *Fú Bǎo Láng* goes to the palace gate (*gé*) to receive (the emperor).
The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the civilian officials of the fourth through sixth ranks and the military officials of the third through fifth ranks,
to their positions outside the gate.
The Emperor (*Húangdì*) proceeds in his palanquin (*yù niǎn*) to *Xuāndé Mén*.
The *Xuān Huī Shǐ* (Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs) leads the classes of the internal bureaus (*Nèi Zhū Sī Bān*) in paying respects,
and guides the Emperor to the gatehouse (*gé*),
where he dons the imperial ceremonial robes and crown (*gǔn miǎn*).
The *Shì Zhōng* descends the eastern steps,
removes his sword and shoes,
ascends the hall,
and reports on a tablet that the outside preparations are complete.
The *Tài Cháng Bó Shì* guides the *Tài Cháng Qīng*,
and the *Tài Cháng Qīng* guides the Emperor (*Dì*).
The internal bureaus withdraw.
The *Xié Lǜ Láng* raises the banner,
the *Tài Yuè Lìng* commands the striking of the *Huáng Zhōng* bell,
the five bells to the left all respond,
the musicians beat the wooden percussion box (*zhù*),
and the music begins;
The Emperor immediately takes the imperial seat (*Yù Zuò*),
the *Xuān Huī Shǐ* announces the closing of the screen/fans,
the music stops;
he announces the rolling up of the curtain,
and the screen/fans open.
The *Fú Bǎo Láng* presents the seal (*bǎo*) and advances.
The Left and Right *Jīn Wú* (Golden Crow Guards) report safety and peace.
The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the civilian officials of the third rank and the military officials of the second rank and above to enter the gate,
the music begins;
when they have finished taking their facing positions,
the music stops.

The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the retinue class (*Shì Cóng Bān*), and the Southern Class (*Nán Bān*) civilian officials of the third rank and military officials of the second rank and above, to combine their ranks,
facing north.
The Eastern Class moves west (in the order of rank),
the Western Class moves east (in the order of rank).
They pay respects,
performing seven bows.
They separate their ranks,
and each returns to his position.
The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the *Yā Cè Guān* escorting the patent down the western steps,
to the Vermilion Platform (*Dān Chí*),
where they place the incense stand and the patent stand in front of the hall.
When the patent is placed,
the music begins;
they take their positions,
and the music stops.
The officials holding the patent (*Pěng Cè Guān*) stand close behind,
standing opposite each other, east and west.
The *Shè Rén* leads the retinue class and the Southern Class to combine their ranks,
facing north as before.
The announcer calls for a second bow,
and all those present bow twice;
they perform the ceremonial dance (*wǔ dǎo*),
bowing five times.
They separate their ranks,
and each returns to his position as before.
The *Pěng Cè Guān* proceeds to the mat for removing swords below the western steps,
removes his sword and shoes,
ascends the hall via the western steps, holding the patent,
the music begins;
he places the patent in front of the imperial seat (*Yù Zuò*),
standing east and west,
facing north.
The *Pěng Cè Guān* stands below the western wall,
moving northward (to his position),
the music stops.
The official reading the patent (*Dú Cè Guān*) steps out of formation,
and stands in front of the hall.
The announcer calls for a second bow,
and three cheers of
“Long Live the Emperor” (*wàn suì*).
He proceeds to the mat for removing swords below the western steps,
removes his sword and shoes,
ascends the hall via the western steps,
and stands inside the balustrade,
in front of the imperial seat.
The *Shì Zhōng* takes the patent.
The *Pěng Cè Guān* brings the patent box and kneels before the *Dú Cè Guān*,
facing him and holding the patent.
The *Dú Cè Guān* kneels prostrate;
when he finishes reading,
he rises from prostration.
The *Pěng Cè Guān* kneels on his left knee,
and presents the patent to the *Shì Zhōng*.
The *Shì Zhōng* receives the patent,
hands the patent to the attendant,
descends the western steps,
and after putting on his sword and shoes,
returns to his position in front of the hall.
The announcer calls for a second bow,
and three cheers of
“Long Live the Emperor” (*wàn suì*),
and they return to their separate formation positions.
The *Shè Rén* leads the retinue class and the Southern Class to combine their ranks,
facing north as before.
The announcer calls for a bow,
and all those present bow;
they perform the ceremonial dance (*wǔ dǎo*) and bow (at the waist) as before.
The *Tōng Shì Shè Rén* leads the head of the ranks down the western steps,
where he removes his sword and shoes.
He ascends the hall,
the music begins;
he proceeds to his position inside the balustrade,
the music stops.
He kneels prostrate,
states his full title, and on behalf of all officials, presents the congratulatory address;
when finished, he rises from prostration.
He descends below the western steps,
puts on his sword,
puts on his ceremonial shoes (*xì*),
the music begins;
he returns to his position,
the music stops.
The announcer calls for a bow,
all those present bow twice,
perform the ceremonial dance,
bow five times,
and bow (at the waist).
The *Shì Zhōng* faces west from the veranda,
announcing,
“There is an imperial decree (*yǒu zhì*).”
All bow twice.
When the *Shì Zhōng* finishes proclaiming the reply,
the announcer calls for all to bow twice,
perform the ceremonial dance,
bow five times,
separate their ranks, and each return to his position.
Those of the third rank and above exit,
the music begins;
when they have finished exiting the gate,
the music stops.
The *Shì Zhōng* kneels prostrate before the imperial seat,
states his full title, and reports,
“The ceremony is complete.”
He rises from prostration.
He withdraws,
descends the hall via the eastern steps,
puts on his sword,
puts on his shoes,
and returns to his position.
The *Xuān Huī Shǐ* announces the closing of the screen/fans,
and the lowering of the curtain.
The *Tài Cháng Bó Shì* and the *Tài Cháng Qīng* guide the Emperor to rise,
the music begins;
when they reach the gatehouse (*gé*),
the music stops.
The *Shè Rén* leads the civilian officials of the fourth rank and the military officials of the third rank and below out of the gate,
where they stand in separate ranks;
next, he leads the retinue class out,
next, the *Bīng Bù* (Ministry of War) and *Lì Bù* (Ministry of Personnel) exit,
next, the *Jīn Wú* exit,
next, the *Qǐ Jū Láng* (Drafters of the Daily Records) and *Shè Rén* exit,
next, the *Diàn Zhōng Jiān* and *Shǎo Jiān* escort the *Jīn Wú* Light Guards (*Xì Zhàng*) out,
who still stand behind the officials.
Next, the Eastern and Western Senior Palace Gate Messengers (*Shàng Gé Mén Shǐ*) bow inside the Vermilion Platform (*Dān Chí*),
report that there is no incident within the government office (*yá*),
and exit in a rolled-up formation.
The Palace Gate Messenger (*Gé Mén Shǐ*) bows inside the Vermilion Platform,
and salutes,
“By imperial decree (*fèng chì*), the guards are dismissed.”
Go out,
stand centered between the ranks of civil and military officials outside the gate,
and call the Chéngshòu Guān.
The Chéngshòu Guān answers with a respectful assent,
goes behind the Géshǐ,
bows,
and salutes.
The Géshǐ bows,
and declares,
“By imperial decree, release the Imperial Guard.”
The Chéngshòu answers with a respectful assent,
bows,
salutes,
stands upright,
and proclaims aloud,
“By imperial decree, release the Imperial Guard.”
When the proclamation is finished,
he withdraws quickly.
The civil and military officials join ranks,
and perform the second bow.
One Shèrén acts as the Cílíng Guān,
bows before the palace hall,
salutes,
and declares,
“By imperial decree, release the Huánghuī Zhàng,”
and exits.
The release of the Jīnwú Zhàng is also done similarly.
The next day,
civil and military officials enter to inquire about the Sacred Person’s health.
In the first year of Tàipíng,
this ceremony was carried out,
largely following the old rituals of Táng and Jìn.
Furthermore, there was the ceremony for presenting the credentials to the Qìdān,
which mixed the wood-burning ceremonial registration ritual of Zhǔwǔ Kèhán
with Táng rituals.
Furthermore, there was the ceremony for presenting credentials to the Hàn,
which was largely the same as this ceremony, with minor differences,
adding the ritual for presenting the Imperial Seal.
Rites for the Investiture of the Huángtàihòu: Preceding the date,
the arrangements in the Yuánhé Diàn are set up according to the Rites for the Huángdì receiving investiture.
On the day itself,
the Huángdì proceeds to the Hóngzhèng Diàn.
The document of investiture enters,
the Retainers enter in formation,
outside the gate, the Jīnwú arrange the guards,
and the civil and military officials separate into formations.
The Shìzhōng removes his sword,
and announces
"The inner security measures are ready."
The Xuānhuī Shǐ requesting the wooden tally and summoning the guard follow the same procedure.
The musicians enter,
the Géshǐ stands between the formations of civil and military officials outside the gate,
and summons the Chéngshòu Guān.
(He) answers with an affirmation,
and hurries to stand behind the Géshǐ.
The Géshǐ bows,
salutes,
and says
"By imperial decree, summon the guard."
The Chéngshòu Guān bows,
answers with an affirmation,
salutes,
and leads the cry:
"By imperial decree, summon the guard!"
The civil and military officials join formations,
and perform the repeated bow.
The Diànzhōng Jiān leads the guard in,
the civil and military formations enter,
also following the same procedure.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ leads the officials and attendants of the various internal bureaus to wait in formation at the Tiānqiáo.
The Huángtàihòu proceeds to the Zǐchén Diàn,
riding a Píngtóu Niǎn,
led by children and young women playing musical instruments.
Upon reaching the Jīnluán Mén,
the Géshǐ presents the greetings of the Internal Bureaus,
(then) prompts the guidance of the carriage,
which proceeds first from below to the Yuánhé Diàn.
The Huángtàihòu enters the chamber in the northwest corner to change clothes.
The Shìzhōng removes his sword,
ascends the hall and reports that the outside preparations are complete.
The Xuānhuī (Shǐ) receives the tablet and enters to report.
The Shìzhōng descends,
and returns to his position.
The Xiélǜ Láng raises the standard,
and the music begins.
The Tàiyuè Lìng and Tàicháng Qīng guide the Huángtàihòu to ascend and take her seat.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ announces the closing of the fans,
the rolling up of the curtain,
the opening of the fans,
and the music ceases.
The Fúbǎo Láng respectfully places the seal to the right of the Huángtàihòu's seat.
The Left and Right Jīnwú Dàjiāngjūn exchange salutes,
bow,
and report:
"The military at home and abroad is peaceful."
The Dōng Shàng Gé Mén Fùshǐ guides the Chéngxiàng to enter by the eastern gate,
the Xī Shàng Gé Mén Fùshǐ guides the Qīnwáng to enter by the western gate,
the Tōngshì Shèrén guides the civil and military formations to enter,
according to the rites,
and the music begins;
when they reach their positions,
the music ceases.
The civil and military formations hurry forward,
face each other and perform the repeated bow,
then withdraw and return to their positions.
The Dōng Xī Shàng Gé Mén Shǐ and the Xuānhuī Shǐ guide the Huángdì, riding a palanquin, from the Hóngzhèng Diàn to below the West Side Gate.
(He) is guided through the gate,
and the music begins;
when he reaches his position in front of the hall,
the music ceases.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ prompts the Huángdì to bow,
to inquire of the Huángtàihòu:
"May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings,"
(then) bows again.
The Huángdì proceeds to sit in the West Chamber,
and all formations rise and greet him according to the rites.
The Běifǔ Zǎixiàng leads the investiture document,
eight minor officials from the Zhōngshū and Shūmì carry the document,
the Dōng Xī Shàng Gé Mén Shǐ guide the document,
the Xuānhuī Shǐ guides the Huángdì to escort the document,
and the music begins;
when they reach the position for placing the document in front of the hall,
the music ceases.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ prompts the Huángdì to perform the repeated bow,
and cry out
"Wànsuì,"
the assembled officials follow in their positions,
and salute.
Four Hànlín Xuéshì and four Dàjiāngjūn carry the document.
The Huángdì holds the document and proceeds,
performing the three ritual movements,
and presents the document.
It is carried up the western steps and onto the hall,
and the music begins.
It is placed in front of the Tàihòu’s seat,
and the music ceases.
The Huángdì stands west-facing, east of the investiture document.
The Shèrén guides the Chéngxiàng to perform the repeated bow in the hall,
and thrice cry
"Wànsuì,"
remove his sword,
ascend the hall by the western steps,
and the music begins;
when he reaches the position for reading the document,
the music ceases.
He bows low, kneels, and finishes reading the document,
bows low and thrice cries
"Wànsuì,"
then returns to his formation position.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ guides the Huángdì to descend the hall,
and the music begins;
when he reaches his position in front of the hall,
the music ceases.
The Huángdì bows,
performs the ritual dance,
finishes bowing,
and is guided up the western steps to the hall.
When he reaches the position in front of the Huángtàihòu’s seat,
he bows and kneels;
after delivering the address,
he bows low and rises.
He is guided down the western steps,
reaches his position in front of the hall,
bows,
performs the ritual dance,
bows,
and makes an obeisance.
The Shìzhōng approaches the balcony,
and announces the Tàihòu’s reply, stating
"A decree has been issued,"
and the Huángdì performs the repeated bow.
After the announcement,
the Huángdì is guided up the hall,
and the music begins;
when he reaches the West Chamber,
the music ceases.
The Chéngxiàng, Qīnwáng, Retainers, and civil and military officials join formations,
prompt bows,
perform the ritual dance,
and thrice cry
"Wànsuì,"
according to the rites.
The Chéngxiàng offers congratulations,
and the Shìzhōng announces the reply according to the rites.
The Chéngxiàng and those below him exit,
the music is played;
upon exiting the gate,
the music ceases.
The Shìzhōng reports
"The rites are complete,"
the Xuānhuī (Shǐ) requests the fans,
the fans close,
and the curtain is lowered.
The Huángtàihòu rises,
the music is played;
when she enters the chamber,
the music ceases.
The civil and military officials exit the gate and separate into formations as retainers.
The Bīngbù and Lìbù offer greetings,
the Jīnwú guard exits,
according to the rites.
The Géshǐ reports
"Dismiss the guard,"
all following the Rites for the Huángdì receiving investiture.
Rites for the Investiture of an Empress (Cè Huánghòu Yí): On the appointed day,
the civil and military officials from the north and south, and the inner and outer court ladies (Mìngfù), proceed to the side chamber (Mùcì) of the Duāngǒng Diàn.
When the Empress reaches the inner gate (Gé),
the Grand Councilor (Shìzhōng) announces
"The center is secure" (Zhōng Yán).
The court ladies are led in
and stand in facing positions, east and west.
The Emperor attends the balcony (Lín Xuān)
and orders the envoy to deliver the investiture scroll (Cè).
The Chief Envoy (Shǐ) and Deputy Envoy (Fù) escort the scroll to the side chamber outside the Duāngǒng Diàn gate.
The Shìzhōng announces that the outer preparations are complete (Wài Bàn).
The responsible office (Suǒ Sī) receives the imperial command (Chéng Zhǐ) to retrieve the screen fan (Shàn).
The fan is raised.
The banner (Huī) is raised.
Music begins.
The Empress exits the inner gate and ascends to her seat.
The fan opens.
The screen curtain (Lián) is rolled up.
The banner is lowered (Yǎn Huī).
The music stops.
The court ladies are led to face the palace hall to pay respects (Qǐjū),
performing eight bows (Bā Bài).
The Empress descends from her seat.
Music begins.
She proceeds to the kneeling mat (Rùwèi) below the hall.
The music stops.
The investiture scroll is led in
and placed in front of the Empress's kneeling mat.
The Shìzhōng relays the imperial declaration (Chuán Xuān).
The Empress performs four bows.
The accompanying court ladies all bow.
The official designated to read the scroll (Dú Cè Guān) is led to the front of the Empress's kneeling mat.
He prostrates (Fǔ Fú) and kneels to finish reading.
The Empress performs four bows.
The accompanying persons all bow.
The Empress is led up to the hall.
The imperial envoy leads the investiture scroll
and places it on the scroll table (Cè Àn) in front of the Empress's seat.
He retires
and stands waiting, facing west.
The court ladies offer congratulations (Chēng Hè) in the hall,
performing four bows.
The leader of the ranks (Bān Shǒu) is led up the eastern steps to the hall.
After presenting the congratulatory address (Zhì Cí),
he descends the hall via the eastern steps,
returns to his position,
and performs four bows.
The Shìzhōng announces the imperial reply (Xuān Dá), stating,
"There is an imperial decree" (Yǒu Jiàozhǐ).
[They perform] four bows.
After the reply is announced,
[they perform] four bows.
The Bān Shǒu ascends the hall to present wine (Jìn Jiǔ).
After the Empress bestows wine upon the Chief and Deputy Envoys escorting the scroll,
the Shìzhōng announces,
"The rites are concluded" (Lǐ Bì).
The Chéng Zhǐ retrieves the screen fan.
Music begins.
The Empress rises.
She enters the inner gate.
The music stops.
The court ladies are guided out through the east and west gates.
Rites for the Investiture of the Crown Prince (Cè Huángtàizǐ Yí): One day prior,
a curtained seat (Wò Zuò) is set up in the Xuānqìng Diàn.
Side chambers for the civil and military officials are set up in the court hall (Cháotáng),
along with board-marked positions (Bǎnwèi) in the courtyard.
The Director of Grand Music (Tài Yuè Lìng) arranges the palace orchestra (Gōng Xuán).
All arrangements are the same as the Rites for the Emperor's Receipt of Investiture.
The Palace Guard (Shǒugōng) sets up the Crown Prince's position in the north of the Cháotáng,
facing west.
The Director of Imperial Stables (Chéng Huáng Lìng) arranges the gold carriage (Jīn Luò) outside the Cháotáng gate,
facing west.
The Crown Prince's honor guard (Yízhàng), reed pipes (Jiā Xiāo), drums, and wind instruments (Gǔ Chuī) are arrayed outside the Xuānqìng Mén.
The Director of Rites (Diǎnyí) sets up the Crown Prince's board-marked position south of the horizontal street (Héng Jiē) of the palace hall,
close to the northeast, facing northeast.
Positions for civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above are set up east and west of the orchestra.
Positions for other officials follow the standard rites.
On the appointed day,
the Vice Director of the Palace Administration (Ménxià Shìláng) carries the investiture scroll.
The Vice Director of the Chancellery (Zhōngshū Shìláng) carries the imperial seal and ribbon (Bǎo Shòu).
Each item is placed on a table (Àn).
Two clerks (Lìshǐ) in crimson robes
stand facing each other, holding up the tables.
The seal table is north of the Héng Jiē, facing west.
The scroll table is north of that.
The Ménxià Shìláng and the Zhōngshū Shìláng stand together behind the tables.
The Shìzhōng announces on a tablet
"The center is secure."
The Crown Prince, wearing the Far Roaming Crown (Yuǎnyóu Guān)
and a crimson gauze robe (Jiàng Shā Páo),
and holding a ceremonial jade tablet (Bǐng Guī), exits.
The Crown Prince's Attendants (Tàizǐ Shèrén) lead him in.
He takes his position at the Bǎnwèi, facing the hall northwards.
Officials of the Eastern Palace (Dōnggōng), from the Three Mentors (Sān Shī) down, all follow,
standing southeast of the Crown Prince,
facing west.
When the Crown Prince enters the gate,
music begins.
When he reaches his position,
the music stops.
The Diǎnyí instructs the Crown Prince to bow twice (Zài Bài).
All those present bow twice.
The Director of the Chancellery (Zhōngshū Lìng) stands northeast of the Crown Prince,
facing west.
The Ménxià Shìláng leads the scroll table forward.
The Zhōngshū Shìláng takes the scroll,
advances, and hands it to the Zhōngshū Lìng,
then retires and returns to his position.
The officer relaying the decree (Chuán Xuān Guān) announces,
"There is an edict" (Yǒu Zhì).
The Crown Prince bows twice.
After the decree is relayed,
[he bows] twice.
The Zhōngshū Lìng kneels to read the scroll;
he prostrates, then rises.
The Crown Prince bows twice,
receives the scroll,
and retires to hand it to the Left Chief Administrator (Zuǒ Shùzǐ).
The Zhōngshū Shìláng takes the seal,
advances, and hands it to the Zhōngshū Lìng.
The Crown Prince advances to receive the seal,
and retires to hand it to the Zuǒ Shùzǐ.
The Zhōngshū Lìng and those below retire
and return to their positions.
The bearers of the tables (Yú Àn Zhě) retire with the tables.
The Diǎnyí instructs a double bow.
The Crown Prince bows.
All those present bow twice.
The Tàizǐ Shèrén lead the Crown Prince to retire.
Music begins.
When he exits the gate,
the music stops.
The Shìzhōng announces,
"The rites are concluded."
The Crown Prince ascends the Jīn Luò.
The Zuǒ Shùzǐ and those below stand attendant on either side.
The honor guard, drums, and wind instruments are arrayed outside the Xuānqìng Mén.
The Sān Shī, the Three Junior Mentors (Sān Shǎo), and all palace officials escort him before and after the Jīn Luò,
sounding the bells (Míng Náor) as they proceed,
returning to the Eastern Palace (Dōnggōng).
The palace courtyard has previously set up guards and honor ranks according to regulations.
When they reach the palace gate,
the bells stop.
The Crown Prince descends the Jīn Luò.
The Shèrén lead him in to his position and seat him.
The civil and military palace officials form ranks to offer congratulations.
The rites are concluded.
Rites for the Investiture of a Royal Consort (Wáng Fēi) or a Princess (Gōngzhǔ): On the appointed day,
the Chief and Deputy Envoys escorting the scroll, along with the scroll-reading officials, enter via the East Side Gate (Dōng Biàn Mén),
preceded by the staff-bearer (Chí Jié) to the palace hall.
The scroll table is placed north of the Héng Jiē, slightly to the east.
The envoys are led to stand facing the hall and bow low (Jūgōng).
The Shìzhōng attends the balcony and announces,
"There is an edict."
All bow twice
and bow low.
After the edict is announced,
they perform the dance of rejoicing (Wǔ Dǎo),
five bows,
and lead the scroll out through the Xuānqìng Mén.
The envoys escort the honor guard and the scroll table
to the reception hall (Tīng Qián) of the respective private residence (Sī Dì),
where they are arrayed facing the imperial palace (Quē).
A kneeling mat for receiving the decree (Shòu Cè Bài Rù) is set up.
The scroll table is placed to the left of the mat,
its cover removed.
The envoys stand in order to the right of the table.
The recipient of the scroll proceeds to her position and stands.
The Chuán Xuān Guān announces,
"There is an edict."
[The recipient] bows twice.
When the edict is announced,
the person carrying the scroll (Yú Cè Rén) lifts the scroll box, kneels, and holds it in front of the mat.
The official who reads the scroll and the recipient both prostrate and kneel.
After the reading is concluded,
they both prostrate and rise.
The recipient expresses gratitude (Xiè Ēn).
A King (Guówáng) performs five bows.
A Wáng Fēi or Gōngzhǔ performs four bows.
If multiple investiture rites occur on the same day,
the scroll and seal for the Grand Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) are presented first.
Next, the simultaneous edict is issued from the balcony.
Envoys are dispatched to invest the Empress, the Royal Consorts, and the Princesses.
Finally, the Crown Prince is invested.
The Rites for the Huángdì's Reception of the Hòu: A propitious day is selected.
When the day arrives,
the Hòu's clan gathers completely.
At dawn,
the Hòu exits her private residence,
and sits in the main hall.
The Huángdì dispatches envoys and matchmakers,
who arrive at the door with meat offerings, wine, and provisions.
The officiating officer reports this,
and the envoys and matchmakers enter to pay respects,
bow twice,
stand up straight.
After a short while,
they bow,
and present wine to the Huánghòu,
followed by the Hòu's parents, clan elders, and brothers.
When the wine has circulated,
they bow twice.
They present the betrothal gifts (nàbì),
deliver the formal address,
and having completed the two bows,
all members of the Hòu's clan take their seats.
The lady Tìyǐn bows four times,
and requests the Hòu to proceed to the carriage.
The Hòu takes leave of her parents, paternal uncles and aunts, and older brothers,
bowing four times to each;
to the elders of her clan,
she bows twice.
The Huánghòu ascends the carriage,
her parents offer her wine,
and deliver words of admonition,
which are then offered to the envoys, matchmakers, and escorts.
When the procession sets off,
her paternal uncles and aunts, and older brothers offer the Hòu wine as before.
The Bureau of Music (Jiàofāng) blocks the road, offering praises and blessings,
and the Hòu orders gifts to be bestowed upon them.
The Hòu's clan follows and bows,
presents wine,
and then the procession proceeds.
Approaching the palace gate,
the prime minister (zǎixiàng) transmits an imperial edict (chì),
bestowing wine upon the Huánghòu,
and extending it to all the escorts.
Upon arrival,
the Tìyǐn leads the imperial clan to welcome her,
bowing twice.
The Huánghòu's carriage stops seventy paces southeast of the side palace (biàndiàn),
and the lady Tìyǐn requests her to descend from the carriage.
Carrying a silver jar (yīng) on her back,
holding a silk cord (téng),
she walks along the ‘Yellow Path’ (huángdào).
One person follows behind, spreading a lambskin, as if dressing her in it,
and one woman walks in front, holding a mirror and walking backward.
A saddle is placed upon the path,
and the Hòu steps over it.
She then proceeds to the chamber of the spirit tablets (shénzhǔ), bowing three times,
once facing south and once facing north,
and pours libation wine.
She bows once toward the usher (yèzhě).
After offering congratulations,
she bows twice.
Next, she proceeds to the portraits of her parents-in-law (jiùgū yùróng) and bows,
offering ceremonial wine (diànjiǔ).
Select women from the imperial clan who are deemed suitable for bearing heirs (yízǐsūn)
bow to her twice,
and present her with the jar (yīng) and the cord (téng).
She then proceeds to the portraits of the previous emperors (zhū dì yùróng) and bows,
offering ceremonial wine.
The spirits bestow upon her ceremonial garments (xíyī), pearls and jade, and girdle ornaments (pèishì);
she bows to receive them and puts them on.
The Hòu's elder sisters or younger sisters, and those attending her in bowing (péibàizhě), are each given gifts.
Wine is bestowed upon all members of the imperial clan who came to welcome her and the members of the Hòu's clan who escorted her,
and after they have paired up and finished drinking,
the Hòu is seated in a separate hall (biédiàn),
while the escorts retire to eat in their assigned quarters (cì).
The matchmaker transmits the imperial decree, ordering the escorts to line up north of the hall.
Awaiting the Huángdì to take his seat on the throne (yùzuò),
one respected elder from the imperial clan is selected to sit in the honored position (dāng àozuò),
to preside over the marriage rites.
The officiating officers are commanded to go back and forth delivering messages to the Hòu's clan,
and lead the head of the Hòu's clan, along with the escorts, up to the hall,
to stand facing the imperial seat (yùzuò);
they all bow twice;
they bow once more,
move slightly forward,
and whisper the address regarding the delivery of the Hòu;
they withdraw and return to their position,
bowing twice.
The head of the Hòu's clan and the escorts bow three times toward the one presiding in the honored position (dāng àozhě),
once facing south and once facing north,
and bow once toward the usher.
The head of the Hòu's clan kneels and asks
“May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings” (Shènggōng wànfú),
bows twice;
and then repeats the address regarding the delivery of the Hòu,
bowing twice again.
The presiding elder and the matchmaker circulate wine three times,
order the escorts to bow twice,
and all take their seats,
concluding the banquet.
The next day (yìrì),
the Huángdì rises early,
proceeds to the portrait of the late emperor (xiāndì yùróng) and bows,
after offering ceremonial wine,
he returns to the imperial hall (yùdiàn),
to host a banquet for the Hòu's clan and the assembled officials (qúnchén).
The imperial clan and the Hòu's clan drink paired up as before,
while various performances (bǎixì), wrestling (jiǎochǐ), and horse games (xìmǎ) are held in competition for entertainment.
The day after that (yòu yìrì),
the Huángdì presides in the imperial hall,
bestowing gifts upon the Hòu's clan and those who presented the escort gifts (zhènsòngzhě),
each according to a defined hierarchy (yǒu chāi).
Those receiving the gifts bow twice,
present wine,
and bow twice again.
The Huángdì presides in a side hall (biédiàn),
and the relevant officers (yǒusī) present the register of the Huánghòu's garments and adornments (fúshì zhī jí).
After five rounds of wine,
the escorts take their leave,
the imperial clan presents gifts to the Hòu's clan;
the Hòu's clan returns gifts in thanks to the presiding elder (dāng àozhě).
The ceremony is complete.
The Rites for a Gōngzhǔ Marrying Out (Gōngzhǔ xiàjià yí): One paternal uncle of the Gōngzhǔ is selected to be the principal of the marriage (hūnzhǔ).
The procedures for the presiding elder (dāng àozhě) and the matchmaker to deliver messages,
from the offering of betrothal gifts (nàbì) up to the completion of the rites,
are generally similar to the Rites for the Reception of the Hòu.
A propitious day is selected,
and at dawn,
the matchmaker urges the household marrying the Gōngzhǔ (shàngzhǔ zhī jiā) to proceed to the palace.
Awaiting the Huángdì and Huánghòu to take their seats in the side palace,
they lead their clan members to enter and pay respects.
After presenting wine,
the imperial clan and the clan marrying the Gōngzhǔ are commanded to drink paired up.
The next day,
the household marrying the Gōngzhǔ, leading the Gōngzhǔ and the son-in-law (xù) and their clan, enter to pay respects,
and host a banquet for the Huángdì and Huánghòu.
After presenting the gifts for the escorts,
they formally take their leave (cháocí).
The Gōngzhǔ is bestowed two carriages with blue curtains (qīngxiǎn chē),
the heads of the ridgepole (chītóu) and the covers (gàibù) are all adorned with silver,
drawn by camels;
and one carriage for funeral escort (sòngzhōng chē),
the carriage tower (chēlóu) covered entirely in brocade,
with silver chī ornaments,
hanging bells (duó),
a large felt hanging at the back,
drawn by an ox,
carrying one sheep,
called the sacrificial sheep (jìyáng),
representing the articles for funeral escort,
including everything needed for the ritual of covering the corpse (fùshī yíwù).
Her son-in-law is bestowed court attire (cháofú), four seasonal suits of clothing (sìshí xíyī), saddle, and horse;
in total, all necessities are fully provided.
One person from the imperial clan is selected,
to escort them to their home.
The marriage rites for the daughters of Prince Qīnwáng who are enfeoffed as Gōngzhǔ: They follow this model (fǎngcǐ),
with rank reduced according to closeness or distance of kinship (yǐ qīn shū wéi chāijiàng).
Treatise 22, Ritual Treatises 6, Auspicious Rites, Part 2 (Zhì Dì Èrshí'èr, Lǐ Zhì Liù, Jiā Yí Xià)
Ceremony for the Morning Congratulation on the Empress Dowager's (Huángtàihòu) Birthday: On the appointed day,
the officials enter the court,
the national envoys proceed to the tent (mù),
the ranks are aligned,
following the standard ceremony.
The Empress Dowager ascends the hall and sits,
the Emperor (Huángdì) sits facing east, slightly to the side.
The Qìdān retainers announce the names in the hall.
The Qìdān and Hàn people officials,
and the Sòng envoys and deputies attach themselves to the ranks of the Hanlín Academicians.
They enter through the eastern and western side doors (dòngmén),
join the ranks, and offer congratulations.
The head of the ranks ascends the hall to offer birthday wishes.
They are guided out in separate ranks,
all following the ceremony of the First Day of the Year (Zhèngdàn).
The Music Bureau (Jiàofāng) offers greetings,
bowing seven times.
The Qìdān and Hàn people officials enter,
presenting wine,
all following the ceremony of the First Day of the Year,
except that the response is proclaimed, calling it
"Sovereign Edict" (Shèngzhǐ).
The Emperor descends from the imperial seat,
presenting birthday gifts to the Empress Dowager.
After the presentation is complete,
the Emperor bows twice in the hall,
and the officials below the hall all bow twice.
The Emperor ascends the imperial seat.
The officials are guided out in separate ranks.
The Chancellor (Zhōngshūlìng) and the Northern Great King (Běidàwáng) are guided up the western steps to the hall,
presenting the tribute offered by the Qìdān officials.
Next, the tribute offered by the Hàn people officials and all circuits (zhū dào) is presented.
The Guards (Kònghè guān) set up the litter beds (dānchuáng),
offering greetings,
and completing the four bows.
The Guiding Envoy (Yǐnjìn shǐ) bows respectfully,
announcing the presentation from such-and-such official (mǒu guān mǒu) and below among the civil and military officials (wénwǔ bǎiliáo), as well as from Gāolì, the Xià Kingdom, and all circuits.
The Commissioner of the Privy Council (Xuānhuī shǐ) proclaims in the hall that all the tribute presented shall be handed over to the relevant departments (suǒ sī).
The Guards sound their assent (shēng nuò).
After the litter beds pass,
the Qìdān and Hàn people officials offer thanks in sequence,
bowing five times.
The herald proclaims that they shall wait in attendance (zhīhòu),
and they are guided out.
The thank-you ceremony performed by the Music Bureau and the envoys presenting tribute from the various circuits is similar.
The Qìdān officials offer thanks for the proclamation of the feast (xuānyàn),
and are guided up the hall to stand in position.
The Hàn people officials and the Sòng envoys and deputies enter through the eastern side door,
facing west, offering thanks for the proclamation of the feast,
following the ceremony of the First Day of the Year.
The herald proclaims that they shall all ascend the hall to wait in attendance.
The officials and envoys and deputies ascend the hall to stand in position,
which is also similar.
The Wine Steward (Jiānzhǎn) and the Music Bureau ascend the hall.
The attendants enter and stand in the eastern corridor,
all following the same procedure.
The imperial couch (yùchuáng) enters.
When the Emperor first presents wine,
the officials take their places and accompany the bow.
When the Empress Dowager drinks the wine,
the officials seated or standing in attendance in the hall all bow,
exclaiming
"Ten Thousand Years" (wànsuì).
The herald proclaims that they shall wait in attendance,
standing.
When the Empress Dowager finishes drinking,
she personally bestows wine upon the Emperor.
The Emperor kneels,
finishes drinking,
retreats to the cushion position (rùwèi),
bows twice,
and the officials all accompany the bow.
If the Emperor personally bestows wine upon the chancellors (shǐxiàng), officials, or the Sòng envoys and deputies,
they all stand to drink.
The Emperor ascends to his seat.
The herald proclaims that the officials who should be seated, along with the envoys and deputies, shall all bow,
exclaiming
"Ten Thousand Years."
The herald proclaims that they shall all take their seats.
Wine is served to the officials in the hall on square mats (fāngyīn wù),
following the ceremony of the First Day of the Year.
When wine is presented once,
the attendants in the two corridors bow,
exclaiming
"Ten Thousand Years,"
and they all take their seats.
The imperial princes (qīnwáng) present wine,
following the ceremony of the First Day of the Year.
If the Empress Dowager personally bestows wine upon an imperial prince,
he kneels until he finishes drinking,
retreats to the open terrace (lùtái) above,
and bows five times.
The herald proclaims "Wait in attendance."
Wine is presented three times in the hall,
and after cakes and tea are served,
the Music Bureau kneels,
presenting a ceremonial address (zhì yǔ).
The officials, envoys and deputies, and the attendants below the corridor all rise with a respectful hand gesture (yī).
When the improvised verse (kǒuhào) ends,
the herald's command to bow (zàn bài) is also similar.
The serving of tea and the serving of cooked food (xiáoshàn),
are all similar.
The grand feast (dàzhuàn) enters,
and bowls of porridge (zhōuwǎn) are served.
Wine is presented seven times in the hall.
When the music for the chancellors and officials ends,
the attendants below the corridor are motioned to rise,
they bow,
exclaiming
"Ten Thousand Years."
[The herald proclaims] "Each proceed well" (gè hǎo qù).
The receiving officials (chéngshòu guān) guide them out through the two doors.
When the music piece (qǔ pò) ends,
the officials, envoys, and deputies are motioned to rise,
bowing respectfully.
The herald proclaims the bow,
and they all bow,
exclaiming
"Ten Thousand Years."
The herald proclaims that they shall wait in attendance.
The officials, envoys, and deputies are guided down the hall.
After the Qìdān officials finish thanking for the feast,
they exit.
The Hàn people officials and the envoys and deputies perform the ritual dance (wǔdǎo).
After finishing the five bows,
the herald proclaims
"Each proceed well."
After they exit the side doors,
the Gate Guard (Gémén) reports that there is nothing further,
and the Empress Dowager and the Emperor rise.
Whenever a Sòng envoy came
to offer congratulations on the birthday or the First Day of the Year during a Sòng festival (shèngjié),
this ceremony was instituted for the first time;
hence, it is detailed in the Guest Ceremony (Bīnyí).
The Five Bows (wǔ bài) procedure is: Bow,
Rise.
Bow again,
Rise.
Kneel,
Tuck in the writing tablet (hù),
Perform the ritual dance three times,
Kowtow three times,
Take out the writing tablet,
Immediately bow,
Rise.
Bow,
Rise.
Bow
again,
Rise.
That immediate bow (jiù bài)
is also called bowing low and rising (fǔfú xīng).
In the Guest Ceremony,
it is said that the officials shall all sit (zuò);
in this ceremony, it is called the high cushion (gāoyīn),
which is different from the square mat (fāngyīn).
Ceremony for the Emperor's (Huángdì) Birthday Morning Audience (Zhāohè Yí): Officials (Chénliáo) and envoys of foreign states (Guóshǐ) are lined up,
the Emperor ascends the hall and sits.
Officials, envoys, and deputy envoys (Shǐfù) enter,
form a unified line (Hébān) and offer congratulations (Chēnghè),
form a unified line and exit,
all according to the ceremony for the Empress Dowager's (Huáng Tàihòu) birthday.
The Director of the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Lìng) and the Prince of the North (Běidà Wáng) report the list of tributary items (Jìnfèng Biǎomù) submitted by the various circuits (Zhūdào).
The Office of Music (Jiàofāng) pays respects (Qǐjū),
performing seven bows.
Officials enter through the East and West Gates,
form a unified line and bow twice (Zàibài).
The herald (Zàn) announces the presentation of wine (Jìnjiǔ),
the head of the line (Bānshǒu) ascends the hall and presents the wine.
The Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Affairs (Xuānhuī Shǐ) pronounces the reply (Xuāndá),
the assembled officials (Qúnchén) thank the Imperial Edict (Xuānyù),
and divide into lines (Fēnbān).
Music is played,
the Emperor finishes drinking,
and they form a unified line.
The head of the line descends the hall,
divides into lines, and exits.
All is according to the ceremony of the New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn).
All tributary presentations are according to the ceremony for the Empress Dowager's birthday.
The Emperor proceeds to the Empress Dowager's hall (Huáng Tàihòu Diàn),
immediate imperial family members (Jìnshàng Huángzú), maternal relatives (Wàiqī), and high ministers (Dàchén) all follow,
respectfully welcoming the Empress Dowager (Tàihòu) to sit at the Emperor's hall.
The Empress Dowager rides in a small palanquin (Xiǎoniǎn),
the Emperor walks accompanying the palanquin at the side,
officials divide into ranks and lead the procession,
the Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Affairs (Xuānhuī Shǐ), the various offices (Zhūsī), and the Palace Gate (Gémén) form ranks and lead the vanguard.
The Office of Music plays music,
the Palace Guards (Kònghè) pay respects,
performing four bows.
The officials leading the procession stand waiting to the south of the Mountain Tower (Shānlóu).
The Empress Dowager enters the inner apartments (Rù Gé),
and bows to the envoys, deputy envoys, and officials who enter the side tents (Mùcì).
The Empress Dowager ascends the hall and sits,
the Emperor sits to the side facing East (Dōngfāng).
The Khitan (Qìdān) and Han (Hànrén) officials, along with the envoys and deputy envoys, are led in through the two side entrances (Liǎng Dòngmén),
form a unified line,
pay respects,
perform the ceremonial dance (Wǔdǎo),
performing five bows.
The herald announces they should stand waiting (Zhīhòu),
standing facing the hall.
The Emperor descends from the Imperial Seat (Yùzuò),
and stands upon the hall,
presenting birthday gifts (Shēngchén Wù) to the Empress Dowager.
After the presentation is finished,
the Emperor bows twice upon the hall,
and the officials above and below the hall all bow.
The Emperor ascends the Imperial Seat,
and the officials are led out in separate lines.
Khitan officials enter,
thanking for the announcement of the banquet (Xiè Xuānyàn).
Han officials, envoys, and deputy envoys enter,
announce their names and thank for the announcement of the banquet,
and ascend the hall to take their places (Jiùwèi).
Officials who are not required to sit exit,
attendants (Cóngrén) enter,
all according to the ceremony (Rú Yí).
The Imperial Table (Yùchuáng) is brought in,
the Emperor first presents wine to the Empress Dowager,
the Empress Dowager bestows wine upon the Emperor,
all according to the ceremony for the Empress Dowager's birthday.
The herald announces that all should take their seats,
and wine is served.
The announcement is made that the drinking is finished,
they return to their positions and offer thanks according to the ceremony.
After the first serving of wine on the hall is finished,
attendants enter and take their positions according to the ceremony.
Imperial Princes (Qīnwáng) present wine,
cake and tea are served,
the Office of Music offers felicitations (Zhìyǔ) according to the ceremony.
Tea, snacks (Yáoxiàn), and food are served according to the ceremony.
Wine is presented seven times,
when the music for the high officials (Shǐxiàng Yuè) ends,
the attendants stand up.
When the main musical piece (Qǔpò) finishes,
the officials, envoys, and deputy envoys stand up.
The rest is all according to the ceremony of the New Year's Day.
Ceremony for the Empress's (Huánghòu) Birthday: Officials hold court at dawn (Mèishuǎng Cháo).
The Emperor and the Empress bow to the sun (Bàirì) in front of the Great Tent (Dàzhàng),
Khitan and Han officials join in the bow.
The Emperor ascends the hall and sits,
the Empress bows twice,
the officials below the hall form a unified line and join in the bow.
The Emperor bestows birthday gifts (Shēngchén Lǐwù) upon the Empress,
the Empress offers thanks upon the hall,
bows twice,
and the officials all bow.
Khitan Gentlemen-in-Waiting (Shèrén) announce their names,
Khitan and Han officials enter in turn to offer congratulations.
The ceremonial cups (Zhǎn) are brought in,
the Gentlemen-in-Waiting act as heralds,
they perform the ceremonial dance,
performing five bows,
and when paying respects, they do not state
"May the Sacred Person (Shèng Gōng) enjoy ten thousand blessings (Wàn Fú)."
The herald announces two bows.
The head of the line ascends the hall, bows, and kneels,
announces his full official title (Quánxián) and offers birthday wishes,
is led down the hall,
